3.grammar: A completed (past-tense) verb of being. The ending -at marks a third-person feminine-singular subject, 'she' or 'it (feminine)', so it reads 'she/it was'. As a being-verb it normally introduces a description of that subject.
3.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

4.meaning: A short phrase meaning 'for you / to you (plural)' — expressing that something belongs to, is owed to, or is directed toward a group.
4.grammar: The prefix la- is a preposition meaning 'for' or 'to', expressing benefit or possession. The attached pronoun -kum means 'you (plural)'; its final vowel becomes -u (kumu) as a connecting sound before the next word. So it reads 'for you (all)'.

5.meaning: A noun meaning 'the home / the abode / the dwelling-place' — a settled place of residence or a realm in which one abides.
5.grammar: A definite noun, made definite by the prefix al- ('the'). The -u ending is the nominative case, typically marking the noun as the subject or the thing being identified. So it reads 'the home/abode'.

6.meaning: An adjective/noun meaning 'the Hereafter / the last (one) / the final', referring to what comes last and to the life to come after this world.
6.grammar: A definite feminine adjective made definite by al- ('the'). The feminine ending is written with tāʾ marbūṭa (ة); before a following case vowel it is pronounced as -t-, so the suffix here sounds -atu: the -a- is the feminine marker and the -u is the nominative case (the case used for the subject or the thing being identified, or to match a noun in that role). It conveys 'the last / the final (one)'.
6.root: ء-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — being last, coming after, the end

7.meaning: 'With / in the presence of / near' — an adverb of place and relation meaning at, by, in the sight or estimation of someone. It indicates nearness, possession, or what holds in someone's view (as in 'with Allah' = in His sight).
7.grammar: An adverb of place that is always followed by a noun it relates to. It carries a fixed -a ending; this accusative-type vowel is characteristic of such adverbs of place and shows the word is functioning to locate something ('at, near, in the presence of').

8.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
8.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

9.meaning: An adjective meaning 'pure / unmixed / exclusive' — something purely and solely one thing, free of any admixture, reserved for one party alone.
9.grammar: A feminine adjective (the ة marks the feminine form). The ending -an (written -tan with the feminine ة) is the indefinite accusative — the case often used for the object of a verb or for a descriptive/state word, and the extra -n (nunation) signals 'a/an', i.e. indefinite. It conveys '(being) purely/exclusively'.

10.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
10.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

11.meaning: A noun used to mean 'besides', 'other than', 'apart from', or 'short of'. It points to something or someone set apart from, or lower/lesser than, a named party. Often used in the phrase 'besides Allah'.
11.grammar: 'dūn' functions as an adverb-like noun of place/relation. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, which appears because it follows a preposition (such as 'min', 'from') and because it links to a following noun ('other than …'). It commonly heads the construction 'besides/other than [someone]'.
11.root: د-و-ن (d-w-n) — to be low/beneath, to fall short; hence 'below, other than, besides'

12.meaning: Humankind, people, mankind — the collective of human beings.
12.grammar: A collective noun ('people, mankind') carrying the definite article al- ('the'); the 'l' of the article assimilates into the following 'n', doubling it (al-nās → an-nās). The genitive ending -i marks the word as governed by a preposition or as the second term of a possessive.
12.root: ء-ن-س (ʾ-n-s) — humankind, sociability, familiarity; the word for 'people' is most commonly traced to this root (related to insān, 'human being')

13.meaning: A command meaning 'then long for / then wish for / then crave' — to desire and yearn for something, calling it to mind as a hoped-for thing.
13.grammar: The prefix fa- means 'then' or 'so', drawing a consequence. The verb is a command (imperative) addressed to a group: the masculine-plural 'you (all)' ending is the wāw with ḍamma (وُ, pronounced -ū) telling the group to do the action. The alif (ا) written after it is the silent spelling-alif (alif al-fāriqa) — a writing convention that is never pronounced.

14.meaning: A noun meaning 'death' — the ending of earthly life, the departure of the soul.
14.grammar: A definite noun, made definite by al- ('the'). The -a ending is the accusative case, most commonly marking the noun as the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon). So it reads '(the) death' as something received or aimed at.

15.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
15.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

16.meaning: A past-tense verb of 'being' addressed to a group: 'you (all) were', 'you (all) used to be'. From kāna, the core verb 'to be'. With a following predicate it often means 'you were (in a state of) …' or 'you used to …'.
16.grammar: This is a past-tense verb. The '-tum' suffix is the attached subject marker for a masculine plural 'you all'. As the doer is built into the suffix, the verb itself is in its base past form ('you all were').
16.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

17.meaning: The plural of 'ṣādiq': 'truthful ones', 'those who speak the truth', 'the sincere and reliable'. It describes people whose words and conduct match reality.
17.grammar: 'ṣādiq' is an active participle ('one who is truthful'). The '-īna' ending is a 'sound' masculine plural marker; the '-ī-' form (rather than '-ū-') signals that the noun is functioning as an object or is governed by a preposition/particle, while the '-na' completes the plural ('the truthful ones').
17.root: ص-د-ق (ṣ-d-q) — truthfulness, sincerity, to speak truly

1.meaning: A two-part expression combining 'and' with the particle of emphatic future negation. The core particle 'lan' negates a coming action with finality: 'will never / shall not (ever).' It denies that something will happen in the future, often with a tone of absolute impossibility.
1.grammar: A conjunction 'wa' ('and') joined to the negating particle 'lan'. 'Lan' governs a following present-tense verb, putting it into the subjunctive mood and turning its meaning into an emphatic denial of the future: 'it will never happen.'

2.meaning: A present/future-tense verb meaning 'they long for it / they wish for it / they crave it' — a group desiring and yearning for a thing.
2.grammar: An ongoing or future (present-tense) verb. The ya- prefix together with the -aw/long ending marks a third-person masculine-plural subject, 'they'. The attached -hu is the object 'it' or 'him', so it reads 'they wish for it'.

3.meaning: An adverb meaning 'ever / forever / at any time' — used to stress that something will never (or always) be the case throughout all time, especially with a negative to mean 'never, not ever'.
3.grammar: A noun used adverbially. The ending -an is the indefinite accusative, the form regularly used to turn a word into an adverb of time ('… ever / forever'); the -n (nunation) marks it as indefinite. Paired with a negation it strengthens it to 'never, not ever'.

4.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
4.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

5.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'she/it put forward / sent ahead / advanced beforehand' — to send something on ahead, often used of deeds a person has done in advance and dispatched before themselves.
5.grammar: A completed (past-tense) verb in an intensive pattern (doubled middle letter) that conveys deliberately putting something forward. The ending -at marks a third-person feminine-singular subject, 'she' or 'it (feminine)', so it reads 'she/it sent ahead'.
5.root: ق-د-م (q-d-m) — coming before, advancing, putting forward

6.meaning: Their hands. The plural noun 'hands' carrying the masculine plural possessive 'their'; often used idiomatically for what people do, produce, or are responsible for through their own deeds.
6.grammar: A plural noun with an attached possessive pronoun '-him' meaning 'their' (a group of males, or mixed). 'aydī' is the irregular ('broken') plural of 'yad' (hand). The pronoun ending makes the whole construction definite and possessed; the 'i'-coloured stem before the suffix reflects its genitive/possessed state, the form typically following a preposition or standing as object.

7.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
7.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
7.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

8.meaning: An intensive adjective/name meaning 'All-Knowing / fully aware' — one whose knowledge is complete, deep, and all-encompassing; as a divine attribute it denotes Allah's perfect knowledge.
8.grammar: An intensive adjective (the pattern faʿīl conveys 'thoroughly, abundantly'). The ending -un is the indefinite nominative — the nominative case marks it as the subject or the quality being affirmed, and the -n (nunation) signals 'a / an', i.e. indefinite. So it reads '(is) all-knowing'.

9.meaning: A noun phrase meaning 'of / about the wrongdoers' — those who do wrong, act unjustly, or put things out of their rightful place, especially by transgressing against truth and against themselves.
9.grammar: The prefix bi- is a preposition ('of', 'about', 'with'); al- makes the noun definite ('the'). The ending -īna is the masculine sound plural in its non-subject (oblique/genitive-accusative) form, which is the form required after a preposition. So it reads 'of the wrongdoers'.

1.meaning: An emphatic future verb with attached object meaning 'and you will most certainly find them' — to find, come upon, or discover someone to be in a certain state.
1.grammar: Two emphasis markers frame this present/future verb: the prefix la- ('surely') and the heavy ending -anna ('most certainly') together strongly affirm it will happen. The ta- prefix marks the addressee 'you'; the attached -hum is the object 'them'. So it reads 'and you will most certainly find them'.

2.meaning: A comparative/superlative adjective meaning 'more / most eager, greedy, or covetous' — keenest in clinging to and craving something.
2.grammar: A comparative/superlative adjective in the 'aCCaC' pattern, which conveys 'more / most …'. The -a ending is the accusative case, commonly marking the word as an object or as a description following certain words. So it reads 'more / most greedy'.

3.meaning: Humankind, people, mankind — the collective of human beings.
3.grammar: A collective noun ('people, mankind') carrying the definite article al- ('the'); the 'l' of the article assimilates into the following 'n', doubling it (al-nās → an-nās). The genitive ending -i marks the word as governed by a preposition or as the second term of a possessive.
3.root: ء-ن-س (ʾ-n-s) — humankind, sociability, familiarity; the word for 'people' is most commonly traced to this root (related to insān, 'human being')

4.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
4.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

5.meaning: A noun meaning 'a life / living' — the state of being alive, vitality, the span of one's existence.
5.grammar: A feminine noun whose feminine ending is written with tāʾ marbūṭa (ة). Before a case vowel the ة is pronounced -t-, so the suffix sounds -atin: the -a- is the feminine marker and the ending -in is the indefinite genitive (the genitive links the noun to a preceding word or follows a preposition, '… of …', and the -n / nunation signals 'a / an', i.e. indefinite). So it reads 'of a life'.

6.meaning: A connector meaning 'and', joined to the preposition 'from / of', introducing a portion or origin — 'and from' or 'and among'.
6.grammar: Two particles: wa- ('and') plus the preposition min ('from, of, among'). Min normally appears as 'min', but its final vowel shifts to 'mina' when the next word begins with the definite article, simply to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

7.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
7.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

8.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'they associated partners / they set up partners (with Allah)' — to ascribe partners or equals to Allah, the act underlying idolatry and polytheism.
8.grammar: A completed (past-tense) verb in a pattern meaning 'to make (someone) a partner'. The ending -ū marks a masculine-plural subject, 'they', so it reads 'they associated partners (with Allah)'.

9.meaning: A present/future-tense verb meaning 'he wishes / he would love / he ardently desires' — to want and warmly long for something, blending affection with desire.
9.grammar: An ongoing or future (present-tense) verb. The ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine-singular subject, 'he'. The final -u ending is the plain present-tense form (the mood used for a simple statement of fact). So it reads 'he wishes / he would love'.

10.meaning: A combination of 'one/a single one' with an attached pronoun meaning 'of them' — i.e. 'one of them', 'any one of them', a single individual singled out from a group.
10.grammar: The stem 'aḥad' means 'one, a single one'. The -u ending is nominative, the case typically used for the subject of a verb ('the one who…') or a word standing on its own as topic. The attached 'hum' is a possessive/partitive pronoun 'them / of them' (a group of males or a mixed group).

11.meaning: A conditional particle introducing a hypothetical or contrary-to-fact supposition: 'if (it were the case that…)'. It typically presents a condition that is unfulfilled or merely imagined, often implying the result did not or would not happen.
11.grammar: An indeclinable particle (no case ending). It signals a hypothetical 'if': it sets up a supposed condition whose consequence is then stated, frequently with the sense 'if X were so, then Y would be so' — often where X is contrary to fact.

12.meaning: 'He is given a long life / he is granted length of years' — to have one's lifespan extended, to be made to live long.
12.grammar: A present-tense passive verb. The yu- prefix with the -u vowel pattern marks third-person masculine singular passive ('he is/can be …-ed'). The doubled middle consonant belongs to the intensive (Form II) pattern, here carrying the sense 'to be granted a long/extended life'. The final -u is the indicative ending, used for a plain ongoing or general action.

13.meaning: The cardinal number 'a thousand'.
13.grammar: A noun for the number 1000. The -a ending is accusative, the case used for the object of a verb and, characteristically for numbers, for the counted item or for adverbial/quantity expressions; it also commonly precedes a following noun naming what is counted.

14.meaning: 'A year' — a single year, one complete cycle of time.
14.grammar: A feminine singular noun. The -in ending (tanwīn) is genitive plus indefiniteness: 'of a year / a year', the form a noun takes after a preposition or, especially after numbers, as the singular item being counted (e.g. 'a thousand of … year').

15.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
15.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

16.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
16.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

17.meaning: A combination meaning 'something that removes/displaces him' or 'that which would shift him away' — formed from a preposition 'with/by', an active participle 'remover, one who moves [something] away', and 'him'. The doubled root conveys pushing or dragging something off from its place.
17.grammar: The prefix bi- is a preposition ('with/by'), often used to reinforce a predicate. The stem 'muzaḥziḥ' is an active participle (the mu- prefix forms the doer) meaning 'one that removes or displaces'. After bi- the participle takes the genitive -i ending. The attached 'hi' is the object pronoun 'him' (the -i vowel of 'hi' here harmonizing after the preceding -i).
17.root: ز-ح-ز-ح (z-ḥ-z-ḥ) — to move/shove away, dislodge from a place

18.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
18.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

19.meaning: The punishment, torment, or chastisement — severe penalty or suffering inflicted as retribution.
19.grammar: A singular masculine noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending is the genitive, which typically links it to a preceding noun ('… of the punishment') or follows a preposition.

20.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
20.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

21.meaning: 'That he be given a long life / be granted length of years' — the same verb as 'to be granted long life', in a form used after particles that cast the action as wished, intended, or dependent.
21.grammar: A present-tense passive verb, third-person masculine singular ('he is …-ed'), built on the intensive (Form II) doubled pattern meaning 'to be granted a long life'. The final -a is the subjunctive ending, which appears after certain particles (such as 'that', 'so that', or 'lest') and casts the action as intended, hoped-for, or contingent rather than a plain fact.

22.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
22.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
22.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

23.meaning: 'All-Seeing / fully observant' — one who sees clearly and with complete insight; as a divine attribute, the One who perceives all things.
23.grammar: An intensive adjective on the faʿīl pattern, denoting one who possesses sight to a high degree — 'all-seeing'. The -un ending (tanwīn) is nominative plus indefiniteness, the form used for a subject or for a predicate ('[He] is all-seeing').

24.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
24.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.
24.root: — (particle + relative pronoun)

25.meaning: 'They do / they work / they act' — to perform deeds or carry out actions, ongoing or habitual.
25.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ya-…-ūna frame marks third-person masculine plural ('they do/work'). The retained final -na (the 'ūna' ending) is the indicative form, used for a plain, ongoing, or habitual action that is simply being stated.
25.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, work, act; deeds

1.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
1.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

2.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
2.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

3.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

3.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

4.meaning: 'An enemy / a foe' — one who is hostile or opposed; can refer to a single enemy or collectively to enemies.
4.grammar: A noun/adjective meaning 'enemy', on a pattern with a doubled final consonant. The -an ending (tanwīn) is accusative plus indefiniteness, the form used for the object of a verb or as a predicate after certain verbs (e.g. 'took/became an enemy').

5.meaning: The proper name Jibrīl (the angel Gabriel) prefixed with 'to/for' — 'to Jibrīl / for Jibrīl'.
5.grammar: The prefix li- is a preposition meaning 'to / for'. The name 'Jibrīl' is a proper noun of foreign origin; such names are 'diptote', so after the preposition they take an -a ending rather than the usual genitive -i. The ending here simply marks the noun as governed by 'to/for'.

6.meaning: A cluster of three elements: a connective 'so/then', the emphasis particle 'inna' that strongly affirms a statement ('indeed, truly'), and 'he/it'. Together: 'so indeed he / then truly it'.
6.grammar: 'fa-' is a connecting particle showing sequence or consequence ('so, then'). 'inna' is an emphatic particle that strongly affirms the sentence that follows and grammatically governs the following noun/pronoun in the accusative. The attached 'hu' is that pronoun, 'he/it', here serving as the subject being emphasized.

7.meaning: 'He sent it down / brought it down (in stages)' — the doubled stem conveys a gradual or repeated sending down. With the attached object: 'he brought it down'.
7.grammar: A past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he …-ed'), on the intensive (Form II) doubled pattern, which here adds the sense of sending down piece by piece or repeatedly. The attached 'hu' is the object pronoun 'it/him', receiving the action.

8.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
8.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

9.meaning: 'Your heart' — the heart (the seat of understanding, feeling, and faith), addressed to a single male: 'your heart'.
9.grammar: The noun 'qalb' means 'heart'. The -i before the pronoun is genitive, the case used after a preposition or to show possession ('… of …'); together with the attached 'ka' it reads 'your heart'. The -ka ending addresses one male person ('your').
9.root: ق-ل-ب (q-l-b) — heart; to turn over, turn about

10.meaning: 'By the leave of / with the permission of' — formed from 'with/by' plus 'permission, leave, sanction'. It conveys that something happens by someone's authorization or enabling will.
10.grammar: The prefix bi- is a preposition 'with/by'. The noun 'idhn' means 'permission, leave, sanction'. After the preposition it takes the genitive -i ending, the form used following a preposition and typically linking on to a following noun ('the permission OF …').
10.root: أ-ذ-ن (ʾ-dh-n) — to permit, give leave; also listening/ear

11.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
11.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

12.meaning: Confirming, verifying, attesting to the truth of something — declaring that a thing is true and corroborating it.
12.grammar: An active participle of the intensive (fa''ala) pattern, naming the doer of the action ('one confirming'). The -an ending is the indefinite accusative, often marking a noun as an object or describing the manner/state in which something occurs ('as a confirmer').

13.meaning: To / for that which — a preposition 'to, for' joined to a relative word meaning 'what' or 'that which'.
13.grammar: A combination of the preposition li- ('to, for') with the relative pronoun mā ('that which'). Together they introduce something toward or for which an action is directed; mā itself does not change for case.

14.meaning: Between; in the midst of two things. An adverb of place marking the space separating or lying among parties or points.
14.grammar: An adverb of place ('between'). It always ends in -a and grammatically governs what follows it, putting the following noun(s) into the genitive 'of' relationship. It does not change to show 'the' or a case of its own; the fixed -a is simply how this word is formed.
14.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies between

15.meaning: 'His two hands' — literally a dual 'two hands' with 'his' attached. Often used idiomatically for what lies 'in front of' or 'before' someone (i.e. between his hands).
15.grammar: The noun 'yad' (hand) in its dual form 'two hands'. The -ay ending is the dual in the genitive/accusative state (as opposed to -ā for the subject case), used after prepositions or in possessive links. The attached 'hi' means 'his' (the -i vowel of 'hi' harmonizing after the -ay). In construct, the dual's final -n drops before the pronoun.

16.meaning: A connective 'and' plus 'guidance' — 'and guidance': right direction, the showing of the correct way, that which leads one rightly.
16.grammar: The prefix wa- is the connective 'and'. 'hudā' is a noun meaning 'guidance'; because it ends in a special shortened alif, its indefinite ending appears as -an (written with tanwīn over the preceding letter). This -an is the indefinite marker; on such alif-ending nouns the case is not separately shown, so the word can stand as subject, object, or predicate alike.

17.meaning: A connective 'and' plus 'glad tidings / good news' — joyful news that brings cheer, an announcement of something good to come.
17.grammar: The prefix wa- is the connective 'and'. 'bushrā' is a noun meaning 'glad tidings'. It ends in a fixed long -ā (a non-inflecting feminine ending), so it shows no case vowel and no tanwīn; the same form serves whatever role it plays in a sentence.
17.root: ب-ش-ر (b-sh-r) — good news; also skin, human being

18.meaning: A combination meaning 'for the believers' — 'to/for' + 'the' + 'those who have faith': people characterized by belief, trust, and security in faith.
18.grammar: The prefix li- is the preposition 'for/to'; 'al-' ('the') follows, its alif elided after li-. 'mu'minīn' is the active participle 'believers' (the mu- prefix forms the doer: 'those who have faith'). The -īna ending is the masculine plural in the genitive/accusative state (versus -ūna for the subject case), here governed by the preposition 'for'.
18.root: أ-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — safety, security; faith, trust

1.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
1.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

2.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

2.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

3.meaning: 'An enemy / a foe' — one who is hostile or opposed; can refer to a single enemy or collectively to enemies.
3.grammar: A noun/adjective meaning 'enemy', on a pattern with a doubled final consonant. The -an ending (tanwīn) is accusative plus indefiniteness, the form used for the object of a verb or as a predicate after certain verbs (e.g. 'took/became an enemy').

4.meaning: A combination 'to/for Allah / belonging to Allah' — the preposition 'to/for' joined to the name Allah, expressing that something is due to, owned by, or directed toward Allah.
4.grammar: The prefix li- is the preposition 'to / for / belonging to'. 'Allah' follows, with the initial alif of 'Allāh' elided after li-. The final -i is the genitive ending required after a preposition; it marks Allah as the One to whom something belongs or is directed.

5.meaning: A combination 'and His angels' — 'and' + 'angels' + 'His'. Angels are created beings who serve and obey their Lord.
5.grammar: The prefix wa- is the connective 'and'. 'malāʾika' is the plural 'angels' (a broken/internal plural, feminine in agreement). The -i before the pronoun is genitive, the case used after prepositions or in possessive links; with the attached 'hi' ('His') it reads 'His angels'. The -hi ('His') refers to a single male/divine possessor.
5.root: م-ل-ك / أ-ل-ك (m-l-k / ʾ-l-k) — to send a message (angel as messenger)

6.meaning: A combination 'and His messengers' — 'and' + 'messengers' + 'His'. Messengers are those sent by Allah to convey His revelation to humankind.
6.grammar: The prefix wa- is the connective 'and'. 'rusul' is the plural 'messengers'. The -i before the pronoun is genitive, used after prepositions or to show possession; with attached 'hi' ('His') it means 'His messengers'. The -hi ('His') indicates a single male/divine possessor.

7.meaning: A connective 'and' plus the proper name Jibrīl (the angel Gabriel) — 'and Jibrīl'.
7.grammar: The prefix wa- is the connective 'and'. 'Jibrīl' is a proper noun of foreign origin and therefore 'diptote' — it does not take tanwīn and shows -a where another noun would show genitive -i. The -a ending here simply reflects this special inflection of foreign proper names.

8.meaning: A connective 'and' plus the proper name Mīkāl (the angel Michael) — 'and Mīkāl'.
8.grammar: The prefix wa- is the connective 'and'. 'Mīkāl' is a proper noun of foreign origin and therefore 'diptote' — it takes no tanwīn and shows an -a ending where another noun would take genitive -i. The -a here reflects this special inflection of foreign proper names.

9.meaning: A two-part connector meaning 'so/then, indeed…'. It joins fa- ('so', 'then', marking a result or consequence) to inna, an emphatic particle that strongly affirms the statement that follows ('truly', 'verily').
9.grammar: fa- is a connective prefix signaling that what follows is a consequence or next step. inna is an emphatic particle that introduces a nominal sentence, puts its following noun in the accusative, and strengthens the assertion; it does not itself take a case ending.

10.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
10.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

11.meaning: A noun meaning 'enemy', 'foe', or 'adversary' — one who shows hostility or opposition. The single Arabic form can refer to one enemy or collectively to enemies.
11.grammar: A noun carrying the -un ending: nominative case (typically the subject, or the completing word after 'to be') combined with tanwīn, the indefinite '-n' that marks it as 'an enemy' rather than 'the enemy'.
11.root: ع-د-و (ʿ-d-w) — hostility, enmity, transgressing a limit

12.meaning: For/to those who reject faith — the active participle 'kāfir' (one who covers over, conceals, and so denies the truth) in its sound masculine plural, preceded by the preposition 'li-' meaning 'to' or 'for'.
12.grammar: The 'li-' prefix means 'to/for'. The '-īna' ending is the sound masculine plural in its genitive/accusative (oblique) form, used after a preposition; it marks 'the rejecters' as the object of 'for'. The base is an active participle: 'one who is rejecting/covering up faith'.
12.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal, and thus reject or disbelieve

1.meaning: "And indeed / and most certainly" — combines 'and' with the emphatic 'la-' and the particle 'qad'; before a past-tense verb 'qad' affirms that the action has definitely and already happened, reinforced into 'and indeed it surely did'.
1.grammar: The conjunction 'and' plus the emphatic 'la-' ('surely') plus the particle 'qad'. With a past-tense verb, 'qad' stresses that the act is real and completed ('has indeed happened'); together they form a strong oath-like affirmation. These are function words and are not inflected.

2.meaning: We sent down / We caused to descend — a past-tense verb (form IV of n-z-l) conveying the act of sending something down from a higher source, especially revelation, with 'We' as the doer.
2.grammar: Past tense. The '-nā' suffix is the subject pronoun 'we', so the whole word means 'we sent down'. The form IV pattern (a- prefix on the stem) gives a causative sense: to make something come down.
2.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — to come down, descend; (causative) to send down

3.meaning: 'To you' (addressing one person): indicating direction or motion toward a single individual — that toward which something moves or is directed.
3.grammar: The preposition ilā ('to, towards') with an attached pronoun; before a suffix ilā takes the form ilay-. The -ka ending is the pronoun 'you' for a single male addressee. Pronouns following a preposition stand in the genitive relationship, though their form does not visibly change for case.

4.meaning: Signs / verses / evidentiary marks — the plural of 'āyah', a sign or token that points to something beyond itself; used for miraculous signs, natural wonders, and the discrete verses of revelation.
4.grammar: A sound feminine plural. The '-in' (nunation) ending marks it as indefinite ('signs', not 'the signs') and is the genitive/accusative (oblique) case form, typical of an object or a word governed by a preposition.
4.root: ا-ي-ي (ʾ-y-y) — a sign, mark, or token that indicates something

5.meaning: Clear, manifest, self-evident — the feminine plural of 'bayyin', describing things that are plainly evident and make matters distinct; an intensive adjective implying something that clarifies and is itself unmistakable.
5.grammar: A sound feminine plural adjective. The '-in' (nunation) ending marks it indefinite and in the genitive/accusative (oblique) case, so it agrees with an indefinite feminine plural noun it describes ('clear ___').
5.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — to be clear, distinct, evident; to make plain

6.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
6.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

7.meaning: He disbelieves / rejects / covers up — the present-tense act of denying or being ungrateful, refusing to accept the truth; done by a single male (or impersonal) subject.
7.grammar: Present/imperfect tense. The 'ya-' prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'). The final '-u' ending is the indicative mood, the default form for a simple ongoing or habitual statement ('he disbelieves').
7.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal, and thus reject or be ungrateful

8.meaning: In it / in them / by it — the preposition 'bi-' (with, in, by) joined to the attached pronoun 'hā' referring to a single feminine or non-human plural antecedent.
8.grammar: A preposition plus pronoun. 'bi-' means 'in/with/by'; the suffix '-hā' is the object pronoun for a feminine singular or a non-human plural ('it'/'them'). Pronouns after a preposition take this attached (genitive) form.
8.root: — (particle with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

9.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
9.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

10.meaning: Those who defiantly disobey — the active participle 'fāsiq' (one who breaks away from obedience, transgressing moral and religious limits) in its sound masculine plural, with the definite article.
10.grammar: Definite ('al-') sound masculine plural active participle. The '-ūna' ending is the nominative (subject) form of the masculine plural, used when the word is the doer of an action or the subject of a sentence.
10.root: ف-س-ق (f-s-q) — to break away, depart from obedience; to act immorally

1.meaning: Is it not that...? / And every time...? — a cluster of three particles: the questioning 'a-' (asking for affirmation or rebuke), the connecting 'wa' (and), and 'kullamā' meaning 'every time / whenever' which introduces a recurring condition.
1.grammar: A compound of particles. 'a-' opens a question (often rhetorical, expecting agreement). 'wa' joins to what precedes. 'kullamā' (literally 'every that') is a conjunction meaning 'every time / whenever', introducing an action that repeats whenever a condition recurs.

2.meaning: They made a covenant / pledged — past-tense form III of ʿ-h-d, denoting a mutual binding agreement or solemn promise undertaken by a male plural subject.
2.grammar: Past tense. The '-ū' suffix marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'). The form III pattern (long 'ā' after the first root letter) often conveys a mutual or reciprocal action — here, entering into a covenant with another party.
2.root: ع-ه-د (ʿ-h-d) — a covenant, pledge, binding commitment

3.meaning: A covenant / pledge — a binding agreement, promise, or solemn commitment; an undertaking one is obliged to keep.
3.grammar: An indefinite noun. The '-an' ending (nunation) is indefinite accusative, the case that typically marks the direct object of a verb — the thing taken, made, or given.

4.meaning: He cast it aside / flung it away — the past-tense act of throwing something off or discarding it, often figuratively rejecting or disregarding it, with an attached object pronoun 'it'.
4.grammar: Past tense, third-person masculine singular ('he ___'). The '-hu' suffix is the object pronoun 'it/him', so the verb-plus-suffix means 'he cast it aside'. The verb carries the nuance of tossing something away as worthless.
4.root: ن-ب-ذ (n-b-dh) — to throw away, cast off, discard

5.meaning: A group, party, or faction — a portion or section of people set apart from a larger body.
5.grammar: A masculine singular noun. The '-un' (tanwīn) marks it indefinite ('a group') and in the nominative case, typically used for the subject of a sentence.
5.root: ف-ر-ق (f-r-q) — to separate, divide; a division

6.meaning: 'Among them / from them / some of them' — the preposition 'min' ('from, of, among') joined to the attached pronoun 'hum' ('them').
6.grammar: The preposition 'min' ('from / of / among') with the attached pronoun 'hum' ('them'), referring to a masculine plural group. Together they often express 'part of them' or 'some among them'.

7.meaning: A particle of retraction meaning 'rather,' 'no, but,' or 'nay' — it cancels or sets aside what was just said and shifts to a corrected or contrasting statement that follows.
7.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it never changes form). Its function is to redirect the discourse: it dismisses a prior idea and introduces what is actually the case.

8.meaning: Most of them / the greater part of them — the noun 'akthar' (the greater number, the majority), built on a comparative/superlative pattern of k-th-r ('much/many'), with the pronoun 'them'.
8.grammar: A noun in possessive (genitive) construction: 'aktharu' ('the most of') plus the attached pronoun '-hum' ('them') yields 'most of them'. The '-u' on 'akthar' is the nominative ending, typical when this phrase serves as the subject.
8.root: ك-ث-ر (k-th-r) — to be much, many, numerous

9.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
9.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

10.meaning: 'They believe / they have faith' — to affirm something as true with trusting inner conviction and to feel secure in it. The verb carries both believing and being at peace through that belief; in religious use it is to commit oneself in faith.
10.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb, masculine plural. The yu-…-una frame means 'they (men, or a mixed group) do' the action now or habitually. The retained final -na marks the indicative (a plain, unqualified statement) — 'they believe' — as opposed to forms where that -na drops. The verb is Form IV (amana), used intransitively here meaning simply 'to believe / to have faith'.

1.meaning: A compound meaning 'and when' — it sets up a circumstance in past time, marking the moment at which something occurred, with the result clause typically following. It carries the sense of 'when, at the time that.'
1.grammar: A particle phrase introducing a past-time clause. Lammā signals 'when' for completed events and expects a following clause stating what then happened; the wa- prefix means 'and.'

2.meaning: To come to, to arrive at someone; the act of something or someone reaching or presenting itself to a person. A core verb for arrival and the coming of events, messengers, or messages.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third-person masculine singular ('he/it came') — the -a ending marks a completed act by a single masculine subject. The attached -hum is the object 'them,' the ones reached by the coming.

3.meaning: "a messenger" — one who is sent bearing a message; an envoy or apostle, here in the indefinite sense "a messenger."
3.grammar: The -un ending is nominative with nunation: the -u marks it as a subject (the doer/topic), and the final -n signals that it is indefinite ("a messenger," not "the messenger").

4.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
4.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

5.meaning: 'In the presence of / from with / from the side of' — a noun of place and source meaning nearness or 'with,' used for what is in someone's keeping, possession, or vicinity, and figuratively what proceeds from them.
5.grammar: An adverbial noun meaning 'at / with / in the presence of,' here in the genitive case (the -i ending), as happens when it follows a preposition or links to a following noun ('the presence OF …'). It typically expresses 'from the side of' or 'in the keeping of' someone.
5.root: ع-ن-د (ʿ-n-d) — being at, near, or with; presence and proximity

6.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
6.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

7.meaning: Confirming, verifying, attesting as true — one that bears out and corroborates something else, declaring it authentic. Used of a scripture, it means one that affirms the truth of what came before it.
7.grammar: An active participle ('one confirming') with the -un ending, the nominative indefinite case, typically marking a subject or describing one. The mu- prefix forms the doer of the action; the doubled middle consonant gives the sense of actively affirming truth.
7.root: ص-د-ق (ṣ-d-q) — to be true/truthful; truth, confirmation

8.meaning: To / for that which — a preposition 'to, for' joined to a relative word meaning 'what' or 'that which'.
8.grammar: A combination of the preposition li- ('to, for') with the relative pronoun mā ('that which'). Together they introduce something toward or for which an action is directed; mā itself does not change for case.

9.meaning: With them, in their company or possession — expressing accompaniment or togetherness. Maʿa denotes being alongside or in the presence of someone or something.
9.grammar: An adverb of accompaniment ('with') fixed in the -a form, joined to the pronoun -hum ('them'). Together they express that something is in the company or possession of a group.

10.meaning: He cast aside / threw away — the bare past-tense verb of discarding or flinging something off, often used figuratively for rejecting or paying no heed.
10.grammar: Past tense, third-person masculine singular: simply 'he cast aside / threw away'. With no attached pronoun, the object (what was thrown) stands as a separate word. The verb implies treating something as worthless.
10.root: ن-ب-ذ (n-b-dh) — to throw away, cast off, discard

11.meaning: A group, party, or faction — a portion or section of people set apart from a larger body.
11.grammar: A masculine singular noun. The '-un' (tanwīn) marks it indefinite ('a group') and in the nominative case, typically used for the subject of a sentence.
11.root: ف-ر-ق (f-r-q) — to separate, divide; a division

12.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
12.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

13.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
13.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

14.meaning: They were given / granted — the passive past tense of the verb 'to give/bring' (form IV of ʾ-t-y), where a plural group receives something without the giver being named.
14.grammar: Passive past tense. The internal vowelling (u-...-u) marks it as passive — the subject receives the action rather than doing it. The '-ū' ending means 'they', giving 'they were given' (the giver left unmentioned).
14.root: ا-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (form IV) to bring or give

15.meaning: The Book / the Scripture — 'kitāb' denotes a written record or prescribed scripture; with the definite article it points to the revealed Book, that which is written and decreed.
15.grammar: Definite noun ('al-'). The final '-a' ending is the accusative case, which commonly marks the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon). 'kitāb' literally means 'something written'.
15.root: ك-ت-ب (k-t-b) — to write; a written record, scripture

16.meaning: Book / Scripture (of...) — the same noun 'kitāb' (a written record or revealed scripture) without the article, in a form ready to be joined to a following word in a possessive 'Book of ___' relationship.
16.grammar: Indefinite-form noun with the '-a' accusative ending. The accusative often marks a direct object; without the article it frequently heads a possessive construct ('the Book of ___'), drawing its definiteness from the word that follows.
16.root: ك-ت-ب (k-t-b) — to write; a written record, scripture

17.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
17.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

18.meaning: Behind / beyond — an adverb of place meaning what lies behind or past something; it can also denote what is beyond or in addition to a thing.
18.grammar: An adverb of place (functioning like a preposition). The '-a' ending is the accusative, the standard form for such place-words; it links to a following noun to mean 'behind ___ / beyond ___'.
18.root: و-ر-ي (w-r-y) — that which is behind or hidden from view

19.meaning: Their backs — the plural noun 'ẓuhūr' ('backs', plural of 'ẓahr'), with the attached pronoun 'their'; the back as the rear of the body, often used in idioms for turning away.
19.grammar: A plural noun plus possessive pronoun. The '-i' ending before the pronoun is genitive, the form taken when a noun follows a preposition or is itself possessed; '-him' ('their') completes the possessive phrase 'their backs'.
19.root: ظ-ه-ر (ẓ-h-r) — the back; to appear, be outward/manifest

20.meaning: As though they / as if they (were) — the comparison particle 'ka-anna' ('as if', likening one thing to another) joined to the pronoun 'they', introducing a supposed or apparent state.
20.grammar: A compound particle: 'ka-' ('like/as') fused with the emphatic 'anna' ('that') to form 'ka-anna' = 'as if'. It governs the following pronoun '-hum' ('they'), which takes the accusative form as its subject. It sets up a comparison: things appear as though a certain (often untrue) state held.

21.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
21.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

22.meaning: They know / have knowledge — the present-tense act of knowing, understanding, or being aware, performed by a male plural subject.
22.grammar: Present/imperfect tense. The 'ya-' prefix with the '-ūna' ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'). The full '-ūna' (with the final 'na' retained) is the indicative mood, the default for a plain statement of ongoing fact ('they know').

1.meaning: And they followed / pursued — form VIII of t-b-ʿ, the past-tense act of following after, going along with, or adopting something, with 'and' prefixed and a male plural subject.
1.grammar: Past tense with 'wa' ('and') prefixed. The '-ū' suffix marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'). This is form VIII, whose hallmark is an infixed 't' after the first root letter; here that infixed 't' meets the first radical 't' of the root t-b-ʿ and the two identical consonants merge into a doubled 'tt' (hence ittabaʿa). Form VIII often adds the sense of doing something for oneself — here, taking to following or pursuing.
1.root: ت-ب-ع (t-b-ʿ) — to follow, come after, pursue

2.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
2.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

3.meaning: You all recite / they (fem.) recite — the present-tense act of reciting aloud, reading out, or rehearsing words in sequence (especially scripture), addressed to a male plural group ('you all') or done by a female plural subject ('they').
3.grammar: Present/imperfect tense. The 'ta-' prefix together with the '-ū' plural suffix marks either a second-person masculine plural subject ('you all recite') or a third-person feminine plural ('they recite'); a feminine singular reading is ruled out because the '-ū' suffix is plural. The ending '-ū' (without final 'na') is the shortened subjunctive/jussive mood, used after certain particles or in dependent clauses. The verb means 'recite/read out in sequence'.
3.root: ت-ل-و (t-l-w) — to recite, read out, follow in sequence

4.meaning: The satans / devils — the plural of 'shayṭān', a rebellious, malevolent being (from a root sense of being remote from good or burning with rebellion) who tempts and leads astray; with the definite article.
4.grammar: Definite ('al-') broken (internal) plural. The final '-u' ending is the nominative case, the form used when the word is the subject or doer of an action ('the devils ___').
4.root: ش-ط-ن (sh-ṭ-n) — to be far/remote (from good); rebellious, devil

5.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
5.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

6.meaning: Kingdom / dominion / sovereignty — 'mulk' denotes the power to own, rule, and command; royal authority and possession over a realm.
6.grammar: A noun with the '-i' genitive ending, the case taken after a preposition or when one noun is possessed by another ('the dominion of ___'). 'mulk' is the abstract sense of holding sovereign power and ownership.
6.root: م-ل-ك (m-l-k) — to own, possess, hold dominion; kingship

7.meaning: Sulaymān (Solomon) — the proper name of the prophet-king Solomon, son of David.
7.grammar: A proper name. The '-a' ending is the form this name takes in the genitive/accusative; as a foreign (non-Arabic) proper name it is diptote, meaning it resists the usual case-marking and takes '-a' for cases other than the nominative, without nunation.

8.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
8.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

9.meaning: He disbelieved, rejected faith, or was ungrateful. The verb denotes covering over or concealing the truth — refusing to acknowledge what is true, and by extension being ungrateful for a blessing one will not recognize.
9.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he did' the action, viewed as completed. The bare -a ending with no attached subject pronoun signals a single male doer.
9.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; hence to disbelieve or be ungrateful

10.meaning: Sulaymān (Solomon), the proper name of the prophet-king, son of Dāwūd.
10.grammar: A proper name functioning as a noun in the nominative case, shown by the final -u, which generally marks the subject or naming-form of a sentence. As a foreign/diptote name it does not take nunation (no final -n).

11.meaning: But; however; rather. A particle of correction or contrast that cancels or qualifies a preceding statement and introduces what is actually the case.
11.grammar: A connective wa- ('and') joined to the emphatic particle lākinna. Lākinna belongs to the 'inna family: it governs the noun that follows it, putting it in the accusative case, and adds a sense of firm contrast — 'but in fact …'.

12.meaning: The devils / satans — rebellious, malevolent beings who tempt and lead astray; the plural of shayṭān.
12.grammar: A definite (with al- 'the') broken plural in the accusative case. The plural pattern itself is shayāṭīn-; the accusative is marked by the single final vowel -a added to that stem (giving shayāṭīn-a), which typically marks the object of a verb or a noun governed by a particle such as inna/lākinna. As a diptote plural it takes no nunation.
12.root: ش-ط-ن (sh-ṭ-n) — to be remote/rebellious; hence a devil

13.meaning: 'They disbelieved / rejected faith' — from a root meaning to cover over or conceal. To disbelieve in this sense is to cover up and refuse the truth, and also to be ungrateful, hiding or denying favours received.
13.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
13.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

14.meaning: They teach / instruct (others). The verb conveys imparting knowledge repeatedly and deliberately, training someone in something.
14.grammar: A present/imperfect verb in Form II (intensive 'cause to know = teach'), third-person masculine plural. The yu- prefix marks present tense, and the -ūna ending means 'they' (more than two males) and marks the indicative mood (an ongoing, asserted action).
14.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know; Form II: to teach

15.meaning: Mankind, humanity, people in general — the collective of human beings.
15.grammar: A definite noun ('the people') with the attached 'al-' ('the'). The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'n' (a sun letter), which is why the 'n' is doubled — this is a pronunciation effect, not a separate piece. The final '-a' ending is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb (the one being acted upon) or the subject of certain particles.
15.root: ن-و-س (n-w-s) — to move/sway; by extension, people

16.meaning: Magic, sorcery; illicit enchantment that beguiles and deceives the senses.
16.grammar: A definite masculine noun in the accusative case, shown by the final -a, which generally marks the noun as the object of a verb.

17.meaning: And what / and that which. Combines the connective 'and' with mā, a word that can mean 'what / that which', or function as a negating particle ('not'), depending on usage.
17.grammar: The connective wa- ('and') joined to mā, an indeclinable particle (it never changes its ending). It serves either as a relative/interrogative 'what' or as a negation 'not', so its sense is fixed by context rather than by a case ending.

18.meaning: 'It was sent down / revealed': the act of being caused to descend, used especially of revelation brought down from Allah. The passive form puts the focus on the thing sent down rather than on the sender.
18.grammar: A past-tense passive verb in Form IV (anzala 'to send down' → unzila 'was sent down'). The prefix is only the u- vowel carried on the connecting hamza; the nūn that follows is the first root letter (of ن-ز-ل), not part of the prefix. The internal vowel pattern u–i marks it as passive ('was/were sent down'), with no named doer. The final -a marks the subject as 'he/it', a single masculine thing, and signals completed action.
18.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — to descend, come down; (Form IV) to send down

19.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
19.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
19.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

20.meaning: The two angels — pure beings created of light who carry out the commands of Allah; the dual of malak.
20.grammar: A definite dual noun (exactly two). The -ayni ending is the dual form used in the accusative or genitive case — the form a noun takes as an object or after a preposition — rather than the nominative dual ending -āni.
20.root: م-ل-ك (m-l-k) — message, mission; hence malak, a messenger-angel

21.meaning: In Babylon — the place-name Bābil, the ancient city, here with the preposition 'in / at'.
21.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in/at') attached to the place-name Bābil. As a foreign, diptote proper name it takes a final -a in place of the usual genitive -i and does not take nunation, even though the preposition would normally call for the genitive.

22.meaning: Hārūt — a proper name, one of a pair of named angels.
22.grammar: A proper name, here a diptote (a noun that resists full inflection): it ends in -a and takes no nunation. As such, the -a can stand for the accusative (the appositive/object form) without the indefinite -n.

23.meaning: And Mārūt — a proper name, the second of the pair of named angels, joined by 'and'.
23.grammar: The connective wa- ('and') plus the proper name Mārūt, a diptote: it ends in -a and takes no nunation, so the -a serves as its inflection (e.g. accusative/appositive) without the indefinite -n.

24.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
24.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.
24.root: — (relative pronoun / particle)

25.meaning: They two teach / instruct. The dual form of the verb 'to teach' — two parties imparting knowledge.
25.grammar: A present/imperfect Form II verb (intensive 'teach'), third-person masculine dual. The yu- prefix marks present tense, and the -āni ending means 'the two of them' and signals the indicative mood (an asserted, ongoing action).
25.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know; Form II: to teach

26.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
26.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

27.meaning: One; anyone; a single individual. Often used in negative or conditional contexts to mean 'anyone (at all)'.
27.grammar: An indefinite noun in the genitive case. The -in ending combines the genitive marker -i (the form taken after a preposition or in a possessive link, '… of …') with nunation (-n), the sign of an indefinite 'a / any'.
27.root: أ-ح-د (ʾ-ḥ-d) — oneness, unity; one

28.meaning: 'Until / up to the point that; so that' — a particle marking a limit or goal. It expresses the end-point reached ('until') or the purpose aimed at ('so that, in order that').
28.grammar: A particle indicating a goal or limit. When followed by a present-tense verb it places that verb in the subjunctive mood (clipping its ending to -a), conveying 'until / so that' something comes about. Ḥattā itself is invariable.

29.meaning: They two say / speak. The dual of the verb 'to say', in a form used after certain particles.
29.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, third-person masculine dual, in the subjunctive/jussive mood — shown by the loss of the final -ni from the dual ending (yaqūlāni → yaqūlā). This shortened form appears when the verb is governed by a particle (such as 'until', 'so that', or a conditional), expressing a dependent or non-asserted action.
29.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, speak

30.meaning: 'Only / nothing but' — a restrictive particle that limits and emphasizes, asserting that the matter is exclusively so and no other ('it is only...'). It combines the emphatic 'inna' with the restricting 'mā'.
30.grammar: A compound particle formed from the emphatic inna ('indeed') and mā, which together work as a tool of restriction meaning 'only / nothing but'. It both stresses and confines the statement that follows to a single truth, excluding all alternatives.

31.meaning: 'We' — the standalone pronoun for a speaker including others (or a single speaker of majesty). It stands alone to name or emphasize the subject 'we'.
31.grammar: A detached (standalone) personal pronoun, first-person plural, 'we'. Such independent pronouns are used to state or emphasize the subject, often highlighting 'we' as the ones who do or are something.

32.meaning: A trial, test, or temptation; affliction or seduction that puts faith and character to the proof and may lead one into discord or sin.
32.grammar: A feminine singular noun (the -ah/-at ending) in the nominative case. The -un ending pairs the nominative marker -u (subject / predicate form) with nunation (-n), marking it indefinite: 'a trial'.
32.root: ف-ت-ن (f-t-n) — to test by fire, try; trial, temptation

33.meaning: A two-part word: the connective particle 'fa-' meaning 'so', 'then', or 'therefore' (drawing a consequence from what precedes), joined to 'lā', the particle of negation/prohibition. Together they convey 'so do not …' or 'so there is no …'.
33.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that links a clause to what came before and often signals a result or consequence. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a present-tense verb it commonly forms a prohibition ('do not …') or a simple negation ('not'). It carries no ending of its own.

34.meaning: Do not disbelieve / you (should) not reject faith. The verbal idea of covering the truth, disbelieving, or being ungrateful, addressed to a single person.
34.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, second-person masculine singular ('you'), in the jussive mood — shown by the bare, vowel-less final consonant (-r, sukūn). The jussive is the form used after particles of prohibition ('do not …') or condition, so it expresses a command, prohibition, or conditional 'if you …'.
34.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to disbelieve / be ungrateful

35.meaning: But / so they learn (for themselves). The verb means to acquire knowledge through effort and study, taking it on as one's own.
35.grammar: The connective fa- ('so/then') plus a present/imperfect Form V verb (taʿallama, 'to learn' — the reflexive of 'teach'), third-person masculine plural. The -ūna ending means 'they' (more than two males) and marks the indicative mood (an ongoing, asserted action).
35.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know; Form V: to learn

36.meaning: From the two of them; from those two. A preposition meaning 'from / out of' fused with the dual 'them'.
36.grammar: The preposition min ('from') with the attached dual pronoun -humā ('the two of them'). Pronouns following a preposition are in the genitive/object form; -humā specifically refers to exactly two.
36.root: — (particle + pronoun)

37.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
37.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

38.meaning: They cause separation / division; they part one thing from another. The verb conveys actively splitting or setting apart, repeatedly or thoroughly.
38.grammar: A present/imperfect Form II verb (intensive 'cause separation'), third-person masculine plural. The yu- prefix marks present tense, and the -ūna ending means 'they' (more than two males) and marks the indicative mood (an asserted, ongoing action).
38.root: ف-ر-ق (f-r-q) — to separate, divide, distinguish

39.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
39.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

40.meaning: Between; in the midst of two things. An adverb of place marking the space separating or lying among parties or points.
40.grammar: An adverb of place ('between'). It always ends in -a and grammatically governs what follows it, putting the following noun(s) into the genitive 'of' relationship. It does not change to show 'the' or a case of its own; the fixed -a is simply how this word is formed.
40.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies between

41.meaning: The man; the person, the human individual (the noun for a man as a single human being).
41.grammar: A definite masculine noun in the genitive case, shown by the final -i, which typically appears after a preposition or in a possessive link ('… of the man').

42.meaning: And his spouse / his wife (or mate). The noun zawj means a partner of a pair — a husband or wife, one member of a couple — here with 'and' and 'his'.
42.grammar: The connective wa- ('and') plus the noun zawj with the attached pronoun -hi ('his'). The noun is in the genitive case (-i), the form taken after a preposition or in a possessive link; the attached -hi is itself an 'of him / his' possessor.
42.root: ز-و-ج (z-w-j) — to pair, couple; spouse, mate, pair

43.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
43.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

44.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (referring to a group of males, or a mixed group). Because it stands on its own rather than being attached to a verb or noun, it often adds emphasis, singling out or stressing the subject ('they themselves', 'it is they who').
44.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It does not take case endings; the fixed -m simply marks the plural 'they'. Standing alone, it commonly serves to emphasise or isolate the subject.

45.meaning: Causing harm; being ones who injure or do damage. The plural active participle 'harmers / those who harm', typically following a preposition or negation ('not harming at all').
45.grammar: The preposition bi- (often attached to a predicate after a negation for emphasis) plus a sound masculine plural active participle 'harmers'. The -īna ending marks masculine plural in the genitive/object form — the case the preposition bi- requires.

46.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
46.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

47.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
47.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

48.meaning: One; anyone; a single individual. Often used in negative or conditional contexts to mean 'anyone (at all)'.
48.grammar: An indefinite noun in the genitive case. The -in ending combines the genitive marker -i (the form taken after a preposition or in a possessive link, '… of …') with nunation (-n), the sign of an indefinite 'a / any'.

49.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
49.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

50.meaning: 'By the leave of / with the permission of' — formed from 'with/by' plus 'permission, leave, sanction'. It conveys that something happens by someone's authorization or enabling will.
50.grammar: The prefix bi- is a preposition 'with/by'. The noun 'idhn' means 'permission, leave, sanction'. After the preposition it takes the genitive -i ending, the form used following a preposition and typically linking on to a following noun ('the permission OF …').
50.root: أ-ذ-ن (ʾ-dh-n) — to permit, give leave; also listening/ear

51.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
51.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

52.meaning: And they learn (for themselves). The connective 'and' with the verb meaning to acquire knowledge through study, taking it on as one's own.
52.grammar: The connective wa- ('and') plus a present/imperfect Form V verb (taʿallama, 'to learn'), third-person masculine plural. The -ūna ending means 'they' (more than two males) and marks the indicative mood (an ongoing, asserted action).
52.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know; Form V: to learn

53.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
53.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

54.meaning: It harms them; it injures or damages them. The verb 'to harm' with 'them' as the ones harmed.
54.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it'), with the attached object pronoun -hum ('them'). The ya- prefix marks present tense and a single (or unspecified) doer; -hum is the receiver of the action.

55.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
