6.meaning: "he recites / he reads aloud / he follows" — to recite or read out (especially scripture), conveying the sense of following the words one after another; 'talā' is to recite, and also to follow closely.
6.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he recites / will recite'). The 'ya-' prefix marks 'he/it' as the doer. The verb is from a root ending in a weak letter, which surfaces as the long 'ū' ('yatlū'); the final long vowel here reflects the indicative (statement) mood. Final '-ā' in the script (alif) is a spelling convention.
6.root: ت-ل-و (t-l-w) — to recite, read aloud; to follow

7.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon them' or 'against them': the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over, against') joined to the plural pronoun 'them'. It conveys something resting on, being incumbent upon, or weighing against a group.
7.grammar: ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The suffix -him is the attached pronominal suffix for a masculine plural group ('them'); after a preposition it carries genitive/prepositional force, and the -i- vowel reflects its position after this preposition. Together they signal a relationship of something being over, upon, or burdensome to that group.
7.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

8.meaning: "Your signs / Your verses" — 'āyāt' are signs, tokens, or proofs that point to something beyond themselves; the word also denotes the verses of revelation. With 'Your' it means signs/verses belonging to a single addressee.
8.grammar: A feminine plural noun (singular āya) with the possessive pronoun '-ka' ('your') attached. The 'i' ending on the noun is the genitive case, used here because the noun is possessed (linked to the following 'your'); the sound feminine plural takes this same '-i' for both object and genitive roles.

9.meaning: "and he teaches them / instructs them" — to teach, instruct, or impart knowledge; 'ʿallama' (form II) is the intensive/causative of 'to know,' i.e. to cause someone to know, to school them in something.
9.grammar: A present-tense form-II verb, third-person masculine singular ('he teaches'), with the object pronoun 'them' attached. The 'yu-' prefix (with 'u') marks the doubled-middle-letter form-II verb and means 'he/it.' The pronoun is normally '-hum,' but its vowel becomes 'u' ('-humu') to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a vowel-cluster.
9.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — knowledge, knowing; (form II) to teach

10.meaning: The Book, the Scripture — a written revelation; the term for a divinely revealed text.
10.grammar: A definite noun ('the Book') with attached 'al-' ('the'). The final '-a' ending is the accusative case, typically marking the word as the direct object of a verb.
10.root: ك-ت-ب (k-t-b) — to write; a writing, book

11.meaning: "and the wisdom" — sound judgement and deep understanding that puts things in their right place; 'ḥikma' is wisdom: knowledge joined to right action, insight into the true nature and proper order of things.
11.grammar: A definite feminine noun ('the wisdom'); 'wa-' is 'and' and 'al-' is 'the.' The final '-a' is the accusative case ending, the form a noun takes as the direct object of a verb or when joined to another accusative noun.
11.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to judge, govern wisely; wisdom, sound judgement

12.meaning: "and he purifies them / cleanses and improves them" — to purify, cleanse, and cause to grow in goodness; 'zakkā' (form II) means to make pure and wholesome, removing what is corrupt and nurturing what is righteous.

parts.en: purify / cleanse and cause to grow

12.grammar: A present-tense form-II verb, third-person masculine singular ('he purifies'), with the object pronoun 'them' attached. The 'yu-' prefix marks 'he/it' for this doubled-letter form-II verb; the long 'ī' before the pronoun is the verb's weak final letter. The pronoun '-him' is third-person masculine plural ('them'), its vowel 'i' following the 'ī' sound.
12.root: ز-ك-و / ز-ك-ي (z-k-w / z-k-y) — purity, growth, increase in goodness

13.meaning: 'Indeed you' — an emphasis particle meaning 'truly / indeed' joined to the pronoun 'you', used to open a statement with certainty and stress about the person addressed.
13.grammar: The emphasis particle 'inna' ('indeed, truly') with an attached pronoun. 'inna' adds strong assertion to a sentence and grammatically governs the following noun/pronoun in the accusative. The suffix '-ka' means 'you' (masculine singular) as its subject.

14.meaning: 'You' — the standalone, independent pronoun for addressing a single male person directly.
14.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, second-person masculine singular. Unlike attached pronoun suffixes, it stands alone and is typically used to identify or emphasize the subject ('you [yourself]').

15.meaning: "the All-Mighty / the Ever-Dominant" — one who is mighty, invincible, and held in honour; as a divine name 'al-ʿAzīz' denotes the One who is supremely powerful, unconquerable, and exalted above all.
15.grammar: A definite intensive adjective/noun on the faʿīl pattern, conveying a strong, enduring quality. The 'al-' prefix makes it definite ('the'). The final '-u' is the nominative case ending, the form used when the word is the subject of a sentence or a predicate/description following it.

16.meaning: "the All-Wise" — one full of wisdom, who judges and orders everything with perfect, sound judgement; as a divine name 'al-Ḥakīm' denotes the One whose every act and decree is supremely wise.
16.grammar: A definite intensive adjective/noun on the faʿīl pattern, expressing a deep, abiding quality ('ever-wise'). The 'al-' prefix makes it definite ('the'). The final '-u' is the nominative case ending, the form a word takes as the subject of a sentence or a predicate/description.
16.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to judge wisely, govern; wisdom

1.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
1.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

2.meaning: "he turns away from / he is averse to" (or, with a different preposition, 'he desires/longs for') — 'raghiba' expresses inclination: with 'ʿan' it means to shun or turn away from in distaste; with 'fī/ilā' it means to desire and incline toward.

parts.en: incline toward / turn away from (with prep.)

2.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he inclines / turns away'). The 'ya-' prefix marks 'he/it' as the doer. The final '-u' is the indicative (statement) mood ending, the default form of the present verb when simply reporting an action. Its precise sense (desiring vs. shunning) depends on the preposition that follows it.

3.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on behalf of,' 'for,' 'about,' or 'away from.' It often conveys removing a burden from someone or acting in their place.

parts.en: on behalf of / for / away from

3.grammar: A preposition (a linking particle). It governs the noun that follows it, putting that noun into the genitive case. It does not change form.

4.meaning: "creed / religion / way" — 'milla' is a religion or way of life understood as a body of belief and practice followed by a community, often associated with the path of a founding prophet.
4.grammar: A feminine singular noun in the genitive case, marked by the final '-i.' The genitive typically links the word to a following noun ('… of …'), or shows that it follows a preposition or oath particle. (Here the doubled initial consonant in the script reflects an assimilated preceding word, but the word itself is 'milla.')
4.root: م-ل-ل (m-l-l) — a religion, creed, community's way

5.meaning: Ibrahim (Abraham), the proper name of the patriarch and prophet.
5.grammar: A proper name of non-Arabic origin. Because such foreign names are 'diptotes,' they take a single -a ending for both the object (accusative) and possessive/after-preposition (genitive) roles, and they do not take the usual -n (nunation). The -a here shows it is functioning as an object or after a preposition.

6.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
6.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

7.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
7.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

8.meaning: "he was foolish / acted foolishly / made a fool of himself" — 'safiha' denotes folly: lightness of mind, lack of sound judgement, behaving foolishly or holding something in foolish contempt.
8.grammar: A past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he was foolish / he acted foolishly.' The bare three-letter form with the final '-a' vowel is the basic past tense with a built-in 'he' as its subject. The 'i' vowel in the middle (the faʿila pattern) is typical of verbs describing a state or quality.
8.root: س-ف-ه (s-f-h) — folly, foolishness, lightness of mind

9.meaning: His own self, soul, or very being — the inner person or essence of an individual. The base noun nafs denotes the soul/self, and the attached 'his' makes it reflexive ('himself') or possessive ('his soul').
9.grammar: A noun carrying the -a (accusative) ending, which typically marks it as the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon) or the object of certain particles. The suffix -hu means 'his/him', here making the noun reflexive or possessive.
9.root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s) — self, soul, breath of life

10.meaning: A combination of three emphatic particles meaning roughly 'and most certainly indeed' — used to open a statement with strong, solemn affirmation that what follows is firmly established and true.
10.grammar: Particles, not a declinable word. 'wa' joins to what precedes; 'la-' is an emphatic prefix stressing certainty; 'qad' before a past-tense verb confirms the action definitely happened. Its final vowel appears as -i here only to ease pronunciation before a following consonant cluster (it carries no case meaning).

11.meaning: We selected, chose, or picked out (someone) as preferred — to single out and elect a person, giving them a chosen, favored standing above others.
11.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -nā suffix is the subject 'we' (the doers of the choosing), and the -hu suffix is the object 'him' (the one chosen). The Form VIII pattern here adds a sense of careful selecting/picking out for oneself.
11.root: ص-ف-و (ṣ-f-w) — purity, clearness; to select the choicest

12.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
12.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

13.meaning: 'The nearer (life) / this world' — literally 'the nearest/lowest,' a name for the present worldly life as opposed to the Hereafter.
13.grammar: The definite article al- with dunyā, a feminine superlative/elative adjective ('the nearest, the lowest') used as a name for the present world. Its ending (alif maqṣūra) is invariable — it does not change for case — and it commonly describes 'the [worldly] life.'
13.root: د-ن-و (d-n-w) — nearness, being close or low; hence the 'near' present world

14.meaning: A linkage of 'and' with the emphatic particle inna ('truly, indeed') plus 'he' — meaning 'and truly he…', opening a clause with firm assurance about the person referred to.
14.grammar: 'wa' is the connector 'and'. 'inna' is an emphatic particle that strongly affirms the statement and grammatically governs the following noun/pronoun in the accusative. The attached -hu ('he/him') is the subject of the inna-clause, expressed in object form as inna requires.

15.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
15.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

16.meaning: The Hereafter — the final, lasting life that comes after death and the present world; literally 'the last/latter (abode or life)', as opposed to the first, nearer life.
16.grammar: A feminine adjective used as a noun, with 'the'. The -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF …'), or follows a preposition or oath particle.
16.root: ء-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — to be last, to come after, end

17.meaning: An emphatic 'truly/surely' joined to the preposition min ('from, among, of') — conveying 'surely (one) of / among', stressing belonging to a group.
17.grammar: Two particles. 'la-' is the emphatic prefix adding certainty (often paired with inna). 'min' is a preposition meaning 'from/among/of' and puts the noun after it into the genitive case. Its final -a here is a connecting vowel used before the definite article 'al-'.

18.meaning: The righteous, upright, and morally sound ones — people who are good, virtuous, and act rightly, putting things into proper order. Plural and referring to people.
18.grammar: A definite noun/adjective ('al-' = 'the') in the sound masculine plural. The -īna ending marks the plural in its accusative/genitive (object or 'of/from') form — the form used as a direct object or after a preposition; the parallel subject form would be -ūna.
18.root: ص-ل-ح (ṣ-l-ḥ) — soundness, righteousness, setting things right

1.meaning: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the time that', used to point back to a past moment or event and introduce a recollection of something that occurred.
1.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). It signals a point in past time, typically introducing a clause that recalls 'the time when' something happened.

2.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
2.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

3.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
3.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

4.meaning: His Lord, Master, and Sustainer. 'Rabb' denotes the One who owns, nurtures, governs, and brings a thing to its completion; the attached pronoun makes it 'his.'
4.grammar: A noun followed by a possessive pronoun. The -u on 'rabb' is the nominative ending, the case used for the subject/doer of a sentence ('the one who does'). The attached -hu means 'his.'
4.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, lord over

5.meaning: A command: 'Submit!', 'Surrender (yourself)!', 'Commit wholly (to Allah)!' — an order to give oneself over in willing submission and peace.
5.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a single male: 'you, do this!' The form is built on the Form IV pattern (aslama), which means to enter into submission/peace. Its bare ending with no added vowel is the standard shape of a direct order.
5.root: س-ل-م (s-l-m) — peace, safety, wholeness; to submit

6.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
6.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

7.meaning: I have submitted, surrendered, devoted myself wholly (to Allah) — a declaration of having entered into willing submission and peace.
7.grammar: A past-tense verb. The suffix -tu marks the speaker as the subject: 'I (did the action).' The Form IV pattern gives the meaning of entering into submission and peace, i.e. devoting oneself.
7.root: س-ل-م (s-l-m) — peace, safety, wholeness; to submit

8.meaning: 'To/for the Lord' — the preposition 'to/for' joined to rabb, a richly loaded term meaning the Lord, Master, Owner, Sustainer and Nurturer who creates, sustains, and brings to maturity all He governs.
8.grammar: The prefix 'li-' is a preposition ('to/for') that places the following noun in the genitive. Accordingly rabb takes the -i (genitive) ending, marking it as governed by the preposition and typically standing in construct with a following noun ('Lord OF …').

9.meaning: The worlds, all created realms — the totality of beings and peoples; in 'Lord of the worlds,' the whole of creation across all its kinds.
9.grammar: A definite plural noun ('the worlds') with 'al-' ('the'). The '-īna' ending marks a masculine sound plural in the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) form — the form used after a preposition, in an 'of' linkage, or as a direct object.
9.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know; a 'world' as a sign by which the Creator is known

1.meaning: He earnestly enjoined, charged, or instructed — to give a firm, weighty directive or counsel, urging compliance, often as a lasting charge or bequest.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third-person masculine singular ('he did it'), with the connector 'wa' ('and') prefixed. The Form II (doubled-middle) pattern intensifies the sense — strongly urging or solemnly charging. The final long -ā belongs to the verb's weak (root-final) shape.
1.root: و-ص-ي (w-ṣ-y) — to enjoin, charge, bequeath, counsel

2.meaning: In it / in them / by it — the preposition 'bi-' (with, in, by) joined to the attached pronoun 'hā' referring to a single feminine or non-human plural antecedent.
2.grammar: A preposition plus pronoun. 'bi-' means 'in/with/by'; the suffix '-hā' is the object pronoun for a feminine singular or a non-human plural ('it'/'them'). Pronouns after a preposition take this attached (genitive) form.
2.root: — (particle with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

3.meaning: Ibrāhīm (Abraham), the proper name of the patriarch and prophet, revered as a model of pure devotion to Allah.
3.grammar: A proper name (of non-Arabic origin). The final -u ending is nominative, the case used for the subject or the one doing/being something in a sentence. Being a foreign name, it does not take nunation (no '-un').

4.meaning: His sons / his children — the plural 'sons' (banūn, from ibn 'son') combined with the possessive 'his'.
4.grammar: A plural noun in its accusative/genitive ('oblique') form, shown by -ī before the pronoun — the shape used as an object or after a preposition. The suffix -hi means 'his'. (The plural's -na drops when a possessive is attached.)

5.meaning: The proper name Yaʿqūb (the Prophet Jacob), here joined with 'and'.
5.grammar: A proper name (a non-Arabic name treated as grammatically 'unable to take the full range of endings'), prefixed with 'wa' ('and'). The -u ending here marks it as a subject (the one doing/being something); such names do not take the 'n' (tanwīn) that ordinary nouns would.

6.meaning: 'O my sons!' — a direct, affectionate call to one's own children: the call-word 'O' plus 'sons' plus 'my'.
6.grammar: A vocative (a form used to call or address someone), marked by the particle 'yā' ('O'). 'Sons' appears in its oblique plural shape merged with the possessive -ya ('my'), the two blending into -iyya. The whole means 'O my sons!'

7.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
7.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

8.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
8.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

9.meaning: He selected, chose, or singled out as preferred — to elect and favor someone, giving them a chosen standing above others.
9.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third-person masculine singular ('he did it'). The Form VIII pattern conveys carefully selecting or picking out the best for oneself. The final long -ā reflects the verb's weak (root-final) shape.
9.root: ص-ف-و (ṣ-f-w) — purity, clearness; to select the choicest

10.meaning: 'for you,' 'to you,' 'for your benefit' — the preposition 'for/to' joined to 'you (plural).' It marks the party for whose sake, benefit, or possession something is done or given.
10.grammar: A preposition ('for/to') with the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you, plural'). Such prepositions assign a benefit, purpose, or recipient. The pronoun's vowel appears as '-u' (kumu) to ease pronunciation when a word follows.

11.meaning: The dīn — a deep term covering religion, the way of life, the path of obedience and worship owed to Allah, and the reckoning/recompense for it; a complete system of belief and practice with accountability.
11.grammar: A definite noun ('al-' = 'the') with the -a (accusative) ending, which typically marks it as the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon) or the object of certain particles.

12.meaning: A two-part word: the connective particle 'fa-' meaning 'so', 'then', or 'therefore' (drawing a consequence from what precedes), joined to 'lā', the particle of negation/prohibition. Together they convey 'so do not …' or 'so there is no …'.
12.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that links a clause to what came before and often signals a result or consequence. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a present-tense verb it commonly forms a prohibition ('do not …') or a simple negation ('not'). It carries no ending of its own.

13.meaning: You will surely die / you shall most certainly die — the verb 'to die' addressed to a group ('you all'), carrying heavy emphasis that the dying will inevitably happen.
13.grammar: A present/future verb, second-person masculine plural, with the heavy emphatic ending. Without emphasis the form would be tamūtūna ('you all die'): the 'ta-' prefix marks the 'you' subject and the long -ūna marks the masculine plural. Before the doubled emphatic -nna, that plural -ūna loses its nūn and its vowel shortens, leaving only the residual damma (-u) shown here — so the -u is the remnant of the plural suffix, not part of the bare stem. The -nna ending stresses that the action will most certainly occur and fixes the verb's mood.

14.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
14.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

15.meaning: And you / while you (all) — the conjunction 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'you' (masculine plural), often introducing an accompanying circumstance ('while you …').
15.grammar: The conjunction wa- joined to the detached subject pronoun 'you all' (masculine). This standalone pronoun stands as a subject or for emphasis; it has a fixed form and does not change for case. With wa- it can mark a simultaneous state ('and you / while you').

16.meaning: Ones who submit / are submitted — those in a state of willing surrender and peace toward Allah (the people described by the word 'Muslim'). Plural, referring to people.
16.grammar: An active participle (a 'one-who-does' word) in the sound masculine plural. The -ūna ending marks the plural in its subject form — the form used when the word is the doer or the thing being described (as a predicate); the parallel object/'of' form would be -īna.
16.root: س-ل-م (s-l-m) — peace, safety, wholeness; to submit

1.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'or', specifically the 'or' that pairs with a preceding question to offer an alternative ('…or…?'). It links two possibilities being weighed against each other, often after an opening interrogative.

parts.en: or (in alternatives, esp. after a question)

1.grammar: An indeclinable particle (no case or tense ending). It typically introduces the second branch of a two-part question or a balanced alternative, presenting the two as equally consequential.

2.meaning: A past-tense verb of 'being' addressed to a group: 'you (all) were', 'you (all) used to be'. From kāna, the core verb 'to be'. With a following predicate it often means 'you were (in a state of) …' or 'you used to …'.
2.grammar: This is a past-tense verb. The '-tum' suffix is the attached subject marker for a masculine plural 'you all'. Since the doer is built into the suffix, the verb stands in its base past form ('you all were').
2.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

3.meaning: Witnesses — those present who observe and can testify to what they saw; can also carry the sense of those who bear witness. Plural.
3.grammar: A broken plural on the fuʿalāʾ (فُعَلَاء) pattern, which is a diptote: it takes the -a ending for BOTH the accusative and the genitive and never takes tanwīn (the final 'n'). Because of this, the -a alone does not tell you the case — the word could be a direct object (accusative) or governed by a preposition ('of/among', genitive). Only when made definite or put into construct would it take the ordinary -i in the genitive.
3.root: ش-ه-د (sh-h-d) — to witness, observe, testify, be present

4.meaning: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the time that', used to point back to a past moment or event and introduce a recollection of something that occurred.
4.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). It signals a point in past time, typically introducing a clause that recalls 'the time when' something happened.

5.meaning: He/it came, drew near, approached, or was present — to arrive at or attend something, to be on hand.
5.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third-person masculine singular ('he/it did it'). The final -a is the standard ending of this basic past-tense form. It conveys a completed action: the arriving or being-present has occurred.

6.meaning: The proper name Yaʿqūb (the Prophet Jacob).
6.grammar: A proper name (a non-Arabic name treated as grammatically 'unable to take the full range of endings'). The -a ending marks it as an object or otherwise governed into the accusative; because such names are 'restricted', they take a single -a and do not add the 'n' (tanwīn) that ordinary nouns would.

7.meaning: Death — the ending of earthly life; the state or event of dying.
7.grammar: A definite noun ('al-' = 'the') with the -u (nominative) ending, which typically marks it as the subject — the one doing or being something in the sentence.

8.meaning: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the time that', used to point back to a past moment or event and introduce a recollection of something that occurred.
8.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). It signals a point in past time, typically introducing a clause that recalls 'the time when' something happened.

9.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
9.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

10.meaning: 'To/for his sons' — the preposition 'to/for' joined to 'sons' plus the possessive 'his'.
10.grammar: The prefix 'li-' is a preposition ('to/for') that governs the following noun into the genitive — shown here by the plural's oblique -ī shape before the pronoun. The suffix -hi means 'his'. (The plural's -na drops when a possessive is attached.)

11.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
11.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

12.meaning: You worship (Him) — to serve, devote oneself to, and submit in obedient adoration to a deity. The verb conveys total devotion: not merely outward ritual but the humble servitude a worshipper owes to the One worshipped.
12.grammar: Present/future-tense verb addressed to a group of males ('you all'). The ta- prefix marks second person ('you'), and the -ūna ending marks masculine plural subjects and the indicative mood (a plain statement of fact, 'you do/will worship'), as opposed to a command or a negated/subjunctive form which would drop the final -na.
12.root: ع-ب-د (ʿ-b-d) — to worship, serve, submit as a devoted servant

13.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
13.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

14.meaning: 'After me' — the noun baʿd ('after, afterwards, the time following') joined to the possessive 'my', i.e. the period or state following the speaker.
14.grammar: A noun (baʿd, 'after') of time/sequence with the first-person possessive suffix -ī ('my') attached. The noun's original case vowel is replaced by a connecting kasra, which IS pronounced before the possessive yāʾ — hence baʿdī ('after me'). baʿd commonly functions adverbially, indicating 'following' in time.
14.root: ب-ع-د (b-ʿ-d) — afterness, distance, what comes later

15.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
15.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.

16.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning 'we worship / we serve / we devote ourselves in obedience.' The root denotes humble worship and willing servitude rendered to a master, expressing total devotion of the self.
16.grammar: Present/imperfect verb. The na- prefix marks the subject as 'we'. The final -u ending marks the indicative mood, the plain statement form ('we do / we will do'), as opposed to commands or negated-future forms.
16.root: ع-ب-د (ʿ-b-d) — to worship, serve, submit in devotion

17.meaning: 'Your god / your deity' — the object of worship belonging to the one addressed. The base word means 'a god, an object of worship,' and the attached pronoun ties that deity to a single male addressee.
17.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive pronoun. The -ka suffix means 'your,' addressed to one male. The -a vowel before it is the accusative ending, the form a noun takes when it is the object of a verb or otherwise governed into that case.
17.root: ء-ل-ه (ʾ-l-h) — godhood, that which is worshipped

18.meaning: 'And a god / and the deity' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the noun for a god or object of worship.
18.grammar: Conjunction 'wa' (and) prefixed to a noun. The -a ending is accusative, the case a noun shows when it is a verb's object or otherwise placed in that grammatical role; it also commonly precedes an attached possessor in a construct phrase ('god of …').
18.root: ء-ل-ه (ʾ-l-h) — godhood, that which is worshipped

19.meaning: 'Your forefathers / your fathers, ancestors' — the plural of 'father,' with a pronoun marking them as belonging to a single male addressee.
19.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural noun with an attached possessive pronoun. The -ka suffix means 'your,' to one male. The -i vowel before it is the genitive ending, the case a noun takes after a preposition or when it is possessed by/linked to a following word ('the … of …').

20.meaning: Ibrahim (Abraham), the proper name of the patriarch and prophet.
20.grammar: A proper name of non-Arabic origin. Because such foreign names are 'diptotes,' they take a single -a ending for both the object (accusative) and possessive/after-preposition (genitive) roles, and they do not take the usual -n (nunation). The -a here shows it is functioning as an object or after a preposition.

21.meaning: And Ismāʿīl (Ishmael), the proper name of the prophet, son of Ibrahim; preceded by the connector 'and.'
21.grammar: The connector 'wa-' ('and') joined to a proper name of non-Arabic origin. As a 'diptote' foreign name, it takes a single -a ending for both the object (accusative) and possessive/after-preposition (genitive) roles, and it does not take nunation.

22.meaning: The proper name 'Isaac' (Isḥāq), the prophet, joined to the conjunction 'and.'
22.grammar: Conjunction 'wa' (and) prefixed to a proper name. The final -a is the accusative/genitive ending; because this is a foreign (non-Arabic) name, it is grammatically 'diptote,' meaning it takes -a for both those cases and never takes nunation (the -n sound).

23.meaning: 'A god / a deity, an object of worship' — the word in its indefinite form, naming a single divine being without specifying which.
23.grammar: A singular indefinite noun. The -an ending combines two things: the accusative case (the form for a verb's object or, often, a noun described by a following adjective) and nunation, the -n sound that signals 'a/an,' i.e. indefiniteness.
23.root: ء-ل-ه (ʾ-l-h) — godhood, that which is worshipped

24.meaning: 'And one / and single, sole' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the cardinal number one. The number 'one' stresses uniqueness and oneness, often attached to a preceding noun as a description. The opening waw carries a shadda because the conjunction 'wa' has merged with the initial w- of 'wāḥid.'
24.grammar: Conjunction 'wa' (and) prefixed to an adjective/number in the active-participle pattern; the doubled (shadda) waw represents 'wa' contracted onto the word's own initial w-. The -an ending is accusative plus nunation: it marks indefiniteness ('a/an' / 'one') and the accusative case, the form an adjective takes to agree with a noun it describes that is itself in the accusative.
24.root: و-ح-د (w-ḥ-d) — oneness, to be single/unique

25.meaning: 'And we' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'we,' which emphasizes the speakers as the subject.
25.grammar: Conjunction 'wa' (and) prefixed to an independent subject pronoun. 'Naḥnu' is a fixed, unchanging word meaning 'we'; it does not take case endings, and its final -u is part of the set form rather than a grammatical case marker.

26.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
26.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

27.meaning: 'Ones who submit / those who surrender themselves to Allah' — the plural of the active participle 'muslim,' i.e. one who willingly submits and devotes himself in obedience to Allah.
27.grammar: A masculine plural active participle (a doer-noun). The -ūna ending marks a sound masculine plural in the nominative case, the form used when the word stands as the subject or as the predicate naming who/what the subject is.
27.root: س-ل-م (s-l-m) — peace, safety, submission/surrender

1.meaning: That; a demonstrative used to point to something distant or already mentioned. It singles out a single feminine (or grammatically feminine) thing, roughly 'that one over there.'
1.grammar: A feminine singular demonstrative pronoun pointing to something far off. The -ka element signals remoteness ('that yonder' rather than 'this near'). Being a demonstrative, it does not take case endings; its form is fixed.

2.meaning: 'A community / a nation, a people' — a body of people bound together as a single group, often by shared faith, way, or era.
2.grammar: A singular indefinite noun. The -un ending is nominative plus nunation: the -n sound signals 'a/an' (indefinite), and the -u marks the nominative case, the form used when the word is the subject or the thing being named.
2.root: ء-م-م (ʾ-m-m) — to head toward; a community, way, model

3.meaning: A short particle placed before a verb to emphasize or affirm it. Before a past-tense verb it means 'indeed / certainly / has already (happened)'; before a present-tense verb it can mean 'sometimes / may'. It sharpens and confirms the verb that follows.
3.grammar: An indeclinable particle (its form never changes). It does not take case or tense endings; its job is to color the following verb — affirming and intensifying a past action ('has indeed done') or signaling occasional possibility with a present verb.

4.meaning: 'It passed away / went by, came to an end' — said of a community, time, or era that has elapsed and is now gone. The root carries the sense of being emptied out, hence of time or people that have passed.
4.grammar: Past-tense verb. The -t (sukūn-marked -at) suffix marks a third-person feminine singular subject, 'she/it,' used here because the noun it refers to is grammatically feminine. The past tense states a completed action.
4.root: خ-ل-و (kh-l-w) — to be empty/vacant; to pass away, elapse

5.meaning: 'For it / to it, belonging to it' — the preposition 'for/to' joined to a pronoun referring to a feminine singular thing; it expresses possession or benefit ('it has / it gets').
5.grammar: Preposition 'li-' (here vowelled 'la-' before a pronoun) plus an attached object pronoun. The -hā suffix means 'it/her,' a feminine singular. Pronouns that follow a preposition are in the genitive (object-of-preposition) role; -hā is a fixed form and does not change shape.

6.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
6.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

7.meaning: 'It earned / acquired, gained' — said of deeds and their consequences; the root means to gain or acquire something, especially the moral 'earnings' of one's actions.
7.grammar: Past-tense verb. The -t (sukūn-marked -at) suffix marks a third-person feminine singular subject, 'she/it.' The past tense presents the action as completed.
7.root: ك-س-ب (k-s-b) — to earn, acquire, gain (esp. deeds)

8.meaning: A short phrase meaning 'and for you' or 'and you have'. It joins a new statement with 'and', then uses 'for/to you' to express possession or benefit belonging to a group.
8.grammar: Three pieces: wa- ('and') linking to what came before, the preposition la- ('for/to'), and the attached pronoun -kum ('you all', plural). A preposition-plus-'you' phrase like this commonly conveys 'you have' or 'belonging to you'.

9.meaning: A short, highly versatile particle 'mā.' It can mean 'what' or 'that which,' can negate ('not'), and can serve as an intensifier attached to another word. Its precise force depends on what it accompanies, but its core is to point to a thing or to add emphasis.
9.grammar: A multifunctional particle. It does not take case endings. Depending on usage it can be a relative ('that which'), an interrogative ('what?'), a negator ('not'), or — when joined to another particle — an emphasizer. It is uninflected and indeclinable.

10.meaning: 'You earned / acquired, gained' — the same verb of earning addressed to a group of people, referring to the deeds they have done.
10.grammar: Past-tense verb. The -tum suffix marks the subject as second-person masculine plural, 'you (all).' The past tense presents the action as completed.
10.root: ك-س-ب (k-s-b) — to earn, acquire, gain (esp. deeds)

11.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
11.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

12.meaning: 'You are asked / will be questioned' — a passive verb meaning that a group is questioned or held to account by someone else; the doing of the asking lies with an unnamed party.
12.grammar: Present-tense passive verb. The tu-…-ūna frame marks a second-person masculine plural subject, 'you (all),' as the receiver of the action ('you are asked'). The -ūna ending also signals the indicative mood, the plain statement form. The internal -u- vowelling shows it is passive (action done to the subject).

13.meaning: 'About what' / 'of that which' — the preposition 'ʿan' ('about, concerning, away from') merged with 'mā' ('what, that which').
13.grammar: A fusion of the preposition 'ʿan' ('about, concerning') with the relative/interrogative 'mā' ('what'); the 'n' of 'ʿan' assimilates into 'mā' to give 'ʿammā'. It introduces the thing being spoken about.

14.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
14.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
14.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

15.meaning: 'They do / they work, they act' — a present-tense verb of doing and working, covering deeds and actions carried out by a group.
15.grammar: Present/imperfect verb. The ya-…-ūna frame marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (do).' The -ūna ending also marks the indicative mood, the plain statement form, as opposed to command or negated-future forms.
15.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, work, act; deeds

1.meaning: And they said — to utter or declare in speech, with the action presented as completed by a group.
1.grammar: The prefix 'wa-' means 'and'. 'qāla' is the past-tense verb 'to say'; the '-ū' suffix marks a completed action done by 'they' (a masculine or mixed group). The stem shown here ('qālu') carries only the stem vowel before the suffix, with the plural '-ū' supplied by the separate ending. Past tense, so the speaking is presented as already finished.

2.meaning: 'Be! / Become!' — a command addressed to a group, telling them to be or become something. From the verb of being/existing.
2.grammar: An imperative (command) verb. The -ū ending directs the command to a masculine plural 'you (all).' (The written alif after it is a silent spelling convention, not a separate sound.) As a command, it calls for the action to be carried out.

3.meaning: Jews / followers of Judaism — used as a plural describing adherents of the Jewish faith (associated in form with the name of the people and with the idea of being guided or returning).
3.grammar: A plural noun in the indefinite accusative: the -an ending (nunation) marks it as indefinite and accusative. The accusative is the case used for a direct object or to state what someone is said or claimed to be.
3.root: ه-و-د (h-w-d) — to return, repent; (associated with) Jewishness

4.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
4.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

5.meaning: Christians; the plural noun for the followers of the Messiah ʿĪsā (Jesus). It denotes the religious community known as the Naṣārā, traditionally connected with the town of Nazareth or with the idea of 'helpers/supporters' (anṣār) of the Messiah.
5.grammar: A plural noun (a so-called 'broken'/irregular plural). It ends in a fixed long -ā that does not change for case, so its form stays the same whether it functions as a subject, object, or after a preposition.
5.root: ن-ص-ر (n-ṣ-r) — to help, aid, give victory (and, by association, the Christians as 'helpers' of the Messiah)

6.meaning: 'You become rightly guided / you find the right way' — a present-tense verb meaning to accept and follow true guidance, to be set on the right path.

parts.en: be guided / find the right way

6.grammar: Present-tense verb (a reflexive/'accept-for-oneself' pattern of the guidance root). The ta-…-ū frame marks a second-person masculine plural subject, 'you (all).' The -ū ending here (with the dropped final -na) shows the verb is in a subordinate mood — the form used after certain particles, e.g. as the result of a condition ('… then you will be guided').
6.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — to guide, lead rightly; guidance

7.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
7.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

8.meaning: A particle of retraction meaning 'rather,' 'no, but,' or 'nay' — it cancels or sets aside what was just said and shifts to a corrected or contrasting statement that follows.
8.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it never changes form). Its function is to redirect the discourse: it dismisses a prior idea and introduces what is actually the case.

9.meaning: 'Religion / creed, the way and community of belief' — a path of faith and the set of beliefs and practices defining a religious community, especially the way ascribed to a founding figure.
9.grammar: A singular noun. The -a ending is the accusative case, the form a noun takes when it is the object of a verb, or when it stands in apposition to / specifies a preceding word; it also commonly precedes an attached possessor ('the creed of …').
9.root: م-ل-ل (m-l-l) — a religion, creed, communal way

10.meaning: Ibrahim (Abraham), the proper name of the patriarch and prophet.
10.grammar: A proper name of non-Arabic origin. Because such foreign names are 'diptotes,' they take a single -a ending for both the object (accusative) and possessive/after-preposition (genitive) roles, and they do not take the usual -n (nunation). The -a here shows it is functioning as an object or after a preposition.

11.meaning: 'Upright in faith, naturally inclined to pure monotheism' — one who turns away from all false worship toward sincere devotion to the one Allah; a term for steadfast, primordial monotheistic faith.
11.grammar: A singular indefinite noun/adjective (an intensive 'faʿīl' pattern). The -an ending is accusative plus nunation: it marks indefiniteness ('a/an') and the accusative case, the form used for an object, a descriptive term, or a circumstantial state ('… as one upright in faith').
11.root: ح-ن-ف (ḥ-n-f) — to incline away (from error) toward pure monotheism

12.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
12.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

13.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

13.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

14.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
14.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

15.meaning: Those who associate partners with Allah — idolaters / polytheists who set up others alongside the one God in worship or devotion.
15.grammar: An active participle used as a noun, with 'the', in the masculine sound plural. The -īna ending marks the plural in the genitive/accusative case — the form used after a preposition or as the object of a verb.

1.meaning: 'Say! / Speak!' — a command addressed to a group, telling them to say or utter something.
1.grammar: An imperative (command) verb. The -ū ending directs the command to a masculine plural 'you (all).' (The written alif after it is a silent spelling convention.) As a command, it calls for the speech to be made.

2.meaning: We have believed; we have come to faith and trust — to affirm belief, give one's trust, and feel secure in that conviction, stated by a group about themselves.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb on the form-IV pattern (āmana, 'to believe / to have faith'). The ending -nā (a single morpheme, نَا) attached to a past verb marks the subject as 'we'. The doubled 'n' heard in 'āmannā' comes from the verb stem's final 'n' meeting the 'n' that begins the -nā ending.

3.meaning: A phrase 'in Allah / by Allah', combining the preposition 'with/in/by' and the divine name Allah, the proper name of the One God.
3.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') prefixed to the divine name Allah. A preposition always forces the following noun into the genitive case, which is why Allah here ends in -i. With verbs of believing, bi- conveys the object of faith — to believe IN.
3.root: — (Allah is the proper name of God and is not derived from a triliteral root in the usual sense)

4.meaning: And what / and that which. Combines the connective 'and' with mā, a word that can mean 'what / that which', or function as a negating particle ('not'), depending on usage.
4.grammar: The connective wa- ('and') joined to mā, an indeclinable particle (it never changes its ending). It serves either as a relative/interrogative 'what' or as a negation 'not', so its sense is fixed by context rather than by a case ending.

5.meaning: 'It was sent down / revealed': the act of being caused to descend, used especially of revelation brought down from Allah. The passive form puts the focus on the thing sent down rather than on the sender.
5.grammar: A past-tense passive verb in Form IV (anzala 'to send down' → unzila 'was sent down'). The prefix is only the u- vowel carried on the connecting hamza; the nūn that follows is the first root letter (of ن-ز-ل), not part of the prefix. The internal vowel pattern u–i marks it as passive ('was/were sent down'), with no named doer. The final -a marks the subject as 'he/it', a single masculine thing, and signals completed action.
5.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — to descend, come down; (Form IV) to send down

6.meaning: 'To us / toward us' — the preposition 'to/toward' joined to the pronoun 'us,' expressing direction or motion toward the speakers.
6.grammar: Preposition 'ilā' (to/toward), which shifts to the form 'ilay-' before a pronoun, plus the attached pronoun -nā, 'us.' Pronouns after a preposition stand in the genitive (object-of-preposition) role; -nā is a fixed form and does not change shape.

7.meaning: And what / and that which. Combines the connective 'and' with mā, a word that can mean 'what / that which', or function as a negating particle ('not'), depending on usage.
7.grammar: The connective wa- ('and') joined to mā, an indeclinable particle (it never changes its ending). It serves either as a relative/interrogative 'what' or as a negation 'not', so its sense is fixed by context rather than by a case ending.

8.meaning: 'It was sent down / revealed': the act of being caused to descend, used especially of revelation brought down from Allah. The passive form puts the focus on the thing sent down rather than on the sender.
8.grammar: A past-tense passive verb in Form IV (anzala 'to send down' → unzila 'was sent down'). The prefix is only the u- vowel carried on the connecting hamza; the nūn that follows is the first root letter (of ن-ز-ل), not part of the prefix. The internal vowel pattern u–i marks it as passive ('was/were sent down'), with no named doer. The final -a marks the subject as 'he/it', a single masculine thing, and signals completed action.
8.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — to descend, come down; (Form IV) to send down

9.meaning: "to / towards" — a preposition marking the end-point, goal, or direction of a movement or extent ("up to," "as far as," "toward").
9.grammar: An indeclinable preposition; it has no case ending of its own and always governs a following noun in the genitive case.

10.meaning: Ibrahim (Abraham), the proper name of the patriarch and prophet.
10.grammar: A proper name of non-Arabic origin. Because such foreign names are 'diptotes,' they take a single -a ending for both the object (accusative) and possessive/after-preposition (genitive) roles, and they do not take the usual -n (nunation). The -a here shows it is functioning as an object or after a preposition.

11.meaning: And Ismāʿīl (Ishmael), the proper name of the prophet, son of Ibrahim; preceded by the connector 'and.'
11.grammar: The connector 'wa-' ('and') joined to a proper name of non-Arabic origin. As a 'diptote' foreign name, it takes a single -a ending for both the object (accusative) and possessive/after-preposition (genitive) roles, and it does not take nunation.

12.meaning: The proper name 'Isaac' (Isḥāq), the prophet, joined to the conjunction 'and.'
12.grammar: Conjunction 'wa' (and) prefixed to a proper name. The final -a is the accusative/genitive ending; because this is a foreign (non-Arabic) name, it is grammatically 'diptote,' meaning it takes -a for both those cases and never takes nunation (the -n sound).

13.meaning: The proper name 'Jacob' (Yaʿqūb), the prophet, joined to the conjunction 'and.'
13.grammar: Conjunction 'wa' (and) prefixed to a proper name. The final -a is the accusative/genitive ending; as a foreign (non-Arabic) name it is 'diptote,' taking -a for both those cases and never taking nunation (the -n sound).

14.meaning: 'The tribes / the descendants' — specifically the tribes descended from the twelve sons of Jacob (the Israelite tribes); the plural of a word for a grandson, descendant, or tribal branch.
14.grammar: Conjunction 'wa' (and) plus the definite article 'al-' (the) on a broken (irregular) plural noun. The -i ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to / possessed by a preceding word, or to match an earlier genitive noun in a list.
14.root: س-ب-ط (s-b-ṭ) — a tribe, descendant line (esp. of Jacob)

15.meaning: And what / and that which. Combines the connective 'and' with mā, a word that can mean 'what / that which', or function as a negating particle ('not'), depending on usage.
15.grammar: The connective wa- ('and') joined to mā, an indeclinable particle (it never changes its ending). It serves either as a relative/interrogative 'what' or as a negation 'not', so its sense is fixed by context rather than by a case ending.

16.meaning: A passive verb meaning 'was given / was granted / was brought (something)'. It conveys that someone received something from an unnamed giver, with the focus on the recipient and the gift rather than the giver.

parts.en: was (passive prefix of the Form IV verb 'to give/bring')
given/brought (middle root letter of the passive stem)
final weak root letter (yāʾ) surfacing in the passive perfect

16.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in the passive voice, third person masculine singular ('he/it was given'). It is the passive of a Form IV verb (active 'to give/bring'), formed from the Form IV stem rather than by a Form I internal vowel change; the subject ending is zero (no added pronoun). The final -ya is the weak third root letter (yāʾ) appearing in this passive perfect form, not a personal suffix.
16.root: ا-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; in Form IV, to bring or give

17.meaning: Mūsā (Moses) — the proper name of the prophet. As a name it has no Arabic root meaning; it is a non-inflecting (indeclinable) noun whose ending does not change for case.
17.grammar: A proper name ending in a fixed long -ā (written as alif maqṣūra). It is fully indeclinable (invariable): the final -ā never changes, so the word shows no case distinction at all — it looks and sounds identical whether subject, object, or possessor. (This is unlike a diptote, which still alternates between two case vowels; here there is no alternation.)

18.meaning: The proper name 'Isa' (Jesus), prefixed with 'and'. It refers to the prophet Isa, son of Maryam.
18.grammar: A proper noun joined by the connector 'wa' ('and'). The name ends in a long ā (written with the dagger alif) and is indeclinable, so it does not change its ending for case; it simply names the person.
18.root: — (proper name)

19.meaning: And what / and that which. Combines the connective 'and' with mā, a word that can mean 'what / that which', or function as a negating particle ('not'), depending on usage.
19.grammar: The connective wa- ('and') joined to mā, an indeclinable particle (it never changes its ending). It serves either as a relative/interrogative 'what' or as a negation 'not', so its sense is fixed by context rather than by a case ending.

20.meaning: A passive verb meaning 'was given / was granted / was brought (something)'. It conveys that someone received something from an unnamed giver, with the focus on the recipient and the gift rather than the giver.

parts.en: was (passive prefix of the Form IV verb 'to give/bring')
given/brought (middle root letter of the passive stem)
final weak root letter (yāʾ) surfacing in the passive perfect

20.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in the passive voice, third person masculine singular ('he/it was given'). It is the passive of a Form IV verb (active 'to give/bring'), formed from the Form IV stem rather than by a Form I internal vowel change; the subject ending is zero (no added pronoun). The final -ya is the weak third root letter (yāʾ) appearing in this passive perfect form, not a personal suffix.
20.root: ا-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; in Form IV, to bring or give

21.meaning: 'The prophets' — those chosen by Allah to receive revelation and convey His message to humanity.
21.grammar: A definite masculine sound (regular) plural noun with the prefixed article 'al-' ('the'). The ending -ūna is the nominative case for this kind of plural, the form used when the noun is the subject or doer of a sentence ('the prophets [did/were] …').
21.root: ن-ب-ا (n-b-ʾ) — news, tidings; a prophet conveys news from Allah

22.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
22.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

23.meaning: 'Their Lord / their Sustainer.' The noun 'rabb' — a master who owns, nurtures, sustains, and brings to maturity all under His care — joined to 'their.' It conveys far more than 'lord': the one who creates, provides for, and governs His servants.
23.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive pronoun -him ('their,' masculine plural). The -i ending is the genitive case, which typically appears after a preposition or links the word to another in an 'of / belonging to' relationship; here it pairs with the attached 'their.'
23.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master; lordship, ownership, care

24.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
24.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

25.meaning: 'We make a distinction / we separate / we differentiate (between things)'. It expresses treating items as separate or unequal, singling some out from others.
25.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, first person plural: the 'nu-' prefix means 'we'. The doubled middle root letter marks the intensive (Form II) pattern, giving the sense of actively differentiating or sorting. The final -u marks the plain indicative mood (a simple statement: 'we do …').

26.meaning: Between; in the midst of two things. An adverb of place marking the space separating or lying among parties or points.
26.grammar: An adverb of place ('between'). It always ends in -a and grammatically governs what follows it, putting the following noun(s) into the genitive 'of' relationship. It does not change to show 'the' or a case of its own; the fixed -a is simply how this word is formed.
26.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies between

27.meaning: One; anyone; a single individual. Often used in negative or conditional contexts to mean 'anyone (at all)'.
27.grammar: An indefinite noun in the genitive case. The -in ending combines the genitive marker -i (the form taken after a preposition or in a possessive link, '… of …') with nunation (-n), the sign of an indefinite 'a / any'.
27.root: أ-ح-د (ʾ-ḥ-d) — oneness, unity; one

28.meaning: 'From / of them' — the preposition 'from' joined to the pronoun 'them' (a group of males or a mixed group).
28.grammar: A preposition ('min', meaning 'from' or 'of') with an attached object pronoun '-hum' ('them'). The pronoun refers to a plural group, and as the object of a preposition it stays in this fixed form.

29.meaning: 'And we' — the standalone pronoun 'we' (a group including the speaker), prefixed with the connector 'and'; often used to set up a contrast ('while we…').
29.grammar: A detached subject pronoun meaning 'we,' here introduced by wa- ('and' / 'while'). As an independent pronoun it stands on its own (not attached to a verb) and is invariable — it is fixed in form and takes no case ending that changes.
29.root: — (pronoun, no triliteral root)

30.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
30.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

31.meaning: 'Ones who submit / those who surrender themselves to Allah' — the plural of the active participle 'muslim,' i.e. one who willingly submits and devotes himself in obedience to Allah.
31.grammar: A masculine plural active participle (a doer-noun). The -ūna ending marks a sound masculine plural in the nominative case, the form used when the word stands as the subject or as the predicate naming who/what the subject is.
31.root: س-ل-م (s-l-m) — peace, safety, submission/surrender

1.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'fa-' ('then', 'so', 'but') drawing a consequence, joined to the conditional particle 'in' ('if'). Together: 'then if …', 'but if …'.
1.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that signals a result or transition ('then/so'). 'in' is the conditional particle 'if', introducing a supposed condition. Both are indeclinable particles with no case ending.

2.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
2.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

3.meaning: 'With/by the like (of) …' — the preposition 'with/by' joined to a noun meaning 'likeness, similar, equivalent'. It introduces a comparison: something matching or equal to another.

parts.en: like / similar / equivalent (genitive after the preposition)

3.grammar: A preposition 'bi-' ('with/by') attached to the noun 'mithl' ('likeness, the like of'). The final -i on 'mithl' is the genitive case vowel, required after a preposition; it also links this noun to a following noun in a possessive chain ('the like OF …').

4.meaning: A word meaning 'what' or 'that which' — a relative/indefinite particle pointing to an unspecified thing ('what', 'whatever', 'that which').
4.grammar: An invariable particle (mā) with no case ending. Depending on context it works as a relative pronoun ('that which') introducing a clause, or as an interrogative/indefinite ('what'). It does not inflect for case, gender, or number.

5.meaning: 'You (all) have believed / you came to faith' — to affirm trust and belief, especially faith in Allah and what He has revealed.

parts.en: believed (initial long vowel of the Form IV stem 'to have faith')
you all (2nd person masculine plural subject)

5.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb, second person masculine plural: the ending '-tum' means 'you all (did) …'. The Form IV pattern (with the long initial ā) carries the sense of coming to and holding faith. It states a completed act: 'you have believed'.
5.root: ا-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — safety, trust; to believe, have faith

6.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
6.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

7.meaning: 'Then/so, indeed …' — the connector 'then/so' joined to the particle 'qad', which before a past-tense verb stresses that the action has certainly and already happened.
7.grammar: A connecting particle 'fa-' ('then/so', often signalling a result) plus 'qad'. With a following perfect verb, 'qad' emphasises that the act is real and completed ('have indeed …'). The final -i on 'qad' is a helping vowel added to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a cluster; it carries no grammatical meaning of its own.

8.meaning: 'They became rightly guided / they found the right way' — to be led onto the correct path, especially the path of true guidance from Allah.

parts.en: prefix of the reflexive (Form VIII) verb

8.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb, third person masculine plural: the ending '-aw' (with the silent alif after the wāw) means 'they (did) …'. The Form VIII pattern gives a sense of taking guidance for oneself, i.e. becoming guided. It states a completed act.
8.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — guidance, to guide, to show the way

9.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
9.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

10.meaning: 'They turned away / they turned their backs / they turned aside'. It conveys turning oneself away from something, often implying rejection or withdrawal.
10.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb, third person masculine plural: the ending '-aw' means 'they (did) …'. The Form V pattern (with the 'ta-' prefix and doubled middle letter) gives a reflexive sense — turning oneself away. It states a completed act.
10.root: و-ل-ي (w-l-y) — to be near/turn toward; in this form, to turn away

11.meaning: A compound particle 'so it is only …' or 'then indeed only.' It joins a consequence ('so/then') to an emphatic restriction ('only / nothing more than'), confining the statement to exactly what follows.
11.grammar: A cluster of particles: 'fa-' introduces a result ('so/then'), 'inna' gives emphasis ('truly'), and the attached 'mā' turns the emphasis into restriction, so the whole means 'so it is only/nothing but.' These are connective and emphatic words; they have no case ending of their own.

12.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (referring to a group of males, or a mixed group). Because it stands on its own rather than being attached to a verb or noun, it often adds emphasis, singling out or stressing the subject ('they themselves', 'it is they who').
12.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It does not take case endings; the fixed -m simply marks the plural 'they'. Standing alone, it commonly serves to emphasise or isolate the subject.

13.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
13.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

14.meaning: 'Schism, split, discord, opposition' — a state of being in conflict or at odds, two sides set against each other.
14.grammar: An indefinite noun in the genitive case. The ending '-in' combines genitive case with indefiniteness ('a …'), the doubled 'n' sound (tanwīn) marking it as indefinite; this case typically follows a preposition or links the noun to a preceding noun.
14.root: ش-ق-ق (sh-q-q) — to split, cleave; division, discord

15.meaning: 'So He/it will suffice you against them' — a verb meaning 'to be enough for, to spare someone the burden of', combined with markers for a future act, the one being spared ('you'), and those against whom protection is given ('them').
15.grammar: A present/imperfect verb carrying several attached pieces: the connector 'fa-' ('so'), the future prefix 'sa-' ('will'), and the subject prefix 'ya-' ('he/it'). Two object pronouns follow the verb: '-ka' ('you', singular) and '-hum(u)' ('them'). The final 'u' on '-humu' is a connecting vowel eased before a following word. Overall: 'so He will make [it] enough for you concerning them'.
15.root: ك-ف-ي (k-f-y) — to suffice, to be enough

16.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
16.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

17.meaning: 'And He' — the connective 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'He' (a single masculine person or thing), often introducing a new clause about the same subject.
17.grammar: A connective particle plus an independent pronoun. The wa- prefix means 'and', joining clauses or words. 'Huwa' is the detached third-person masculine singular pronoun; it carries no case ending, its final -a being fixed.

18.meaning: "the All-Hearing" — one who hears, perceiving all sounds completely and constantly; used as a divine name it denotes the One whose hearing is perfect and all-encompassing.
18.grammar: A definite intensive adjective/noun on the faʿīl pattern, which conveys a deep, enduring quality ('ever-hearing,' not merely 'hearing once'). The 'al-' prefix makes it definite ('the'). The final '-u' is the nominative case ending, the form a word takes when it is the subject of a sentence or a predicate/description following it.
18.root: س-م-ع (s-m-ʿ) — hearing, listening

19.meaning: The All-Knowing — one whose knowledge is complete, perfect, and all-encompassing; an intensive form stressing that knowing is an essential, constant attribute.
19.grammar: A definite noun/adjective in an intensive pattern (faʿīl) that stresses depth and permanence of the quality. The prefix 'al-' means 'the'; the final -u (ḍamma) marks the nominative case, which typically signals the subject of a sentence or a predicate describing it.

1.meaning: 'Dye, coloring, hue' — by extension, a distinctive imprint or stamp on something, figuratively the 'coloring' that a faith or way gives to a person.
1.grammar: A feminine noun in the accusative case. The -a ending on the feminine ending (tā' marbūṭa) marks the accusative, the case used for the object of a verb or for emphatic/exclamatory naming of a thing.

2.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
2.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

3.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
3.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

4.meaning: 'Better, finer, more excellent / best, finest' — the comparative-superlative form of 'good, beautiful', meaning surpassing in goodness or beauty.
4.grammar: A comparative/superlative adjective on the pattern 'afʿal' ('more/most …'). The final -u marks the nominative case, the form used when the word is the subject or predicate of a sentence ('… is better/best'). As a comparative of this pattern it does not take the indefinite tanwīn.

5.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
5.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

6.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
6.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

7.meaning: 'A dye, a coloring, a hue' — the same word as 'coloring/imprint', here in its indefinite form ('a coloring').
7.grammar: An indefinite feminine noun in the accusative case. The ending '-tan' combines accusative case with indefiniteness, the doubled 'n' sound (tanwīn) marking 'a …'. The accusative here is the case used, among other things, for a noun of specification ('… in respect of coloring').

8.meaning: 'And we' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'we,' which emphasizes the speakers as the subject.
8.grammar: Conjunction 'wa' (and) prefixed to an independent subject pronoun. 'Naḥnu' is a fixed, unchanging word meaning 'we'; it does not take case endings, and its final -u is part of the set form rather than a grammatical case marker.

9.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
9.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

10.meaning: 'Worshippers / servants who worship' — those who devote acts of worship and humble service, especially to Allah.
10.grammar: A masculine sound (regular) plural of an active participle ('one who worships'). The ending -ūna is the nominative case, used when the word is the subject or predicate of a sentence ('[they] are worshippers').
10.root: ع-ب-د (ʿ-b-d) — to worship, to serve; servitude to Allah

1.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
