1.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

2.meaning: 'Do you (all) argue/dispute with us?' — a question formed from a verb meaning 'to dispute, argue, contend (using proofs)', with 'us' as the party argued against.
2.grammar: A present/imperfect verb opened by the question particle 'a-' ('do …?'). It is second person masculine plural ('you all'), built on the Form III pattern that implies a mutual or back-and-forth action (arguing with one another). The plural ending '-na' is kept and the object pronoun '-nā' ('us') is attached: 'do you dispute with us?'.
2.root: ح-ج-ج (ḥ-j-j) — to argue, to bring a proof; disputation

3.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
3.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

4.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
4.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

5.meaning: 'And He' — the connective 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'He' (a single masculine person or thing), often introducing a new clause about the same subject.
5.grammar: A connective particle plus an independent pronoun. The wa- prefix means 'and', joining clauses or words. 'Huwa' is the detached third-person masculine singular pronoun; it carries no case ending, its final -a being fixed.

6.meaning: 'Our Lord' — 'Rabb' (Lord, Master, Sustainer who creates, owns, nurtures and governs) joined to 'our'. A weighty term for Allah as the One who brings up and sustains all that exists.
6.grammar: A noun with the attached possessive pronoun '-nā' ('our'). The -u before the pronoun is the nominative case, used when the word is the subject or predicate of a sentence ('[He] is our Lord').
6.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master; lordship

7.meaning: 'And your Lord' — the connector 'and' plus 'Rabb' (Lord, Master, Sustainer) joined to 'your' (plural). It names Allah as the Lord of the addressed group.
7.grammar: The connector 'wa' ('and') with a noun carrying the possessive pronoun '-kum' ('your', referring to a group). The -u before the pronoun is the nominative case, used when the word is the subject or predicate ('[He] is your Lord').
7.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master; lordship

8.meaning: 'And for/to us' — the connector 'and' with the preposition 'for/to' joined to the pronoun 'us'. It expresses belonging or what is due to a group ('ours / for us').
8.grammar: The connector 'wa' ('and') with the preposition 'li-' ('for/to') attached to the pronoun '-nā' ('us'). The preposition's vowel shifts to 'la-' before an attached pronoun. This phrase expresses possession or entitlement: 'and for us [belongs] …'.

9.meaning: 'Our deeds / our works / our actions' — the plural of 'deed, action, work' joined to 'our'.
9.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural noun with the attached possessive '-nā' ('our'). The -u before the pronoun is the nominative case, used when the word is the subject or predicate of a sentence ('our deeds [are] …').
9.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, to work; deed, action

10.meaning: A short phrase meaning 'and for you' or 'and you have'. It joins a new statement with 'and', then uses 'for/to you' to express possession or benefit belonging to a group.
10.grammar: Three pieces: wa- ('and') linking to what came before, the preposition la- ('for/to'), and the attached pronoun -kum ('you all', plural). A preposition-plus-'you' phrase like this commonly conveys 'you have' or 'belonging to you'.

11.meaning: 'Your deeds / your works / your actions' — the plural of 'deed, action, work' joined to 'your' (plural).
11.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural noun with the attached possessive '-kum' ('your', referring to a group). The -u before the pronoun is the nominative case, used when the word is the subject or predicate of a sentence ('your deeds [are] …').
11.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, to work; deed, action

12.meaning: 'And we' — the standalone pronoun 'we' (a group including the speaker), prefixed with the connector 'and'; often used to set up a contrast ('while we…').
12.grammar: A detached subject pronoun meaning 'we,' here introduced by wa- ('and' / 'while'). As an independent pronoun it stands on its own (not attached to a verb) and is invariable — it is fixed in form and takes no case ending that changes.

13.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
13.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

14.meaning: 'Sincere ones / those who are devoted purely' — those who make their faith and worship purely and exclusively for Allah, free of show or rival motive.
14.grammar: A masculine sound (regular) plural of an active participle ('one who makes [something] pure/sincere'), built on the Form IV pattern. The ending -ūna is the nominative case, used when the word is the subject or predicate of a sentence ('[they] are sincere').
14.root: خ-ل-ص (kh-l-ṣ) — to be pure, clear, unmixed; sincerity

1.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'or', specifically the 'or' that pairs with a preceding question to offer an alternative ('…or…?'). It links two possibilities being weighed against each other, often after an opening interrogative.

parts.en: or (in alternatives, esp. after a question)

1.grammar: An indeclinable particle (no case or tense ending). It typically introduces the second branch of a two-part question or a balanced alternative, presenting the two as equally consequential.

2.meaning: You say / do you say — to utter or declare in speech, addressed to a group ('you all'), presented as ongoing or habitual.
2.grammar: Present-tense verb. The 'ta-' prefix with the '-ūna' ending marks 'you' (masculine plural) speaking now or habitually. The full '-ūna' ending signals the indicative mood — a plain statement or question, not a command.

3.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
3.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

4.meaning: Ibrahim (Abraham), the proper name of the patriarch and prophet.
4.grammar: A proper name of non-Arabic origin. Because such foreign names are 'diptotes,' they take a single -a ending for both the object (accusative) and possessive/after-preposition (genitive) roles, and they do not take the usual -n (nunation). The -a here shows it is functioning as an object or after a preposition.

5.meaning: And Ismāʿīl (Ishmael), the proper name of the prophet, son of Ibrahim; preceded by the connector 'and.'
5.grammar: The connector 'wa-' ('and') joined to a proper name of non-Arabic origin. As a 'diptote' foreign name, it takes a single -a ending for both the object (accusative) and possessive/after-preposition (genitive) roles, and it does not take nunation.

6.meaning: The proper name 'Isaac' (Isḥāq), the prophet, joined to the conjunction 'and.'
6.grammar: Conjunction 'wa' (and) prefixed to a proper name. The final -a is the accusative/genitive ending; because this is a foreign (non-Arabic) name, it is grammatically 'diptote,' meaning it takes -a for both those cases and never takes nunation (the -n sound).

7.meaning: The proper name 'Jacob' (Yaʿqūb), the prophet, joined to the conjunction 'and.'
7.grammar: Conjunction 'wa' (and) prefixed to a proper name. The final -a is the accusative/genitive ending; as a foreign (non-Arabic) name it is 'diptote,' taking -a for both those cases and never taking nunation (the -n sound).

8.meaning: 'And the tribes / the descendants' — the connector 'and' with 'al-asbāṭ', the plural of 'sibṭ', referring to the tribal descendants (the offspring of Yaʿqūb).
8.grammar: The connector 'wa' ('and') with a definite broken (irregular) plural noun, carrying the article 'al-' ('the'). The final -a marks the accusative case, the form used for the object of a verb or an item in a listed sequence of such objects.
8.root: س-ب-ط (s-b-ṭ) — a tribe, a line of descendants

9.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
9.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
9.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

10.meaning: Jews / followers of Judaism — used as a plural describing adherents of the Jewish faith (associated in form with the name of the people and with the idea of being guided or returning).
10.grammar: A plural noun in the indefinite accusative: the -an ending (nunation) marks it as indefinite and accusative. The accusative is the case used for a direct object or to state what someone is said or claimed to be.
10.root: ه-و-د (h-w-d) — to return, repent; (associated with) Jewishness

11.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
11.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

12.meaning: Christians; the plural noun for the followers of the Messiah ʿĪsā (Jesus). It denotes the religious community known as the Naṣārā, traditionally connected with the town of Nazareth or with the idea of 'helpers/supporters' (anṣār) of the Messiah.
12.grammar: A plural noun (a so-called 'broken'/irregular plural). It ends in a fixed long -ā that does not change for case, so its form stays the same whether it functions as a subject, object, or after a preposition.
12.root: ن-ص-ر (n-ṣ-r) — to help, aid, give victory (and, by association, the Christians as 'helpers' of the Messiah)

13.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
13.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

14.meaning: An emphatic, pointed way of asking 'Is it you (plural)…?' — formed by attaching the interrogative particle a- ('do/are…?') to the independent pronoun 'you (group of people)'. Fronting the pronoun gives a sense of singling out or challenging the addressees, roughly 'Is it really YOU who…?'
14.grammar: The opening hamza (a-) is the interrogative particle that turns a statement into a yes/no question. 'antum' is the standalone subject pronoun for a group of males (or a mixed group); it is invariable and carries no case ending. Placing this independent pronoun at the front typically adds emphasis on the doer ('you yourselves').

15.meaning: 'I know' — a present-tense verb of knowing: to have certain knowledge or awareness of something.
15.grammar: A present/future (Form I) verb, first-person singular ('I'), marked by the prefix a-. This a- is the first-person agreement marker built into the conjugation, not a free-standing pronoun. The final -u marks the indicative — a plain statement of ongoing or habitual knowing.

16.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'or', used especially to introduce the second part of a question ('…or…?'). The form 'ami' is the particle 'am' with a helping vowel -i added so it can be pronounced smoothly before a following word that begins with a connecting (elidable) alif.
16.grammar: 'am' is a coordinating particle that links alternatives, characteristically in an either/or question. The final -i here is not a case ending; it is a connecting vowel added to avoid an awkward consonant cluster when the next word begins with a silent (linking) alif.

17.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
17.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

18.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
18.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.
18.root: — (pronoun/particle; no triliteral root)

19.meaning: An elative adjective meaning 'more / most wrongdoing, unjust, or oppressive' — comparing degrees of ẓulm (placing things out of their rightful place, transgression).
19.grammar: An elative (comparative/superlative) noun on the pattern afʿal, meaning 'more/most unjust'. It ends in -u (nominative), the case typical of a subject or predicate.
19.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — wrongdoing, injustice, putting something where it does not belong

20.meaning: A compound meaning 'than one who / than whoever' — combining the preposition of comparison 'than' with the relative pronoun 'who', used to compare a person against others.
20.grammar: The preposition 'min' (here 'than', used after elatives) followed by the indeclinable relative 'man' ('who'). The final nūn of 'min' undergoes regressive assimilation into the following mīm of 'man', producing a doubled mīm; the resulting shadda sits on the mīm of 'man'. Both words are indeclinable particles and take no case ending.

21.meaning: 'He concealed / hid / kept (something) secret' — to deliberately suppress or withhold information, knowledge, or testimony so that others do not learn it.
21.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he concealed'. The pattern fa‘ala with the final -a vowel marks a completed act done by a single male subject. It describes the action as finished, not ongoing.

22.meaning: 'A testimony / witnessing / attestation' — the act or content of bearing witness: giving evidence about something one knows to be true, or formal certification of a fact.
22.grammar: A feminine singular noun, indefinite. The -an ending (written on the tied tā’, hence -tan) is the accusative with 'tanwīn': it marks the word as 'a testimony' (no 'the') and signals that the noun typically functions as the direct object of a verb or otherwise stands in the accusative.

23.meaning: 'With him / in his keeping / that he has' — combining the locational word 'ind ('at, with, in the presence/possession of') with the pronoun 'him'. It conveys that something is held by, present with, or belongs to him.
23.grammar: 'ʿinda' is an adverb of place/possession that always governs a following word in the genitive; here it takes the attached pronoun -hu ('him/his'). The -a on 'ʿinda' is its fixed accusative-style ending as an adverbial. The pronoun -hu means the thing is located with, or owned by, a single male.

24.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
24.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

25.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
25.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

26.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
26.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

27.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
27.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
27.root: — (proper divine name)

28.meaning: 'With/being heedless' — the preposition/particle 'bi' attached to 'ghāfil', one who is unaware, inattentive, or neglectful, failing to take notice.
28.grammar: The particle 'bi-' governs the following word into the genitive case. 'Ghāfil' is an active participle ('one who is heedless'). The '-in' (tanwīn) marks it indefinite and genitive; the 'bi-' here commonly adds emphasis within a negation ('not at all heedless').

29.meaning: 'About what' / 'of that which' — the preposition 'ʿan' ('about, concerning, away from') merged with 'mā' ('what, that which').
29.grammar: A fusion of the preposition 'ʿan' ('about, concerning') with the relative/interrogative 'mā' ('what'); the 'n' of 'ʿan' assimilates into 'mā' to give 'ʿammā'. It introduces the thing being spoken about.

30.meaning: You (all) do / work / act — to carry out deeds or labor.
30.grammar: A present-tense verb (Form I). The 'ta-' prefix with the '-ūna' ending marks the second-person masculine plural ('you all'). The '-ūna' (with final 'n') is the indicative form, marking a plain ongoing or habitual statement.
30.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, work, act; deeds

1.meaning: That; a demonstrative used to point to something distant or already mentioned. It singles out a single feminine (or grammatically feminine) thing, roughly 'that one over there.'
1.grammar: A feminine singular demonstrative pronoun pointing to something far off. The -ka element signals remoteness ('that yonder' rather than 'this near'). Being a demonstrative, it does not take case endings; its form is fixed.

2.meaning: 'A community / a nation, a people' — a body of people bound together as a single group, often by shared faith, way, or era.
2.grammar: A singular indefinite noun. The -un ending is nominative plus nunation: the -n sound signals 'a/an' (indefinite), and the -u marks the nominative case, the form used when the word is the subject or the thing being named.
2.root: ء-م-م (ʾ-m-m) — to head toward; a community, way, model

3.meaning: A short particle placed before a verb to emphasize or affirm it. Before a past-tense verb it means 'indeed / certainly / has already (happened)'; before a present-tense verb it can mean 'sometimes / may'. It sharpens and confirms the verb that follows.
3.grammar: An indeclinable particle (its form never changes). It does not take case or tense endings; its job is to color the following verb — affirming and intensifying a past action ('has indeed done') or signaling occasional possibility with a present verb.

4.meaning: 'It passed away / went by, came to an end' — said of a community, time, or era that has elapsed and is now gone. The root carries the sense of being emptied out, hence of time or people that have passed.
4.grammar: Past-tense verb. The -t (sukūn-marked -at) suffix marks a third-person feminine singular subject, 'she/it,' used here because the noun it refers to is grammatically feminine. The past tense states a completed action.
4.root: خ-ل-و (kh-l-w) — to be empty/vacant; to pass away, elapse

5.meaning: 'For it / to it, belonging to it' — the preposition 'for/to' joined to a pronoun referring to a feminine singular thing; it expresses possession or benefit ('it has / it gets').
5.grammar: Preposition 'li-' (here vowelled 'la-' before a pronoun) plus an attached object pronoun. The -hā suffix means 'it/her,' a feminine singular. Pronouns that follow a preposition are in the genitive (object-of-preposition) role; -hā is a fixed form and does not change shape.

6.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
6.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

7.meaning: 'It earned / acquired, gained' — said of deeds and their consequences; the root means to gain or acquire something, especially the moral 'earnings' of one's actions.
7.grammar: Past-tense verb. The -t (sukūn-marked -at) suffix marks a third-person feminine singular subject, 'she/it.' The past tense presents the action as completed.
7.root: ك-س-ب (k-s-b) — to earn, acquire, gain (esp. deeds)

8.meaning: A short phrase meaning 'and for you' or 'and you have'. It joins a new statement with 'and', then uses 'for/to you' to express possession or benefit belonging to a group.
8.grammar: Three pieces: wa- ('and') linking to what came before, the preposition la- ('for/to'), and the attached pronoun -kum ('you all', plural). A preposition-plus-'you' phrase like this commonly conveys 'you have' or 'belonging to you'.

9.meaning: A short, highly versatile particle 'mā.' It can mean 'what' or 'that which,' can negate ('not'), and can serve as an intensifier attached to another word. Its precise force depends on what it accompanies, but its core is to point to a thing or to add emphasis.
9.grammar: A multifunctional particle. It does not take case endings. Depending on usage it can be a relative ('that which'), an interrogative ('what?'), a negator ('not'), or — when joined to another particle — an emphasizer. It is uninflected and indeclinable.

10.meaning: 'You earned / acquired, gained' — the same verb of earning addressed to a group of people, referring to the deeds they have done.
10.grammar: Past-tense verb. The -tum suffix marks the subject as second-person masculine plural, 'you (all).' The past tense presents the action as completed.
10.root: ك-س-ب (k-s-b) — to earn, acquire, gain (esp. deeds)

11.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
11.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

12.meaning: 'You are asked / will be questioned' — a passive verb meaning that a group is questioned or held to account by someone else; the doing of the asking lies with an unnamed party.
12.grammar: Present-tense passive verb. The tu-…-ūna frame marks a second-person masculine plural subject, 'you (all),' as the receiver of the action ('you are asked'). The -ūna ending also signals the indicative mood, the plain statement form. The internal -u- vowelling shows it is passive (action done to the subject).

13.meaning: 'About what' / 'of that which' — the preposition 'ʿan' ('about, concerning, away from') merged with 'mā' ('what, that which').
13.grammar: A fusion of the preposition 'ʿan' ('about, concerning') with the relative/interrogative 'mā' ('what'); the 'n' of 'ʿan' assimilates into 'mā' to give 'ʿammā'. It introduces the thing being spoken about.

14.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
14.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
14.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

15.meaning: 'They do / they work / they act' — to perform deeds or carry out actions, ongoing or habitual.
15.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ya-…-ūna frame marks third-person masculine plural ('they do/work'). The retained final -na (the 'ūna' ending) is the indicative form, used for a plain, ongoing, or habitual action that is simply being stated.
15.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, work, act; deeds

1.meaning: 'He/it will say' — a statement of future speech. Built from the present-tense verb 'he says' with the prefixed particle sa- ('will, shall, is going to'), marking an action expected to happen soon.
1.grammar: The prefix sa- places the verb in the near future ('will say'). The base verb is present-tense, third-person masculine singular: the ya- prefix means 'he', and the final -u ending marks the indicative mood (a plain, factual statement, as opposed to commands or subjunctive forms).

2.meaning: The foolish, weak-minded ones; people lacking sound judgment, prudence, and self-restraint. The term denotes those whose intellect or conduct is light and ill-considered, especially in matters of right belief and proper handling of wealth.
2.grammar: A plural noun carrying 'the' (al-). The final -u ending is nominative, the case that typically marks the doer or subject of a sentence, or a noun being identified or described.
2.root: س-ف-ه (s-f-h) — foolishness, light-mindedness, lack of sound judgment

3.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
3.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

4.meaning: Humankind, people, mankind — the collective of human beings.
4.grammar: A collective noun ('people, mankind') carrying the definite article al- ('the'); the 'l' of the article assimilates into the following 'n', doubling it (al-nās → an-nās). The genitive ending -i marks the word as governed by a preposition or as the second term of a possessive.
4.root: ء-ن-س (ʾ-n-s) — humankind, sociability, familiarity; the word for 'people' is most commonly traced to this root (related to insān, 'human being')

5.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
5.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

6.meaning: 'He turned them / directed them' — the verb wallā ('to turn someone/something toward, to cause to face away or toward') joined to the object pronoun 'them'. It conveys causing a group to turn away from, or to turn toward, a particular direction.
6.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb of the doubled (Form II) pattern fa‘‘ala, third-person masculine singular ('he turned/directed'), built on a final-weak root so it ends in a long -ā. The attached -hum is the object pronoun for a group (three or more males or a mixed group), marking them as the ones acted upon ('he turned them'). There is no divine name here; the doubled lām belongs to the verb itself.
6.root: و-ل-ي (w-l-y) — turning, directing, facing toward, being near/in charge

7.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on behalf of,' 'for,' 'about,' or 'away from.' It often conveys removing a burden from someone or acting in their place.

parts.en: on behalf of / for / away from

7.grammar: A preposition (a linking particle). It governs the noun that follows it, putting that noun into the genitive case. It does not change form.

8.meaning: 'Their prayer-direction' — the qibla, the fixed direction a worshipper faces in prayer, here held by a group ('their'). A qibla is the orientation point toward which ritual prayer is directed.
8.grammar: A feminine noun ('qibla') with the attached possessive pronoun -him ('their', for a group). The -i ending (shown as -ti on the tied tā’) is genitive, the case used when a noun is possessed by a following pronoun ('the qibla OF them') or governed by a preposition. The final -u on -himu is a linking vowel added before a following word.
8.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — facing, turning toward, what is in front

9.meaning: A feminine singular relative pronoun: 'the one which / that which / who' (referring to a single feminine thing). It introduces a descriptive clause that tells us more about a preceding feminine noun.
9.grammar: A relative pronoun, feminine singular, fixed in form (it does not change for case). It links a feminine noun to a following clause describing it, the equivalent of English 'which,' 'that,' or 'who.'

10.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
10.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
10.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

11.meaning: 'On it / upon it / over it' — the preposition 'alā ('on, upon, against') joined to the pronoun 'it/her', referring to a single feminine or grammatically feminine thing.
11.grammar: 'ʿalā' is a preposition meaning 'on/upon/over'; its ending shifts to -ay when a pronoun is attached. The suffix -hā is the object pronoun for a single feminine (or feminine-gender) thing. Together they mean 'on it'. Words after a preposition stand in the genitive, though attached pronouns like -hā do not visibly change form.

12.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
12.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

13.meaning: A combination 'to/for Allah / belonging to Allah' — the preposition 'to/for' joined to the name Allah, expressing that something is due to, owned by, or directed toward Allah.
13.grammar: The prefix li- is the preposition 'to / for / belonging to'. 'Allah' follows, with the initial alif of 'Allāh' elided after li-. The final -i is the genitive ending required after a preposition; it marks Allah as the One to whom something belongs or is directed.

14.meaning: The noun 'the east' — the direction of sunrise, the place where the sun rises.
14.grammar: A noun of place (where the sun rises) with the definite article 'al-' ('the'). It ends in -u (nominative), the case typical of a subject or predicate.
14.root: ش-ر-ق (sh-r-q) — to rise (of the sun), the east, radiance

15.meaning: 'And the west' — the direction of the setting sun, or by extension the western region/lands. Here it carries the connector 'and' plus the definite article 'the'.
15.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'; 'al-' is the definite article 'the'. 'maghrib' is a noun of place from the root for 'setting/going down', literally 'the place/time of sunset'. The final -u is the nominative ending, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or a word that simply names something.
15.root: غ-ر-ب (gh-r-b) — setting (of the sun), going west, being distant/strange

16.meaning: 'He guides / leads on the right way' — to show someone the correct path, direct them rightly, or lead them to a goal, whether literally or in matters of belief and conduct.
16.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular: the ya- prefix means 'he'. The verb ends in a long -ī (a weak final letter); in this indicative form the long vowel stands in place of the usual -u mood marker, still conveying a plain, ongoing statement ('he guides').
16.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — guidance, showing the way, leading rightly

17.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
17.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

18.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning 'he wills, he wishes, he chooses' — to want or intend something by one's own decision.
18.grammar: A present/ongoing action by a single masculine subject ('he'); the ya- prefix marks third-person masculine singular, and the final -u marks the indicative mood — a plain statement of fact ('he wills'), as opposed to a command or a verb governed by 'that.'
18.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʾ) — willing, wishing; the root behind 'thing' (shayʾ)

19.meaning: A preposition meaning 'to,' 'toward,' or 'up to' — pointing to the end-point, goal, or limit of a motion, direction, or extent.
19.grammar: A preposition (a small linking word). It governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the genitive case, and points to a destination or limit ('to,' 'toward,' 'as far as').

20.meaning: 'A path / road / way' — a route one travels; frequently used in a moral or spiritual sense for a way of life or course of conduct.
20.grammar: A masculine noun, indefinite. The -in ending (the genitive with 'tanwīn') marks it as 'a path' (no 'the') and signals the genitive case — the case used after prepositions or when a noun is linked to a following noun. It often corresponds to English 'to/of a path'.

21.meaning: 'Straight / upright / undeviating' — describing something that runs true without bending or wandering; applied to a 'path' it means a direct, correct way that leads soundly to its goal.
21.grammar: An active participle (a describing word, 'straight/upright') from a verb meaning 'to be/become straight'. It is indefinite, and the -in ending is the genitive with 'tanwīn'. As a describing word it normally follows and agrees with the noun it modifies, matching that noun in being indefinite and in the genitive case.

1.meaning: 'And likewise / and in the same way / and thus' — a connective phrase pointing back to a manner just mentioned and saying 'in that very way…'. Built from 'and' + 'like' + 'that'.
1.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'; the prefix ka- means 'like/as'; 'dhālika' is the demonstrative 'that' (pointing to something distant or already mentioned). Because ka- acts like a preposition, the word after it stands in the genitive, though the demonstrative 'dhālika' keeps a fixed form and shows no visible case change. The whole means 'and just like that / and thus'.

2.meaning: 'We made / appointed / rendered you (plural)' — to bring about, establish, or designate a group as something. The verb 'ja‘ala' often means not just 'to make' physically but 'to appoint/turn into' a certain state or role.
2.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb. The suffix -nā marks the subject as 'we' (the doers). The further suffix -kum is the object pronoun 'you', addressed to a group (masculine or mixed). So the verb means 'we made/appointed you (all)', describing a completed act.
2.root: ج-ع-ل (j-‘-l) — making, placing, appointing, rendering into a state

3.meaning: "a community / a nation / a people" — a single group bound together as one body, typically by shared faith, way of life, or leadership; 'umma' is a collective people united around something.
3.grammar: A feminine singular noun, indefinite ('a community'). The '-an' ending (tanwīn fatḥ) is the indefinite accusative case, the form a noun takes as the object of a verb or as a predicate after certain verbs of making/becoming; the final alif is the written seat of this ending.
3.root: أ-م-م (ʾ-m-m) — to head toward, intend; a community/leadership (cf. imām)

4.meaning: 'A middle / midmost / balanced' thing — the middle point between extremes; figuratively the just, moderate, well-balanced position, and also the 'best/choicest' since the middle is the most protected and esteemed.
4.grammar: A noun/describing word, indefinite. The -an ending (the accusative with 'tanwīn') marks it as indefinite ('a middle…') and places it in the accusative — the case used for direct objects, or for a word describing the object, or for adverbial expressions. (The doubled w at the start reflects merging with a preceding 'wa'.)
4.root: و-س-ط (w-s-ṭ) — middle, center, moderation, the choicest part

5.meaning: 'So that you (plural) may be / become' — expressing purpose ('in order that you be…'). Combines the purpose particle 'so that' with the verb 'to be' addressed to a group.
5.grammar: The prefix li- ('so that, in order to') introduces a purpose and puts the following verb in the subjunctive. The verb is 'to be', second person plural ('you all'): the ta- prefix marks 'you', and the plural ending appears as -ū (with a silent written alif). Because of li-, the usual plural ending -ūna drops its final -na, giving -ū, which signals purpose/intent rather than a plain fact.
5.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, becoming, coming to exist

6.meaning: Witnesses — those present who observe and can testify to what they saw; can also carry the sense of those who bear witness. Plural.
6.grammar: A broken plural on the fuʿalāʾ (فُعَلَاء) pattern, which is a diptote: it takes the -a ending for BOTH the accusative and the genitive and never takes tanwīn (the final 'n'). Because of this, the -a alone does not tell you the case — the word could be a direct object (accusative) or governed by a preposition ('of/among', genitive). Only when made definite or put into construct would it take the ordinary -i in the genitive.
6.root: ش-ه-د (sh-h-d) — to witness, observe, testify, be present

7.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
7.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
7.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

8.meaning: Humankind, people, mankind — the collective of human beings.
8.grammar: A collective noun ('people, mankind') carrying the definite article al- ('the'); the 'l' of the article assimilates into the following 'n', doubling it (al-nās → an-nās). The genitive ending -i marks the word as governed by a preposition or as the second term of a possessive.
8.root: ء-ن-س (ʾ-n-s) — humankind, sociability, familiarity; the word for 'people' is most commonly traced to this root (related to insān, 'human being')

9.meaning: 'And (so that) he/it may be / become' — the connector 'and' joined to the verb 'to be' for a single male/thing, typically continuing a statement of purpose ('…and that he be…').
9.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. The verb is 'to be', third-person masculine singular ('he/it'): the ya- prefix means 'he'. The final -a is the subjunctive ending, used when the verb depends on a purpose word like 'so that' (often carried over from an earlier li-). It marks intended/anticipated being rather than an accomplished fact.
9.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, becoming, coming to exist

10.meaning: 'The Messenger' — one sent with a message; in religious usage, a prophet commissioned by Allah to deliver revelation to people.
10.grammar: 'al-' is the definite article 'the' (its 'l' assimilates into the following r, doubling it). 'rasūl' is a noun meaning 'one who is sent, an envoy/messenger'. The final -u is the nominative ending, the case typically marking the subject of a sentence or a word simply being named.

11.meaning: 'Upon you (all)' — the preposition 'upon/on/over' joined to the plural 'you,' indicating something resting on or directed at a group.
11.grammar: The preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon/on/over') in its joined form 'ʿalay-' plus the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you all,' masculine plural). It marks the group as the recipients or target of whatever is laid 'upon' them.

12.meaning: 'A witness' — one who sees and attests, who can give evidence; also carries the sense of one who is present and observant, and at times 'a martyr' (one who bears witness with their life).
12.grammar: An intensive describing-noun (pattern fa‘īl) meaning 'a witness, one who fully attests', indefinite. The -an ending (the accusative with 'tanwīn') marks it as indefinite and in the accusative — the case used for a direct object, or for a word that describes the state or role in which someone stands.

13.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
13.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

14.meaning: We made, rendered, set up, or appointed. A completed act of making or designating, done by a group or by a majestic 'We.'
14.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb with the attached subject ending -nā, meaning 'we' did the action. 'Jaʿala' carries senses from 'to make/create' to 'to render X into Y' or 'to appoint.'
14.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, render, appoint, place

15.meaning: 'The prayer-direction' — the qibla, the fixed direction faced in ritual prayer, here marked as definite ('the').
15.grammar: 'al-' is the definite article 'the'. 'qibla' is a feminine noun meaning the direction one turns to face in prayer. The final -a (on the tied tā’) is the accusative ending, the case used chiefly when the noun is the direct object of a verb ('the qibla' as the thing acted upon).
15.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — facing, turning toward, what is in front

16.meaning: A feminine singular relative pronoun: 'the one which / that which / who' (referring to a single feminine thing). It introduces a descriptive clause that tells us more about a preceding feminine noun.
16.grammar: A relative pronoun, feminine singular, fixed in form (it does not change for case). It links a feminine noun to a following clause describing it, the equivalent of English 'which,' 'that,' or 'who.'

17.meaning: 'You (single male) were / used to be' — the past tense of 'to be', describing a past state, and often an ongoing or habitual condition in the past ('you used to…').
17.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) form of the verb 'to be'. The suffix -ta marks the subject as 'you', a single male. It states a condition that held in the past; paired with a following present-tense verb it often gives the sense 'you used to / you would (habitually)'.
17.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, becoming, coming to exist

18.meaning: 'On it / upon it / over it' — the preposition 'alā ('on, upon') joined to the pronoun 'it/her', referring to a single feminine or grammatically feminine thing.
18.grammar: 'ʿalā' is a preposition meaning 'on/upon/over'; its ending becomes -ay when a pronoun is attached. The suffix -hā is the object pronoun for a single feminine (or feminine-gender) thing. A word governed by a preposition is in the genitive, though attached pronouns like -hā show no visible change.

19.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
19.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

20.meaning: 'So that We may know / make known' — expressing purpose joined to the verb 'to know'. The sense covers coming to know by observing, and by extension bringing knowledge to light / distinguishing one thing from another.
20.grammar: The prefix li- ('so that, in order to') introduces purpose and puts the verb in the subjunctive. The verb is 'to know', first person plural: the na- prefix means 'we'. The final -a is the subjunctive ending, signaling an intended or sought-after result ('in order that we know') rather than a simple statement of fact.

21.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
21.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

22.meaning: He/it follows, goes after, comes behind, or pursues; in religious usage it carries the sense of taking someone as a guide and obeying them, walking in their footsteps.
22.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular ('he' or 'it'). The ya- prefix marks the 'he/it' doer; the final -u ending marks the indicative mood, the plain factual 'does/is doing' form (as opposed to forms ending in -a or with no vowel that signal command or dependence on another particle). This is Form VIII (iftaʿala), which adds a sense of personally undertaking or adopting the action for oneself.

23.meaning: The messenger, envoy, or emissary: one who is sent with a message; in the Qur'an typically a prophet sent by Allah bearing revelation to a people.
23.grammar: A noun on the form faʿūl (an intensive/agent pattern, 'one sent'), prefixed with al- ('the'). The final -a ending is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb ('… the messenger') or the subject of certain particles. The 'l' of al- assimilates into the following 'r' (a 'sun letter'), pronounced ar-rasūl.

24.meaning: A compound meaning 'than one who / than whoever' — combining the preposition of comparison 'than' with the relative pronoun 'who', used to compare a person against others.
24.grammar: The preposition 'min' (here 'than', used after elatives) followed by the indeclinable relative 'man' ('who'). The final nūn of 'min' undergoes regressive assimilation into the following mīm of 'man', producing a doubled mīm; the resulting shadda sits on the mīm of 'man'. Both words are indeclinable particles and take no case ending.

25.meaning: He/it turns back, turns around, reverses course, or returns; can imply spinning round on oneself, being overturned, or reverting to a former state.
25.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular ('he' or 'it'). The ya- prefix marks the 'he/it' doer; the final -u ending is the indicative mood, the plain factual 'does/is doing' form. This is Form VII (infaʿala), which carries a passive or reflexive sense — the subject undergoes the turning or turns of itself.

26.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
26.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

27.meaning: His two heels; the back parts of the feet. The phrase 'to turn on one's heels' idiomatically means to turn back, retreat, or abandon a path one had set out on.
27.grammar: A dual noun ('two heels') with the attached pronoun -hi ('his/its'). The -ay- ending is the dual form used in the accusative/genitive (it would be -ā in the nominative), marking exactly two of something. The pronoun ending -hi (rather than -hu) takes its 'i' vowel to harmonize with the preceding 'y' sound.
27.root: ع-ق-ب (ʿ-q-b) — heel, that which comes behind/after

28.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
28.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

29.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'she was / it was / it became' — from the core verb of being, linking a subject to a description or state, often setting it in past or established time.
29.grammar: A completed (past-tense) verb of being. The ending -at marks a third-person feminine-singular subject, 'she' or 'it (feminine)', so it reads 'she/it was'. As a being-verb it normally introduces a description of that subject.
29.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

30.meaning: Truly something great, weighty, momentous, or hard to bear; a thing of large magnitude — and by extension a heavy burden or severe trial.
30.grammar: An adjective/noun on the form faʿīl ('great, big'), feminine (the -a/tā' marbūṭa), carrying the emphatic prefix la- ('truly/certainly'). The ending -tan (written as tanwīn on the tā') is the accusative case combined with indefiniteness ('a great [thing]'), the form typically used for a predicate after certain emphatic constructions or as a direct object.
30.root: ك-ب-ر (k-b-r) — greatness, largeness, weightiness

31.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
31.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.
31.root: — (particle)

32.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
32.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
32.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

33.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
33.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

34.meaning: He guided, led aright, showed the way; to direct someone toward a goal or onto the right path. Of Allah, it denotes granting guidance to truth and faith.

parts.en: he (past-tense ending, with weak final letter)

34.grammar: A past/perfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular ('he guided'). This is a 'defective' verb whose third root letter is a weak letter, so the final syllable appears as a long -ā (written with alif maqṣūra ى). The past tense states a completed action. With no attached subject pronoun, it simply means 'he/it guided'.
34.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — guidance, showing the right way

35.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
35.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

36.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
36.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.
36.root: — (relative pronoun / particle)

37.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

37.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

38.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
38.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
38.root: — (proper divine name)

39.meaning: So that He/it may cause to be lost, let go to waste, squander, or render fruitless; to allow something to perish or come to nothing.
39.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular, in Form IV (afʿala), which makes the action causative — 'to cause to be lost.' The yu- prefix (with 'u') marks both the 'he/it' doer and this causative pattern. The prefixed li- ('so that') puts the verb in the subjunctive mood, shown by the final -a ending, which expresses purpose or intended result ('in order that he may …').

40.meaning: Your faith, belief, trust; the inward assent and security of believing — specifically faith in Allah and what He has revealed. Addressed to a group ('your', plural).
40.grammar: A verbal noun (maṣdar of Form IV, 'believing') with the attached pronoun -kum ('your', for a group, grammatically masculine plural). The -a ending before the pronoun is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as a direct object ('… your faith'). The pronoun -kum addresses two or more people.
40.root: أ-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — security, trust, safety; whence belief

41.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
41.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

42.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
42.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.
42.root: — (proper name)

43.meaning: With/to mankind, the people, humankind; human beings collectively. The prefix conveys 'with', 'toward', or 'in respect of' people.
43.grammar: The noun 'the people/mankind' (al-nās) governed by the preposition bi- ('with/to/toward'). The final -i ending is the genitive case, which is regularly required after a preposition. The 'l' of al- assimilates into the following 'n' (a 'sun letter'), pronounced an-nās.
43.root: ن-و-س / أ-ن-س (n-w-s / ʾ-n-s) — people, humankind; sociability

44.meaning: Truly most kind, compassionate, tender; one who shows raʾfa — gentle pity and clemency, an especially soft and caring form of mercy. Used as a divine attribute.
44.grammar: An intensive adjective on the form faʿūl ('full of kindness'), with the emphatic prefix la- ('truly'). The ending -un (tanwīn) is the nominative case combined with indefiniteness, the form typically used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate describing it ('[He] is truly most kind').

45.meaning: Most merciful, ever-merciful; one whose mercy is constant and abundant. As a divine attribute it denotes Allah's enduring, all-embracing compassion toward His creation.
45.grammar: An intensive adjective on the form faʿīl ('abundantly/constantly merciful'). The ending -un (tanwīn) is the nominative case with indefiniteness, the form typically used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate describing it ('[He] is most merciful').

1.meaning: A short particle placed before a verb to emphasize or affirm it. Before a past-tense verb it means 'indeed / certainly / has already (happened)'; before a present-tense verb it can mean 'sometimes / may'. It sharpens and confirms the verb that follows.
1.grammar: An indeclinable particle (its form never changes). It does not take case or tense endings; its job is to color the following verb — affirming and intensifying a past action ('has indeed done') or signaling occasional possibility with a present verb.

2.meaning: We see, perceive, behold, or observe; to take in with the eye, and by extension to know or witness. Carries a sense of attentive regard.
2.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, 1st person plural ('we'). The na- prefix marks the 'we' doer. This is a 'defective' verb with a weak third root letter, so it ends in a long -ā. In the indicative (the plain factual 'we do/are doing' sense) this ending stays as -ā.

3.meaning: A turning about, shifting, or moving to and fro; repeated turning of something this way and that — for a face, the turning of the gaze in different directions.
3.grammar: A verbal noun (maṣdar) of Form V (tafaʿʿul), a pattern that conveys repeated or intensive turning ('a turning this way and that'). The final -a ending is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb ('[We see] the turning …').

4.meaning: Your face; the front of the head — and by extension one's countenance, direction, or self. Addressed to a single male ('your').
4.grammar: The noun 'face' (wajh) with the attached pronoun -ka ('your', for one male). The -i ending before the pronoun is the genitive case, which typically links the word to a following possessor ('the … OF …') or follows a preposition; here the possessor is the attached 'your'.
4.root: و-ج-ه (w-j-h) — face, direction, that which one faces

5.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
5.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

6.meaning: The sky or heaven — the canopy overhead; the expanse above the earth, also that which is elevated or raised over something. With the definite article it means 'the sky / the heaven'.
6.grammar: A noun with the definite article al- ('the'), in the genitive marked by the -i ending. (The 'l' of al- assimilates in sound into the following 's', a 'sun letter', though it is still written.) The genitive -i ending typically appears after a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …').

7.meaning: Then We shall most certainly turn you / make you turn toward (something); to direct or appoint someone to face a particular way. Heavily emphasized as a sure promise.
7.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, 1st person plural ('we'), in Form II (faʿʿala, transitive/causative: 'to turn someone'). The nu- prefix marks the 'we' doer. It carries a double emphasis: the prefix la- ('certainly') plus the heavy ending -nna (the 'emphatic nūn'), which together turn it into a solemn promise — 'we shall most surely …'. The attached -ka is the object pronoun, 'you' (one male). The leading fa- means 'then/so'.
7.root: و-ل-ي (w-l-y) — turning toward, being near, directing

8.meaning: A qibla — the direction one faces, especially the fixed direction toward which prayer is oriented; a focal point or bearing for worship.
8.grammar: A noun on the form fiʿla, which often denotes a manner or state — here the direction in which one faces. The ending -tan (tanwīn on the tā') is the accusative case with indefiniteness ('a direction'), the form typically used for a direct object or the predicate of certain verbs.
8.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — facing, fronting, that which is before one

9.meaning: You are pleased with it / find it satisfying / approve of it; to accept something gladly and willingly. The 'it' refers to a feminine thing.

parts.en: be pleased with, approve (stem, weak final letter)

9.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, 2nd person masculine singular ('you'), with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it/her', feminine). The ta- prefix marks the 'you' doer. This is a 'defective' verb with a weak final root letter, giving the long -ā vowel before the pronoun. The plain factual ('you do') sense is intended.
9.root: ر-ض-و / ر-ض-ي (r-ḍ-w / r-ḍ-y) — contentment, good pleasure, approval

10.meaning: Turn! / direct (something) toward!; a command to make one's face or self turn in a given direction. Addressed to a single male.
10.grammar: A command (imperative) verb, addressed to one male, in Form II (faʿʿala, 'to turn something/someone'). Because the root has a weak final letter, the command form drops that final weak letter, leaving the short form 'walli' (the missing vowel is the sign of the command). The leading fa- means 'then/so'.
10.root: و-ل-ي (w-l-y) — turning toward, directing, being near

11.meaning: Your face; the front of the head — and by extension one's countenance or direction. Addressed to a single male ('your'), and here the object of an action.
11.grammar: The noun 'face' (wajh) with the attached pronoun -ka ('your', for one male). The -a ending before the pronoun is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb ('turn … your face').
11.root: و-ج-ه (w-j-h) — face, direction, that which one faces

12.meaning: Toward, in the direction of, the side of; the part or region facing something. It indicates the bearing or course toward a thing.
12.grammar: A noun meaning 'direction/side', used adverbially to mean 'toward'. The -a ending is the accusative case; in this adverb-like use it expresses 'in the direction of' and is typically followed by a noun in the genitive showing what is faced ('toward … OF …').
12.root: ش-ط-ر (sh-ṭ-r) — a part, half, side, direction

13.meaning: The place of prostration; a mosque — literally the spot where one bows down (sajda) in worship. With the following 'sacred', it names the Sacred Mosque.
13.grammar: A noun of place on the form mafʿil ('the place where prostration is done'), prefixed with al- ('the'). The final -i ending is the genitive case, which typically marks the word as following a preposition or as the possessed/qualified noun after another ('… OF the mosque').
13.root: س-ج-د (s-j-d) — prostration, bowing down in worship

14.meaning: The sacred, inviolable, forbidden; that which is set apart and protected, whose violation is prohibited out of reverence. Describes something hallowed.
14.grammar: An adjective on the form faʿāl ('sacred/forbidden'), prefixed with al- ('the'). The final -i ending is the genitive case; an adjective takes the same case as the noun it describes, so this -i matches a preceding genitive noun ('the … sacred').
14.root: ح-ر-م (ḥ-r-m) — being forbidden, sacred, set apart, inviolable

15.meaning: And wherever, and in whatever place; introduces a general 'in any place that …'. The 'and' links it to what precedes.
15.grammar: A connective particle wa ('and') joined to the adverb ḥaythu ('where/wherever'), which points to place ('in the place where …'). Ḥaythu is invariable: it always ends in -u and never changes for case. It commonly introduces a following clause stating a condition of place.

16.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
16.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

17.meaning: A past-tense verb of 'being' addressed to a group: 'you (all) were', 'you (all) used to be'. From kāna, the core verb 'to be'. With a following predicate it often means 'you were (in a state of) …' or 'you used to …'.
17.grammar: This is a past-tense verb. The '-tum' suffix is the attached subject marker for a masculine plural 'you all'. Since the doer is built into the suffix, the verb stands in its base past form ('you all were').
17.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

18.meaning: So turn! / direct (yourselves/it) toward!; a command addressed to a group of people to make their faces or selves turn in a given direction.
18.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a group (masculine plural), in Form II (faʿʿala, 'to turn something'). The ending -ū is the plural 'you all' marker (written with a silent alif after the wāw). The leading fa- means 'then/so'.
18.root: و-ل-ي (w-l-y) — turning toward, directing, being near

19.meaning: Faces belonging to a plural 'you' — the front of the heads, the part one turns and directs toward something; can also figuratively mean attention, orientation, or one's whole self as turned somewhere.
19.grammar: A plural noun (singular wajh, 'face') carrying the attached pronoun -kum, 'your' for a group. The -a ending before the pronoun is accusative, the case typically used for the direct object of a verb (the thing being acted upon, e.g. what is turned or directed).
19.root: و-ج-ه (w-j-h) — face, direction, to turn toward

20.meaning: Toward the direction or side of something — the bearing or part of a thing one orients toward; 'his/its direction' when combined with the pronoun.
20.grammar: A noun meaning 'direction toward' with the attached pronoun -hu, 'his/its'. The -a ending is accusative; for a word like this it functions adverbially, marking the goal or direction of motion ('toward …'). The lengthened -hū reflects the pronoun following a vowel.

21.meaning: 'And indeed' / 'and truly' — the joining word 'wa' ('and') attached to the emphatic particle 'inna', which introduces a statement and strongly affirms it, adding certainty like 'surely' or 'indeed'.
21.grammar: A connective 'wa' ('and') plus 'inna', a particle of emphasis that opens a nominal sentence. 'Inna' puts its following noun (the subject) into the accusative case while strongly affirming the truth of the statement.

22.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
22.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

23.meaning: They were given / granted — the passive past tense of the verb 'to give/bring' (form IV of ʾ-t-y), where a plural group receives something without the giver being named.
23.grammar: Passive past tense. The internal vowelling (u-...-u) marks it as passive — the subject receives the action rather than doing it. The '-ū' ending means 'they', giving 'they were given' (the giver left unmentioned).
23.root: ا-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (form IV) to bring or give

24.meaning: The Book, the Scripture — a written revelation; the term for a divinely revealed text.
24.grammar: A definite noun ('the Book') with attached 'al-' ('the'). The final '-a' ending is the accusative case, typically marking the word as the direct object of a verb.
24.root: ك-ت-ب (k-t-b) — to write; a writing, book

25.meaning: They most certainly know — to have firm, certain knowledge of something, emphatically affirmed of a group.
25.grammar: A present-tense verb 'to know'. The opening la- is an emphasis particle ('surely, indeed'). The -ūna ending marks a masculine-plural subject ('they') in the ongoing/indicative form. Together the prefix ya- and suffix -ūna give the 'they' meaning.

26.meaning: 'That it (is) …' The emphasizing particle 'anna' ('that … indeed') with an attached 'it/he,' used to introduce a firmly asserted statement and tie it to a preceding verb such as 'know' or 'say.'
26.grammar: The particle anna ('that, indeed') with the attached pronoun -hu ('it/he,' masculine singular) as its subject. Anna introduces a strongly affirmed noun-clause ('that it is indeed…') and places its subject in the accusative; it commonly follows verbs of knowing, saying, or believing.

27.meaning: 'The truth / the reality; what is right, real, and rightfully due.' A weighty noun meaning that which is firmly true and real, as opposed to falsehood; it also carries the senses of a rightful claim, a duty owed, and justice. With the article it denotes 'the Truth' in a definite, absolute sense.
27.grammar: A definite noun: the prefix al- ('the') plus the stem. The final -u ending is the nominative case, typically used for the subject of a sentence or for a word identifying what something is (as in 'X is the truth').
27.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, reality, rightness; that which is established and rightfully due

28.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
28.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

29.meaning: 'Their Lord / their Sustainer.' The noun 'rabb' — a master who owns, nurtures, sustains, and brings to maturity all under His care — joined to 'their.' It conveys far more than 'lord': the one who creates, provides for, and governs His servants.
29.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive pronoun -him ('their,' masculine plural). The -i ending is the genitive case, which typically appears after a preposition or links the word to another in an 'of / belonging to' relationship; here it pairs with the attached 'their.'
29.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master; lordship, ownership, care

30.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
30.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.
30.root: — (relative pronoun / particle)

31.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
31.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
31.root: — (proper divine name)

32.meaning: 'With/being heedless' — the preposition/particle 'bi' attached to 'ghāfil', one who is unaware, inattentive, or neglectful, failing to take notice.
32.grammar: The particle 'bi-' governs the following word into the genitive case. 'Ghāfil' is an active participle ('one who is heedless'). The '-in' (tanwīn) marks it indefinite and genitive; the 'bi-' here commonly adds emphasis within a negation ('not at all heedless').

33.meaning: 'About what' / 'of that which' — the preposition 'ʿan' ('about, concerning, away from') merged with 'mā' ('what, that which').
33.grammar: A fusion of the preposition 'ʿan' ('about, concerning') with the relative/interrogative 'mā' ('what'); the 'n' of 'ʿan' assimilates into 'mā' to give 'ʿammā'. It introduces the thing being spoken about.

34.meaning: 'They do / they work, they act' — a present-tense verb of doing and working, covering deeds and actions carried out by a group.
34.grammar: Present/imperfect verb. The ya-…-ūna frame marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (do).' The -ūna ending also marks the indicative mood, the plain statement form, as opposed to command or negated-future forms.
34.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, work, act; deeds

1.meaning: A combination meaning 'and surely if' — introducing a hypothetical condition ('if…') sworn by an implied oath, so that the outcome is strongly anticipated; roughly 'and by all means, if…'.
1.grammar: A cluster of particles, not a noun or verb, so it takes no case ending: wa- 'and', the lam al-qasam (the 'lam of swearing') that marks the following condition as sworn by an implied oath, and in 'if' which sets up the condition. This oath-lam construction correlates with a later response clause that itself carries emphasis (an emphatic lam plus the 'nūn of emphasis' on its verb), giving the sense 'and [I swear] if … they would surely …'.

2.meaning: You brought / you came to (someone with something) — a past act of bringing, giving, or coming, addressed to a single male 'you'.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb. The suffix -ta marks the doer as 'you', a single male. The verb can mean both 'to come' and, with an object, 'to bring/give'.

3.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
3.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

4.meaning: They were given / granted — the passive past tense of the verb 'to give/bring' (form IV of ʾ-t-y), where a plural group receives something without the giver being named.
4.grammar: Passive past tense. The internal vowelling (u-...-u) marks it as passive — the subject receives the action rather than doing it. The '-ū' ending means 'they', giving 'they were given' (the giver left unmentioned).
4.root: ا-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (form IV) to bring or give

5.meaning: The Book, the Scripture — a written revelation; the term for a divinely revealed text.
5.grammar: A definite noun ('the Book') with attached 'al-' ('the'). The final '-a' ending is the accusative case, typically marking the word as the direct object of a verb.
5.root: ك-ت-ب (k-t-b) — to write; a writing, book

6.meaning: 'Of every / with all' — the preposition 'bi' ('with / in / by') joined to the word 'every / each / all', expressing comprehensiveness applied to whatever noun follows.
6.grammar: A preposition plus a noun. The prefix bi- ('with / in / by') always places the following noun in the genitive ('of') state. The final -i on 'kull' is that genitive ending, signalling the word is governed by the preposition. 'Kull' denotes totality — 'every (single)' or 'all'.

7.meaning: A sign, token, or miraculous indication; also a discrete verse of revelation — a marker that points beyond itself to a deeper truth or to its Author.
