7.grammar: A singular feminine noun, indefinite ('a sign'). The final -in (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite and in the genitive case — the doubled-n 'nunation' shows there is no 'the', and the -i base vowel indicates the genitive (used after prepositions or in a possessive link).

8.meaning: A short, highly versatile particle 'mā.' It can mean 'what' or 'that which,' can negate ('not'), and can serve as an intensifier attached to another word. Its precise force depends on what it accompanies, but its core is to point to a thing or to add emphasis.
8.grammar: A multifunctional particle. It does not take case endings. Depending on usage it can be a relative ('that which'), an interrogative ('what?'), a negator ('not'), or — when joined to another particle — an emphasizer. It is uninflected and indeclinable.

9.meaning: They followed / would follow — to come after and go along with someone, to adopt their way or accept their lead, said of a group.
9.grammar: A past-tense verb 'to follow'. The suffix -ū marks a masculine-plural subject ('they'); the silent alif written after it (-ū + ا) is a spelling convention for this plural ending and is not pronounced.

10.meaning: The qibla belonging to a single male 'you' — the fixed point or direction one faces in prayer; more broadly, an appointed direction toward which one turns.
10.grammar: A noun (the direction faced in prayer) with the attached pronoun -ka, 'your' for one male. The -a ending before the pronoun is accusative, the case for a direct object (the thing being acted upon, e.g. followed or faced). The feminine ending -ah becomes -at- when a pronoun is attached.

11.meaning: And what / and that which. Combines the connective 'and' with mā, a word that can mean 'what / that which', or function as a negating particle ('not'), depending on usage.
11.grammar: The connective wa- ('and') joined to mā, an indeclinable particle (it never changes its ending). It serves either as a relative/interrogative 'what' or as a negation 'not', so its sense is fixed by context rather than by a case ending.

12.meaning: 'You' — the standalone, independent pronoun for addressing a single male person directly.
12.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, second-person masculine singular. Unlike attached pronoun suffixes, it stands alone and is typically used to identify or emphasize the subject ('you [yourself]').

13.meaning: A follower — one who comes after and goes along with another's way or lead.
13.grammar: An active participle, 'one who follows', preceded by the particle bi- ('with/by'). The ending -in is genitive (the case after a preposition) and its final -n (tanwīn) marks the word as indefinite ('a follower'). The participle pattern fāʿil names the doer of the action; here it stands alone, with no attached object.

14.meaning: The qibla belonging to a group — the direction they face in prayer; the appointed direction toward which they turn.
14.grammar: The noun for the prayer-direction with the attached pronoun -hum, 'their' for a group of males. The -a ending before the pronoun is accusative, the case for a direct object (the thing acted upon). The feminine ending -ah becomes -at- before a pronoun.

15.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
15.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

16.meaning: 'Some of them' / 'a part of them' — a noun meaning 'a portion, part, or some' joined to an attached pronoun 'them'. Often paired with itself to express 'one another / each other'.
16.grammar: A noun 'part/some' in the nominative case (the -u ending), which typically marks it as the subject or doer. The suffix -hum is a genitive (possessive) pronoun meaning 'their' (masculine plural); attached to a noun this way it sits in the possessor slot, giving 'some of them'.
16.root: ب-ع-ض (b-ʿ-ḍ) — a part, portion, or some of a whole

17.meaning: A follower — one who comes after and goes along with another's way or lead.
17.grammar: An active participle, 'one who follows', preceded by the particle bi- ('with/by'). The ending -in is genitive (the case after a preposition) and its final -n (tanwīn) marks the word as indefinite ('a follower'). The participle pattern fāʿil names the doer of the action; here it stands alone, with no attached object.

18.meaning: Qibla — the direction one faces in prayer; an appointed bearing toward which worshippers turn.
18.grammar: A noun in its plain form (no attached pronoun). The final -a is accusative, the case marking a direct object (the thing acted upon) or otherwise governed word. The written tāʾ marbūṭa (ة) sounds as -t- here because a vowel follows.
18.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to face, front, direction

19.meaning: 'Some (others)' / 'a part' — the same noun for 'a portion or some,' here left indefinite, often functioning as the counterpart in the 'one another' construction.
19.grammar: A noun 'part/some' in the genitive case with indefinite marking (the -in ending, called tanwīn). The genitive typically follows a preposition or links it to a preceding noun ('… of …'); the doubled -n sound marks it as indefinite ('a part / some').
19.root: ب-ع-ض (b-ʿ-ḍ) — a part, portion, or some of a whole

20.meaning: And surely if — a combination meaning 'and if', strengthened by an emphatic particle so it reads 'and indeed, should it be that …'.
20.grammar: A cluster of particles: wa- ('and'), an emphatic la- ('surely, indeed') that strengthens what follows, and in ('if') introducing a condition. The final short -i is a helping vowel added to ease pronunciation before the next word. Together they set up an emphatic conditional, 'and surely if …'.

21.meaning: You followed / you took as a guide — completed action of going after and adhering to someone's way.
21.grammar: A past-tense verb of Form VIII (reflexive 'to follow after, take as a guide'); the initial helping 'i' and doubled 'tt' belong to this pattern. The suffix -ta marks the doer as second-person masculine singular ('you', one male). It states a completed act of following.
21.root: ت-ب-ع (t-b-ʿ) — to follow, come after, pursue

22.meaning: Their desires, inclinations, cravings; the pulls of personal whim and passion — what one leans toward apart from guidance, here belonging to 'them'.
22.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural of hawā ('desire, inclination, whim'). The case-vowel -a (accusative) typically marks the object of a verb. The attached pronoun -hum means 'their' (a group of males or mixed). Altogether: 'their desires/whims'.
22.root: ه-و-ي (h-w-y) — inclination, desire, whim; to incline toward, to fall

23.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
23.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

24.meaning: A noun/adverb meaning 'after' — the time or position following something; 'afterward', 'following'.
24.grammar: An adverb of time functioning as a noun, here in the genitive case marked by the final -i. The genitive ending typically appears after a preposition or as the second term of a construct ('after THE …'), linking 'after' to a following noun to specify what it comes after.
24.root: ب-ع-د (b-ʿ-d) — to be after, to follow, distance in place or time

25.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
25.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

26.meaning: It came to you / reached you — a completed arrival of something reaching a person (one male).
26.grammar: A past-tense verb, 'he/it came', whose final -a vowel is the inherent third-person masculine singular inflection built into the verb form itself (not a separate piece). The attached pronoun -ka ('you', one male) is the object reached — 'it came to you'.

27.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
27.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

28.meaning: The knowledge; sure and certain knowing, established information and understanding (with the definite article).
28.grammar: A definite verbal noun: al- means 'the'. The final -i is the genitive ending, which typically follows a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun in an 'of' relationship. It denotes knowledge as a settled, certain thing.

29.meaning: 'Indeed you' — an emphasis particle meaning 'truly / indeed' joined to the pronoun 'you', used to open a statement with certainty and stress about the person addressed.
29.grammar: The emphasis particle 'inna' ('indeed, truly') with an attached pronoun. 'inna' adds strong assertion to a sentence and grammatically governs the following noun/pronoun in the accusative. The suffix '-ka' means 'you' (masculine singular) as its subject.

30.meaning: In that case / then — a response particle signaling that what follows is the consequence of a just-stated condition or supposition ('if so, then…').
30.grammar: A response/consequence particle, not a noun or verb. The -an ending is a fixed part of the word (written with a final alif), not a live grammatical case. It introduces the result side of a hypothetical ('then you would…').

31.meaning: A combination meaning 'surely among / truly from' — an emphatic affirmation ('indeed') joined to the word 'from/among', marking belonging to a group or origin from a source.
31.grammar: Two particles together: an emphatic la- ('surely') and the preposition min ('from/among'). Particles take no case ending. Min is normally written 'min' but appears as 'mina' when the next word begins with 'al-' ('the'), to ease pronunciation.

32.meaning: The wrongdoers — those who do wrong or injustice; literally those who put things out of their rightful place, transgressing limits and harming themselves or others. The root sense is darkness.
32.grammar: 'al-' is 'the' (its 'l' assimilates into the 'ẓ', doubling it). The stem is an active participle ('one who wrongs') made plural for masculine people. The -īna ending is the object/genitive form of the sound masculine plural, marking the word as an object of a verb or governed by a preposition.

1.meaning: Those who / the ones who — a plural relative pronoun (masculine) introducing a description: 'those (people) who …'.
1.grammar: A relative pronoun, masculine plural, meaning 'those who / the ones who'. It refers back to a group already in view and introduces a clause describing them. Its form is fixed and does not change for case.

2.meaning: We gave them / We granted them — a completed act of bestowing or conferring something upon a group, done by 'We'.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb of Form IV ('to give, bestow, grant'). The suffix -nā marks the doer as 'we'. The attached pronoun -hum(u) is the object, 'them' (a group); its vowel is lengthened to -humu to ease pronunciation before the next word. Altogether: 'We gave them'.
2.root: ء-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (Form IV) to give, bring, bestow

3.meaning: The Book, the Scripture — a written revelation; the term for a divinely revealed text.
3.grammar: A definite noun ('the Book') with attached 'al-' ('the'). The final '-a' ending is the accusative case, typically marking the word as the direct object of a verb.
3.root: ك-ت-ب (k-t-b) — to write; a writing, book

4.meaning: They recognize him/it — to know something by its marks, to identify or acknowledge a thing already familiar, said of a group toward a single object.
4.grammar: A present-tense verb 'to recognize/know', with subject and object built in: the prefix ya- with suffix -ūna gives a masculine-plural 'they', and the attached -hu is the object 'him/it'. The -ūna ending marks the ongoing/indicative form; it is the lengthened -hū because a vowel precedes.
4.root: ع-ر-ف (ʿ-r-f) — to know, recognize, be acquainted

5.meaning: 'Just as / in the same way that' — a phrase of comparison joining 'like / as' to 'what', meaning 'like that which...' or 'in the manner that...'.
5.grammar: The comparison particle ka- ('like / as') joined to mā ('what / that which'). Together they introduce a likeness or manner — 'just as...', 'in the same way that...' — comparing one thing or action to another.

6.meaning: They recognize / know — to identify something by its signs, to acknowledge what is already familiar, said of a group.
6.grammar: A present-tense verb 'to recognize'. The prefix ya- together with the suffix -ūna marks a masculine-plural subject ('they') in the ongoing/indicative form.
6.root: ع-ر-ف (ʿ-r-f) — to know, recognize, be acquainted

7.meaning: Sons belonging to a group — male children or, more broadly, offspring and descendants.
7.grammar: A plural noun (singular ibn, 'son') with the attached pronoun -hum, 'their'. The -a ending before the pronoun is accusative, the case for a direct object (the thing acted upon, e.g. what is known or recognized).

8.meaning: 'And indeed' / 'and truly' — the joining word 'wa' ('and') attached to the emphatic particle 'inna', which introduces a statement and strongly affirms it, adding certainty like 'surely' or 'indeed'.
8.grammar: A connective 'wa' ('and') plus 'inna', a particle of emphasis that opens a nominal sentence. 'Inna' puts its following noun (the subject) into the accusative case while strongly affirming the truth of the statement.

9.meaning: A group, faction, party, or portion of people — a section split off from a larger body.
9.grammar: A singular indefinite noun. The -an (tanwīn fatḥ) ending marks the accusative case with indefiniteness, typically signalling the direct object of a verb ('a group'), or an adverbial sense.

10.meaning: 'Among them / from them / some of them' — the preposition 'min' ('from, of, among') joined to the attached pronoun 'hum' ('them').
10.grammar: The preposition 'min' ('from / of / among') with the attached pronoun 'hum' ('them'), referring to a masculine plural group. Together they often express 'part of them' or 'some among them'.

11.meaning: They most certainly conceal / hide — to keep something secret, to suppress or withhold what is known, emphatically affirmed of a group.
11.grammar: A present-tense verb 'to conceal'. The opening la- is an emphasis particle ('surely'). The prefix ya- with the suffix -ūna marks a masculine-plural subject ('they') in the ongoing/indicative form.
11.root: ك-ت-م (k-t-m) — to conceal, suppress, keep secret

12.meaning: The truth — that which is real, right, and established; reality, the just due, the genuine as opposed to the false.
12.grammar: A definite noun with 'the'. The -a ending is the accusative, typically marking the noun as the direct object of a verb ('the truth').
12.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, right, that which is established and real

13.meaning: 'While they / and they' — the word 'wa' (here 'while' or 'and') joined to the standalone pronoun 'hum' ('they'), referring to a masculine plural group.
13.grammar: A connective 'wa' — often circumstantial 'while' — plus the independent subject pronoun 'hum' ('they'), used for a masculine plural group. As an independent pronoun it usually stands as the subject of a following statement.

14.meaning: They know, have knowledge, are aware. Expresses ongoing or habitual knowing held by a group of males (or a mixed group).
14.grammar: A present/future-tense verb. The ya- prefix with the -ūna ending means 'they' (a group of males). The full -ūna ending (rather than a shortened -ū) marks the indicative mood, signaling a plain statement of fact: 'they (do) know.'

1.meaning: The truth — that which is real, established, and right; what genuinely corresponds to reality, and so also what is rightfully due. A weighty term spanning truth, reality, and rightful claim.
1.grammar: A noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -u ending is nominative, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or for a word standing on its own as the topic. The doubled q (shadda) is part of the root.
1.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, reality, right, to be established

2.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
2.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

3.meaning: The Lord belonging to a single male 'you' — Rabb is the Master, Owner, and Sustainer who creates, nurtures, and brings to maturity; here 'your Lord'.
3.grammar: The noun rabb (Lord, Sustainer) with the attached pronoun -ka, 'your' for one male. The -i ending before the pronoun is genitive, the case that typically links a word to a following possessor or follows a preposition (here showing the possession 'of you'). The doubled b (shadda) belongs to the root.

4.meaning: A two-part word: the connective particle 'fa-' meaning 'so', 'then', or 'therefore' (drawing a consequence from what precedes), joined to 'lā', the particle of negation/prohibition. Together they convey 'so do not …' or 'so there is no …'.
4.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that links a clause to what came before and often signals a result or consequence. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a present-tense verb it commonly forms a prohibition ('do not …') or a simple negation ('not'). It carries no ending of its own.

5.meaning: You must certainly be / never be — an emphatic form of the verb 'to be', stressing that one truly will (or, with a negative, truly must not) be in a certain state.
5.grammar: A present-tense form of the verb 'to be', addressed to 'you' (the prefix ta-). The heavy ending -anna (nūn of emphasis) gives a strong, insistent force — 'you most certainly are/must be' — and is the standard way Arabic stresses a command or warning attached to a verb.
5.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to come into being

6.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
6.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

7.meaning: The doubters — those who dispute or waver in uncertainty, entertaining suspicion rather than firm conviction.
7.grammar: An active participle, 'those who doubt', with the definite article al-. The ending -īna marks a masculine plural in the accusative/genitive (the form used for objects or after a preposition). The participle comes from a Form VIII verb (iftaʿala, here im-ta-rā), a pattern that carries a reflexive/middle sense — the doubt is something one falls into or is caught up in oneself.

1.meaning: A combination meaning 'and for each / and to everyone' — joining 'and' with the preposition 'for/to' and the word 'all, each one', indicating that something belongs to or applies to every one.
1.grammar: A cluster: wa- 'and', the preposition li- 'for/to', and the noun kull 'all/each'. The ending -in is genitive (the case required after the preposition li-), and its final -n (tanwīn) marks the word as indefinite ('every one, each'). The doubled l (shadda) is part of kull.

2.meaning: A direction one faces — the goal or bearing toward which a person turns; an orientation or aim.
2.grammar: A noun built on the pattern for a direction or way faced. The ending -un is nominative (the case for a sentence's subject or a thing being newly mentioned), and its final -n (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('a direction'). The written tāʾ marbūṭa (ة) sounds as -t- when a vowel follows.
2.root: و-ج-ه (w-j-h) — face, direction, to turn toward

3.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
3.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

4.meaning: One who turns toward it, or the one who makes/sets it turn toward something — an agent of directing or facing, joined to the object 'it'.
4.grammar: An active participle from an intensive/causative (Form II) verb (to turn or direct toward), naming the doer ('one who turns toward'). It keeps the governing power of a verb, so the attached pronoun -hā ('it', for a feminine word) is its direct object (accusative), not a possessive link — 'one who turns it toward'.
4.root: و-ل-ي (w-l-y) — to turn, be near, take charge, direct toward

5.meaning: So race ahead / strive to get ahead — an exhortation to a group to hasten and outstrip others in doing something, prefaced by 'so/then'.
5.grammar: A command (imperative) verb from a Form X pattern (istafʿala) of the root meaning 'to seek to get ahead, hasten to precede, outstrip', preceded by the connector fa- ('so/then'). The suffix -ū directs the order at a group of males ('all of you'); the silent alif written after it is a spelling convention for this plural ending and is not pronounced.
5.root: س-ب-ق (s-b-q) — to precede, outstrip, race ahead

6.meaning: The good things; that which is excellent, beneficial, and morally upright. The word denotes good deeds, blessings, and bounties — collectively the things that are good in the fullest sense, whether good works performed or good gifts received.
6.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun ('the good things'). The sound feminine plural ending -āt takes -i for both the genitive case (typically meaning 'of …' or following a preposition) and the accusative case (often the object of a verb); the article al- makes it definite. So the final -i marks it as either linked to a following word/preposition or as a direct object.

7.meaning: Where / wherever. An interrogative or conditional adverb of place: it asks 'where?' or, in a conditional sense, sets up 'wherever / in whatever place'.
7.grammar: An indeclinable adverb of place fixed on a final -a; it does not change for case. It functions either as a question word ('where?') or as a conditional particle introducing a clause ('wherever'), often pairing with a following verb in the jussive mood.

8.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
8.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

9.meaning: You (plural) are / you happen to be. A form of the 'hollow' verb kāna ('to be'), which links a subject to a state or description, or expresses simply being or existing.
9.grammar: Present/imperfect verb, 2nd person masculine plural ('you all'). The ta- prefix marks 2nd person; the -ū ending marks masculine plural. The dropping of the usual final -na (so takūnū rather than takūnūna) shows the verb is in the subjunctive or jussive mood — the form expected after conditional or subordinating particles.
9.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

10.meaning: He/it comes, or brings. From the verb 'to come'; with an object it carries the sense of bringing or producing something.
10.grammar: Present/imperfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular ('he/it'). The ya- prefix marks 3rd person masculine. This root ends weakly in a vowel, and the bare form yati (without a final -ī) shows the jussive or apocopated mood, the clipped form used after conditional particles and in answers to conditions.

11.meaning: 'For you / with you / by means of you' (addressing a group). A preposition fused with a plural 'you', expressing attachment, instrument, or accompaniment depending on context.
11.grammar: A preposition 'bi-' with an attached pronoun object. 'bi-' conveys 'with / by means of / through'; the suffix means a plural 'you'. The final '-u' (instead of the usual '-um') is a connecting vowel added so the word flows smoothly into a following word beginning with a sukūn.

12.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
12.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

13.meaning: A word meaning 'all together', 'all of them', or 'the whole lot' — emphasising that no one and nothing is left out of a group.
13.grammar: A noun meaning 'all/entirety' carrying the -an ending: accusative case with tanwīn (the indefinite '-n'). This accusative form is typical of a word that comes alongside another to specify it as 'all of them, every one', describing the manner or extent.

14.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
14.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

15.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
15.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

16.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
16.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

17.meaning: 'every,' 'each,' or 'all' — a word expressing totality or completeness. It indicates the entirety of something: when joined to a singular indefinite noun it means 'every (single) one,' and when joined to a definite noun it can mean 'all of' or 'the whole of.'
17.grammar: A noun of totality. The final '-i' ending is genitive (the 'of/possession' case): it marks the word as governed by a preceding preposition or as the first term of a possessive link to a following noun, so it typically reads 'of every…' or 'every…' leading into what follows.

18.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
18.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
18.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

19.meaning: All-powerful, fully able, ever-capable — possessing complete and effective power to do whatever is willed; one whose ability never falls short.
19.grammar: An intensive adjective on the faʿīl pattern, which stresses a deep, abiding quality ('thoroughly able'). The final -un is the indefinite nominative (nunation) — the doubled-n shows no 'the', and the -u base vowel marks the nominative case, used when the word is a subject or a predicate ('… is all-powerful').

1.meaning: 'And from / and out of / and among.' A connector 'and' joined to the preposition 'from,' which marks origin, source, a starting point, or 'some of' a larger whole.
1.grammar: Two particles: the connector 'wa-' ('and') and the preposition 'min.' 'Min' indicates origin or source ('from'), a starting point, or partition ('some of'). Particles do not change their endings.

2.meaning: Wherever / in whatever place — an adverb pointing to an unspecified location, 'in the place where ...'.
2.grammar: An invariable adverb of place ('where / wherever'). Although it ends in -u, it is fixed in form and does not change for case; it is normally followed by a clause stating the situation tied to that place.

3.meaning: You went out / departed / set forth. From the verb meaning to go out, emerge, or come forth from a place.
3.grammar: Past/perfect verb, 2nd person masculine singular ('you' — one male). The suffix -ta is the subject ending for 'you (masc. sg.)' attached to a completed action. The perfect tense presents the act as done and finished.

4.meaning: Turn! / direct (something) toward!; a command to make one's face or self turn in a given direction. Addressed to a single male.
4.grammar: A command (imperative) verb, addressed to one male, in Form II (faʿʿala, 'to turn something/someone'). Because the root has a weak final letter, the command form drops that final weak letter, leaving the short form 'walli' (the missing vowel is the sign of the command). The leading fa- means 'then/so'.
4.root: و-ل-ي (w-l-y) — turning toward, directing, being near

5.meaning: Your face; the front of the head — and by extension one's countenance or direction. Addressed to a single male ('your'), and here the object of an action.
5.grammar: The noun 'face' (wajh) with the attached pronoun -ka ('your', for one male). The -a ending before the pronoun is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb ('turn … your face').
5.root: و-ج-ه (w-j-h) — face, direction, that which one faces

6.meaning: Toward, in the direction of, the side of; the part or region facing something. It indicates the bearing or course toward a thing.
6.grammar: A noun meaning 'direction/side', used adverbially to mean 'toward'. The -a ending is the accusative case; in this adverb-like use it expresses 'in the direction of' and is typically followed by a noun in the genitive showing what is faced ('toward … OF …').
6.root: ش-ط-ر (sh-ṭ-r) — a part, half, side, direction

7.meaning: The place of prostration; a mosque — literally the spot where one bows down (sajda) in worship. With the following 'sacred', it names the Sacred Mosque.
7.grammar: A noun of place on the form mafʿil ('the place where prostration is done'), prefixed with al- ('the'). The final -i ending is the genitive case, which typically marks the word as following a preposition or as the possessed/qualified noun after another ('… OF the mosque').
7.root: س-ج-د (s-j-d) — prostration, bowing down in worship

8.meaning: The sacred, inviolable, forbidden; that which is set apart and protected, whose violation is prohibited out of reverence. Describes something hallowed.
8.grammar: An adjective on the form faʿāl ('sacred/forbidden'), prefixed with al- ('the'). The final -i ending is the genitive case; an adjective takes the same case as the noun it describes, so this -i matches a preceding genitive noun ('the … sacred').
8.root: ح-ر-م (ḥ-r-m) — being forbidden, sacred, set apart, inviolable

9.meaning: A linkage of 'and' with the emphatic particle inna ('truly, indeed') plus 'he' — meaning 'and truly he…', opening a clause with firm assurance about the person referred to.
9.grammar: 'wa' is the connector 'and'. 'inna' is an emphatic particle that strongly affirms the statement and grammatically governs the following noun/pronoun in the accusative. The attached -hu ('he/him') is the subject of the inna-clause, expressed in object form as inna requires.

10.meaning: Surely the truth; truly the truth. The noun ḥaqq means truth, reality, what is right and rightfully due; here it is reinforced by an emphatic particle giving the sense 'is most certainly the truth'.
10.grammar: A definite noun carrying the emphatic prefix la- ('surely'). The final -u is the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the predicate (the thing being affirmed about a subject). The la- adds strong assertion, as in 'it is indeed …'.

11.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
11.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

12.meaning: The Lord belonging to a single male 'you' — Rabb is the Master, Owner, and Sustainer who creates, nurtures, and brings to maturity; here 'your Lord'.
12.grammar: The noun rabb (Lord, Sustainer) with the attached pronoun -ka, 'your' for one male. The -i ending before the pronoun is genitive, the case that typically links a word to a following possessor or follows a preposition (here showing the possession 'of you'). The doubled b (shadda) belongs to the root.

13.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
13.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

14.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
14.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

15.meaning: 'With/being heedless' — the preposition/particle 'bi' attached to 'ghāfil', one who is unaware, inattentive, or neglectful, failing to take notice.
15.grammar: The particle 'bi-' governs the following word into the genitive case. 'Ghāfil' is an active participle ('one who is heedless'). The '-in' (tanwīn) marks it indefinite and genitive; the 'bi-' here commonly adds emphasis within a negation ('not at all heedless').

16.meaning: 'About what' / 'of that which' — the preposition 'ʿan' ('about, concerning, away from') merged with 'mā' ('what, that which').
16.grammar: A fusion of the preposition 'ʿan' ('about, concerning') with the relative/interrogative 'mā' ('what'); the 'n' of 'ʿan' assimilates into 'mā' to give 'ʿammā'. It introduces the thing being spoken about.

17.meaning: You (all) do / work / act — to carry out deeds or labor.
17.grammar: A present-tense verb (Form I). The 'ta-' prefix with the '-ūna' ending marks the second-person masculine plural ('you all'). The '-ūna' (with final 'n') is the indicative form, marking a plain ongoing or habitual statement.
17.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, work, act; deeds

8.grammar: An adjective on the form faʿāl ('sacred/forbidden'), prefixed with al- ('the'). The final -i ending is the genitive case; an adjective takes the same case as the noun it describes, so this -i matches a preceding genitive noun ('the … sacred').
8.root: ح-ر-م (ḥ-r-m) — being forbidden, sacred, set apart, inviolable

9.meaning: And wherever, and in whatever place; introduces a general 'in any place that …'. The 'and' links it to what precedes.
9.grammar: A connective particle wa ('and') joined to the adverb ḥaythu ('where/wherever'), which points to place ('in the place where …'). Ḥaythu is invariable: it always ends in -u and never changes for case. It commonly introduces a following clause stating a condition of place.

10.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
10.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

11.meaning: A past-tense verb of 'being' addressed to a group: 'you (all) were', 'you (all) used to be'. From kāna, the core verb 'to be'. With a following predicate it often means 'you were (in a state of) …' or 'you used to …'.
11.grammar: This is a past-tense verb. The '-tum' suffix is the attached subject marker for a masculine plural 'you all'. Since the doer is built into the suffix, the verb stands in its base past form ('you all were').
11.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

12.meaning: So turn! / direct (yourselves/it) toward!; a command addressed to a group of people to make their faces or selves turn in a given direction.
12.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a group (masculine plural), in Form II (faʿʿala, 'to turn something'). The ending -ū is the plural 'you all' marker (written with a silent alif after the wāw). The leading fa- means 'then/so'.
12.root: و-ل-ي (w-l-y) — turning toward, directing, being near

13.meaning: Your (plural) faces. The plural of wajh ('face'), with an attached pronoun meaning 'your'. Wajh can also extend in meaning to a direction one turns toward, or one's self/presence.
13.grammar: A noun ('faces') in the accusative case, shown by the -a ending, with the possessive pronoun -kum ('your', for a group). The accusative -a typically marks the noun as the direct object of a verb. The attached -kum indicates the faces belong to the people addressed.

14.meaning: Toward the direction or side of something — the bearing or part of a thing one orients toward; 'his/its direction' when combined with the pronoun.
14.grammar: A noun meaning 'direction toward' with the attached pronoun -hu, 'his/its'. The -a ending is accusative; for a word like this it functions adverbially, marking the goal or direction of motion ('toward …'). The lengthened -hū reflects the pronoun following a vowel.

15.meaning: So that … not; in order that … not. A compound particle expressing negative purpose — the reason or aim behind an action stated as something to be prevented.
15.grammar: A compound of the purpose particle li- ('so that') with allā, itself a fusion of an ('that') and lā ('not'). Together they introduce a clause of negative purpose, and the following verb takes the subjunctive mood (often shown by a final -a). The whole means 'in order that … should not …'.

16.meaning: He/it is / he comes to be. A form of the verb kāna ('to be'), linking a subject to a state or asserting that something exists or occurs.
16.grammar: Present/imperfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular ('he/it'). The ya- prefix marks 3rd person masculine; the final -a marks the subjunctive mood, the form a verb takes after particles meaning 'so that', 'in order to', or 'that'. It expresses a state being brought about rather than a plain fact.
16.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

17.meaning: To the people, for mankind — addressed or directed toward human beings in general; 'an-nās' is the collective word for 'people, humankind'.
17.grammar: The preposition 'li-' (to/for) joined to 'an-nās' (the people); the article's 'a' drops in pronunciation and its 'l' assimilates into the noun's 'n' (shown by the doubling). The -i ending is the genitive case, required because the word follows the preposition 'li-'. 'nās' is a collective noun for humankind with no singular of its own root form.

18.meaning: 'Upon you (all)' — the preposition 'upon/on/over' joined to the plural 'you,' indicating something resting on or directed at a group.
18.grammar: The preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon/on/over') in its joined form 'ʿalay-' plus the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you all,' masculine plural). It marks the group as the recipients or target of whatever is laid 'upon' them.
18.root: — (preposition; no triliteral root)

19.meaning: An argument, proof, or case put forward; a justification or pretext one might cite. Ḥujja is grounds for a claim — a reasoned plea or evidence advanced in dispute.
19.grammar: An indefinite feminine noun. The ending -un is nominative with 'tanwīn' (the -n sound marking indefiniteness, 'a/an argument'). The nominative typically marks the subject of a sentence or the thing whose existence is being affirmed or denied.
19.root: ح-ج-ج (ḥ-j-j) — to argue, to prove, to present a case

20.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
20.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

21.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
21.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

22.meaning: 'They wronged / did injustice / acted unjustly'. The core idea is putting something out of its rightful place — oppression, transgression, or wronging oneself or others.
22.grammar: A past-tense verb with the plural subject ending -ū ('they', masculine/mixed group), referring to a completed action done by many. The -ū suffix is written with a silent 'alif' after it. It states that a group performed the act of wronging.
22.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — to wrong, oppress; to put a thing out of its proper place

23.meaning: From them; among them; of them. The preposition min ('from / of / among') joined to the pronoun 'them' (a group of males or a mixed group).
23.grammar: A preposition with an attached object pronoun. Min means 'from', 'out of', 'of', or 'among'; the suffix -hum is the pronoun 'them' (masculine plural) serving as its object. Pronouns attached to prepositions do not change case. The phrase indicates origin, partition, or belonging to a group.

24.meaning: A two-part word: the connective particle 'fa-' meaning 'so', 'then', or 'therefore' (drawing a consequence from what precedes), joined to 'lā', the particle of negation/prohibition. Together they convey 'so do not …' or 'so there is no …'.
24.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that links a clause to what came before and often signals a result or consequence. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a present-tense verb it commonly forms a prohibition ('do not …') or a simple negation ('not'). It carries no ending of its own.

25.meaning: You (plural) fear them; you stand in awe or dread of them. From the verb meaning to fear with reverence or apprehension, here directed at 'them'.
25.grammar: Present/imperfect verb, 2nd person masculine plural ('you all'), with the object pronoun -hum ('them'). The ta- prefix marks 2nd person; the plural subject and the weak final root letter appear as the -aw element. The loss of the usual final -na (takhshaw rather than takhshawna) shows subjunctive or jussive mood, expected after subordinating particles.

26.meaning: And fear Me; and stand in awe of Me. A command to fear with reverence, joined by 'and', with 'Me' as the one to be feared.
26.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a masculine plural 'you all', with the first-person object 'Me'. The -aw ending marks the plural addressees. The object 'Me' is the suffix -ī (the yāʾ), and it is joined to the verb by a protective linking nūn (nūn al-wiqāya), giving the cluster -nī. The imperative expresses a direct order, and wa- ('and') joins it to what precedes.

27.meaning: And so that I may complete / perfect / bring to fullness. From the verb meaning to make complete or whole, joined to 'and' and a particle of purpose.
27.grammar: Present/imperfect verb, 1st person singular ('I'), in the causative (form IV) pattern meaning 'to bring to completion'. The u- prefix marks 'I' in this verb pattern; the purpose particle li- ('so that') makes the final letter take the subjunctive -a. The wa- ('and') links it to a preceding purpose. Together: 'and in order that I may perfect …'.
27.root: ت-م-م (t-m-m) — completeness, perfection, fullness

28.meaning: My favor; my blessing; my grace. Niʿma is a bestowed good, a bounty or kindness granted; with the attached 'my' it is a favor belonging to the speaker.
28.grammar: A feminine noun ('favor') with the first-person possessive 'my'. The base noun's final t carries the linking vowel -i before the possessive suffix -ī ('my'). Attaching a possessive pronoun puts the noun in a possessive (genitive) relationship, here meaning 'the favor that is mine'.

29.meaning: 'Upon you (all)' — the preposition 'upon/on/over' joined to the plural 'you,' indicating something resting on or directed at a group.
29.grammar: The preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon/on/over') in its joined form 'ʿalay-' plus the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you all,' masculine plural). It marks the group as the recipients or target of whatever is laid 'upon' them.
29.root: — (preposition; no triliteral root)

30.meaning: And so that you (plural) may; in the hope that you might. The particle laʿalla expresses hope, expectation, or a desired outcome ('perhaps / so that'), here with 'you' as its subject.

parts.en: perhaps / so that / in the hope that

30.grammar: The particle laʿalla ('perhaps / in hope that'), which expresses an anticipated or hoped-for result, with the attached pronoun -kum ('you all') as its subject. Such particles place the following noun or pronoun in the accusative; -kum here is that subject. It typically leads into a verb stating the hoped outcome. The wa- ('and') links it to what comes before.

31.meaning: 'You (plural) are/become guided' — to be led on the right path, to find and follow correct direction. The verb conveys accepting guidance and being set straight, not merely knowing the way but walking it.
31.grammar: A present-tense verb (form VIII) addressed to a group. The ta- prefix marks second person ('you'), and the -ūna ending marks masculine plural in the indicative mood — the ordinary, factual mood used when a verb is not negated or subordinated by a particle that would clip its ending. So it means 'you (all) are guided / become rightly guided.'
31.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — to guide, to lead rightly

1.meaning: Just as; like; in the same way that. A compound expressing comparison or correspondence between one thing and another.
1.grammar: A compound of the comparison particle ka- ('like / as') with mā ('that which / what'). Together they mean 'just as' or 'in the same way that', introducing a comparison with a following clause. Neither element changes for case; the phrase functions as a connective of likeness.

2.meaning: We sent / dispatched. From the causative verb meaning to send forth or commission, especially the sending of messengers; with 'We' as the subject.
2.grammar: Past/perfect verb in the causative (form IV) pattern meaning 'to send', 1st person plural ('we'). The suffix -nā is the subject ending 'we' on a completed action. The perfect tense presents the sending as accomplished and complete.

3.meaning: Among you; in you; within you (plural). The preposition fī ('in / among') joined to the pronoun 'you' (a group).
3.grammar: A preposition with an attached object pronoun. Fī means 'in', 'within', or 'among'; the suffix -kum ('you all') is its object. Pronouns attached to prepositions do not change case. The phrase indicates being inside or in the midst of the group addressed.

4.meaning: "a messenger / an envoy" — one who is sent bearing a message; 'rasūl' is an emissary commissioned to convey something on behalf of the one who sent him, especially a prophet sent with a divine message.
4.grammar: A masculine noun on the faʿūl pattern, indefinite ('a messenger'). The '-an' ending (tanwīn fatḥ) is the indefinite accusative case, the form used for the direct object of a verb; the written alif carries this ending.
4.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send; a message, messenger

5.meaning: From among you / of you — indicating a portion or subset belonging to the addressed group; 'min' (from/of) joined to 'you all'.
5.grammar: The preposition 'min' (from/of) with the attached pronoun '-kum', meaning 'you all' (a group, masculine or mixed). Together they convey 'from among you' — often marking partition (a part of a larger whole) or origin.

6.meaning: "he recites / he reads aloud / he follows" — to recite or read out (especially scripture), conveying the sense of following the words one after another; 'talā' is to recite, and also to follow closely.
6.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he recites / will recite'). The 'ya-' prefix marks 'he/it' as the doer. The verb is from a root ending in a weak letter, which surfaces as the long 'ū' ('yatlū'); the final long vowel here reflects the indicative (statement) mood. Final '-ā' in the script (alif) is a spelling convention.
6.root: ت-ل-و (t-l-w) — to recite, read aloud; to follow

7.meaning: 'Upon you (all)' — the preposition 'upon/on/over' joined to the plural 'you,' indicating something resting on or directed at a group.
7.grammar: The preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon/on/over') in its joined form 'ʿalay-' plus the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you all,' masculine plural). It marks the group as the recipients or target of whatever is laid 'upon' them.

8.meaning: Our signs / verses. The plural of āya — a sign, token, or miraculous proof, and also a verse of revelation — with the attached 'our'.
8.grammar: A feminine plural noun ('signs / verses') with the possessive pronoun -nā ('our'). The sound feminine plural ending -āt shows -i, the case used for the genitive (linked to a following word or after a preposition) and the accusative (object of a verb); attaching -nā ('our') also places it in a possessive relationship. So it means 'signs belonging to Us'.

9.meaning: And He purifies you; and He causes you to grow in purity. From the intensive verb meaning to cleanse, sanctify, and cause to thrive morally and spiritually; with 'you' as the object.
9.grammar: Present/imperfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular ('he'), in the intensive (form II) pattern that adds the sense of thorough or causative action ('to purify thoroughly'). The yu- prefix marks 3rd person in this pattern; the object pronoun -kum ('you all') receives the action. The wa- ('and') links it to what precedes.

10.meaning: And He teaches you; and He instructs you. From the intensive verb meaning to teach, impart knowledge, or instruct carefully; with 'you' as the object. The final vowel here is shaped by the word that follows.
10.grammar: Present/imperfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular ('he'), in the intensive (form II) teaching pattern, with the object pronoun -kum ('you all'). The yu- prefix marks 3rd person in this pattern; the verb's own final vowel -u marks the indicative mood ('he teaches'). The pronoun's normally silent ending takes a helping vowel -u (so -kumu) to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a consonant cluster. The wa- ('and') links it to what precedes.

11.meaning: The Book, the Scripture — a written revelation; the term for a divinely revealed text.
11.grammar: A definite noun ('the Book') with attached 'al-' ('the'). The final '-a' ending is the accusative case, typically marking the word as the direct object of a verb.
11.root: ك-ت-ب (k-t-b) — to write; a writing, book

12.meaning: And wisdom; and sound judgment. Ḥikma is deep wisdom — knowledge joined to right understanding and the putting of things in their proper place.
12.grammar: A definite feminine noun ('the wisdom') in the accusative case. The feminine ending is the tāʾ marbūṭa, and the accusative case vowel (-a) is borne by that same tāʾ — there is no separate ending after it. The accusative typically marks the noun as the direct object of a verb. The article al- makes it definite ('the wisdom'), and wa- ('and') joins it to what precedes.

13.meaning: And He teaches you; and He instructs you. From the intensive verb meaning to teach or impart knowledge carefully; with 'you' as the object.
13.grammar: Present/imperfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular ('he'), in the intensive (form II) teaching pattern, with the object pronoun -kum ('you all'). The yu- prefix marks 3rd person in this pattern; the verb's own final vowel -u marks the indicative mood, the form used for plain statements of fact ('he teaches'). The wa- ('and') links it to what precedes.

14.meaning: A short, highly versatile particle 'mā.' It can mean 'what' or 'that which,' can negate ('not'), and can serve as an intensifier attached to another word. Its precise force depends on what it accompanies, but its core is to point to a thing or to add emphasis.
14.grammar: A multifunctional particle. It does not take case endings. Depending on usage it can be a relative ('that which'), an interrogative ('what?'), a negator ('not'), or — when joined to another particle — an emphasizer. It is uninflected and indeclinable.

15.meaning: A negating particle, 'not', used specifically to deny that an action happened in the past, even though it attaches to a present-tense verb form. It turns 'you do X' into 'you did not do X'.

parts.en: did not (negation of a completed act)

15.grammar: An indeclinable particle that governs the verb after it, putting that verb into the jussive (clipped) mood and giving it past-time meaning. In short: lam + a present-form verb = 'did not [verb]'.

16.meaning: You (plural) are / you happen to be. A form of the 'hollow' verb kāna ('to be'), which links a subject to a state or description, or expresses simply being or existing.
16.grammar: Present/imperfect verb, 2nd person masculine plural ('you all'). The ta- prefix marks 2nd person; the -ū ending marks masculine plural. The dropping of the usual final -na (so takūnū rather than takūnūna) shows the verb is in the subjunctive or jussive mood — the form expected after conditional or subordinating particles.
16.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

17.meaning: A verb addressed to a group: 'you (all) know', 'you have knowledge', 'you are aware'. From the root meaning 'to know'.
17.grammar: The 'ta-' prefix marks a present/future verb addressed to 'you'. The '-ūna' ending marks a masculine plural subject and is the full 'indicative' form, signalling an ongoing, factual statement ('you (all) do know'), as opposed to the shortened '-ū' used after certain particles.

1.meaning: A command meaning 'then/so remember Me' or 'so make mention of Me' — an instruction to call Me to mind, keep Me present in thought and on the tongue. The opening 'fa-' links it as a consequence ('so', 'therefore').
1.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a group: the '-ū' ending marks a plural 'you all'. The attached '-nī' is the object pronoun 'Me'. The 'fa-' prefix presents the action as a response or result of something prior.
1.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — to remember, mention, call to mind

2.meaning: 'I will remember you' or 'I make mention of you' — a first-person statement to call you to mind and hold you in regard, given as the consequence of a preceding command.
2.grammar: A present/future verb in the first-person singular: the 'a-' prefix means 'I'. Its final consonant carries a sukūn (no vowel), marking the jussive (apocopate) form rather than the indicative, which would end in '-u'. This jussive is the standard response to a preceding command (jawāb al-amr): 'remember Me, [and] I will remember you'. The attached '-kum' is the object 'you all'.
2.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — to remember, mention, call to mind

3.meaning: 'And give thanks / be grateful' — a command to acknowledge and show appreciation for blessings received, the opposite of denying or covering them up. The opening 'wa-' joins it to what precedes ('and').
3.grammar: A command (imperative) to a group: the '-ū' ending marks a plural 'you all'. The 'wa-' prefix simply connects it to a preceding statement ('and').

4.meaning: 'to Me' or 'for Me' — the preposition 'to/for' fused with the first-person pronoun, expressing direction, benefit, or belonging toward the speaker.
4.grammar: A preposition ('to/for') with the attached pronoun '-ī' ('me'). Together they express benefit, direction, or attribution toward the first person.

5.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
5.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

6.meaning: 'You (all) deny / are ungrateful to Me' — to reject, disbelieve, or be thanklessly unappreciative; the verb's root sense is to cover over or conceal a truth or a favor.
6.grammar: A present-tense indicative verb addressed to a group: the 'ta-' prefix means 'you', and the '-ū' element marks the plural 'you all'. The final 'n' is the indicative marker (the 'n' of the full '-ūna' ending), which is kept because the verb is indicative. The first-person object 'me' is attached here, and its own vowel is absorbed so only the linking '-i' is heard — hence '-ni' carries both the indicative 'n' and the object 'Me'.
6.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover over; to disbelieve, be ungrateful

1.meaning: O…! A vocative call used to address or summon someone, equivalent to 'O you…' before a noun. It is a frozen attention-getting phrase that introduces who is being addressed.
1.grammar: A compound vocative. 'Yā' is the call-word 'O'; 'ayyu(hā)' is the special form used to call out to someone defined by a following noun. Together they form a fixed expression meaning roughly 'O you…!', introducing the one being addressed.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
3.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

4.meaning: 'Seek help / seek assistance' — a command to ask for aid and support, drawing on another's strength.
4.grammar: A command (imperative) to a group: the '-ū' ending marks a plural 'you all'. The 'ista-' pattern carries the sense of seeking or asking for something — here, seeking help.

5.meaning: Patience, steadfast endurance, self-restraint — the disciplined perseverance to bear hardship and hold firm.
5.grammar: The prefix 'bi-' is a preposition meaning 'with/by/through,' and 'al-' is 'the.' The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 's' (a sun letter), which is why the 's' is doubled — a pronunciation effect, not a separate piece. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition.

6.meaning: The ritual Prayer (ṣalāh) — the formal, prescribed act of worship; more broadly, prayer and supplication directed to Allah.
6.grammar: Begins with 'wa-' ('and') and 'al-' ('the'). The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 's' (a sun letter), which is why the 's' is doubled — a pronunciation effect, not a separate piece. The feminine '-t-' ending carries the final '-i,' which is the genitive case — the form taken after a preposition or in an 'of' linkage to a preceding word.

7.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
7.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

8.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
8.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

9.meaning: With, together with, alongside — indicating company, accompaniment, or being in the same place or time as another.
9.grammar: A preposition of accompaniment ('with, alongside'); grammatically it is an adverbial of place/time (ẓarf) that governs the genitive. It is placed before a following noun to put one thing in the company of another, and that following noun stands in the genitive. The -a is its fixed ending.

10.meaning: 'The patient ones / the steadfast' — those who endure hardship with calm perseverance, restraining themselves and holding firm under trial.
10.grammar: A definite plural noun/participle ('the ones who...') referring to males or a mixed group. The '-īna' ending is the plural form used when the word is an object or follows a preposition (roughly 'the patient ones' as a target of the sentence). The 'al-' prefix means 'the'.
10.root: ص-ب-ر (ṣ-b-r) — to be patient, endure, hold firm

1.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
1.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

2.meaning: You (all) say / utter — referring to speaking or saying words, addressed to a group. In context it is the form used after a particle so that it reads 'do not say' / 'that you may say'.
2.grammar: Present-tense verb, second-person masculine plural ('you all'). The ta- prefix marks the second person; plurality is supplied by the -ū ending. The plain ending here (without final -na) is the form a verb takes after certain particles such as 'do not' or 'so that', signalling command-prohibition or purpose.

3.meaning: 'for whoever / to the one who' — the preposition 'for/to' joined with the relative word 'who', introducing the person(s) about whom something is said.
3.grammar: A preposition ('for/to') combined with the relative/interrogative word 'man' ('who, whoever'). Together they single out a person or group as the focus ('for the one(s) who...').

4.meaning: 'He/it is killed / is slain' — to have one's life taken by another; stated as something happening to the subject rather than done by them.
4.grammar: A present-tense passive verb, third-person masculine singular: the 'yu-' prefix plus the internal vowel pattern signals 'he/it is being —' done to him. The '-u' ending is the basic indicative ('is/does'). It conveys that the action is received, not performed, by the subject.

5.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
5.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

6.meaning: 'path, way, road' — a route or course; figuratively a cause or way of life one travels along. In construct ('the way OF ...').
6.grammar: A singular noun with the '-i' (genitive) ending, which typically links it to a following noun ('the way OF ...') or follows a preposition. It marks the word as connected to or possessed by what comes after.

7.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
7.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

8.meaning: 'dead ones' — those who are no longer living; the plural of 'dead'.
8.grammar: A plural noun/adjective ('dead ones'). The '-un' ending marks it as indefinite ('(some) dead') and in the subject/base case, the form used when the word names or describes the doer or topic of a sentence.

9.meaning: A particle of retraction meaning 'rather,' 'no, but,' or 'nay' — it cancels or sets aside what was just said and shifts to a corrected or contrasting statement that follows.
9.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it never changes form). Its function is to redirect the discourse: it dismisses a prior idea and introduces what is actually the case.

10.meaning: 'living ones, alive' — those who possess life; the plural of 'alive/living'.
10.grammar: A plural noun/adjective ('living ones'). The '-un' ending (here spelled with the hamza, '-ā'un') marks it as indefinite ('(some) living') and in the subject/base case used to name or describe the topic of a sentence.

11.meaning: 'but / however' — a particle that introduces a contrast or correction, setting what follows against what was just said. The opening 'wa-' connects it ('and').
11.grammar: A contrasting particle ('but, however') that signals a turn against the preceding idea. It does not change endings on words; it simply introduces a corrective or opposing clause. The 'wa-' prefix links it to what came before.

12.meaning: 'Not' — a particle of negation. Depending on context it denies a present fact, forbids an action, or rules something out ('do not / there is no').
12.grammar: A negating particle, 'not / no'. It is used to deny or prohibit — negating present-tense statements, expressing 'there is no...', or, with a command form, forbidding an action ('do not...').

13.meaning: 'You (all) perceive / sense / are aware' — to notice or become conscious of something through feeling or insight.
13.grammar: A present-tense verb addressed to a group: the 'ta-' prefix means 'you' and the '-ūna' ending marks the plural 'you all' in the basic indicative ('you do / are doing'). It describes ongoing or general awareness.
13.root: ش-ع-ر (sh-ʿ-r) — to perceive, sense, be aware

1.meaning: 'And We will surely test you' — an emphatic promise to put you through trial, to prove and examine you. It combines 'and', a stress particle, the verb 'We test', a heavy emphasis ending, and the object 'you'.
1.grammar: A first-person plural verb ('We test'): the 'na-' prefix means 'we'. It is wrapped in two layers of emphasis — the 'la-' prefix ('surely') and the doubled '-nna' ending ('most certainly') — which together make it a solemn, definite promise. The final '-kum' is the object 'you all'.
1.root: ب-ل-و (b-l-w) — to test, try, put to the proof

2.meaning: 'with something / with a thing' — by means of some thing or matter; 'shay'' is the most general word for 'a thing'.
2.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the noun 'thing'. The '-in' ending marks the noun as indefinite ('a thing, something') and in the genitive case required after a preposition.
2.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʾ) — thing; to will, to want

3.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
3.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

4.meaning: 'fear' — dread or apprehension of danger or harm; the state of being afraid.
4.grammar: A definite singular noun ('the fear'). The '-i' (genitive) ending typically links it to a preceding noun ('... of fear') or follows a preposition. The 'al-' prefix means 'the'.

5.meaning: 'hunger' — the pang and want of food; the condition of being hungry. The opening 'wa-' joins it ('and').
5.grammar: A definite singular noun ('the hunger'). The '-i' (genitive) ending links it to a preceding noun ('... of hunger') or follows a preposition. The 'al-' prefix means 'the', and the 'wa-' prefix connects it ('and').

6.meaning: 'loss, decrease, diminishing' — a reduction or shortfall, when something is made less or falls short. The opening 'wa-' joins it ('and').
6.grammar: An indefinite singular noun ('a loss, a decrease'). The '-in' ending marks it as indefinite and in the genitive case (linking to a following noun, '... of', or following a preposition). The 'wa-' prefix connects it ('and').
6.root: ن-ق-ص (n-q-ṣ) — to decrease, diminish, fall short

7.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
7.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

8.meaning: 'wealth, properties, possessions' — material goods and assets; the plural of 'māl' (wealth/property).
8.grammar: A definite plural noun ('the possessions'). The '-i' (genitive) ending links it to a preceding noun ('... of wealth') or follows a preposition. The 'al-' prefix means 'the'.

9.meaning: 'lives, selves, souls' — the inner self, the person, or life itself; the plural of 'nafs' (self/soul). The opening 'wa-' joins it ('and').
9.grammar: A definite plural noun ('the selves/lives'). The '-i' (genitive) ending links it to a preceding noun ('... of selves') or follows a preposition. The 'al-' prefix means 'the', and the 'wa-' prefix connects it ('and').

10.meaning: 'fruits, produce, yields' — the fruits of trees and, by extension, the fruits or results of effort; the plural of 'thamarah'. The opening 'wa-' joins it ('and').
10.grammar: A definite plural noun ('the fruits'). This sound feminine plural takes the '-āti' ending, which serves both as an object form and as the genitive ('... of fruits' / after a preposition). The 'al-' prefix means 'the', and the 'wa-' prefix connects it ('and').
10.root: ث-م-ر (th-m-r) — fruit; to bear fruit, produce

11.meaning: A two-part word: 'and' + a command 'give glad tidings, bring good news.' The verb means to announce something joyful that shows on the face — to cheer someone with happy news. It is the standard word for delivering good tidings.
11.grammar: A conjunction 'wa' + an imperative (command) verb, addressed to a single male ('you, give good news'). The base form is bashshir; the final -i here is a connecting vowel added to ease pronunciation before a following word, not a case ending. The doubled middle letter marks an intensive/causative sense: actively bringing good news to someone.

12.meaning: 'The patient ones / the steadfast' — those who endure hardship with calm perseverance, restraining themselves and holding firm under trial.
12.grammar: A definite plural noun/participle ('the ones who...') referring to males or a mixed group. The '-īna' ending is the plural form used when the word is an object or follows a preposition (roughly 'the patient ones' as a target of the sentence). The 'al-' prefix means 'the'.
12.root: ص-ب-ر (ṣ-b-r) — to be patient, endure, hold firm

1.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
1.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

2.meaning: 'when / whenever' — a particle pointing to a time, usually a future or expected occasion ('at the time that ...').
2.grammar: A time particle ('when, whenever') that introduces a clause and points to the moment something happens, typically expected or recurring. It sets up a 'when X, then Y' relationship and does not itself alter word endings.

3.meaning: 'it struck them / befell them / hit them' — when a misfortune, event, or thing reaches and lands upon people; the root sense is hitting the mark or reaching accurately.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb. The '-at/-t' ending marks a feminine singular subject ('she/it'), agreeing with a feminine doer. The attached '-hum' is the object 'them'. It states a completed action that reached or struck its object.
3.root: ص-و-ب (ṣ-w-b) — to hit the mark, reach, befall correctly

4.meaning: A calamity, affliction, or misfortune — something distressing that strikes a person, especially trouble that arrives suddenly and from outside one's control.
4.grammar: An active-participle-based feminine noun, here standing as a singular indefinite noun. The final -un (nunation/tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('a misfortune') and in the nominative case, the form a noun takes when it is the subject of a sentence or the thing being identified.
4.root: ص-و-ب (ṣ-w-b) — to hit a target, to strike, to befall (also linked to what is right/apt)

5.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'they said' or 'they spoke,' attributing an utterance to a group of three or more (grammatically masculine or mixed).
5.grammar: Past-tense verb in the third-person masculine plural. The stem qāl- carries a long ā (from a weak middle root letter), and the plural subject is marked by the wāw vowel -ū fused onto it ('they'). The alif written after the wāw is silent — a purely orthographic spelling convention with no pronunciation.

6.meaning: A two-part expression: an emphatic particle that strongly affirms and confirms a statement ('truly, indeed, certainly'), fused with the attached pronoun 'we.' Together: 'truly we…' / 'indeed we…'
6.grammar: The particle inna gives strong emphasis and certainty to the clause it opens. The attached -ā is the pronoun 'we,' serving as the subject being emphasized: 'truly we…'

7.meaning: A two-part word: the preposition 'li-' meaning 'to', 'for', or 'belonging to', attached to the name 'Allah'. It conveys 'to Allah' or 'for Allah'.
7.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('to/for') pulls the following noun into the genitive case, which is why 'Allah' ends in '-i' (llāhi). The '-i' ending is the regular result of a noun governed by a preposition.

8.meaning: 'And indeed we…' — the connector 'and' (wa) joined to the emphatic particle inna ('truly, indeed') with an attached 'we'. It links to what precedes and strongly asserts a statement about the group.
8.grammar: A connective 'and' (wa-) plus the emphasis particle inna, with an attached pronoun, first person plural (-nā, 'we'). inna strongly affirms the nominal statement that follows; -nā is its ism. The nūn of the pronoun -nā merges in writing with the doubled n of inna (so only the alif is written after the shaddah), but it is phonologically part of the pronoun, giving wa-innā ('and indeed we …').

9.meaning: 'To Him' or 'toward Him' — the preposition expressing direction or endpoint ('to / toward') combined with a pronoun referring to a single masculine person, indicating motion or attention directed at him.
9.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The base 'ilā shifts to 'ilay- when a pronoun is added. The suffix -hi is the third-person masculine singular object of a preposition, 'him'; its -i vowel is the form the pronoun takes after the 'ay' sound.

10.meaning: Ones who return or go back; people in the act of returning to a place or state, with the strong overtone of returning to one's origin or to Allah.
10.grammar: A masculine plural active participle. The -ūna ending is the sound masculine plural in the nominative case, naming a group of people ('those who return') when they are the subject or predicate of a sentence; it shifts to -īna in other cases.
10.root: ر-ج-ع (r-j-ʿ) — to return, go back, revert

1.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'those' — pointing to people or things that are distant or already known. It singles out a group ('those ones', 'it is those who').
1.grammar: A plural demonstrative pronoun, 'those'. It is fixed in form (no case endings). The -ka element signals distance/remoteness, pointing to something far off or notable. It can refer to people of either gender.

2.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon them' or 'against them': the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over, against') joined to the plural pronoun 'them'. It conveys something resting on, being incumbent upon, or weighing against a group.
2.grammar: ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay- before a pronoun.
