The suffix -him is the attached pronominal suffix for a masculine plural group ('them'); after a preposition it carries genitive/prepositional force, and the -i- vowel reflects its position after this preposition. Together they signal a relationship of something being over, upon, or burdensome to that group.
2.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

3.meaning: Blessings, prayers, or graces sent down upon someone; the plural of ṣalāh. When attributed to Allah toward a servant it means His favor, commendation, and mercy poured out upon them.
3.grammar: A feminine plural noun (plural of ṣalāh) carrying the indefinite nominative ending -un (tanwīn). The nominative case marks it as a subject or as the predicate that identifies something ('… are blessings').
3.root: ص-ل-و (ṣ-l-w) — connection through worship; prayer, blessing

4.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
4.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

5.meaning: 'Their Lord / their Sustainer.' The noun 'rabb' — a master who owns, nurtures, sustains, and brings to maturity all under His care — joined to 'their.' It conveys far more than 'lord': the one who creates, provides for, and governs His servants.
5.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive pronoun -him ('their,' masculine plural). The -i ending is the genitive case, which typically appears after a preposition or links the word to another in an 'of / belonging to' relationship; here it pairs with the attached 'their.'
5.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master; lordship, ownership, care

6.meaning: And mercy — compassion that actively does good to its object: tenderness joined with the power and will to relieve, forgive, and care for.
6.grammar: The prefix wa- means 'and', joining this word to what precedes. The noun is feminine singular with the indefinite nominative ending -un (tanwīn), the case used for a subject or a predicate noun ('… and mercy').

7.meaning: 'And those' — the connective 'and' joined to the demonstrative 'those'. It both links to what precedes and points out a group ('and it is those who…').
7.grammar: A connecting particle wa ('and') prefixed to a plural demonstrative pronoun, 'those'. The wa simply joins what follows to what came before. The demonstrative is fixed in form (no case endings), and its -ka element marks distance; it may refer to people of either gender.

8.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (masculine plural). Standing on its own, it typically adds emphasis or marks the group out as the focus ('they, specifically', 'it is they who').
8.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It takes no case endings; the base is hum, and the final vowel appears as -u (humu) as a connecting vowel to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a definite article. Standing alone, it commonly emphasises or isolates the subject.

9.meaning: The rightly guided ones — those who have accepted and are following true guidance, people who have found and kept to the right path.
9.grammar: A definite masculine plural active participle of the eighth verb form (which carries the sense of accepting/taking on guidance for oneself). The prefix al- means 'the'; the -ūna ending is the sound masculine plural in the nominative case (subject or predicate), becoming -īna in other cases.
9.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — to guide, lead rightly, show the way

1.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
1.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

2.meaning: Aṣ-Ṣafā — a proper name of one of the two well-known hillocks at the Sacred Mosque in Mecca; the literal sense of the root is a smooth, clean rock.
2.grammar: A proper noun carrying the definite article al-. Because it ends in a fixed long vowel (alif), its ending does not change to show case; the article marks it as the specific, well-known place named Aṣ-Ṣafā.
2.root: ص-ف-و (ṣ-f-w) — purity, clearness, smoothness (a smooth bare rock)

3.meaning: And al-Marwah — a proper name of the second of the two hillocks at the Sacred Mosque in Mecca; the root sense is a small flint or quartz stone.
3.grammar: A proper noun with the prefix wa- ('and') and the article al- ('the'). The final -a (accusative) is the case ending a noun takes when it is the object of a verb or otherwise governed into that case ('… and al-Marwah').

4.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
4.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

5.meaning: Distinctive marks or sacred symbols — rites, signs, and emblems set apart as tokens of devotion to Allah; outward observances that signal and consecrate worship.
5.grammar: A plural noun (singular shaʿīrah). The -i ending is genitive, the case that typically links a noun to a following noun ('… OF …') in a possessive chain or comes after a preposition.
5.root: ش-ع-ر (sh-ʿ-r) — to be aware, to perceive; a sign/mark by which something is known

6.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
6.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

7.meaning: A compound meaning 'then whoever' or 'so whoever'. It combines 'then/so' with the conditional/relative 'who', introducing whatever person meets a stated condition.
7.grammar: The connector fa- ('then/so', often answering or following a condition) joined to man ('whoever / the one who'), which refers to people and introduces a condition: 'whoever does X…'. man does not change its ending; the clause after it supplies the rest of the meaning.

8.meaning: He performed the Hajj — to undertake the major pilgrimage; the root sense is to set out for and repeatedly visit a venerated destination with deliberate purpose.
8.grammar: A past-tense verb. The final -a marks the third-person masculine singular ('he did it') in the completed/past tense, describing an action seen as already accomplished.
8.root: ح-ج-ج (ḥ-j-j) — to set out for, to repeatedly visit a revered place; pilgrimage

9.meaning: The house, dwelling, or abode. 'Bayt' is a house or place of dwelling; the definite article 'al-' ('the') makes it a specific, identified house rather than just 'a house.'
9.grammar: The definite article 'al-' ('the') prefixed to a noun. The -a ending marks the accusative case, typically used for the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon). Because the noun is made definite by 'al-,' it takes a plain -a with no nunation.
9.root: ب-ي-ت (b-y-t) — to spend the night, dwell; a house

10.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative between two or more options, linking possibilities of which one applies.
10.grammar: A connecting particle meaning 'or'. Its base form is aw; the added -i is a 'helping' vowel given to the otherwise-silent final consonant to smooth the link to a following word that begins with a connecting (hamzat-waṣl) alif. It is not a case ending — particles do not take cases.

11.meaning: He performed the ʿUmrah — to undertake the lesser pilgrimage; the root sense is to visit, and more broadly to tend, inhabit, or keep a place flourishing.
11.grammar: A past-tense verb of the eighth form (which adds a reflexive 'do for oneself' sense). The final -a marks the third-person masculine singular ('he did it') in the completed/past tense; the initial i- is the connecting (helping) vowel this verb pattern carries at its start.
11.root: ع-م-ر (ʿ-m-r) — to visit; to inhabit, build up, keep flourishing; long life

12.meaning: A two-part word: the connective particle 'fa-' meaning 'so', 'then', or 'therefore' (drawing a consequence from what precedes), joined to 'lā', the particle of negation/prohibition. Together they convey 'so do not …' or 'so there is no …'.
12.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that links a clause to what came before and often signals a result or consequence. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a present-tense verb it commonly forms a prohibition ('do not …') or a simple negation ('not'). It carries no ending of its own.

13.meaning: Blame, sin, or fault — moral liability incurred by a wrong action; the sense of wrongdoing that counts against a person, or any leaning toward error.
13.grammar: A masculine noun. The final -a is the accusative case ending; this ending appears, among other uses, on the noun governed by a negating particle (as in the common construction 'there is no blame …').
13.root: ج-ن-ح (j-n-ḥ) — to incline, lean, tilt (toward wrong); hence fault/sin

14.meaning: A preposition fused with a pronoun, meaning 'upon him', 'on him', or 'toward him'. It marks the one to whom an action is directed or upon whom something rests.
14.grammar: The preposition 'upon/on' with an attached object pronoun -hi ('him', third-person masculine singular); its -i vowel is the regular form the pronoun takes after the 'y' sound. Paired with a verb of turning, this 'upon/toward him' marks the person the action reaches.

15.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
15.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

16.meaning: That he go around or circle about — to move repeatedly back and forth between two points, or to circumambulate; encircling motion done again and again.
16.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he …') of an intensive pattern that conveys going around repeatedly. The final -a is the subjunctive mood, which a present verb takes after certain particles (such as 'that' or 'so that'), giving the sense of a hoped-for, intended, or potential action rather than a plain statement of fact.
16.root: ط-و-ف (ṭ-w-f) — to go around, circle, circumambulate

17.meaning: With them two / by them two — the preposition 'with/by' attached to a pronoun referring to a pair (two things or two people). In context the sense of going 'between' the two comes from the accompanying verb of going to and fro, not from this preposition itself.
17.grammar: The preposition bi- ('with/by') with the attached pronoun -himā meaning 'the two of them' (the dual, used for exactly two). A noun or pronoun after a preposition stands in the genitive relation; here that role is carried by the fixed pronoun ending -himā.

18.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
18.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.
18.root: — (pronoun/particle; no triliteral root)

19.meaning: He did something willingly and as a freely-offered extra — to volunteer a good deed beyond what is required, out of one's own eager good will.
19.grammar: A past-tense verb of the fifth form (a reflexive pattern meaning to take something willingly upon oneself). The final -a marks the third-person masculine singular ('he did it') in the completed/past tense.
19.root: ط-و-ع (ṭ-w-ʿ) — obedience, willing compliance; doing freely and gladly

20.meaning: Good — that which is beneficial, virtuous, and excellent; goodness as a thing one can do or possess, and what is better or preferable.
20.grammar: A noun (also serving as the 'better/best' form). The final -an (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite and in the accusative case — the case used for the direct object of a verb ('to do good') and for similar governed roles.

21.meaning: A two-part connector meaning 'so/then, indeed…'. It joins fa- ('so', 'then', marking a result or consequence) to inna, an emphatic particle that strongly affirms the statement that follows ('truly', 'verily').
21.grammar: fa- is a connective prefix signaling that what follows is a consequence or next step. inna is an emphatic particle that introduces a nominal sentence, puts its following noun in the accusative, and strengthens the assertion; it does not itself take a case ending.

22.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
22.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

23.meaning: One who is deeply thankful and appreciative — a recognizer and rewarder of good. Of Allah it means He fully acknowledges even small good and richly repays it.
23.grammar: A masculine singular active participle ('one who is thankful'). The final -un (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite and in the nominative case — the case for a subject or a predicate that describes or identifies ('is appreciative').
23.root: ش-ك-ر (sh-k-r) — to be thankful, to appreciate and acknowledge good

24.meaning: An intensive adjective/name meaning 'All-Knowing / fully aware' — one whose knowledge is complete, deep, and all-encompassing; as a divine attribute it denotes Allah's perfect knowledge.
24.grammar: An intensive adjective (the pattern faʿīl conveys 'thoroughly, abundantly'). The ending -un is the indefinite nominative — the nominative case marks it as the subject or the quality being affirmed, and the -n (nunation) signals 'a / an', i.e. indefinite. So it reads '(is) all-knowing'.
24.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — knowledge, knowing

1.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
1.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: They conceal, hide, or keep something hidden — deliberately suppressing knowledge or truth and withholding it from others.
3.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine plural ('they …'). The ya-…-ūna frame marks an ongoing or habitual present action; the final -ūna (with the retained final nūn) is the indicative mood, the form used for a plain statement of fact.
3.root: ك-ت-م (k-t-m) — to conceal, hide, keep secret

4.meaning: A word meaning 'what' or 'that which' — a relative/indefinite particle pointing to an unspecified thing ('what', 'whatever', 'that which').
4.grammar: An invariable particle (mā) with no case ending. Depending on context it works as a relative pronoun ('that which') introducing a clause, or as an interrogative/indefinite ('what'). It does not inflect for case, gender, or number.

5.meaning: We sent down — to cause something to descend or be revealed from a higher source to a lower; classically used of revelation sent down from on high.
5.grammar: A past-tense verb of the causative (fourth) form, meaning to make something come down. The attached -nā is the subject pronoun 'we', marking the action as completed and done by a 'we' (a form of majestic/collective speech when used of Allah).
5.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — to descend, come down, be sent down

6.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
6.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

7.meaning: "the clear proofs / evident signs" — plural of a feminine word meaning a clear, manifest evidence, proof, or sign that makes the truth plain.
7.grammar: The al- prefix means "the." The -āt is the sound feminine plural ending. Its -i (here -ti) ending serves for both the genitive and the accusative in this plural pattern — marking the word as an object, or as governed by a preposition or a following noun.
7.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — to be clear, to make plain

8.meaning: And the guidance — right direction and true showing of the way; the help by which one is led to truth and kept on the correct path.
8.grammar: A masculine verbal noun with the prefix wa- ('and') and the article al- ('the'). Because it ends in a fixed long vowel (written as a final alif), its ending does not change to show case; the article marks it as the specific, known 'guidance'.
8.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — to guide, lead rightly, show the way

9.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
9.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

10.meaning: A noun/adverb meaning 'after' — the time or position following something; 'afterward', 'following'.
10.grammar: An adverb of time functioning as a noun, here in the genitive case marked by the final -i. The genitive ending typically appears after a preposition or as the second term of a construct ('after THE …'), linking 'after' to a following noun to specify what it comes after.
10.root: ب-ع-د (b-ʿ-d) — to be after, to follow, distance in place or time

11.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
11.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

12.meaning: We made it clear / explained it — to set something out plainly and distinctly, removing ambiguity so it is fully understood, with the action directed at 'it'.
12.grammar: A past-tense verb of the intensive (second) form ('to make plain'), carrying two attached pronouns: the subject 'we' (-nā) and the object 'it/him' (-hu). It states a completed action done by a 'we' upon a single masculine thing ('we made it clear').
12.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — to be clear/distinct; to separate out and make evident

13.meaning: To the people, for mankind — addressed or directed toward human beings in general; 'an-nās' is the collective word for 'people, humankind'.
13.grammar: The preposition 'li-' (to/for) joined to 'an-nās' (the people); the article's 'a' drops in pronunciation and its 'l' assimilates into the noun's 'n' (shown by the doubling). The -i ending is the genitive case, required because the word follows the preposition 'li-'. 'nās' is a collective noun for humankind with no singular of its own root form.

14.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
14.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

15.meaning: 'The Book / the Scripture' — a written record or revealed scripture; literally that which is written.
15.grammar: The definite article al- with the noun kitāb ('book, scripture'), itself a verbal noun from 'to write.' The -i ending is genitive, typically marking the word as following a preposition or standing in an 'of' relationship to a preceding noun.

16.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'those' — pointing to people or things that are distant or already known. It singles out a group ('those ones', 'it is those who').
16.grammar: A plural demonstrative pronoun, 'those'. It is fixed in form (no case endings). The -ka element signals distance/remoteness, pointing to something far off or notable. It can refer to people of either gender.

17.meaning: He/it curses them — to invoke being cut off from mercy upon them, or to expel them from grace; the action falls upon 'them' (a group).
17.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it …'), with the attached object pronoun 'them'. The -u on the verb is the indicative mood (a plain statement of present/ongoing fact); the pronoun, normally -hum, takes the form -humu to ease pronunciation before a following word.
17.root: ل-ع-ن (l-ʿ-n) — to curse; to drive away/banish from mercy

18.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
18.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
18.root: — (proper divine name)

19.meaning: And he/they curse them — the act of cursing (invoking removal from mercy) directed at 'them', joined by 'and' to a preceding statement.
19.grammar: The same present-tense verb of 'cursing' with the prefix wa- ('and') and the attached object pronoun 'them'. The -u marks the indicative mood (a plain present statement); the object pronoun appears as -humu (instead of -hum) to ease pronunciation before a following word.
19.root: ل-ع-ن (l-ʿ-n) — to curse; to drive away/banish from mercy

20.meaning: Those who curse — the ones who invoke that others be cut off from mercy; people characterized by the act of cursing.
20.grammar: A definite masculine plural active participle ('those who curse'). The prefix al- means 'the'; the -ūna ending is the sound masculine plural in the nominative case (the case for a subject or a predicate), which becomes -īna in other cases.
20.root: ل-ع-ن (l-ʿ-n) — to curse; to drive away/banish from mercy

1.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
1.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: They turned back in repentance — a third-person masculine plural past verb meaning 'they repented,' i.e. they returned to Allah, abandoning sin and re-orienting the heart toward Him.
3.grammar: Past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks the subject as 'they' (a group of males or mixed). As a perfect verb it presents the action as completed: 'they turned (back) in repentance.'

4.meaning: And they set right / reformed — they put matters into a sound, wholesome state, mending what was broken or corrupt, whether in deeds, relationships, or themselves.
4.grammar: Prefix 'wa' = 'and' (joining to what precedes). A past-tense verb of the form 'aṣlaḥa' (causative pattern), so it means to MAKE something sound/good. The -ū ending marks the subject as 'they,' and the perfect form presents the act as completed.

5.meaning: And they made clear / openly declared — they explained and disclosed plainly, leaving no ambiguity, so that the truth became evident.
5.grammar: Prefix 'wa' = 'and.' A past-tense verb in the intensive (form II) pattern 'bayyana,' conveying a thorough making-clear/explaining. The -ū ending marks the subject as 'they,' and the perfect form presents the action as completed.

6.meaning: So those / then those are the ones — a connector 'so/then' joined to a demonstrative pointing to a distant or already-mentioned group: 'those people, they (are the ones who)…'.
6.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector meaning 'so/then', often introducing a result or consequence. 'ulā'ika' is a plural demonstrative ('those') pointing to people, typically picking up a previously described group and setting them up as the subject. It is fixed in form and does not change for case.

7.meaning: I accept repentance / I turn (in forgiveness) — a first-person present verb. When said of Allah, the relevant sense is His turning toward the penitent with acceptance and pardon.
7.grammar: Present/future-tense verb. The 'a-' prefix marks the subject as 'I.' The final -u is the indicative ending, signalling an ongoing or habitual action ('I turn / I accept repentance'). From this root, the verb governs the one repented-toward and the one being forgiven.
7.root: ت-و-ب (t-w-b) — turning back, repenting; (of Allah) accepting repentance

8.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon them' or 'against them': the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over, against') joined to the plural pronoun 'them'. It conveys something resting on, being incumbent upon, or weighing against a group.
8.grammar: ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The suffix -him is the attached pronominal suffix for a masculine plural group ('them'); after a preposition it carries genitive/prepositional force, and the -i- vowel reflects its position after this preposition. Together they signal a relationship of something being over, upon, or burdensome to that group.
8.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

9.meaning: And I — the standalone first-person singular pronoun 'I,' here joined by 'and.' As a detached pronoun it stands on its own (typically as subject), unlike the attached endings.
9.grammar: Prefix 'wa' = 'and.' 'anā' is the independent (detached) pronoun 'I,' used for emphasis or to begin/identify the subject; it does not take a case ending and is fixed in form.

10.meaning: A name/quality meaning 'the One who constantly turns with forgiveness' — the Ever-Relenting, who again and again accepts the repentance of those who turn back to Him. The intensive form stresses how abundantly and repeatedly He forgives.
10.grammar: The definite article l- ('the') with a noun in the intensive pattern (faʿʿāl), which signals doing something abundantly or habitually — here, turning to forgive again and again. The -u ending marks nominative case, typical of a subject or a word describing/identifying the subject.

11.meaning: A name/quality meaning 'the Most Merciful' or 'the Bestower of mercy' — the One whose mercy is deeply felt and continually shown to His creation.
11.grammar: The definite article l- ('the') with an intensive adjective on the faʿīl pattern, conveying a deep, enduring quality of mercy. The -u ending marks nominative case, typical of a subject or of a word describing/identifying the subject.

1.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
1.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: 'They disbelieved / rejected faith' — from a root meaning to cover over or conceal. To disbelieve in this sense is to cover up and refuse the truth, and also to be ungrateful, hiding or denying favours received.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
3.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

4.meaning: And they died — a third-person masculine plural past verb: their lives came to an end.
4.grammar: Prefix 'wa' = 'and.' Past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks the subject as 'they,' and the perfect form presents the action as completed: 'they died.'

5.meaning: 'While they / and they' — the word 'wa' (here 'while' or 'and') joined to the standalone pronoun 'hum' ('they'), referring to a masculine plural group.
5.grammar: A connective 'wa' — often circumstantial 'while' — plus the independent subject pronoun 'hum' ('they'), used for a masculine plural group. As an independent pronoun it usually stands as the subject of a following statement.

6.meaning: Disbelievers / deniers (of faith) — a plural noun for those who reject faith and cover over the truth; it can also carry the intensive sense of obstinate, ungrateful concealers of the truth.
6.grammar: A plural noun in the intensive 'fuʿʿāl' pattern (suggesting deep-rooted or habitual disbelief). The -un ending (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('disbelievers') and in the nominative case, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate.
6.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — covering over, concealing; ingratitude, disbelief

7.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'those' — pointing to people or things that are distant or already known. It singles out a group ('those ones', 'it is those who').
7.grammar: A plural demonstrative pronoun, 'those'. It is fixed in form (no case endings). The -ka element signals distance/remoteness, pointing to something far off or notable. It can refer to people of either gender.

8.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon them' or 'against them': the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over, against') joined to the plural pronoun 'them'. It conveys something resting on, being incumbent upon, or weighing against a group.
8.grammar: ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The suffix -him is the attached pronominal suffix for a masculine plural group ('them'); after a preposition it carries genitive/prepositional force, and the -i- vowel reflects its position after this preposition. Together they signal a relationship of something being over, upon, or burdensome to that group.
8.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

9.meaning: The curse / condemnation — being cast away and shut out from mercy; from Allah it denotes expulsion from His grace, and from others it denotes invoking that exclusion upon someone.
9.grammar: A singular noun (the -at is its feminine ending, here pronounced before a following word). The final -u is the nominative case ending, typically marking the subject; with no nunation the word is in a 'construct' state, joining to a following noun to mean 'the curse OF …'.

10.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
10.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

11.meaning: And the angels — luminous beings created by Allah who carry out His commands. The Arabic word is a collective plural ('the angels').
11.grammar: Prefix 'wa' = 'and'; 'al-' = 'the.' A plural noun. The final -i (on the feminine ending, read -ti) is the genitive case: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF …') or follows a preposition.
11.root: م-ل-ك (m-l-k) — messengership, sending; the dominant root for 'angel' (a minority view traces it to ل-أ-ك, l-ʾ-k, message)

12.meaning: And mankind / the people — humankind, people in general. The Arabic noun is collective, denoting humanity as a body.
12.grammar: Prefix 'wa' = 'and'; 'al-' = 'the' (its 'l' assimilates into the following 'n', written al-nās, said an-nās). A collective noun for people. The final -i is the genitive case ending, typically used after a preposition or to link to a preceding noun ('… OF …').
12.root: أ-ن-س (ʾ-n-s) — sociability, familiarity, being human (a minority view traces it to ن-و-س, n-w-s)

13.meaning: All together / one and all — an emphatic word meaning the entirety of a group, every last one without exception.
13.grammar: An emphatic plural used to stress totality ('all of them, every one'). The -īna ending is the sound masculine plural in its accusative/genitive form, agreeing with a plural noun it reinforces.

1.meaning: Ones who abide / remain forever — those who dwell perpetually and permanently in a state or place, without end. The word denotes lasting, undying permanence.
1.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer' word: 'ones abiding'). The -īna ending is the sound masculine plural in its accusative/genitive form, used when the word is an object or governed by a preceding element. It describes people characterized by perpetual abiding.

2.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
2.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.

3.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
3.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

4.meaning: "it is lightened / eased" — to be made light, reduced, relieved, or alleviated (of a burden or hardship).
4.grammar: The yu- prefix with this vowel pattern marks a passive present-tense verb of the intensive (doubled-middle) form, meaning "is being lightened/eased." The final -u marks a third-person masculine singular subject in the indicative (statement) mood.

5.meaning: "from them / off them" — the preposition "from, off, away from" joined to the pronoun "them," expressing removal or relief away from a group.
5.grammar: ʿan is a preposition meaning "from / away from." The attached -hum(u) is the third-person masculine plural object pronoun "them"; its final vowel is lengthened to -u to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with "the."

6.meaning: "the punishment / torment" — a painful penalty or chastisement inflicted as retribution; suffering imposed as a consequence.
6.grammar: The al- prefix means "the." The -u ending is nominative, the case that typically marks the subject of a verb or the doer/topic of a sentence.

7.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
7.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

8.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (referring to a group of males, or a mixed group). Because it stands on its own rather than being attached to a verb or noun, it often adds emphasis, singling out or stressing the subject ('they themselves', 'it is they who').
8.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It does not take case endings; the fixed -m simply marks the plural 'they'. Standing alone, it commonly serves to emphasise or isolate the subject.

9.meaning: They are given respite / looked upon — a present-tense passive verb: they are granted a delay or reprieve (or, by the root's range, they are looked at / awaited).
9.grammar: Present-tense passive verb (the 'yu-' prefix with the internal vowel pattern signals 'is/are being …'). The -ūna ending marks the subject as 'they' (masc. pl.) and is the indicative form, indicating an ongoing or future state: 'they are (being) given respite.'
9.root: ن-ظ-ر (n-ẓ-r) — looking, observing; waiting, granting respite

1.meaning: And your god / object of worship — the deity that is worshipped. With the attached 'your (plural),' it identifies the One whom a group takes as their God.
1.grammar: Prefix 'wa' = 'and.' A noun 'ilāh' (a deity/object of worship). The -u is the nominative case ending, typically marking a subject or predicate. The attached '-kum' is the possessive 'your,' addressing a group ('your God').
1.root: أ-ل-ه (ʾ-l-h) — godhood, worship, being a deity

2.meaning: A god / an object of worship — a being taken as a deity and worshipped. As an indefinite noun it means 'a god' in the general sense.
2.grammar: A singular noun. The -un ending (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a god') and in the nominative case, typically used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate.
2.root: أ-ل-ه (ʾ-l-h) — godhood, worship, being a deity

3.meaning: One / single and unique — denoting oneness: a single individual, undivided and without partner or plurality.
3.grammar: An adjective/numeral meaning 'one.' The -un ending (nunation) marks it as indefinite and in the nominative case, the case typically used for a subject, predicate, or a descriptor agreeing with such a noun.

4.meaning: No / there is no — a negating particle. In the pattern 'lā + noun,' it gives absolute, categorical negation: 'there is no … at all.'
4.grammar: A particle of negation. Used for total denial of a class of things ('no … whatsoever'); when it governs a following indefinite noun it negates that thing absolutely. It is an indeclinable particle with no case ending of its own.

5.meaning: God / object of worship — a deity that is worshipped. The bare noun names the concept of a worshipped god.
5.grammar: A singular noun carrying an -a ending. This short -a typically marks the accusative (object) case; it is also the form a noun takes immediately after the absolute-negation particle 'lā' to mean 'no … (at all).'
5.root: أ-ل-ه (ʾ-l-h) — godhood, worship, being a deity

6.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
6.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

7.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
7.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

8.meaning: The Most Gracious / All-Merciful (al-Raḥmān) — a name of Allah from the root of mercy, in an intensive pattern denoting mercy that is vast, all-encompassing, and overflowing to all creation.
8.grammar: Prefix 'al-' = 'the' (its 'l' assimilates into the 'r', written al-raḥmān, said ar-raḥmān). An intensive noun-form expressing immense, overflowing mercy. The final -u is the nominative case ending, typically marking a subject, predicate, or name in apposition to such.

9.meaning: The Most Merciful / Ever-Merciful (al-Raḥīm) — a name of Allah from the root of mercy, in a pattern denoting constant, enduring mercy that is actively bestowed.
9.grammar: Prefix 'al-' = 'the' (its 'l' assimilates into the 'r', said ar-raḥīm). A 'faʿīl' adjective-form denoting an enduring, established quality of mercy. The final -u is the nominative case ending, typically marking a subject, predicate, or descriptor of such.

1.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
1.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

2.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
2.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

3.meaning: Creation / the act of creating — the bringing of things into existence, or the created order that results; also denotes how something is fashioned or formed.
3.grammar: A verbal noun ('creating / creation'). The final -i is the genitive case ending: it typically links the word to a following noun ('the creation OF …') or follows a preposition.

4.meaning: The heavens / the skies — the plural of 'heaven', referring to the skies above and the celestial realms; the elevated expanse over the earth.
4.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun with the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the heavens') or follows a preposition. In the sound feminine plural, this -i form also covers what would be an object role.

5.meaning: 'And the earth' — the connective 'and' joined to 'the earth', meaning the ground, land, or the world beneath the sky.
5.grammar: The connective 'wa-' ('and') with the definite feminine noun 'al-arḍ' ('the earth'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the earth') or follows a preposition, here matching the case of what it is joined to.

6.meaning: And the alternation / difference — variation and succession one after another (as with turns of night and day), or divergence and disagreement between things.
6.grammar: Prefix 'wa' = 'and.' A verbal noun (form VIII 'ikhtilāf') meaning succession/alternation or divergence. The final -i is the genitive case ending, typically linking to a following noun ('the alternation OF …') or following a preposition.

7.meaning: The night — the period of darkness from sunset to dawn.
7.grammar: Prefix 'al-' = 'the' (its 'l' merges with the word's initial 'l', said al-layl). A noun for night-time. The final -i is the genitive case ending, typically used after a preposition or to link to a preceding noun ('… OF the night').

8.meaning: And the day / daytime — the period of light from dawn to sunset.
8.grammar: Prefix 'wa' = 'and'; 'al-' = 'the' (its 'l' assimilates into the 'n', said an-nahār). A noun for the daylight hours. The final -i is the genitive case ending, typically used after a preposition or to link to a preceding noun ('… OF the day').

9.meaning: And the ships, sea-going vessels. The base noun 'fulk' is unusual in that it serves as both singular ('ship') and plural ('ships') without changing form, and works for both masculine and feminine.
9.grammar: A definite noun ('the …') carried by the connector 'wa' ('and'). The final -i ending is genitive. Here the genitive is governed by a preposition that applies across this coordinated list of nouns, so the noun joined by 'wa' carries the same genitive case.
9.root: ف-ل-ك (f-l-k) — to be round; a ship; a celestial orbit/sphere

10.meaning: A feminine singular relative pronoun: 'the one which / that which / who' (referring to a single feminine thing). It introduces a descriptive clause that tells us more about a preceding feminine noun.
10.grammar: A relative pronoun, feminine singular, fixed in form (it does not change for case). It links a feminine noun to a following clause describing it, the equivalent of English 'which,' 'that,' or 'who.'

11.meaning: A verb 'it flows, runs, streams' — used of water and rivers moving along, and of things that run or course freely. It describes continuous, ongoing motion.
11.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, 3rd person feminine singular. The ta- prefix here marks a feminine 'it/she' subject. The verb describes an ongoing or habitual action: 'it flows / keeps flowing.'

12.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
12.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

13.meaning: The sea, the great body of salt water; figuratively any vast expanse of water.
13.grammar: A definite singular masculine noun ('the …'). The final -i ending is genitive, the case taken after a preposition or when a noun is possessed by a preceding noun ('… of the sea').

14.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
14.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

15.meaning: He/it benefits, profits, or brings advantage to someone; to be of use.
15.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he' or 'it'). The final -u ending is the indicative mood, used for a plain, ongoing or habitual statement of fact ('benefits / is benefiting').

16.meaning: Mankind, humanity, people in general — the collective of human beings.
16.grammar: A definite noun ('the people') with the attached 'al-' ('the'). The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'n' (a sun letter), which is why the 'n' is doubled — this is a pronunciation effect, not a separate piece. The final '-a' ending is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb (the one being acted upon) or the subject of certain particles.
16.root: ن-و-س (n-w-s) — to move/sway; by extension, people

17.meaning: And what / and that which. Combines the connective 'and' with mā, a word that can mean 'what / that which', or function as a negating particle ('not'), depending on usage.
17.grammar: The connective wa- ('and') joined to mā, an indeclinable particle (it never changes its ending). It serves either as a relative/interrogative 'what' or as a negation 'not', so its sense is fixed by context rather than by a case ending.

18.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'he sent down, he caused to descend, he revealed' — used especially of Allah sending down revelation, rain, or blessings from above.
18.grammar: A completed (past) action by a single masculine subject ('he'); the -a ending marks third-person masculine singular. The form IV (causative) pattern means 'to make something come down,' i.e., to send it down.
18.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — coming down, descending, alighting

19.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
19.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

20.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
20.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

21.meaning: The sky or heaven — the canopy overhead; the expanse above the earth, also that which is elevated or raised over something. With the definite article it means 'the sky / the heaven'.
21.grammar: A noun with the definite article al- ('the'), in the genitive marked by the -i ending. (The 'l' of al- assimilates in sound into the following 's', a 'sun letter', though it is still written.) The genitive -i ending typically appears after a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …').

22.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
22.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

23.meaning: Water, the life-giving fluid; rain or any liquid that sustains.
23.grammar: An indefinite singular noun ('water / some water'). The -in ending (nunation) marks it as indefinite and is the genitive case form, taken after a preposition or when a noun follows another in an 'of' relationship.

24.meaning: And so He gave life, revived, brought to life what was lifeless; the causative sense 'to make alive'.
24.grammar: A past-tense verb introduced by 'fa' ('and so / then', often signalling a result or sequence). The verb is third-person masculine singular ('he gave life'); the prefixed 'a' belongs to the causative (Form IV) pattern, turning 'to live' into 'to give life'.
24.root: ح-ي-ي (ḥ-y-y) — life, to live

25.meaning: By it, with it, through it; the preposition 'bi' (with/by means of) joined to a pronoun referring to something previously mentioned.
25.grammar: A preposition plus an attached third-person masculine singular pronoun ('it / him'). 'Bi' conveys instrument or means ('by means of it'); the pronoun takes the -i vowel because words governed by 'bi' stand in the genitive.

26.meaning: 'the earth,' 'the ground,' 'the land' — the earth as a whole, or the land/ground beneath us. It denotes the terrestrial expanse on which creatures live and walk.
26.grammar: A definite noun ('the earth'). The '-a' ending marks the accusative (the 'object' case) — the role of the thing acted upon, e.g. the direct object of a verb. The prefixed 'al-' makes it definite, 'the earth.'

27.meaning: After; following in time or order — the point or moment subsequent to something.
27.grammar: An adverb of time functioning much like a preposition ('after'). It is fixed in the accusative form ending in -a, and is normally followed by a noun in the 'of' relationship, giving 'after (the) …'.
27.root: ب-ع-د (b-ʿ-d) — afterness, that which comes later; distance/remoteness

28.meaning: Its death, its lifelessness or dormancy; the state of being dead, joined to a possessor.
28.grammar: A noun ('death') with an attached third-person feminine singular possessive pronoun ('its / her'). The -i vowel on the noun is genitive, the case taken before a possessor pronoun and after prepositions ('death of it').

29.meaning: And He scattered, spread, or dispersed abroad; to send creatures or things out in all directions.
29.grammar: A past-tense verb joined by 'wa' ('and'). It is third-person masculine singular ('he scattered'); the bare ending with no added suffix is the default form for a completed action done by 'he'.
29.root: ب-ث-ث (b-th-th) — to scatter, spread, disseminate

30.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
30.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.
30.root: — (particle plus pronoun; no root)

31.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
31.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
31.root: — (preposition)

32.meaning: Every, each, the whole/totality of — a word expressing that something applies to all members of a group, or to the entirety of a thing, depending on what follows it.
32.grammar: A noun meaning 'every/all'. The final -i is the genitive ending, which here marks it as joined to a following noun ('every … / all OF …') or as governed by a preceding preposition.

33.meaning: A moving creature, a living thing that treads or walks the earth; any animal that moves of its own accord.
33.grammar: An indefinite singular feminine noun ('a creature'); the -at- syllable is the feminine marker. The -in ending (nunation) signals indefiniteness and is the genitive case, taken after prepositions or in an 'of' linkage.
33.root: د-ب-ب (d-b-b) — to move/creep along, to tread the ground

34.meaning: And the directing, turning about, or steering this way and that; the act of varying and managing something's course (a verbal noun from the causative).
34.grammar: A verbal noun (the action of 'directing/turning') joined by 'wa' ('and'). The taF-…-īl pattern names the action of the Form II (intensive) verb. The final -i ending is genitive, taken after prepositions and when one noun governs a following noun ('the directing of …').
34.root: ص-ر-ف (ṣ-r-f) — to turn, divert, change direction

35.meaning: The winds, moving currents of air.
35.grammar: A definite plural noun ('the winds'): the definite article 'al-' assimilates to the following sun-letter 'r' (so it is written and pronounced 'ar-r'), attached to the noun stem 'riyāḥ'. The final -i ending is genitive, taken after a preposition or when the noun is possessed by a preceding noun ('… of the winds').

36.meaning: And the clouds, the gathered masses of vapour that bring rain.
36.grammar: A definite noun ('the cloud(s)', a collective) carried by 'wa' ('and'). The definite article 'al-' assimilates to the following sun-letter 's' (pronounced 'as-s'). The final -i ending is genitive, taken after prepositions or in an 'of' relationship with a preceding noun.
36.root: س-ح-ب (s-ḥ-b) — to drag/draw along; clouds (drawn across the sky)

37.meaning: The one made subservient, harnessed, or pressed into service; something compelled to function under another's command.
37.grammar: A definite passive participle ('the one that is made subservient'). The mu-…-a- shape with the doubled middle root letter marks the Form II passive participle, describing the receiver of the action. The final -i ending is genitive, agreeing with a preceding genitive noun and following prepositions.
37.root: س-خ-ر (s-kh-r) — to subject, harness, press into service

38.meaning: Between; in the midst of two things. An adverb of place marking the space separating or lying among parties or points.
38.grammar: An adverb of place ('between'). It always ends in -a and grammatically governs what follows it, putting the following noun(s) into the genitive 'of' relationship. It does not change to show 'the' or a case of its own; the fixed -a is simply how this word is formed.
38.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies between

39.meaning: The sky or heaven — the canopy overhead; the expanse above the earth, also that which is elevated or raised over something. With the definite article it means 'the sky / the heaven'.
39.grammar: A noun with the definite article al- ('the'), in the genitive marked by the -i ending. (The 'l' of al- assimilates in sound into the following 's', a 'sun letter', though it is still written.) The genitive -i ending typically appears after a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …').

40.meaning: 'And the earth' — the connective 'and' joined to 'the earth', meaning the ground, land, or the world beneath the sky.
40.grammar: The connective 'wa-' ('and') with the definite feminine noun 'al-arḍ' ('the earth'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the earth') or follows a preposition, here matching the case of what it is joined to.
40.root: أ-ر-ض (ʾ-r-ḍ) — earth, land

41.meaning: Surely signs, tokens, or clear indications; evidences that point to a greater truth. The prefixed lām adds emphasis ('surely / indeed').
41.grammar: An emphatic particle 'la-' ('surely') joined to an indefinite feminine plural noun ('signs'). The -āt- is the sound feminine plural marker; the final -in (nunation) marks it indefinite. For this plural pattern the -in form serves for both the accusative and the genitive case.

42.meaning: For a people, for a folk or community; a group of human beings considered together. Joined to the preposition 'li' ('for / to').
42.grammar: The preposition 'li' ('for / to') plus an indefinite singular noun ('a people'). The -in ending (nunation) marks indefiniteness; it is the genitive form, required because nouns governed by 'li' stand in the genitive.
42.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; a people/community

43.meaning: They use their reason, they understand and reflect; to grasp things with the intellect and restrain oneself accordingly.
43.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ya- prefix together with the -ūna ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'). The -na ending also signals the indicative mood, used for a plain statement of ongoing or habitual action ('they use reason').
43.root: ع-ق-ل (ʿ-q-l) — to reason, understand; to restrain (as a tether restrains)

1.meaning: A connector meaning 'and', joined to the preposition 'from / of', introducing a portion or origin — 'and from' or 'and among'.
1.grammar: Two particles: wa- ('and') plus the preposition min ('from, of, among'). Min normally appears as 'min', but its final vowel shifts to 'mina' when the next word begins with the definite article, simply to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

2.meaning: Humankind, people, mankind — the collective of human beings.
2.grammar: A collective noun ('people, mankind') carrying the definite article al- ('the'); the 'l' of the article assimilates into the following 'n', doubling it (al-nās → an-nās). The genitive ending -i marks the word as governed by a preposition or as the second term of a possessive.
2.root: ء-ن-س (ʾ-n-s) — humankind, sociability, familiarity; the word for 'people' is most commonly traced to this root (related to insān, 'human being')

3.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
3.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

4.meaning: He takes for himself, adopts, or sets up something as his own; to seize upon and make into something.
4.grammar: A present-tense verb of the Form VIII pattern, which often carries a reflexive sense (taking something for oneself). The ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'). The final -u ending is the indicative mood, used for a plain statement of ongoing or habitual action.

5.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
5.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

6.meaning: A noun used to mean 'besides', 'other than', 'apart from', or 'short of'. It points to something or someone set apart from, or lower/lesser than, a named party. Often used in the phrase 'besides Allah'.
6.grammar: 'dūn' functions as an adverb-like noun of place/relation. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, which appears because it follows a preposition (such as 'min', 'from') and because it links to a following noun ('other than …'). It commonly heads the construction 'besides/other than [someone]'.
6.root: د-و-ن (d-w-n) — to be low/beneath, to fall short; hence 'below, other than, besides'

7.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
7.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

8.meaning: The plural of 'nidd': 'rivals', 'equals', or 'peers' — things set up as comparable or equal to something else, especially false objects of worship set up alongside Allah.
8.grammar: 'andād' is a broken (irregular) plural of 'nidd'. The '-an' ending (tanwīn al-fatḥ) marks an indefinite noun in the accusative case, the case typically used for the direct object of a verb ('… some rivals').
8.root: ن-د-د (n-d-d) — to be equal/rival, a counterpart or match

9.meaning: They love them; to feel deep affection or devotion toward others. Combines the verb 'they love' with an object 'them'.
9.grammar: A present-tense verb with an attached object pronoun. The yu- prefix plus -ūna ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they') in the indicative mood (a plain factual statement); the yu- vowel is the marker of the Form IV (causative) pattern of this verb (root doubled, 'aḥabba / yuḥibbu'). The final 'hum' is the object pronoun 'them'.

10.meaning: Like the love of, as one loves; a comparison built on the noun 'love'. The prefixed 'ka' means 'like / as'.
10.grammar: The comparison particle 'ka' ('like / as') joined to the noun 'love'. The final -i ending is genitive, required because a noun after 'ka' (and before a following possessor, 'love of …') stands in the genitive.

11.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
11.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

12.meaning: 'And those who': a connective phrase introducing a specified group of people (masculine plural) about whom something will be said. It links them to what came before.
12.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'), which is masculine plural. A relative pronoun stands for a group and is normally followed by a clause describing them. Its form does not change for case; it stays alladhīna whatever its grammatical role.

13.meaning: They believed, they came to faith; to place trust and security in something and affirm it as true (the inner act of faith).
13.grammar: A past-tense verb of the Form IV (causative) pattern. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they') for a completed action ('they believed'). The final written alif after the wāw is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

14.meaning: 'Harder / more intense / stronger.' A comparative meaning something is greater in hardness, severity, force, or intensity than what it is compared with; the base sense is being firm, severe, and strong.
14.grammar: A comparative/superlative adjective ('more severe / harder'). The -u ending is the nominative case, which typically marks the word as the subject or as the descriptive predicate of the subject. Built on the 'afʿal' pattern used for comparisons ('more …').
14.root: ش-د-د (sh-d-d) — to be firm, intense, severe, strong

15.meaning: Love, ardent affection or devotion, presented as an indefinite noun (often answering 'how much?' or 'in what manner?').
15.grammar: An indefinite singular noun ('love'). The -an ending (nunation) marks it indefinite and is the accusative case, which often marks the object of a verb or specifies degree, manner, or respect ('in love / as to love').

16.meaning: A combination 'to/for Allah / belonging to Allah' — the preposition 'to/for' joined to the name Allah, expressing that something is due to, owned by, or directed toward Allah.
16.grammar: The prefix li- is the preposition 'to / for / belonging to'. 'Allah' follows, with the initial alif of 'Allāh' elided after li-. The final -i is the genitive ending required after a preposition; it marks Allah as the One to whom something belongs or is directed.

17.meaning: 'and if' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the particle 'if'. This particular 'if' (law) introduces a hypothetical or contrary-to-fact condition: 'if (such-and-such had been the case)…', often implying it was not.
17.grammar: A conjunction plus a conditional particle. wa- means 'and'. law is a non-changing particle (no case ending) that sets up a supposition, typically answered by a clause beginning with la- ('… then certainly …').

18.meaning: He sees, perceives with the eye; also to realize or come to know. Can carry the sense 'were he to see / would see'.
18.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'). This is a weak-ending verb whose final long -ā stands in for the mood vowel; it functions as a plain present statement ('he sees').
18.root: ر-ا-ي (r-ʾ-y) — to see, perceive, consider

19.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
19.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

20.meaning: They wronged, did injustice, or oppressed; to put something out of its rightful place, especially to harm others or oneself unjustly.
20.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they') for a completed action ('they wronged'). The final written alif after the wāw is a silent spelling convention, not pronounced.

21.meaning: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the time that', used to point back to a past moment or event and introduce a recollection of something that occurred.
21.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). It signals a point in past time, typically introducing a clause that recalls 'the time when' something happened.

22.meaning: They see, they perceive; also to realize or witness. Looking upon something with the eyes or the understanding.
22.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ya- prefix together with the -na ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'). The -na ending is the indicative mood, used for a plain statement of fact ('they see / they will see').

23.meaning: The punishment, chastisement, or torment — a penalty inflicted as retribution, especially the painful suffering of divine reckoning.
23.grammar: A definite masculine noun ('the punishment'). The final -a is the accusative ending, which generally marks the word as the direct object of a verb or the subject/predicate after certain particles.
23.root: ع-ذ-ب (ʿ-dh-b) — to punish, torment; the inflicting of pain

24.meaning: An emphatic particle meaning 'that' (as in 'I know that...') or 'indeed/surely.' It introduces a statement and gives it certainty and emphasis, presenting what follows as an established fact.
24.grammar: An emphatic particle that introduces a noun-clause ('that...'). It puts the following noun into the accusative case and lends the whole statement a sense of certainty and assertion. It typically comes after verbs of knowing, saying, or informing.

25.meaning: Power, strength, might, or force — the capacity to exert oneself and prevail; firmness and vigor.
25.grammar: A definite feminine noun ('the power'). The feminine ending is the tā' marbūṭa, which in the accusative is pronounced as a full -t- carrying the case vowel -a (quwwat-a); the -t- of the tā' marbūṭa and the accusative vowel are inseparable. The accusative generally marks the word as a direct object or as the subject/predicate following certain particles.
25.root: ق-و-ي (q-w-y) — to be strong; strength, might

26.meaning: A two-part word: the preposition 'li-' meaning 'to', 'for', or 'belonging to', attached to the name 'Allah'. It conveys 'to Allah' or 'for Allah'.
26.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('to/for') pulls the following noun into the genitive case, which is why 'Allah' ends in '-i' (llāhi). The '-i' ending is the regular result of a noun governed by a preposition.

27.meaning: A word meaning 'all together', 'all of them', or 'the whole lot' — emphasising that no one and nothing is left out of a group.
27.grammar: A noun meaning 'all/entirety' carrying the -an ending: accusative case with tanwīn (the indefinite '-n'). This accusative form is typical of a word that comes alongside another to specify it as 'all of them, every one', describing the manner or extent.
27.root: ج-م-ع (j-m-ʿ) — gathering, joining, bringing together

28.meaning: 'And that …' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the particle anna, which introduces and emphasizes a statement, asserting a fact emphatically (roughly 'and indeed that …'), and grammatically governs the noun that follows it.
28.grammar: A conjunction wa ('and') prefixed to anna, an emphatic particle meaning 'that' (asserting a fact). Anna puts the following noun into the accusative case and typically links a clause to a preceding verb of saying, knowing, or perceiving.

29.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
29.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.
29.root: — (proper name)

30.meaning: Severe, intense, harsh, or mighty — describing something powerful and unsparing in its degree.
30.grammar: An adjective on the intensive pattern faʿīl ('severe, intense'). The final -u is the nominative ending, which generally marks the word as a subject or predicate.
30.root: ش-د-د (sh-d-d) — to be strong, intense, severe

31.meaning: The punishment, torment, or chastisement — severe penalty or suffering inflicted as retribution.
31.grammar: A singular masculine noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending is the genitive, which typically links it to a preceding noun ('… of the punishment') or follows a preposition.
31.root: ع-ذ-ب (ʿ-dh-b) — to punish, torment

1.meaning: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the time that', used to point back to a past moment or event and introduce a recollection of something that occurred.
1.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). It signals a point in past time, typically introducing a clause that recalls 'the time when' something happened.

2.meaning: He disowned, renounced, or declared himself quit of someone or something — distancing oneself entirely and cutting off all allegiance, washing one's hands of it.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb (Form V), third-person masculine singular ('he disowned / freed himself of'). The Form V pattern (ta- prefix with doubled middle root letter) often carries a reflexive sense — making oneself free or clear of something. The bare ending with no suffix marks 'he' as the doer.
2.root: ب-ر-ء (b-r-ʾ) — to be free, clear, quit of

3.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
3.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

4.meaning: They were followed — others came after them, took them as guides, or obeyed and imitated them.
4.grammar: A past-tense passive verb (Form VIII), third-person masculine plural ('they were followed'). The passive vowel pattern (u-i) shows the subject received the action rather than performed it; the -ū ending marks a masculine plural 'they' as the ones affected.
4.root: ت-ب-ع (t-b-ʿ) — to follow, come after, pursue

5.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
5.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

6.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
6.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

7.meaning: They followed — they came after, pursued, took as a guide, or obeyed and imitated someone or something.
7.grammar: A past-tense active verb (Form VIII), third-person masculine plural ('they followed'). The -ū ending marks a masculine plural 'they' as the doers of the action.
7.root: ت-ب-ع (t-b-ʿ) — to follow, come after, pursue

8.meaning: 'And they saw' — joined with 'and', a verb meaning that they perceived something with the eyes or beheld and witnessed it.
8.grammar: The conjunction wa ('and') prefixed to a past-tense verb from 'to see', third-person masculine plural ('they saw'). The plural 'they' ending marks a masculine group as the doers of the seeing.

9.meaning: The punishment, chastisement, or torment — a penalty inflicted as retribution, especially the painful suffering of divine reckoning.
9.grammar: A definite masculine noun ('the punishment'). The final -a is the accusative ending, which generally marks the word as the direct object of a verb or the subject/predicate after certain particles.
9.root: ع-ذ-ب (ʿ-dh-b) — to punish, torment; the inflicting of pain

10.meaning: 'And it was cut off / severed' — joined with 'and', a verb meaning that bonds or connections were torn apart, broken up, and severed completely.
10.grammar: The conjunction wa ('and') prefixed to a past-tense verb (Form V), third-person feminine singular ('it was cut off'). Form V here gives an intensive/reflexive sense of being utterly severed; the -at ending marks a feminine singular subject (which in Arabic includes non-human plurals).
10.root: ق-ط-ع (q-ṭ-ʿ) — to cut, sever, cut off

11.meaning: 'By/with them' or 'for them' — the preposition bi ('with, by, through, for') joined to the attached pronoun 'them' (a masculine group).
