11.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
11.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

12.meaning: You mix with, mingle, and share dealings with them — to intermix your affairs and company closely with others.
12.grammar: A present-tense verb of the Form III 'mufāʿala' (mutual/interactive) pattern, conveying doing something together with others. The tu- prefix marks a second-person masculine plural subject ('you all'), and the suffix -hum is the object 'them'. The form lacks the final -na, which usually happens when a preceding particle puts the verb in the subjunctive or jussive ('that you mix with them' / 'if you mix with them').

13.meaning: 'Then they are your brothers' — kinsfolk or brethren who belong to your own group, here a plural 'brothers' joined to 'your'.
13.grammar: A plural noun with the prefix fa- ('then, so', often introducing a result) and the attached pronoun -kum ('your', addressing a group), which makes it definite by possession. The -u before the pronoun reflects the nominative case, used here for a predicate ('they are your brothers').

14.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
14.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
14.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

15.meaning: 'He/it knows' — a present-tense verb of knowing: to have knowledge of, be aware of, recognize, or understand something.
15.grammar: Present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it'). The ya- prefix marks 'he,' and the final -u marks the ordinary (indicative) present, 'he knows / does know.'
15.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — knowledge; knowing, being aware, recognizing

16.meaning: The one who corrupts and spreads ruin — a wrongdoer who causes disorder, spoilage, and harm.
16.grammar: An active participle of the Form IV (if'āl, causative) pattern, naming the doer of corruption, with the definite article al- ('the'). The final -a ending marks the accusative case, typically used for the object of a verb ('[Allah knows] the corrupter').
16.root: ف-س-د (f-s-d) — to be corrupt, to spoil

17.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
17.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

18.meaning: The one who sets right and reforms — a doer of good who repairs, improves, and restores soundness.
18.grammar: An active participle of the Form IV (if'āl, causative) pattern, naming the doer of reform, with the definite article al- ('the'). The final -i ending is genitive, typically marking the word as linked to a preceding noun ('… OF …') or as governed by a preposition.
18.root: ص-ل-ح (ṣ-l-ḥ) — to be good, sound; to set right

19.meaning: 'and if' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the particle 'if'. This particular 'if' (law) introduces a hypothetical or contrary-to-fact condition: 'if (such-and-such had been the case)…', often implying it was not.
19.grammar: A conjunction plus a conditional particle. wa- means 'and'. law is a non-changing particle (no case ending) that sets up a supposition, typically answered by a clause beginning with la- ('… then certainly …').

20.meaning: A past-tense verb 'he willed / he wished / he so desired'. It denotes an act of will or volition bringing something about.
20.grammar: Past-tense (perfect) verb, third person masculine singular ('he'). The bare stem with no suffix is the basic 'he did' form. Its subject and object are typically supplied by context.

21.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
21.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

22.meaning: 'He would surely have burdened you with hardship' — to impose distress, strain, and difficulty on someone; the root sense is hardship and exhausting trouble.
22.grammar: A past-tense verb of the Form IV (causative) pattern ('to cause hardship') preceded by the emphatic la- ('surely'), which often answers a hypothetical 'if'. The verb's bare form (no subject suffix) marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'), and the suffix -kum is the object 'you all'.

23.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
23.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

24.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
24.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.
24.root: — (proper name)

25.meaning: Mighty, invincible, and supremely honoured; one who possesses overwhelming power and dignity such that none can overcome or resist Him. As a divine descriptor it conveys unassailable might joined with exalted worth.
25.grammar: A descriptive noun (adjective) on an intensive pattern, conveying a deep, enduring quality. The -un ending is indefinite and nominative: it typically marks the word as a subject or as a predicate describing something ("is mighty").

26.meaning: All-Wise: possessing perfect wisdom — placing everything in its right place with flawless knowledge, judgment, and purpose. As a divine attribute it denotes Allah's consummate wisdom.
26.grammar: A masculine singular adjective/intensive noun on the faʿīl pattern, expressing a deep, settled quality of wisdom. The final -un (nunation) marks it as indefinite and nominative — the case used for a subject or, very often, a predicate describing the doer ('[He is] All-Wise').
26.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to judge, to be wise

1.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
1.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

2.meaning: A jussive/subjunctive form of the verb 'to marry' / 'to take in marriage', addressed to a group of men. From the root meaning to wed or contract marriage; commonly governs a following object (the woman married).
2.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) verb, 2nd-person masculine plural ('you all'). The ta- prefix with the -ū ending marks 'you (men) do'. The dropped final nūn (tankiḥū, not tankiḥūna) shows the verb is in the jussive/subjunctive mood — the mood used after negative commands ('do not …') or conditional/result particles.
2.root: ن-ك-ح (n-k-ḥ) — to marry, wed, contract marriage

3.meaning: Women who associate partners with Allah — idolatresses or polytheist women; the feminine plural of one who commits shirk (ascribing divinity to other than Allah).
3.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun/participle ('the idolatresses'). The -āt- marks the sound feminine plural; the final -i is the case ending that sound feminine plurals take in both the genitive (after a preposition or in an 'of …' link) and the accusative (as a direct object). Derived from form-IV active participle 'one who associates (partners with Allah)'.
3.root: ش-ر-ك (sh-r-k) — to share, associate; here associating partners with Allah (shirk)

4.meaning: 'Until / up to the point that; so that' — a particle marking a limit or goal. It expresses the end-point reached ('until') or the purpose aimed at ('so that, in order that').
4.grammar: A particle indicating a goal or limit. When followed by a present-tense verb it places that verb in the subjunctive mood (clipping its ending to -a), conveying 'until / so that' something comes about. Ḥattā itself is invariable.

5.meaning: 'They (feminine) believe' — to have faith, specifically faith in Allah; a present-tense verb describing a group of women's believing.
5.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) verb, 3rd-person feminine plural ('they/the women believe'). The combination of the yu- prefix and the heavy -na ending (doubling the nūn) marks a group of females as the subject. This feminine-plural ending stays fixed and is not dropped for mood. From form IV (a-mana), 'to believe, have faith'.
5.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — safety, trust; form IV: to believe, have faith

6.meaning: 'And a bondwoman / female slave' — a woman owned in servitude. Often introduced emphatically ('and surely a bondwoman …').
6.grammar: A singular feminine noun ('a female slave'), prefixed by 'and' plus an emphatic la- ('surely'). The final -un (nunation/tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('a …') and in the nominative case — the case used for the subject of a sentence or, after the emphatic la-, for a noun being highlighted.
6.root: ء-م-و (ʾ-m-w) — bondage, servitude; ama = female slave

7.meaning: 'Believing / faithful (woman)' — a feminine adjective/participle describing one who has faith in Allah.
7.grammar: A feminine singular active participle ('a believing woman'). The mu- prefix forms the doer of a form-IV verb (one who believes). The final -un (tanwīn) marks it indefinite and nominative — the case for a subject or for a description matching an indefinite nominative noun.
7.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — safety, trust; form IV: to believe, have faith

8.meaning: 'Better / best; good' — an adjective of comparison meaning more good, preferable, or superior. It also serves broadly for 'goodness' and that which is good and beneficial.
8.grammar: A noun/adjective bearing the ending -un (nunation): the doubled-u 'n' sound marks the word as both indefinite ('a/an', no 'the') and nominative — the case used for the subject of a sentence or the predicate that describes it.
8.root: خ-ي-ر (kh-y-r) — good, goodness, that which is choice and beneficial

9.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
9.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

10.meaning: 'A woman who associates partners with Allah' — an idolatress/polytheist woman (singular).
10.grammar: A feminine singular active participle ('an idolatress'). The mu- prefix marks the doer of a form-IV action. The final -in (tanwīn) marks it indefinite and in the genitive case — the case used after a preposition or in a comparison/'of …' relationship.
10.root: ش-ر-ك (sh-r-k) — to share, associate; shirk = associating partners with Allah

11.meaning: 'And even if / and though' — a particle pairing 'and' with 'law', which introduces a hypothetical or concessive condition ('even supposing that …').
11.grammar: A compound particle: 'and' + the conditional 'law'. 'Law' introduces a supposition, often a counter-to-expectation one ('even if …'), and is typically followed by a past-tense verb that carries a hypothetical sense. It is a function word with no case ending.

12.meaning: 'She pleased you / impressed you' — the verb 'to please, delight, impress' (to cause wonder or admiration), with a feminine subject acting upon a group of men.
12.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb. The -at ending marks a feminine singular subject ('she did'), and the attached -kum is the object pronoun 'you all (men)'. From form IV (aʿjaba), 'to please/impress someone' — literally to make someone wonder or admire.
12.root: ع-ج-ب (ʿ-j-b) — wonder, amazement; form IV: to please, impress

13.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
13.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

14.meaning: A jussive/subjunctive form of 'to give in marriage / to wed (someone) to another' — the causative of marrying, i.e. to marry off one's womenfolk; addressed to a group of men.

parts.en: give in marriage, marry (someone) off (form-IV stem)

14.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) verb, 2nd-person masculine plural ('you all'), in the form-IV (causative) pattern — note the tu- prefix (vs. ta-), giving the sense 'cause to marry / marry off'. The missing final nūn (tunkiḥū, not tunkiḥūna) shows jussive/subjunctive mood, used after negative commands or conditional/result particles.
14.root: ن-ك-ح (n-k-ḥ) — to marry; form IV: to give in marriage, marry off

15.meaning: Those who associate partners with Allah — idolaters / polytheists who set up others alongside the one God in worship or devotion.
15.grammar: An active participle used as a noun, with 'the', in the masculine sound plural. The -īna ending marks the plural in the genitive/accusative case — the form used after a preposition or as the object of a verb.

16.meaning: 'Until / up to the point that; so that' — a particle marking a limit or goal. It expresses the end-point reached ('until') or the purpose aimed at ('so that, in order that').
16.grammar: A particle indicating a goal or limit. When followed by a present-tense verb it places that verb in the subjunctive mood (clipping its ending to -a), conveying 'until / so that' something comes about. Ḥattā itself is invariable.

17.meaning: 'They (masculine) believe' — to have faith in Allah; a present-tense verb with a masculine-plural subject.
17.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) verb, 3rd-person masculine plural ('they believe'). The yu- prefix with the -ū ending marks 'they (men) do'. The dropped final nūn (yu'minū, not yu'minūna) shows the jussive/subjunctive mood — used after conditional or negative-command particles. From form IV, 'to believe'.
17.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — safety, trust; form IV: to believe, have faith

18.meaning: 'And a bondman / male slave' — a man held in servitude. Often introduced emphatically ('and surely a slave …'). Also bears the broader sense of 'servant (of Allah)'.
18.grammar: A singular masculine noun ('a slave/servant'), prefixed by 'and' plus an emphatic la- ('surely'). The final -un (tanwīn) marks it indefinite ('a …') and in the nominative case — used for a subject or for a noun highlighted after the emphatic la-.
18.root: ع-ب-د (ʿ-b-d) — to serve, worship; ʿabd = slave, servant

19.meaning: 'Believing / faithful (man)' — a masculine adjective/participle for one who has faith in Allah.

parts.en: believing, faithful (masculine active participle) + indefinite nominative '-un'

19.grammar: A masculine singular active participle ('a believing man'). The mu- prefix forms the doer of a form-IV verb (one who believes). The final -un (tanwīn) marks it indefinite and nominative — the case for a subject or a description matching an indefinite nominative noun.
19.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — safety, trust; form IV: to believe, have faith

20.meaning: 'Better / best; good' — an adjective of comparison meaning more good, preferable, or superior. It also serves broadly for 'goodness' and that which is good and beneficial.
20.grammar: A noun/adjective bearing the ending -un (nunation): the doubled-u 'n' sound marks the word as both indefinite ('a/an', no 'the') and nominative — the case used for the subject of a sentence or the predicate that describes it.
20.root: خ-ي-ر (kh-y-r) — good, goodness, that which is choice and beneficial

21.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
21.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

22.meaning: 'A man who associates partners with Allah' — an idolater/polytheist (singular masculine).

parts.en: associating partners (with Allah), idolater + indefinite genitive '-in'

22.grammar: A masculine singular active participle ('an idolater'). The mu- prefix marks the doer of a form-IV action. The final -in (tanwīn) marks it indefinite and in the genitive case — used after a preposition or in an 'of …'/comparison relationship.
22.root: ش-ر-ك (sh-r-k) — to share, associate; shirk = associating partners with Allah

23.meaning: 'And even if / and though' — a particle pairing 'and' with 'law', which introduces a hypothetical or concessive condition ('even supposing that …').
23.grammar: A compound particle: 'and' + the conditional 'law'. 'Law' introduces a supposition, often a counter-to-expectation one ('even if …'), and is typically followed by a past-tense verb that carries a hypothetical sense. It is a function word with no case ending.

24.meaning: 'He pleased you / impressed you' — the verb 'to please, delight, impress', with a masculine subject acting upon a group of men.
24.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb, 3rd-person masculine singular subject ('he did' — shown by the bare aʿjaba with no added subject suffix). The attached -kum is the object pronoun 'you all (men)'. From form IV (aʿjaba), 'to please/impress' — literally to make one wonder or admire.
24.root: ع-ج-ب (ʿ-j-b) — wonder, amazement; form IV: to please, impress

25.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'those' — pointing to people or things that are distant or already known. It singles out a group ('those ones', 'it is those who').
25.grammar: A plural demonstrative pronoun, 'those'. It is fixed in form (no case endings). The -ka element signals distance/remoteness, pointing to something far off or notable. It can refer to people of either gender.

26.meaning: 'They call / invite / summon' — to call upon, invite, or summon (also to pray to or call out to); a present-tense verb with a masculine-plural subject.
26.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) verb, 3rd-person masculine plural ('they call/invite'). The ya- prefix with the full -ūna ending marks 'they (men) do' and shows the indicative mood — the plain statement form ('they do'), with its final nūn intact (contrast the jussive/subjunctive, where it drops).
26.root: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — to call, summon, invite, pray

27.meaning: 'To / toward / up to' — a preposition marking the endpoint, goal, or limit of an action or motion: the direction something moves toward or the boundary at which it stops.
27.grammar: An invariable preposition. It has no case ending of its own but puts the noun that follows it into the genitive ('of / to' state). It indicates direction toward, or the terminal limit of, something.

28.meaning: 'The Fire' — fire, flame; in religious usage often the Fire of Hell, the blazing punishment of the Hereafter.
28.grammar: The definite article 'al-' ('the') plus the feminine noun 'nār' ('fire'). The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'n' (so it is pronounced 'an-nār'). The '-i' ending is genitive, the case used after a preposition or to link the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the Fire').

29.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
29.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
29.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

30.meaning: 'He/it calls / invites / summons' (or a jussive 'let him call') — to call upon, invite, or summon; present-tense with a singular subject.
30.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) verb, 3rd-person masculine singular ('he/it calls'). The ya- prefix marks a single masculine subject. The long final -ū (written with a silent alif) reflects the weak final-root letter (wāw); the form can serve as indicative ('he calls') or, depending on context, jussive/subjunctive — the spelling here ends in the bare long vowel rather than the plural -ūna.
30.root: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — to call, summon, invite, pray

31.meaning: 'To / toward / up to' — a preposition marking the endpoint, goal, or limit of an action or motion: the direction something moves toward or the boundary at which it stops.
31.grammar: An invariable preposition. It has no case ending of its own but puts the noun that follows it into the genitive ('of / to' state). It indicates direction toward, or the terminal limit of, something.

32.meaning: The Garden / Paradise — a definite noun literally meaning 'the garden'; the term for the Garden of Paradise, the abode of reward in the Hereafter.
32.grammar: Definite noun: 'al-' is 'the'. The '-i' ending (on the feminine '-at-') is genitive, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF …') or follows a preposition. 'janna' originally means a lush, shaded garden.
32.root: ج-ن-ن (j-n-n) — to cover, conceal (a garden's dense foliage 'covers' the ground)

33.meaning: 'And the forgiveness / pardon' — Allah's covering over and pardoning of sins; the noun for divine forgiveness.
33.grammar: A definite feminine verbal noun ('the forgiveness'), prefixed by 'and' + 'the'. The final -i is the genitive case ending — used after a preposition or in an 'of …' link to a following noun. The ma- prefix forms a noun of the action 'to forgive'.

34.meaning: 'By His permission / with His leave'. It joins 'with/by' to the noun 'permission, leave, sanction' and an attached pronoun 'His', indicating something done by the authorization of the one referred to.
34.grammar: The prefix 'bi-' is a preposition meaning 'with' or 'by (means of)'. It places the following noun in the genitive case, shown by the '-i' ending. The attached '-hi' is a possessive pronoun, 'His' (or 'its'), so the whole reads 'by His permission'.
34.root: أ-ذ-ن (ʾ-dh-n) — to permit, give leave; to hear/heed

35.meaning: 'And He makes clear / explains / makes plain' — to clarify, expound, or make evident; a present-tense verb with a singular subject.
35.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) verb, 3rd-person masculine singular ('he makes clear'), prefixed by 'and'. The yu- prefix marks a single masculine subject in this form-II (intensive/causative) pattern, whose doubled middle letter gives the sense 'to make plain/expound'. The final -u marks the indicative mood — the plain statement form ('he does').
35.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — to be clear, distinct; form II: to make clear, explain

36.meaning: 'His signs / His verses.' The plural of a word meaning a sign, token, or mark that points to a greater reality — also used for the verses of revelation — here joined to 'his'.
36.grammar: A sound feminine plural ('signs') with an attached possessive 'his'. The -i ending is the genitive case, the form this plural takes when it follows a preposition or is linked as the object of a possessor; the -hi ('his') marks ownership: 'his signs'.
36.root: أ-ي-ي (ʾ-y-y) — a sign, token, mark; a verse of revelation

37.meaning: To the people, for mankind — addressed or directed toward human beings in general; 'an-nās' is the collective word for 'people, humankind'.
37.grammar: The preposition 'li-' (to/for) joined to 'an-nās' (the people); the article's 'a' drops in pronunciation and its 'l' assimilates into the noun's 'n' (shown by the doubling). The -i ending is the genitive case, required because the word follows the preposition 'li-'. 'nās' is a collective noun for humankind with no singular of its own root form.

38.meaning: 'So that they may / perhaps they will.' A particle expressing hope, expectation, or purpose, fused with the pronoun 'them'; it introduces a hoped-for or intended outcome.

parts.en: perhaps / so that / in hope that

38.grammar: The particle laʿalla ('perhaps, in the hope that, so that') with the attached pronoun -hum ('them'), which serves as its subject. Laʿalla belongs to a family of particles that put a following noun or pronoun in the accusative; -hum is that fixed object form. It conveys hope or an intended purpose rather than certainty.
38.root: — (particle with pronoun; no root)

39.meaning: 'They take heed / bear in mind / remember and reflect' — to call to mind and be admonished by it; a present-tense verb with a masculine-plural subject.

parts.en: take heed, bear in mind, reflect (form-V stem)

39.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) verb, 3rd-person masculine plural ('they take heed'). The ya- prefix with the full -ūna ending marks 'they (men) do' and shows the indicative mood (final nūn intact). This is form V (ta- prefix + doubled middle letter), reflexive/intensive: 'to remind oneself, take heed, ponder'.
39.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — to remember, mention; form V: to take heed, be mindful

1.meaning: 'And they ask you' — people direct a question or request to a single male addressee.
1.grammar: A present-tense verb with the prefix wa- ('and'). The ya- prefix plus -na ending mark a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'), and the suffix -ka is the object pronoun 'you' (one male). The indicative form signals a real, ongoing or repeated action ('they ask you').

2.meaning: About / concerning; a particle marking the topic of inquiry or the thing one moves away from.
2.grammar: A preposition meaning 'about, concerning, away from'. Its base form is ʿan; the final -i here is a helping vowel added to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a connecting 'al-'. It governs the genitive case on whatever noun follows.

3.meaning: 'The menstruation' — the monthly menstrual period; the noun for menses (also the place/time of it).
3.grammar: A definite masculine noun ('the menstruation'). The ma- prefix forms a noun from the verb 'to menstruate', denoting the act, time, or condition. The final -i is the genitive case ending — used after a preposition or in an 'of …' link to a following noun.

4.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
4.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

5.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
5.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

6.meaning: Harm, hurt, or an affliction — something offensive or injurious, ranging from a minor irritation or ailment to anything that causes discomfort or distress.
6.grammar: An indefinite noun. The -an ending (written with tanwīn) is the indefinite accusative: it marks 'a harm / some harm' as the object of a verb or as part of a descriptive phrase, with the 'n' sound signalling indefiniteness ('a/an').
6.root: أ-ذ-ي (ʾ-dh-y) — to harm, hurt, injure, cause discomfort

7.meaning: 'So withdraw from / keep away from / hold aloof' — a command to a group of men to keep apart or distance themselves; introduced by 'so/then'.

parts.en: withdraw, keep away, hold aloof (form-VIII stem)

7.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a masculine plural ('you all, keep away!'), introduced by fa- ('so/then', marking a consequence). The -ū ending marks the plural addressees. This is form VIII (infix -t-), reflexive: 'to take oneself away, withdraw, keep aloof'.
7.root: ع-ز-ل (ʿ-z-l) — to set apart, remove; form VIII: to withdraw, keep away

8.meaning: 'The women' — the plural of 'woman' (a suppletive plural drawn from a different stem); women collectively.
8.grammar: A definite plural noun ('the women'). It is a suppletive plural — its singular comes from a different stem (imraʾa, 'woman'). This word is a diptote (mamnūʿ min al-ṣarf): it never takes tanwīn and uses -a for BOTH the accusative and the genitive, so it ends in -a even after a preposition (where an ordinary noun would take -i). The final -a here is therefore the diptote ending, marking the accusative as a direct object — but note it would remain -a, not -i, in the genitive too. (The 'l-' is the assimilated 'the', merging with the following n-.)

9.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
9.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

10.meaning: 'The menstruation' — the monthly menstrual period; the noun for menses (also the place/time of it).
10.grammar: A definite masculine noun ('the menstruation'). The ma- prefix forms a noun from the verb 'to menstruate', denoting the act, time, or condition. The final -i is the genitive case ending — used after a preposition or in an 'of …' link to a following noun.

11.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
11.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

12.meaning: 'You approach them (feminine) / draw near to them' — the verb 'to come near, approach', addressed to a group of men, with a feminine-plural object.

parts.en: approach, come near, draw close (form-I stem)

12.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) verb, 2nd-person masculine plural ('you all approach'), with attached object pronoun -hunna ('them', a group of females). The ta- prefix and -ū ending mark 'you (men) do'; the final nūn is dropped before the pronoun (taqrabū-hunna), reflecting jussive/subjunctive mood used after a negative command ('do not …').
12.root: ق-ر-ب (q-r-b) — to be near, approach, draw close

13.meaning: 'Until / up to the point that; so that' — a particle marking a limit or goal. It expresses the end-point reached ('until') or the purpose aimed at ('so that, in order that').
13.grammar: A particle indicating a goal or limit. When followed by a present-tense verb it places that verb in the subjunctive mood (clipping its ending to -a), conveying 'until / so that' something comes about. Ḥattā itself is invariable.

14.meaning: 'They (feminine) become pure / are cleansed' — to become clean or ritually pure; a present-tense verb with a feminine-plural subject.
14.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) verb, 3rd-person feminine plural ('they/the women become pure'). The ya- prefix together with the -na ending marks a group of females as the subject. This feminine-plural ending is fixed and does not drop for mood. From form I, 'to be/become pure or clean'.
14.root: ط-ه-ر (ṭ-h-r) — to be pure, clean; purity

15.meaning: A connecting phrase meaning 'then when / and when', introducing a circumstance whose occurrence triggers a following response. 'Fa-' links it to what precedes; 'idhā' sets up a 'when … (then) …' condition for something expected to happen.
15.grammar: A particle cluster, not a noun or verb, so it has no case ending. 'Idhā' is a conditional/temporal particle ('when') used for events regarded as bound to occur, and it normally introduces a clause followed by a main response. The prefixed fa- ('then/so') ties the whole condition to the preceding statement.

16.meaning: A verb meaning 'they (feminine plural) have become thoroughly clean/pure' — describing the attainment of full ritual and physical purity. Form V adds the sense of taking on or undergoing the action thoroughly and for oneself.
16.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb of Form V (taṭahhara), formed by prefixing ta- to the Form II base (ṭahhara); Form V typically expresses doing or undergoing the action to and for oneself. The suffix -na marks a third-person feminine plural subject, 'they (women).' The bare past stem signals a completed action.

17.meaning: A command meaning 'then come to / approach them (feminine plural)' — go to them, often with the nuance of conjugal approach. It combines a connecting 'then/so' with an order to draw near.
17.grammar: An imperative (command) verb addressed to a masculine plural 'you,' shown by the long -ū ending ('you all do…'). The prefixed fa- means 'then/so.' The initial alif is a waṣla (connecting alif) that is elided in pronunciation when joined to fa-, so the cluster is read fa-tū, not fa-ʾtū; it is not a glottal stop. The attached -hunna is a feminine-plural object pronoun, 'them (women).'

18.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
18.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
18.root: — (preposition)

19.meaning: Wherever / in whatever place — an adverb pointing to an unspecified location, 'in the place where ...'.
19.grammar: An invariable adverb of place ('where / wherever'). Although it ends in -u, it is fixed in form and does not change for case; it is normally followed by a clause stating the situation tied to that place.

20.meaning: A verb meaning 'He commanded/ordered you (plural)' — to issue an authoritative instruction or directive to someone.
20.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb of Form I, third-person masculine singular ('he commanded'), a completed act. The attached -kum is the masculine-plural object pronoun ('you all'); its final vowel appears here as -kumu to ease pronunciation before a following word that begins with a connecting (waṣla) alif.

21.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
21.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

22.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
22.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

23.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
23.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

24.meaning: He loves / likes / holds dear. To have affection for and approval of something or someone.
24.grammar: A present-tense verb in the fourth pattern, third-person masculine singular ('he…'). The yu- prefix signals a single masculine subject, and the final -u ending marks the indicative mood, presenting the action as an established fact or ongoing reality.
24.root: ح-ب-ب (ḥ-b-b) — love, affection; to hold dear

25.meaning: A noun/adjective in the plural meaning 'those who habitually turn back in repentance' — people characterized by frequently returning from wrongdoing to Allah. The intensive form stresses repeated, abundant repentance.

parts.en: one who turns much in repentance

25.grammar: A definite plural noun ('the …'). It is an intensive form on the faʿʿāl pattern, which doubles the middle radical (here the wāw, giving tawwāb) to denote someone who does the action a great deal — here, repents abundantly. The -īna ending marks a sound masculine plural in the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) state, as opposed to -ūna for the subject state.

26.meaning: A verb meaning 'and He loves' — to love, hold dear, or be well-pleased with. Joined to a preceding statement by 'and.'
26.grammar: A present/future-tense verb of Form IV (aḥabba 'to love'), third-person masculine singular ('he loves'). The final -u marks the indicative mood, the plain, unconditioned present used for stating a fact. The prefixed wa- means 'and.'

27.meaning: A plural noun meaning 'those who purify/cleanse themselves' — people who actively keep themselves pure, physically and spiritually. The Form V participle stresses self-directed, deliberate purification.
27.grammar: A definite plural active participle of Form V (one who undertakes purifying himself). The -īna ending marks a sound masculine plural in the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) state. The prefixed mu- with ta- and the doubled middle radical are the signs of the Form V participle pattern.
27.root: ط-ه-ر (ṭ-h-r) — purity, cleanness

1.meaning: A noun meaning 'your women/wives' — adult females, here possessed by a plural 'you.' The base word covers both 'women' and, by extension, 'wives.'
1.grammar: A noun in the nominative (subject) case, shown by the -u before the pronoun. Because it carries a possessive suffix it stands as the first term of a construct (iḍāfa) phrase, so it takes no nunation; the -u reflects its grammatical role (subject/topic) rather than indefiniteness. The attached -kum is a masculine-plural possessive, 'your (all of you).' 'Nisā'' is a plural with no singular from the same root — its singular is supplied by 'imraʾa/marʾa' from a different root.

2.meaning: A noun meaning 'a tilled field / cultivated land,' and by extension the act of sowing and cultivation. It evokes ground prepared and planted to yield produce.
2.grammar: A noun in the nominative (subject) case with nunation (-un), the doubled 'n' sound that marks it as indefinite ('a tilth'). Nunation typically signals that the noun is non-specific and not joined to a following possessor.
2.root: ح-ر-ث (ḥ-r-th) — to till, to cultivate, sowing

3.meaning: A short phrase meaning 'for you / belonging to you (plural)' — expressing benefit, possession, or assignment to a group of people.
3.grammar: A preposition li- ('for, to'), expressing benefit or belonging, with its vowel shifting to 'la-' before an attached pronoun. The -kum is the masculine-plural pronoun in the object form, 'you all.' Together they signal 'for/to you.'

4.meaning: A command addressed to a group: 'bring!', 'come with!', 'produce!'. From the verb 'to come'; in this pattern with the preposition 'bi-' it means to bring or produce something. Preceded by 'fa-', it reads 'then bring / so produce'.
4.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector signalling a consequence ('then …'). The middle piece is the bare imperative stem of the verb 'to come' (singular '(i)ti'); the '-ū' ending then marks a masculine plural audience ('you all, bring!'). Commands have no case ending. The initial 'i'-sound is a helping vowel that lets the word begin smoothly.
4.root: ا-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (with bi-) to bring, to produce

5.meaning: A noun meaning 'your tillage / your cultivated field' — the land one sows and cultivates, here belonging to a plural 'you.'
5.grammar: A noun in the accusative (object) case, shown by the -a before the pronoun, which commonly marks the word as the direct object of a verb or the goal of an action. The attached -kum is a masculine-plural possessive, 'your (all of you).'
5.root: ح-ر-ث (ḥ-r-th) — to till, to cultivate, sowing

6.meaning: A particle/adverb meaning 'in whatever manner,' 'from wherever,' or 'whenever' — it asks or denotes the how, where, or when of an action in an open-ended way.
6.grammar: An invariable interrogative/conditional adverb; it has no case ending and never changes form. It introduces the manner, place, or time of an action in a general, open sense ('in what way / from where / when').

7.meaning: A verb meaning 'you (plural) willed/wished/desired' — to want or choose something by an act of will.
7.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb of Form I. The suffix -tum marks a second-person masculine plural subject acting in completed time, 'you all willed/wished.' This -tum is a subject ending fused to the verb.
7.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʾ) — to will, to wish; thing

8.meaning: A command meaning 'and put forward / send ahead (in advance)' — to advance something or dispatch it beforehand, as in sending good ahead for one's future benefit.
8.grammar: An imperative (command) verb of Form II (qaddama 'to send/put forward'), addressed to a masculine plural 'you,' shown by the long -ū ending ('you all do…'). Form II (doubled middle radical) often adds a sense of causing or doing something purposefully. The prefixed wa- means 'and.'
8.root: ق-د-م (q-d-m) — to precede, to put forward, to advance

9.meaning: For yourselves / for your own selves — the preposition li- ('for, to') with the plural noun anfus ('selves, souls') and the pronoun 'your', conveying benefit accruing to one's own persons.
9.grammar: The preposition li- ('for/to') governs the noun anfus, which therefore takes the genitive -i ending; the possessive pronoun -kum ('your', plural) is attached. The genitive is required because the noun follows the preposition li-.
9.root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s) — self, soul, breath, inner being

10.meaning: A command addressed to a group: 'guard yourselves / be mindful and on your guard.' The verb conveys taqwā — protecting oneself by being conscious of Allah and shielding oneself from wrongdoing and its consequences.
10.grammar: An imperative (command) verb addressed to a plural 'you (all).' The -ū ending marks the masculine plural addressees ('you all'). The pattern (form VIII, from waqā 'to protect') gives the sense of taking protective care for oneself.
10.root: و-ق-ي (w-q-y) — to guard, shield, protect oneself

11.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
11.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

12.meaning: A command meaning 'and know! / and be aware (you, plural).' Form I of the root, an order to possess knowledge or take note of something.
12.grammar: An imperative (command) to a plural 'you,' joined by wa- ('and'). The -ū ending directs the order to a masculine plural group ('all of you, know…').
12.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know, to be aware

13.meaning: 'That you …' — the emphatic particle anna ('that, indeed') fused with the pronoun 'you' (a group); it introduces a firmly asserted statement and points to the addressees as its subject.
13.grammar: The particle anna ('that, indeed'), used to introduce and stress a reported clause, with the attached pronoun -kum ('you,' addressing a group) as its subject. Anna puts a following noun or pronoun in the accusative, and -kum is that fixed object form.

14.meaning: A phrase meaning 'ones who will meet Him' / 'those who are to encounter Him' — people destined to come face to face with someone. The Form III participle conveys a mutual meeting or encounter.
14.grammar: An active participle of Form III (lāqā 'to meet/encounter'), masculine plural. The plural's normal -ūna ending drops its -na in a construct (iḍāfa) when joined to a following possessor/object — here the attached -hu ('him'). Form III (with the long ā) often signals a reciprocal or mutual action.

15.meaning: A two-part word: 'and' + a command 'give glad tidings, bring good news.' The verb means to announce something joyful that shows on the face — to cheer someone with happy news. It is the standard word for delivering good tidings.
15.grammar: A conjunction 'wa' + an imperative (command) verb, addressed to a single male ('you, give good news'). The base form is bashshir; the final -i here is a connecting vowel added to ease pronunciation before a following word, not a case ending. The doubled middle letter marks an intensive/causative sense: actively bringing good news to someone.

16.meaning: A plural noun meaning 'the believers' — those who have faith, who inwardly trust and affirm. The Form IV participle denotes one who brings about belief and security within.
16.grammar: A definite plural active participle of Form IV (āmana 'to believe'). The -īna ending marks a sound masculine plural in the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) state. The prefixed mu- marks it as a Form IV participle ('one who has/gives faith').

1.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
1.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

2.meaning: A verb addressed to a group of males (or a mixed group): 'you (all) make', 'you set up', 'you place', or 'you render (something into something).' The verb jaʿala carries the sense of making, forming, or appointing.

parts.en: plural 'you all' (and, after a prohibition particle, the cut-off mood)

2.grammar: The 'ta-' prefix marks a present/future verb addressed to 'you'. The '-ū' ending marks a masculine plural subject ('you all'). The dropping of the final 'n' (jussive/subjunctive form) is what a preceding particle like 'lā' of prohibition triggers, turning it into 'do not do …'.
2.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, to place, to render

3.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
3.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

4.meaning: A noun meaning 'something set up as a target/obstacle' — hence a thing exposed or made liable to be used as a pretext or excuse. It conveys placing something in the way as a barrier or excuse.
4.grammar: A noun in the accusative (object) case with nunation (-an, here realized as -tan over the tāʾ marbūṭa), the doubled 'n' sound marking it indefinite ('a pretext/barrier'). The accusative often marks a direct object or the thing affected by an action.
4.root: ع-ر-ض (ʿ-r-ḍ) — to present, expose, set across, width

5.meaning: A phrase meaning 'for/concerning your oaths' — your solemn sworn statements or vows, the things you swear by. The prefix conveys 'for the sake of' or 'with respect to.'
5.grammar: The preposition li- ('for, concerning') joined to a plural noun. 'Aymān' is the plural of 'yamīn' (oath). The -i ending is genitive, the case required after a preposition; the attached -kum is the masculine-plural possessive, 'your (all of you).'
5.root: ي-م-ن (y-m-n) — right hand; oath, the right side

6.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
6.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

7.meaning: A verb meaning 'you (plural) act righteously / do good and act dutifully' — to be virtuous, kind, and faithful in one's obligations. The root carries the sense of devout goodness, especially toward those owed kindness.
7.grammar: A present-tense verb of Form V, second-person masculine plural ('you all'), shown by the ta- prefix combined with the long -ū ending. The bare -ū (without a final -na) indicates the subjunctive/jussive mood — the form used after certain particles or to express purpose ('that you may act righteously'), rather than a plain statement.

8.meaning: A verb meaning 'and you (plural) guard yourselves / are mindful (of Allah)' — to exercise God-conscious caution, shielding oneself from wrongdoing and divine displeasure. This is the verbal sense of taqwā.
8.grammar: A present-tense verb of Form VIII (ittaqā 'to be wary, God-conscious'), second-person masculine plural ('you all'). The first tā' is the second-person present prefix; the second, doubled tā' results from Form VIII's infixed -t- assimilating with the root's initial wāw (wtaqā → ttaqā). The bare -ū ending (without final -na) marks the subjunctive/jussive mood, used after certain particles or to express purpose ('that you may be mindful'). The prefixed wa- means 'and.'

9.meaning: A verb meaning 'and you (plural) set right / make peace / reconcile' — to put matters into good order, mend relations, and bring about reform. The Form IV sense is causative: to make something good or sound.
9.grammar: A present-tense verb of Form IV (aṣlaḥa 'to set right, reconcile'), second-person masculine plural ('you all'); the tu- prefix is typical of Form IV. The bare -ū ending (no final -na) marks the subjunctive/jussive mood, used after certain particles or to express purpose ('that you may make peace'). The prefixed wa- means 'and.'
9.root: ص-ل-ح (ṣ-l-ḥ) — to be sound, good, righteous; to set right

10.meaning: Between; in the midst of two things. An adverb of place marking the space separating or lying among parties or points.
10.grammar: An adverb of place ('between'). It always ends in -a and grammatically governs what follows it, putting the following noun(s) into the genitive 'of' relationship. It does not change to show 'the' or a case of its own; the fixed -a is simply how this word is formed.
10.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies between

11.meaning: Humankind, people, mankind — the collective of human beings.
11.grammar: A collective noun ('people, mankind') carrying the definite article al- ('the'); the 'l' of the article assimilates into the following 'n', doubling it (al-nās → an-nās). The genitive ending -i marks the word as governed by a preposition or as the second term of a possessive.
11.root: ء-ن-س (ʾ-n-s) — humankind, sociability, familiarity; the word for 'people' is most commonly traced to this root (related to insān, 'human being')

12.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
12.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
12.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

13.meaning: All-Hearing / ever-hearing — one who hears completely and perfectly, missing nothing of what is uttered or whispered; an intensive form stressing the fullness of the quality. The '-un' nunation marks it as indefinite nominative.
13.grammar: An intensive adjective (faʿīl pattern) conveying a constant, perfect quality. The '-un' (nunation on the ḍamma) marks it as indefinite and in the nominative case, typically used for a subject or predicate ("is all-hearing").

14.meaning: An intensive adjective/name meaning 'All-Knowing / fully aware' — one whose knowledge is complete, deep, and all-encompassing; as a divine attribute it denotes Allah's perfect knowledge.
14.grammar: An intensive adjective (the pattern faʿīl conveys 'thoroughly, abundantly'). The ending -un is the indefinite nominative — the nominative case marks it as the subject or the quality being affirmed, and the -n (nunation) signals 'a / an', i.e. indefinite. So it reads '(is) all-knowing'.

1.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
1.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

2.meaning: A verb meaning 'He calls you to account / holds you responsible (and penalizes)' — to take someone to task for what they have done. The Form III pattern conveys confronting and dealing with a person over their conduct.

parts.en: he takes to task / holds accountable

2.grammar: A present/future-tense verb of Form III (ākhādha 'to call to account'; the Form I base is akhadha 'to take/seize'), third-person masculine singular ('he holds accountable'). The indicative -u (the plain present mood) sits before the object pronoun; its vowel appears as -kumu to ease pronunciation before a following word with a connecting (waṣla) alif. The -kum is the masculine-plural object, 'you all.'

3.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
3.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

4.meaning: A phrase meaning 'for/by what is idle and unintended (in speech)' — careless, thoughtless utterance that carries no firm intent, such as an oath blurted out without resolve. The prefix marks it as the basis or cause of an action.
4.grammar: The preposition bi- ('for, by, on account of') joined to a definite noun ('the …'). The -i ending is genitive, the case required after a preposition. 'Laghw' denotes vain, purposeless, or unintended talk.
4.root: ل-غ-و (l-gh-w) — idle/vain talk, nonsense, the unintended

5.meaning: The preposition 'in / within / during.' It places something inside a container, period, place, or matter.
5.grammar: A preposition. It governs the noun that follows, putting it in the genitive case and situating something inside it — in space, in time ('during'), or in a circumstance.

6.meaning: A plural noun meaning 'your oaths' — your solemn sworn statements or vows, here belonging to a plural 'you.'
6.grammar: A noun in the genitive (oblique) case, shown by the -i before the pronoun, the case used after prepositions or to link a noun to a possessor in a construct (iḍāfa). 'Aymān' is the plural of 'yamīn' (oath). The attached -kum is the masculine-plural possessive, 'your (all of you).'
6.root: ي-م-ن (y-m-n) — right hand; oath, the right side

7.meaning: 'But / however / yet' — a particle of correction and contrast that sets aside what came before and affirms something different instead.
7.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') attached to lākin ('but / however'). Lākin is a particle of rectification: it draws a contrast with, or corrects, the preceding idea and introduces an opposing or qualifying statement ('... but rather...').

8.meaning: A verb meaning 'He calls you to account / holds you responsible (and penalizes)' — to take someone to task for what they have done. The Form III pattern conveys confronting and dealing with a person over their conduct.

parts.en: he takes to task / holds accountable

8.grammar: A present/future-tense verb of Form III (ākhādha 'to call to account'; the Form I base is akhadha 'to take/seize'), third-person masculine singular ('he holds accountable'). The final -u marks the indicative mood, the plain present used to state a fact. The attached -kum is the masculine-plural object pronoun, 'you all.'

9.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
9.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

10.meaning: 'It earned / acquired, gained' — said of deeds and their consequences; the root means to gain or acquire something, especially the moral 'earnings' of one's actions.
10.grammar: Past-tense verb. The -t (sukūn-marked -at) suffix marks a third-person feminine singular subject, 'she/it.' The past tense presents the action as completed.
10.root: ك-س-ب (k-s-b) — to earn, acquire, gain (esp. deeds)

11.meaning: 'Your hearts.' The plural of 'heart' — the inner seat of feeling, thought, intention, and faith — joined to 'your' (referring to a group).
11.grammar: A plural noun ('hearts') with an attached possessive 'your'. The -u ending is the nominative case, which typically marks the word as the subject — the doer or the thing being described. The -kum ('your') refers to a group including males.
11.root: ق-ل-ب (q-l-b) — heart; to turn over, turn about

12.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
12.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
12.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

13.meaning: An intensive adjective/name meaning 'much-forgiving, ever-ready to forgive, one who veils and pardons faults again and again'. The form stresses abundance, so it conveys forgiveness as a constant, far-reaching quality.
13.grammar: An intensive adjective (the ghafūr 'doer-in-abundance' pattern), used as a divine attribute of Allah. The -un ending is nunation in the nominative case: it marks the word as indefinite and in the nominative, the case typically used for the subject or for a predicate that describes the subject.

14.meaning: An intensive adjective meaning 'most forbearing, clement, gentle' — one who is patient and does not rush to anger or punishment despite having the power to act, but bears with wrongdoing calmly.
14.grammar: An adjective on the intensive faʿīl pattern, conveying a deep and constant quality. The final -un (nominative with tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('a forbearing one') and is the ending typical of a subject or a predicate describing something.

1.meaning: 'For/to those who …' — a preposition 'for / to / belonging to' joined to the masculine plural relative pronoun 'those who,' which introduces a description of a group by something they do.
1.grammar: The preposition li- ('for / to / belonging to') fused with the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'). Relative pronouns like this do not change for case; they point ahead to a clause that describes the group ('those who …').

2.meaning: A verb (imperfect, masculine plural) meaning 'they swear an oath of abstention' — to vow to keep away from one's wife.
2.grammar: Present/imperfect tense, fourth-form verb. The yu-…-ūna frame marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'); the prefix yu- is the form-IV imperfect marker and the long ū together with the final -na is the masculine-plural indicative suffix, signalling a plain, ongoing or habitual action (not negated or subjunctive). The stem keeps only the root consonants ʾ-l.
2.root: أ-ل-و (ʾ-l-w) — to swear an oath (of abstention); to fall short

3.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
3.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

4.meaning: 'Their wives / their women' — the plural noun for 'women' joined to a possessive 'their'.
4.grammar: A plural noun with an attached possessive pronoun -him ('their', masculine plural). The -i case ending is genitive, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when it is possessed/linked to another noun ('… of …').

5.meaning: 'A waiting, an awaiting, a period of expectant delay' — the verbal noun naming the act of waiting and watching for an outcome.
5.grammar: A verbal noun (the 'name of the action') from a fifth-form verb, denoting the activity of waiting itself. The final -u is the nominative case ending, the form used when the word is the subject or the thing being described.
5.root: ر-ب-ص (r-b-ṣ) — to wait, watch and expect

6.meaning: 'Four' — the cardinal number four.
6.grammar: A cardinal number with the feminine -at ending (used when counting masculine nouns). The -i case ending is genitive, the form taken after a preposition or when linked to a following counted noun ('… of …').

7.meaning: 'Months' — the plural of 'month'.
7.grammar: A plural noun (a 'broken'/internal plural of shahr, 'month'). The -in ending is genitive with tanwīn, marking it as indefinite ('months') and is the form used after a preposition or counting word, or when linked to a preceding noun.

8.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'fa-' ('then', 'so', 'but') drawing a consequence, joined to the conditional particle 'in' ('if'). Together: 'then if …', 'but if …'.
8.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that signals a result or transition ('then/so'). 'in' is the conditional particle 'if', introducing a supposed condition. Both are indeclinable particles with no case ending.

9.meaning: A verb (past, masculine plural) meaning 'they returned / came back' — and idiomatically 'they went back (to harmony), reconciled, reverted to the right course'.
9.grammar: Past tense verb. The suffix -ū marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they') and the completed (perfect) aspect — an action presented as already done.
9.root: ف-ي-أ (f-y-ʾ) — to return, come back, revert

10.meaning: A two-part connector meaning 'so/then, indeed…'. It joins fa- ('so', 'then', marking a result or consequence) to inna, an emphatic particle that strongly affirms the statement that follows ('truly', 'verily').
10.grammar: fa- is a connective prefix signaling that what follows is a consequence or next step. inna is an emphatic particle that introduces a nominal sentence, puts its following noun in the accusative, and strengthens the assertion; it does not itself take a case ending.

11.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
11.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

12.meaning: An intensive adjective/name meaning 'much-forgiving, ever-ready to forgive, one who veils and pardons faults again and again'. The form stresses abundance, so it conveys forgiveness as a constant, far-reaching quality.
12.grammar: An intensive adjective (the ghafūr 'doer-in-abundance' pattern), used as a divine attribute of Allah. The -un ending is nunation in the nominative case: it marks the word as indefinite and in the nominative, the case typically used for the subject or for a predicate that describes the subject.

13.meaning: Most merciful, ever-merciful; one whose mercy is constant and abundant. As a divine attribute it denotes Allah's enduring, all-embracing compassion toward His creation.
13.grammar: An intensive adjective on the form faʿīl ('abundantly/constantly merciful'). The ending -un (tanwīn) is the nominative case with indefiniteness, the form typically used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate describing it ('[He] is most merciful').

1.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
1.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

2.meaning: A verb (past, masculine plural) meaning 'they firmly resolved, made up their minds, were determined' upon a course of action.
2.grammar: Past tense verb. The suffix -ū marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they') in the completed (perfect) aspect. (The silent alif after the wāw is a spelling convention for a verb's plural -ū.)

3.meaning: 'Divorce' — the act and legal concept of dissolving a marriage; the noun naming the release of a spouse from the marriage bond.
3.grammar: A definite verbal noun (the l- prefix means 'the'). The final -a is the accusative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the direct object of a verb or otherwise governed in that role.
3.root: ط-ل-ق (ṭ-l-q) — to release, set free, divorce

4.meaning: A two-part connector meaning 'so/then, indeed…'. It joins fa- ('so', 'then', marking a result or consequence) to inna, an emphatic particle that strongly affirms the statement that follows ('truly', 'verily').
4.grammar: fa- is a connective prefix signaling that what follows is a consequence or next step. inna is an emphatic particle that introduces a nominal sentence, puts its following noun in the accusative, and strengthens the assertion; it does not itself take a case ending.

5.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
5.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

6.meaning: All-Hearing / ever-hearing — one who hears completely and perfectly, missing nothing of what is uttered or whispered; an intensive form stressing the fullness of the quality. The '-un' nunation marks it as indefinite nominative.
6.grammar: An intensive adjective (faʿīl pattern) conveying a constant, perfect quality. The '-un' (nunation on the ḍamma) marks it as indefinite and in the nominative case, typically used for a subject or predicate ("is all-hearing").

7.meaning: An intensive adjective/name meaning 'All-Knowing / fully aware' — one whose knowledge is complete, deep, and all-encompassing; as a divine attribute it denotes Allah's perfect knowledge.
7.grammar: An intensive adjective (the pattern faʿīl conveys 'thoroughly, abundantly'). The ending -un is the indefinite nominative — the nominative case marks it as the subject or the quality being affirmed, and the -n (nunation) signals 'a / an', i.e. indefinite. So it reads '(is) all-knowing'.

1.meaning: 'And the divorced women' — the feminine plural participle for women who have been divorced, with a leading 'and'.
1.grammar: A passive participle of a second-form verb ('one who has been divorced'), made feminine plural by -āt and made definite by l- ('the'). The final -u is the nominative case ending, the form used when the word is the subject.
1.root: ط-ل-ق (ṭ-l-q) — to release, set free, divorce

2.meaning: A verb (imperfect, feminine plural) meaning 'they wait, keep waiting, hold themselves in expectant delay'.

parts.en: wait / hold in expectant delay — verb stem

2.grammar: Present/imperfect tense, fifth-form verb. The ya-…-na frame marks a third-person feminine plural subject ('they', women). Here the -na is the feminine-plural subject marker; such forms stay fixed in shape regardless of case.
2.root: ر-ب-ص (r-b-ṣ) — to wait, watch and expect

3.meaning: 'With/concerning themselves' — the noun 'selves/souls' joined to a feminine-plural 'their', preceded by the particle bi-.
3.grammar: The preposition bi- ('with, by, concerning') attached to the plural noun 'selves' (anfus, plural of nafs), which carries the possessive -hinna ('their', feminine plural). The -i ending is genitive — required because the noun follows the preposition bi-.

4.meaning: 'Three' — the cardinal number three.
4.grammar: A cardinal number with the feminine -at ending (used when counting masculine nouns). The final -a is the accusative case ending, the form used for a direct object or for an adverbial expression of measure/extent (e.g. 'for the span of three …').

5.meaning: 'Periods' — the plural of qurʾ, a term for the recurring cycle (used for a woman's menstrual period or, by some usage, the interval of purity between periods).
5.grammar: A plural noun (a broken/internal plural). The -in ending is genitive with tanwīn, marking it indefinite ('periods') and is the form used after a counting word or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of …').
5.root: ق-ر-أ (q-r-ʾ) — a recurring time/cycle; to come together

6.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
6.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

7.meaning: A verb (imperfect) meaning 'it is lawful, it is permitted, it is allowed' — to be religiously/legally permissible.
7.grammar: Present/imperfect tense, third-person masculine singular ('it'). The final -u is the indicative ending, marking a plain statement of fact — an ongoing or general truth, not negated or made conditional.
7.root: ح-ل-ل (ḥ-l-l) — to be lawful, permitted, untied

8.meaning: 'For them / to them' — the preposition 'for/to' joined to a feminine-plural 'them'.
8.grammar: The preposition li- ('for, to') with an attached object pronoun -hunna ('them', feminine plural). It expresses that something belongs to, is owed to, or is on behalf of a group of females. (The vowel appears as 'la-' before the pronoun.)

9.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
9.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

10.meaning: A verb (imperfect, feminine plural) meaning 'they conceal, hide, keep secret' something.
10.grammar: Present/imperfect tense, first-form verb. The ya-…-na frame marks a third-person feminine plural subject ('they', women). The -na is the feminine-plural subject marker; such forms keep a fixed shape regardless of case.

11.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
11.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

12.meaning: 'He created' — to bring into being, to originate and shape something that did not exist before, from the root denoting creation and the fashioning of things from nothing.
12.grammar: Past tense, third-person masculine singular ('he'), completed action ('he created'). This is a form I verb of the CaCaCa pattern. The masculine singular 'he' here is the unmarked (zero-suffix) form — there is no separate person ending; the final -a is the inherent stem vowel of the base pattern, not a person or tense suffix.

13.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
13.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

14.meaning: The preposition 'in / within / during.' It places something inside a container, period, place, or matter.
14.grammar: A preposition. It governs the noun that follows, putting it in the genitive case and situating something inside it — in space, in time ('during'), or in a circumstance.

15.meaning: 'Their wombs' — the plural noun 'wombs' joined to a feminine-plural 'their'.
15.grammar: A plural noun (a broken/internal plural of raḥim, 'womb') carrying the possessive -hinna ('their', feminine plural). The -i ending is genitive, the form used after a preposition or when the noun is possessed/linked to another ('… of …').

16.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
16.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

17.meaning: A verb (past, feminine plural) from the verb 'to be', meaning 'they were' — used to set an action or state in the past, or as a linking 'were'.
17.grammar: Past tense of the verb 'to be' (kāna), third-person feminine plural ('they were', women). The suffix is -na (feminine-plural subject marker) added to the stem kun-; the two nūns meet and merge, producing the written doubled nūn of kunna. It is the completed (perfect) aspect.
17.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

18.meaning: 'They (feminine) believe' — to have faith, specifically faith in Allah; a present-tense verb describing a group of women's believing.
18.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) verb, 3rd-person feminine plural ('they/the women believe'). The combination of the yu- prefix and the heavy -na ending (doubling the nūn) marks a group of females as the subject. This feminine-plural ending stays fixed and is not dropped for mood. From form IV (a-mana), 'to believe, have faith'.
18.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — safety, trust; form IV: to believe, have faith

19.meaning: A phrase 'in Allah / by Allah', combining the preposition 'with/in/by' and the divine name Allah, the proper name of the One God.
19.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') prefixed to the divine name Allah. A preposition always forces the following noun into the genitive case, which is why Allah here ends in -i. With verbs of believing, bi- conveys the object of faith — to believe IN.
19.root: — (Allah is the proper name of God and is not derived from a triliteral root in the usual sense)

20.meaning: "And the Day" — a stretch of time, a day; also used for the appointed Day of Judgement and Resurrection. The opening element is the conjunction 'and'.
20.grammar: A masculine singular noun with the definite article 'the' and the conjunction 'and'. The final -i is the genitive case ending: it typically signals that the word is linked to a preceding noun ('… of …') or governed by a preposition or oath particle.

21.meaning: An adjective meaning 'the last,' 'the latter,' or 'the final' — that which comes at the end of a sequence. It is the common counterpart to 'the first,' and is often used as a name for the world or life to come (the Hereafter, the Last Day), i.e. the ultimate end of all things.
21.grammar: An active-participle-type adjective on the pattern fāʿil. It carries the definite article 'al-' ('the'). The final -i is the genitive case, signaling that the word is governed by a preceding preposition or particle, or stands as the second term of a possessive link ('… of …'). It is masculine singular.
21.root: ء-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — to be last, to come after, to defer / postpone

22.meaning: 'And their husbands' — the noun 'husbands' joined to a feminine-plural 'their', with a leading 'and'.
22.grammar: A plural noun ('husbands', plural of baʿl) carrying the possessive -hunna ('their', feminine plural). The -u ending is nominative, the form used when the word is the subject of a sentence.
