23.meaning: An adjective meaning 'more entitled, having a better/greater right, more deserving' of something.
23.grammar: A comparative/superlative adjective on the afʿal pattern, meaning 'more/most entitled'. The final -u is the nominative case ending, the form used when the word serves as the subject or as a predicate describing the subject.
23.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, right, just claim, what is due

24.meaning: 'In taking them back / in their return' — the verbal noun for 'taking back, returning' joined to a feminine-plural 'them', preceded by the particle bi-.
24.grammar: The preposition bi- attached to the verbal noun radd ('the act of bringing back, restoring'), which carries the object pronoun -hinna ('them', feminine plural). The -i ending is genitive — required because the noun follows the preposition bi-.
24.root: ر-د-د (r-d-d) — to send back, return, restore, repel

25.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
25.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

26.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
26.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

27.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
27.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

28.meaning: A verb (past, masculine plural) meaning 'they wanted, willed, intended, desired' something.
28.grammar: Past tense, fourth-form verb. The suffix -ū marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they') in the completed (perfect) aspect — an action or intention presented as accomplished. (The silent alif after the wāw is a spelling convention.)
28.root: ر-و-د (r-w-d) — to seek, want, will; to go to and fro

29.meaning: 'Setting right, reconciliation, putting matters back in order, making peace and improvement' — the verbal noun for bringing about reform and amends.
29.grammar: A verbal noun (the 'name of the action') from a fourth-form verb meaning 'to set right, reform, reconcile'. The -an ending is accusative with tanwīn, marking it indefinite and signalling the role of a direct object (the thing wanted/done) or a stated purpose.
29.root: ص-ل-ح (ṣ-l-ḥ) — to be sound/good; to set right, reconcile

30.meaning: A compound meaning 'and for them (a group of females)' or 'and to them belongs.' It joins a clause with 'and,' then asserts that something is due to, owed to, or belongs to a group of women.
30.grammar: Starts with the connector wa ('and'). The particle li- ('for, to, belonging to') carries the sense of possession or entitlement; before an attached pronoun it appears as la-. The suffix -hunna is the third-person feminine plural pronoun, 'them,' used specifically of a group of females.

31.meaning: 'The like (of),' 'an equivalent,' 'something matching or comparable.' It denotes a counterpart of equal measure or kind to something else.
31.grammar: A noun in the nominative case, shown by the final -u, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the thing being identified ('X is …'). It is regularly followed by a noun in the genitive to mean 'the like OF …'.
31.root: م-ث-ل (m-th-l) — likeness, similarity, comparison

32.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
32.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

33.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon them' or 'against them (a group of females).' It places a duty, burden, or claim 'on' a group of women — what is incumbent upon or held against them.
33.grammar: The preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, against') takes the form ʿalay- when an attached pronoun follows, often conveying obligation or something weighing upon someone. The suffix -hinna is the third-person feminine plural pronoun 'them,' for a group of females; the -i- vowel is the form the pronoun takes after this preposition.

34.meaning: 'In/with what is recognized as right and fitting' — that is, in a kind, fair, and honourable manner that accords with sound custom and goodness. Al-maʿrūf is conduct universally acknowledged as proper and decent.

parts.en: what is known to be good / fitting

34.grammar: Opens with the preposition bi- ('with, in, by means of'). The definite article al- ('the') makes the noun specific. Maʿrūf is a passive participle, literally 'that which is known/recognized,' used as a noun for what is acknowledged as good and proper. The final -i is the genitive ending, the case required after a preposition.
34.root: ع-ر-ف (ʿ-r-f) — to know, recognize; what is recognized as good

35.meaning: A compound meaning 'and for the men,' 'and to men belongs.' It joins with 'and' and assigns something as due to, or belonging to, men.
35.grammar: Begins with wa ('and') and the particle li- ('for, to, belonging to'), expressing entitlement. The article al- ('the') is here assimilated into the following 'r' sound (heard as 'r-rijāl'). Rijāl is the plural of rajul, 'men.' The final -i is the genitive ending required after li-.
35.root: ر-ج-ل (r-j-l) — man, manhood; (also foot, on foot)

36.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon them' or 'against them (a group of females).' It places a duty, burden, or claim 'on' a group of women — what is incumbent upon or held against them.
36.grammar: The preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, against') takes the form ʿalay- when an attached pronoun follows, often conveying obligation or something weighing upon someone. The suffix -hinna is the third-person feminine plural pronoun 'them,' for a group of females; the -i- vowel is the form the pronoun takes after this preposition.

37.meaning: 'A degree,' 'a rank,' 'a step or level.' It denotes a measure of rising, a stage above, or a position of higher standing.
37.grammar: A feminine noun in the nominative case with indefinite ('a/an') marking, shown by the ending -un (the 'nunation' that signals an unspecified, non-definite noun). The nominative typically marks the subject or the thing being asserted to exist ('there is a degree').
37.root: د-ر-ج (d-r-j) — to ascend by steps; degree, gradation

38.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
38.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
38.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

39.meaning: Mighty, invincible, and supremely honoured; one who possesses overwhelming power and dignity such that none can overcome or resist Him. As a divine descriptor it conveys unassailable might joined with exalted worth.
39.grammar: A descriptive noun (adjective) on an intensive pattern, conveying a deep, enduring quality. The -un ending is indefinite and nominative: it typically marks the word as a subject or as a predicate describing something ("is mighty").

40.meaning: 'All-Wise,' 'profoundly wise.' It describes one whose every judgement, decree, and act is perfectly sound, fitting, and placed exactly where it should be. As a divine attribute of Allah it points to flawless wisdom in all things.
40.grammar: An intensive adjective on the faʿīl pattern, conveying a deep, settled quality of wisdom. It is in the nominative case with indefinite marking, shown by -un, the form used for a predicate or descriptive noun that is not made definite.
40.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to judge, decide wisely; wisdom, governance

1.meaning: 'The divorce' — the formal dissolution or release of a marriage bond; the act of a husband releasing his wife from the marriage tie.
1.grammar: A verbal noun (the name of the action) made definite by the article al- ('the'). The ṭ here is a 'sun letter,' so the 'l' of the article assimilates into it: the 'l' is dropped and the emphatic ṭ is doubled instead, heard as 'aṭ-ṭalāq.' The final -u is the nominative ending, typically marking the subject or topic of a statement.
1.root: ط-ل-ق (ṭ-l-q) — to set free, release, let go

2.meaning: 'Two times,' 'twice.' It is the dual of 'a time/occurrence,' specifying exactly two instances.
2.grammar: A dual noun — Arabic has a special form for exactly two of something. The ending -āni is the dual in the nominative case (the subject form); in the accusative/genitive it would shift to -ayni. So the word means precisely 'two occurrences.'
2.root: م-ر-ر (m-r-r) — to pass by; a pass, an instance, a time

3.meaning: A compound: 'so/then a holding-fast' — that is, 'then retaining (in marriage),' keeping hold of the bond rather than letting it go. Imsāk is the act of holding, gripping, or keeping something back.
3.grammar: Opens with the connective fa- ('so, then'), which links a consequence to what precedes. Imsāk is a verbal noun (the name of the action of holding) of Form IV. It is nominative and indefinite, shown by -un, marking it as the thing asserted ('then there is a retaining').
3.root: م-س-ك (m-s-k) — to hold, grasp, retain, keep

4.meaning: 'With/in goodness and fairness' — in a kind, decent, honourable way that is recognized as right. Maʿrūf is conduct acknowledged by sound sense and custom as proper.

parts.en: what is known to be good / fitting

4.grammar: The preposition bi- ('with, in') governs the noun. Maʿrūf is a passive participle used as a noun, 'that which is recognized as good.' The ending -in is the genitive (required after the preposition) combined with indefinite marking, i.e. 'in a [manner that is] fitting.'
4.root: ع-ر-ف (ʿ-r-f) — to know, recognize; what is recognized as good

5.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
5.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

6.meaning: 'A releasing,' 'a setting free,' 'sending away (kindly).' Tasrīḥ is letting something go its way; of a marriage, it is releasing the spouse gracefully.
6.grammar: A verbal noun (the name of the action) of Form II, a pattern that often adds force or thoroughness to the basic sense. It is nominative and indefinite, shown by -un, marking it as the thing being asserted ('or a releasing').
6.root: س-ر-ح (s-r-ḥ) — to send out (as cattle to pasture), let go, release

7.meaning: 'With excellence / kindness / doing things beautifully' — bi- ('with') joined to iḥsān, the doing of something in the finest, most generous and good way; goodness that goes beyond the bare minimum.
7.grammar: The bi- prefix is a preposition 'with'. The stem iḥsān is a verbal noun for doing good in the best way. The final -in is the indefinite genitive: the 'n'-sound (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('with a kindness'), and the -i is the genitive form required after a preposition.

8.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
8.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

9.meaning: A verb (imperfect) meaning 'it is lawful, it is permitted, it is allowed' — to be religiously/legally permissible.
9.grammar: Present/imperfect tense, third-person masculine singular ('it'). The final -u is the indicative ending, marking a plain statement of fact — an ongoing or general truth, not negated or made conditional.
9.root: ح-ل-ل (ḥ-l-l) — to be lawful, permitted, untied

10.meaning: 'For you / to you (plural)' — the preposition li- ('for, to, belonging to') joined to the attached pronoun for a group being addressed.
10.grammar: li- is a preposition meaning 'for/to'; its vowel appears here as 'la' before the attached pronoun. The -kum ending is the attached pronoun for a masculine plural 'you', so the whole means 'for you (all)'.

11.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
11.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

12.meaning: 'You (men) take,' 'you take back,' 'you seize/receive.' It refers to a group taking or taking possession of something.
12.grammar: A present/subjunctive verb of Form I. The ta- prefix marks a second-person ('you') subject, and the -ū ending marks it as masculine plural ('you all'). The middle is the present-tense stem -khudhu- (full form ta-khudhu-), not the bare imperative. The absence of the final -na (it is -ū, not -ūna) shows the verb is in a dependent (subjunctive/jussive) mood, the form used after certain particles such as 'that,' 'not,' or 'lest.'

13.meaning: 'From what,' 'of that which,' 'some of what.' It is a fusion of the preposition 'from/of' with the relative 'what,' introducing a thing or category being drawn upon or partly taken.
13.grammar: A contraction of the preposition min ('from, of, some of') with the relative pronoun mā ('what, that which'); the 'n' of min merges into the 'm' of mā, giving mimmā. It introduces a relative clause meaning 'from that which …,' and can carry a partitive sense ('some of what …').

14.meaning: A full compound verb: 'you (men) have given them (women).' It states that a group of males bestowed or handed something over to a group of females.
14.grammar: A past-tense verb of Form IV (ātā, 'to give, bring to'). The subject ending -tum means 'you (masculine plural) did'; its vowel is here stretched to -tumū to carry the following object. The object pronoun -hunna means 'them' (a group of females). So the whole reads 'you all gave them.'
14.root: أ-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (Form IV) to bring, give, bestow

15.meaning: A thing; something or anything. With a negation it commonly amounts to 'nothing at all.'
15.grammar: A singular masculine noun, indefinite ('a thing'). The -an ending (tanwīn fatḥa) is the indefinite accusative, often used here as an object or an adverbial 'in any respect / at all.'

16.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
16.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

17.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
17.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

18.meaning: 'They two fear,' 'the two of them are afraid/apprehensive.' It expresses fear or wary concern on the part of exactly two people.
18.grammar: A present/subjunctive verb. The ya- prefix marks a third-person subject ('he/they'), and the -ā ending makes it dual — 'they two.' The dual ending here lacks the final -ni (it is -ā, not -āni), showing a dependent (subjunctive/jussive) mood used after particles like 'that,' 'if,' or 'lest.'
18.root: خ-و-ف (kh-w-f) — to fear, be afraid, be in awe

19.meaning: A compound particle meaning 'that … not,' 'lest,' 'so as not to.' It introduces a clause of something feared, intended-to-prevent, or negated after a verb.
19.grammar: A merging of the particle an ('that,' which introduces a verb in the subjunctive) with the negative lā ('not'); the 'n' of an assimilates into lā, giving allā. Together they mean 'that … not' and put the following verb into the subjunctive mood, often after verbs of fearing, wishing, or commanding.

20.meaning: 'They two uphold,' 'the two of them maintain/keep up,' 'establish firmly.' Of limits or duties, it means to keep them standing — observe and maintain them properly.
20.grammar: A present/subjunctive verb of Form IV (the causative pattern: 'to make stand, set up, uphold'). The yu- prefix marks a third-person subject, and the -ā ending makes it dual, 'they two.' The dual without final -ni (-ā, not -āni) shows a dependent (subjunctive/jussive) mood used after particles like 'that' or 'not.'
20.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; (Form IV) to set up, establish, uphold

21.meaning: 'Limits,' 'bounds,' 'set boundaries.' Ḥudūd are the fixed edges or restrictions that mark off what is permitted from what is not — the appointed lines that are not to be overstepped.
21.grammar: The plural of ḥadd ('a limit, boundary, edge'). The final -a is the accusative ending, which typically marks the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon) — here, the bounds that are kept, transgressed, etc. This word also commonly stands in a possessive link with a following noun ('the limits OF …').
21.root: ح-د-د (ḥ-d-d) — to limit, demarcate; edge, boundary, restriction

22.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
22.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

23.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'fa-' ('then', 'so', 'but') drawing a consequence, joined to the conditional particle 'in' ('if'). Together: 'then if …', 'but if …'.
23.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that signals a result or transition ('then/so'). 'in' is the conditional particle 'if', introducing a supposed condition. Both are indeclinable particles with no case ending.

24.meaning: 'You (all) feared,' 'you became afraid/apprehensive.' It states that a group experienced fear or wary concern in the past.
24.grammar: A past-tense verb. The ending -tum marks the subject as second-person masculine plural, 'you all (did).' The hollow root's middle letter has dropped before the consonant ending, leaving the short stem khif- (compare khāfa, 'he feared').
24.root: خ-و-ف (kh-w-f) — to fear, be afraid, be in awe

25.meaning: A compound particle meaning 'that … not,' 'lest,' 'so as not to.' It introduces a clause of something feared, intended-to-prevent, or negated after a verb.
25.grammar: A merging of the particle an ('that,' which introduces a verb in the subjunctive) with the negative lā ('not'); the 'n' of an assimilates into lā, giving allā. Together they mean 'that … not' and put the following verb into the subjunctive mood, often after verbs of fearing, wishing, or commanding.

26.meaning: 'They two uphold,' 'the two of them maintain/keep up,' 'establish firmly.' Of limits or duties, it means to keep them standing — observe and maintain them properly.
26.grammar: A present/subjunctive verb of Form IV (the causative pattern: 'to make stand, set up, uphold'). The yu- prefix marks a third-person subject, and the -ā ending makes it dual, 'they two.' The dual without final -ni (-ā, not -āni) shows a dependent (subjunctive/jussive) mood used after particles like 'that' or 'not.'
26.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; (Form IV) to set up, establish, uphold

27.meaning: 'Limits,' 'bounds,' 'set boundaries.' Ḥudūd are the fixed edges or restrictions that mark off what is permitted from what is not — the appointed lines that are not to be overstepped.
27.grammar: The plural of ḥadd ('a limit, boundary, edge'). The final -a is the accusative ending, which typically marks the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon) — here, the bounds that are kept, transgressed, etc. This word also commonly stands in a possessive link with a following noun ('the limits OF …').
27.root: ح-د-د (ḥ-d-d) — to limit, demarcate; edge, boundary, restriction

28.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
28.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

29.meaning: A two-part word: the connective particle 'fa-' meaning 'so', 'then', or 'therefore' (drawing a consequence from what precedes), joined to 'lā', the particle of negation/prohibition. Together they convey 'so do not …' or 'so there is no …'.
29.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that links a clause to what came before and often signals a result or consequence. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a present-tense verb it commonly forms a prohibition ('do not …') or a simple negation ('not'). It carries no ending of its own.

30.meaning: Blame, sin, or fault — moral liability incurred by a wrong action; the sense of wrongdoing that counts against a person, or any leaning toward error.
30.grammar: A masculine noun. The final -a is the accusative case ending; this ending appears, among other uses, on the noun governed by a negating particle (as in the common construction 'there is no blame …').
30.root: ج-ن-ح (j-n-ḥ) — to incline, lean, tilt (toward wrong); hence fault/sin

31.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon the two of them,' 'on both of them,' 'against them two.' It places a duty, blame, or claim on exactly two parties.
31.grammar: The preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, against') takes the form ʿalay- before an attached pronoun, often conveying obligation or something weighing on someone. The suffix -himā is the dual pronoun 'the two of them'; the -i- vowel is the form the pronoun takes after this preposition.

32.meaning: A compound particle joining the preposition 'in/about' with the relative pronoun 'what', yielding 'in that which' or 'concerning what' — pointing to the matter or subject about which something is said or done.
32.grammar: A fixed combination of the preposition 'fī' and the indeclinable relative 'mā'. Being particles, neither takes a case ending; the phrase functions as 'in/about what…'.

33.meaning: 'She ransomed (herself),' 'she gave something to redeem/free herself.' Iftadā is to pay a price to release or buy back; in the feminine, a woman offering compensation to secure her own release.
33.grammar: A past-tense verb of Form VIII, a reflexive/middle pattern here giving the sense 'to ransom oneself, redeem oneself.' The ending -t (the feminine -at, with its vowel elided before the following word) marks a third-person feminine singular subject, 'she did.'
33.root: ف-د-ي (f-d-y) — to ransom, redeem, offer compensation

34.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
34.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

35.meaning: That; a demonstrative used to point to something distant or already mentioned. It singles out a single feminine (or grammatically feminine) thing, roughly 'that one over there.'
35.grammar: A feminine singular demonstrative pronoun pointing to something far off. The -ka element signals remoteness ('that yonder' rather than 'this near'). Being a demonstrative, it does not take case endings; its form is fixed.

36.meaning: Limits, bounds, or set boundaries; the fixed edges that mark what is permitted from what is forbidden.
36.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural noun, masculine. The -u ending marks the nominative case, the form used for the subject of a sentence or for naming what something is.
36.root: ح-د-د (ḥ-d-d) — to limit, define an edge; a boundary

37.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
37.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

38.meaning: A two-part word: the connective particle 'fa-' meaning 'so', 'then', or 'therefore' (drawing a consequence from what precedes), joined to 'lā', the particle of negation/prohibition. Together they convey 'so do not …' or 'so there is no …'.
38.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that links a clause to what came before and often signals a result or consequence. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a present-tense verb it commonly forms a prohibition ('do not …') or a simple negation ('not'). It carries no ending of its own.

39.meaning: A compound verb: 'you (all) overstep / transgress them,' 'go beyond them.' Iʿtadā is to exceed the proper bounds, to violate or commit aggression past a set limit.
39.grammar: A present/subjunctive verb of Form VIII (often conveying excess or transgression). The ta- prefix marks a second-person ('you') subject and the -ū ending makes it masculine plural, 'you all.' The lack of final -na (-ū, not -ūna) shows a dependent (subjunctive/jussive) mood, used after particles like 'not' or 'lest.' The suffix -hā is the object 'them/it' (feminine), referring back to a feminine or plural thing.
39.root: ع-د-و (ʿ-d-w) — to cross over, exceed; (Form VIII) to transgress, commit aggression

40.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
40.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.
40.root: — (pronoun/particle; no triliteral root)

41.meaning: 'He oversteps / transgresses,' 'goes beyond the proper bounds.' Yataʿaddā is to exceed a set limit, to violate or trespass past what is appointed.
41.grammar: A present-tense verb of Form V (a reflexive pattern, 'to take oneself across, to transgress'). The ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject, 'he.' The root ends in a weak letter, so the full form is yataʿaddā; in a dependent (jussive) mood that final weak letter (ā) is dropped. The fatḥa heard at the end (-da) is simply the inherent vowel sitting on the doubled dāl of the Form V stem, not a separate mood ending — the jussive is signalled by the deletion of the final weak letter, not by any added vowel.
41.root: ع-د-و (ʿ-d-w) — to cross over, exceed; (Form V) to transgress, overstep

42.meaning: 'Limits,' 'bounds,' 'set boundaries.' Ḥudūd are the fixed edges or restrictions that mark off what is permitted from what is not — the appointed lines that are not to be overstepped.
42.grammar: The plural of ḥadd ('a limit, boundary, edge'). The final -a is the accusative ending, which typically marks the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon) — here, the bounds that are kept, transgressed, etc. This word also commonly stands in a possessive link with a following noun ('the limits OF …').
42.root: ح-د-د (ḥ-d-d) — to limit, demarcate; edge, boundary, restriction

43.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
43.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

44.meaning: So those / then those are the ones — a connector 'so/then' joined to a demonstrative pointing to a distant or already-mentioned group: 'those people, they (are the ones who)…'.
44.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector meaning 'so/then', often introducing a result or consequence. 'ulā'ika' is a plural demonstrative ('those') pointing to people, typically picking up a previously described group and setting them up as the subject. It is fixed in form and does not change for case.

45.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (masculine plural). Standing on its own, it typically adds emphasis or marks the group out as the focus ('they, specifically', 'it is they who').
45.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It takes no case endings; the base is hum, and the final vowel appears as -u (humu) as a connecting vowel to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a definite article. Standing alone, it commonly emphasises or isolates the subject.

46.meaning: The wrongdoers; those who do wrong, act unjustly, or place things where they do not belong. The underlying image is one who oppresses, transgresses limits, and deals unjustly with others or with themselves.
46.grammar: An active participle (the doer of the action) made definite by the prefix al- ('the'). The -ūna ending marks a masculine plural in the nominative (subject) case, the form used when the word functions as the doer of a verb or the subject of a sentence.

1.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'fa-' ('then', 'so', 'but') drawing a consequence, joined to the conditional particle 'in' ('if'). Together: 'then if …', 'but if …'.
1.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that signals a result or transition ('then/so'). 'in' is the conditional particle 'if', introducing a supposed condition. Both are indeclinable particles with no case ending.

2.meaning: He divorced her; he formally released a wife from the marriage bond, setting her free of it. The verb form conveys an intensive, decisive act of releasing or letting go.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb in the intensive (Form II) pattern, third-person masculine singular ('he'). The -a on the stem marks completed past action by a single male; the attached -hā is the object pronoun 'her'.

3.meaning: A two-part word: the connective particle 'fa-' meaning 'so', 'then', or 'therefore' (drawing a consequence from what precedes), joined to 'lā', the particle of negation/prohibition. Together they convey 'so do not …' or 'so there is no …'.
3.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that links a clause to what came before and often signals a result or consequence. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a present-tense verb it commonly forms a prohibition ('do not …') or a simple negation ('not'). It carries no ending of its own.

4.meaning: She/it becomes lawful, permitted, or allowed; the act of something being released from prohibition so that it is permissible. The same root also carries the sense of something untying or becoming free.
4.grammar: A present/future-tense verb, third-person feminine singular ('she' or 'it'). The ta- prefix signals a feminine singular subject; the -u ending marks the ordinary (indicative) present tense, describing an ongoing or habitual reality.

5.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
5.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

6.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
6.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

7.meaning: After; afterward, subsequent in time or sequence. It points to what comes following something else. In this particular vowel-form it stands on its own as 'afterward' without naming what it comes after.
7.grammar: An adverb of time. The final -u here is a fixed ending taken when the word is used absolutely ('afterward'), with the thing it follows understood rather than stated, rather than being linked to a following noun.

8.meaning: 'Until / up to the point that; so that' — a particle marking a limit or goal. It expresses the end-point reached ('until') or the purpose aimed at ('so that, in order that').
8.grammar: A particle indicating a goal or limit. When followed by a present-tense verb it places that verb in the subjunctive mood (clipping its ending to -a), conveying 'until / so that' something comes about. Ḥattā itself is invariable.

9.meaning: She marries; she enters into the marriage bond, taking a husband. The verb denotes contracting marriage.
9.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person feminine singular ('she'). The ta- prefix marks the feminine singular subject. The final -a is the subjunctive ending, the form a present verb takes after certain particles such as 'until' or 'that', often giving the sense of a hoped-for or dependent action.

10.meaning: A spouse, mate, or partner; one of a pair. The word denotes either member of a married couple (husband or wife) and more broadly any one of a matched pair.

parts.en: spouse / mate / one of a pair

10.grammar: A singular noun. The -an ending marks it as indefinite ('a spouse') and in the object (accusative) case, the form used when the noun is the object of a verb or otherwise governed in that case.

11.meaning: Other than him; someone else, different from him. The word 'ghayr' expresses otherness or difference, here joined to 'him' to mean 'one different from him'.
11.grammar: A noun meaning 'other than', carrying the object (accusative) -a ending, with the attached pronoun -hu ('him'). It functions to negate sameness, marking the following or attached thing as distinct from another.

12.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'fa-' ('then', 'so', 'but') drawing a consequence, joined to the conditional particle 'in' ('if'). Together: 'then if …', 'but if …'.
12.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that signals a result or transition ('then/so'). 'in' is the conditional particle 'if', introducing a supposed condition. Both are indeclinable particles with no case ending.

13.meaning: He divorced her; he formally released a wife from the marriage bond, setting her free of it. The verb form conveys an intensive, decisive act of releasing or letting go.
13.grammar: A past-tense verb in the intensive (Form II) pattern, third-person masculine singular ('he'). The -a on the stem marks completed past action by a single male; the attached -hā is the object pronoun 'her'.

14.meaning: A two-part word: the connective particle 'fa-' meaning 'so', 'then', or 'therefore' (drawing a consequence from what precedes), joined to 'lā', the particle of negation/prohibition. Together they convey 'so do not …' or 'so there is no …'.
14.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that links a clause to what came before and often signals a result or consequence. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a present-tense verb it commonly forms a prohibition ('do not …') or a simple negation ('not'). It carries no ending of its own.

15.meaning: Blame, sin, or fault — moral liability incurred by a wrong action; the sense of wrongdoing that counts against a person, or any leaning toward error.
15.grammar: A masculine noun. The final -a is the accusative case ending; this ending appears, among other uses, on the noun governed by a negating particle (as in the common construction 'there is no blame …').
15.root: ج-ن-ح (j-n-ḥ) — to incline, lean, tilt (toward wrong); hence fault/sin

16.meaning: Upon the two of them; on, over, or incumbent upon a pair. The preposition 'ʿalā' carries the sense of being on top of, or of an obligation resting on someone, joined to a 'they-two' pronoun.
16.grammar: The preposition ʿalā ('upon, against, incumbent on') with the attached dual pronoun -himā, which specifically means 'the two of them'. The pronoun takes the -i vowel because it follows a preposition.

17.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
17.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

18.meaning: The two of them return to one another; a pair come back together, each turning back toward the other. The reciprocal verb form conveys a mutual, two-way returning.
18.grammar: A present-tense verb in the reciprocal (Form VI) pattern, which expresses an action done mutually between two or more parties. The ya- prefix marks a third-person subject and the final -ā marks the dual ('the two of them'); in this case it also serves as the subjunctive/jussive form taken after certain particles.
18.root: ر-ج-ع (r-j-ʿ) — returning, coming back, reverting

19.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
19.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

20.meaning: The two of them thought, supposed, or were of the opinion; a pair held a belief or expectation. The root spans the range from conjecture and supposition to firm conviction.
20.grammar: A past-tense verb, third-person dual ('the two of them'). The -ā ending marks completed past action done by exactly two subjects.
20.root: ظ-ن-ن (ẓ-n-n) — supposing, thinking, conjecture or conviction

21.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
21.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

22.meaning: The two of them uphold or keep up; a pair establish, maintain, and make something stand firm. The verb (Form IV) conveys causing something to stand upright, to be observed and kept in force.
22.grammar: A present-tense verb in the causative (Form IV) pattern, third-person subject with the dual -ā ending ('the two of them'). The yu- prefix is typical of Form IV present verbs; the -ā here also reflects the subjunctive/jussive form taken after certain particles, dropping the final -n of the fuller ending.

23.meaning: 'Limits,' 'bounds,' 'set boundaries.' Ḥudūd are the fixed edges or restrictions that mark off what is permitted from what is not — the appointed lines that are not to be overstepped.
23.grammar: The plural of ḥadd ('a limit, boundary, edge'). The final -a is the accusative ending, which typically marks the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon) — here, the bounds that are kept, transgressed, etc. This word also commonly stands in a possessive link with a following noun ('the limits OF …').
23.root: ح-د-د (ḥ-d-d) — to limit, demarcate; edge, boundary, restriction

24.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
24.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

25.meaning: And that; and that one. 'Tilka' is a demonstrative pointing to something distant or notable ('that' / 'those'), prefixed with 'and'. It singles out and draws attention to a thing set apart.
25.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') joined to a feminine demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' or 'those'. As a demonstrative it is fixed in form (it does not change for case) and serves to point out and identify something at a distance.

26.meaning: Limits, bounds, or set boundaries; the fixed edges that mark what is permitted from what is forbidden.
26.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural noun, masculine. The -u ending marks the nominative case, the form used for the subject of a sentence or for naming what something is.
26.root: ح-د-د (ḥ-d-d) — to limit, define an edge; a boundary

27.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
27.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

28.meaning: He makes them clear; He explains, clarifies, and sets them forth plainly so they become evident. The verb (Form II) carries the sense of making something distinct and unmistakable.
28.grammar: A present-tense verb in the intensive (Form II) pattern, third-person masculine singular ('he'). The yu- prefix marks the singular male subject; the -u ending marks the ordinary (indicative) present tense; the attached -hā is the object pronoun 'them' (referring to a feminine or non-human plural).

29.meaning: 'For a people / for a folk' — directed toward a community or group of human beings considered collectively.
29.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('for/to') joined to a noun 'people.' Because it follows a preposition, the noun takes the genitive, and the tanwīn (the -in ending) marks it as indefinite ('a people'). The whole phrase means 'for a people,' directing something toward that group.
29.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand/rise; a people, community

30.meaning: They know; they have knowledge, understanding, or awareness of something. The verb denotes possessing knowledge as an ongoing state.
30.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine plural ('they'). The ya- prefix marks the subject and the -ūna ending marks a masculine plural in the ordinary (indicative) present tense, describing ongoing or habitual knowing.
30.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — knowledge, knowing, awareness

1.meaning: 'And when...' — a linking phrase joining 'and' to 'when', used to introduce a circumstance or a recurring situation: 'and whenever / and at the time that...'.
1.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') attached to idhā ('when'). Idhā is a particle pointing to a time or condition, generally referring to something expected or recurring in the future ('when / whenever' it happens), and it normally introduces a following clause that states what occurs at that time.

2.meaning: You divorced; you (a group) formally released wives from the marriage bond. The intensive verb form conveys the decisive act of releasing.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb in the intensive (Form II) pattern. The suffix -tum(u) marks the subject as 'you' (a masculine plural group) who completed the action; the extra -u vowel is a connecting vowel that appears when another word follows.

3.meaning: 'The women' — the plural of 'woman' (a suppletive plural drawn from a different stem); women collectively.
3.grammar: A definite plural noun ('the women'). It is a suppletive plural — its singular comes from a different stem (imraʾa, 'woman'). This word is a diptote (mamnūʿ min al-ṣarf): it never takes tanwīn and uses -a for BOTH the accusative and the genitive, so it ends in -a even after a preposition (where an ordinary noun would take -i). The final -a here is therefore the diptote ending, marking the accusative as a direct object — but note it would remain -a, not -i, in the genitive too. (The 'l-' is the assimilated 'the', merging with the following n-.)

4.meaning: Then they (women) reached or attained; a group of females arrived at or came to the end of something, such as a term or limit. Prefixed with 'then', marking sequence.
4.grammar: The connector fa- ('then, so', marking sequence or consequence) joined to a past-tense verb. The -na ending marks the subject as a feminine plural ('they', women) who completed the action.
4.root: ب-ل-غ (b-l-gh) — reaching, attaining, arriving at a limit

5.meaning: Their term; the appointed time, deadline, or fixed period belonging to a group of females. 'Ajal' is a set span of time with a defined end-point.
5.grammar: A noun carrying the object (accusative) -a ending, with the attached possessive pronoun -hunna ('their', referring to a group of females). The noun denotes a fixed, bounded period of time.
5.root: أ-ج-ل (ʾ-j-l) — appointed term, fixed span of time

6.meaning: Then hold on to them / retain them; a command to a group to keep, take, and hold firmly onto females (such as wives). Prefixed with 'then', marking what follows in sequence. The verb (Form IV) conveys grasping and keeping firmly.
6.grammar: The connector fa- ('then, so') joined to a command (imperative) verb in the causative (Form IV) pattern addressed to 'you all' (masculine plural), shown by the -ū ending. The attached -hunna is the object 'them' (a group of females).

7.meaning: 'With/in goodness and fairness' — in a kind, decent, honourable way that is recognized as right. Maʿrūf is conduct acknowledged by sound sense and custom as proper.

parts.en: what is known to be good / fitting

7.grammar: The preposition bi- ('with, in') governs the noun. Maʿrūf is a passive participle used as a noun, 'that which is recognized as good.' The ending -in is the genitive (required after the preposition) combined with indefinite marking, i.e. 'in a [manner that is] fitting.'
7.root: ع-ر-ف (ʿ-r-f) — to know, recognize; what is recognized as good

8.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
8.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

9.meaning: Release them / let them go; a command to a group to set females free, send them away, and let them depart. The intensive verb form (Form II) conveys releasing freely and fully.
9.grammar: A command (imperative) verb in the intensive (Form II) pattern addressed to 'you all' (masculine plural), marked by the -ū ending. The attached -hunna is the object pronoun 'them' (a group of females).
9.root: س-ر-ح (s-r-ḥ) — sending forth, letting go, releasing freely

10.meaning: In a fitting/honorable manner; with what is recognized as good, right, and customary. 'Maʿrūf' is literally 'that which is known/recognized' — conduct commonly acknowledged as decent and proper. Prefixed with 'with/in'.

parts.en: what is recognized as good / fitting

10.grammar: The preposition bi- ('with, in, by means of') joined to a passive participle ('that which is known/recognized'). The -in ending is indefinite and genitive — the case form regularly taken by a noun after a preposition.
10.root: ع-ر-ف (ʿ-r-f) — knowing, recognizing, what is well-known as good

11.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
11.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

12.meaning: You hold on to them / retain them; a group keeps, takes, and holds firmly onto females (such as wives). The verb (Form IV) conveys grasping and keeping firmly in place.
12.grammar: A present-tense verb in the causative (Form IV) pattern, addressed to 'you all' (masculine plural). The tu- prefix marks a second-person subject and the -ū marks the masculine plural; the dropping of the fuller ending's final -n reflects the subjunctive/jussive form taken after certain particles. The attached -hunna is the object 'them' (a group of females).

13.meaning: Harming, injury, causing damage; the act of inflicting hurt or harm on someone, especially deliberately. The form suggests mutual or persistent harm-doing.
13.grammar: A verbal noun (naming the action itself) carrying the indefinite object (accusative) -an ending. In this case form it often functions to express purpose or manner — 'as harm' or 'so as to cause harm'.

14.meaning: So that you overstep / transgress; in order that a group exceed the proper bounds and commit aggression. 'Iʿtadā' (Form VIII) means to go beyond the limit, to wrong and act aggressively. Prefixed with 'so that', marking purpose.
14.grammar: The particle li- ('so that, in order to') expressing purpose, joined to a present-tense verb addressed to 'you all' (masculine plural). The -ū ending marks the masculine plural subject; after the purpose particle li-, the verb takes the subjunctive form (its fuller ending's final -n is dropped), giving the sense of an intended outcome.

15.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
15.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

16.meaning: He does, makes, or carries out; the doing or performing of an act. A general verb for engaging in or committing some deed.
16.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he'). The ya- prefix marks the singular male subject. The final consonant carries no vowel (the jussive/conditional form), which is the shortened form a present verb takes after conditional or certain other particles, typically giving the sense 'if/whoever does…'.
16.root: ف-ع-ل (f-ʿ-l) — doing, making, performing an act

17.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
17.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

18.meaning: A two-part connector: fa- means 'so', 'then', or 'and so', linking what follows as a result or consequence; qad before a past-tense verb intensifies it, conveying 'certainly', 'indeed', or 'already' — stressing that the action has truly and definitely occurred.
18.grammar: fa- is a connecting particle meaning 'so' or 'then', often marking a result. qad is a particle of emphasis; placed before a completed (past-tense) verb it affirms that the action has definitely or already happened. Neither part takes a case ending.

19.meaning: He did wrong; he acted unjustly or oppressively. The verb denotes putting something out of its rightful place — committing injustice, trespassing against what is due to Allah, to others, or to oneself.
19.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third-person masculine singular ('he'). The bare -a ending with no prefix marks a completed past action performed by a single male, or by an unspecified 'one' in general statements.

20.meaning: His own self, soul, or very being — the inner person or essence of an individual. The base noun nafs denotes the soul/self, and the attached 'his' makes it reflexive ('himself') or possessive ('his soul').
20.grammar: A noun carrying the -a (accusative) ending, which typically marks it as the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon) or the object of certain particles. The suffix -hu means 'his/him', here making the noun reflexive or possessive.
20.root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s) — self, soul, breath of life

21.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
21.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

22.meaning: That you (plural) take to yourselves, adopt, or seize for your own — the reflexive form carries the sense of taking something and making it one's own, e.g. choosing or treating something as such-and-such.

parts.en: take/adopt for yourselves (the wāw -ū marks the plural subject)
silent spelling-only alif (ألف الفارقة); not pronounced and carries no meaning

22.grammar: A present/future verb, second-person masculine plural ('you all'). The ta- prefix signals 'you', and the wāw (read -ū) on the preceding segment is the plural subject marker. The final alif is the orthographic alif al-fāriqa — a silent spelling convention written after a plural wāw, never pronounced. The absence of a final nūn shows the verb is in the subjunctive/jussive mood, typical after particles like 'that', 'not', or in prohibitions.

23.meaning: Signs, tokens, or evident proofs; also used for the discrete verses of revelation. An āya is a marker that points beyond itself to a deeper truth or to its Author.
23.grammar: A feminine plural noun ('signs/verses'). The sound-feminine plural takes -i in both the genitive and accusative; the -i ending here links it to a following noun ('… of …') or marks it as the object of a verb or preposition.

24.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
24.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

25.meaning: Mockery, ridicule, jest; something taken as an object of derision. It denotes treating a matter as a laughing-stock rather than with the seriousness it deserves.
25.grammar: A masculine indefinite noun in the accusative case, marked by the -an ('tanwīn') ending. This case commonly marks the direct object of a verb or expresses a state/manner ('as a mockery', 'in jest').

26.meaning: "And remember! / call to mind! / mention!" — a command to remember, bear in mind, or make mention of something; addressed to a group. Opened by the conjunction 'and'.
26.grammar: An imperative (command) verb addressed to a masculine plural 'you all'. The '-ū' ending directs the order at a group; the trailing silent 'alif' merely caps the plural verb. The leading 'a' of 'udhkur' is a helping vowel that drops in pronunciation after the conjunction 'and'.
26.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — to remember / mention / call to mind

27.meaning: A favor, blessing, or grace bestowed; the bounty and kindness shown by a giver, especially the abundant gifts of Allah.
27.grammar: A feminine singular noun ('favor'). The final tā' is pronounced (rather than as silent -h) because the word is in a construct chain, joining to a following noun ('the favor of …'); the -a ending here marks the accusative case, typical of a direct object.
27.root: ن-ع-م (n-ʿ-m) — favor, blessing, comfort, grace

28.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
28.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

29.meaning: 'Upon you (all)' — the preposition 'upon/on/over' joined to the plural 'you,' indicating something resting on or directed at a group.
29.grammar: The preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon/on/over') in its joined form 'ʿalay-' plus the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you all,' masculine plural). It marks the group as the recipients or target of whatever is laid 'upon' them.
29.root: — (preposition; no triliteral root)

30.meaning: And what / and that which. Combines the connective 'and' with mā, a word that can mean 'what / that which', or function as a negating particle ('not'), depending on usage.
30.grammar: The connective wa- ('and') joined to mā, an indeclinable particle (it never changes its ending). It serves either as a relative/interrogative 'what' or as a negation 'not', so its sense is fixed by context rather than by a case ending.
30.root: — (particle)

31.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'he sent down, he caused to descend, he revealed' — used especially of Allah sending down revelation, rain, or blessings from above.
31.grammar: A completed (past) action by a single masculine subject ('he'); the -a ending marks third-person masculine singular. The form IV (causative) pattern means 'to make something come down,' i.e., to send it down.
31.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — coming down, descending, alighting

32.meaning: 'Upon you (all)' — the preposition 'upon/on/over' joined to the plural 'you,' indicating something resting on or directed at a group.
32.grammar: The preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon/on/over') in its joined form 'ʿalay-' plus the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you all,' masculine plural). It marks the group as the recipients or target of whatever is laid 'upon' them.

33.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
33.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

34.meaning: 'The Book / the Scripture' — a written record or revealed scripture; literally that which is written.
34.grammar: The definite article al- with the noun kitāb ('book, scripture'), itself a verbal noun from 'to write.' The -i ending is genitive, typically marking the word as following a preposition or standing in an 'of' relationship to a preceding noun.
34.root: ك-ت-ب (k-t-b) — writing, inscribing, recording

35.meaning: And the wisdom — sound judgment, deep understanding, and the placing of things rightly; knowledge joined to right action. It often denotes Allah-given insight or the wise content of revelation.
35.grammar: The conjunction 'and' plus the definite article 'the' attached to a feminine singular noun ('wisdom'). The -i ending is genitive, which typically follows a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …').

36.meaning: He admonishes / counsels you (plural) — to exhort, warn, and instruct in a way that softens the heart and turns one toward right conduct.
36.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he'), with the ya- prefix marking 'he/it'. The -u before the suffix shows the indicative mood (a plain ongoing or habitual statement). The attached -kum is the object pronoun 'you all'.
36.root: و-ع-ظ (w-ʿ-ẓ) — admonition, exhortation, counsel

37.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
37.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

38.meaning: A command addressed to a group: 'guard yourselves / be mindful and on your guard.' The verb conveys taqwā — protecting oneself by being conscious of Allah and shielding oneself from wrongdoing and its consequences.
38.grammar: An imperative (command) verb addressed to a plural 'you (all).' The -ū ending marks the masculine plural addressees ('you all'). The pattern (form VIII, from waqā 'to protect') gives the sense of taking protective care for oneself.
38.root: و-ق-ي (w-q-y) — to guard, shield, protect oneself

39.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
39.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

40.meaning: A command meaning 'and know! / and be aware (you, plural).' Form I of the root, an order to possess knowledge or take note of something.
40.grammar: An imperative (command) to a plural 'you,' joined by wa- ('and'). The -ū ending directs the order to a masculine plural group ('all of you, know…').
40.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know, to be aware

41.meaning: An emphatic particle meaning 'that' (as in 'I know that...') or 'indeed/surely.' It introduces a statement and gives it certainty and emphasis, presenting what follows as an established fact.
41.grammar: An emphatic particle that introduces a noun-clause ('that...'). It puts the following noun into the accusative case and lends the whole statement a sense of certainty and assertion. It typically comes after verbs of knowing, saying, or informing.

42.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
42.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.
42.root: — (proper name)

43.meaning: 'Of every / with all' — the preposition 'bi' ('with / in / by') joined to the word 'every / each / all', expressing comprehensiveness applied to whatever noun follows.
43.grammar: A preposition plus a noun. The prefix bi- ('with / in / by') always places the following noun in the genitive ('of') state. The final -i on 'kull' is that genitive ending, signalling the word is governed by the preposition. 'Kull' denotes totality — 'every (single)' or 'all'.

44.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
44.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
44.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

45.meaning: 'All-Knowing / deeply knowledgeable' — an intensive adjective from the root for knowledge, describing one whose knowledge is vast and complete; when applied in the highest sense it means perfectly and comprehensively knowing all things.
45.grammar: An intensive adjective/noun of the 'faʿīl' pattern, expressing an abundant, deep-seated quality ('one who knows thoroughly'). The final -un is the nominative case with 'tanwīn' (nunation) and indefiniteness — the nominative is the basic 'subject / predicate' state, and the doubled-n sound marks it as indefinite ('(an) all-knowing one').

1.meaning: 'And when...' — a linking phrase joining 'and' to 'when', used to introduce a circumstance or a recurring situation: 'and whenever / and at the time that...'.
1.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') attached to idhā ('when'). Idhā is a particle pointing to a time or condition, generally referring to something expected or recurring in the future ('when / whenever' it happens), and it normally introduces a following clause that states what occurs at that time.

2.meaning: You divorced; you (a group) formally released wives from the marriage bond. The intensive verb form conveys the decisive act of releasing.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb in the intensive (Form II) pattern. The suffix -tum(u) marks the subject as 'you' (a masculine plural group) who completed the action; the extra -u vowel is a connecting vowel that appears when another word follows.

3.meaning: 'The women' — the plural of 'woman' (a suppletive plural drawn from a different stem); women collectively.
3.grammar: A definite plural noun ('the women'). It is a suppletive plural — its singular comes from a different stem (imraʾa, 'woman'). This word is a diptote (mamnūʿ min al-ṣarf): it never takes tanwīn and uses -a for BOTH the accusative and the genitive, so it ends in -a even after a preposition (where an ordinary noun would take -i). The final -a here is therefore the diptote ending, marking the accusative as a direct object — but note it would remain -a, not -i, in the genitive too. (The 'l-' is the assimilated 'the', merging with the following n-.)

4.meaning: Then they (women) reached or attained; a group of females arrived at or came to the end of something, such as a term or limit. Prefixed with 'then', marking sequence.
4.grammar: The connector fa- ('then, so', marking sequence or consequence) joined to a past-tense verb. The -na ending marks the subject as a feminine plural ('they', women) who completed the action.
4.root: ب-ل-غ (b-l-gh) — reaching, attaining, arriving at a limit

5.meaning: Their term; the appointed time, deadline, or fixed period belonging to a group of females. 'Ajal' is a set span of time with a defined end-point.
5.grammar: A noun carrying the object (accusative) -a ending, with the attached possessive pronoun -hunna ('their', referring to a group of females). The noun denotes a fixed, bounded period of time.
5.root: أ-ج-ل (ʾ-j-l) — appointed term, fixed span of time

6.meaning: A two-part word: the connective particle 'fa-' meaning 'so', 'then', or 'therefore' (drawing a consequence from what precedes), joined to 'lā', the particle of negation/prohibition. Together they convey 'so do not …' or 'so there is no …'.
6.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that links a clause to what came before and often signals a result or consequence. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a present-tense verb it commonly forms a prohibition ('do not …') or a simple negation ('not'). It carries no ending of its own.

7.meaning: That you (plural) prevent or hold them (feminine) back; to obstruct or constrain, especially keeping someone from a course they are entitled to take.
7.grammar: A present/future verb, second-person masculine plural ('you all'), with ta- for 'you' and -ū for the plural subject. The dropped final nūn marks the subjunctive/jussive (after particles like 'that' or 'not'). The attached -hunna is the object pronoun 'them' (a group of females).

8.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
8.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

9.meaning: They (feminine) marry; the act of entering into marriage. The verb denotes contracting marriage and the conjugal bond.
9.grammar: A present/future verb, third-person feminine plural ('they', a group of females). The ya- prefix with the -na ending marks a female group as the subject. With the feminine-plural -na, the verb form stays the same across moods (indicative or subjunctive/jussive).

10.meaning: Their (feminine) spouses/husbands. The noun zawj means a 'pair-member' — one of a matched couple, hence a husband or wife; the plural denotes the marriage partners.
10.grammar: A masculine plural noun ('spouses') with the possessive pronoun -hunna ('their', referring to a group of females). The -a ending marks the accusative case, typical of a direct object.

11.meaning: 'When' — a particle introducing a time or circumstance, generally pointing to something expected or definite to come ('when/whenever it happens'). It sets up a condition or moment whose outcome then follows.
11.grammar: An indeclinable adverb/particle of time; it has no case ending and never changes form. It typically introduces a clause about a future or recurring event ('when …'), and is normally followed by a verb describing what takes place.

12.meaning: They (plural) mutually agreed / were pleased with one another. The form denotes reciprocal good-will — both sides arriving at willing, mutual consent.
12.grammar: A past-tense verb, third-person masculine plural ('they all'). The -aw ending (with the silent alif) marks a completed past action by a plural subject. The internal pattern (tafāʿala) conveys a mutual, two-way action ('agreed with each other').

13.meaning: An adverb of place meaning 'between' or 'among', here joined to the attached pronoun 'them'; together it conveys 'between them / amongst them', signalling something situated in the midst of a group or shared among parties.
13.grammar: An adverb of place (ẓarf) ending in -a, the accusative marker typical of such adverbs, indicating a location or relationship. The attached suffix '-hum' is a possessive/object pronoun meaning 'them' (a group of males or a mixed group).
13.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies in the midst

14.meaning: 'In a fitting / honourable / customary way' — bi- ('with/in') joined to al-ma'rūf, literally 'that which is known and recognised', i.e. what is right, decent, and approved by sound custom and morality.

parts.en: what is right / recognised as good

14.grammar: The bi- prefix is a preposition 'with / in'. The l- is 'the'. The stem is a passive participle meaning 'that which is known/recognised (as good)'. The final -i is the genitive case, the form taken after a preposition like bi-.
14.root: ع-ر-ف (ʿ-r-f) — to know, recognise; hence what is recognised as good

15.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
15.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

16.meaning: He/it is admonished, counseled, or warned — the passive sense of receiving exhortation that calls one to heed and reform.
16.grammar: A present-tense passive verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it is …'). The yu- prefix with the internal vowel pattern marks the passive voice (the subject receives the action). The final -u marks the indicative mood (a plain statement).

17.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
17.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

18.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
18.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.
18.root: — (pronoun)

19.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

19.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

20.meaning: A combination meaning 'from among you' or 'of you' — singling out a part or some individuals out of a larger group being addressed.
20.grammar: The preposition min ('from, among, some of') with the attached pronoun -kum, which means 'you' for a group of two or more (grammatically masculine plural). Because the pronoun follows a preposition, it is in the object form; the whole expression partitions or draws out individuals from the addressed group.
20.root: — (min is a particle/preposition; -kum is a pronoun)

21.meaning: He believes; he has faith. The verb denotes giving heartfelt trust and assent, especially affirming faith in Allah and what He has revealed; the form also carries the sense of granting security.
21.grammar: A present/future verb, third-person masculine singular ('he'). The yu- prefix marks 'he' for this verb pattern (form IV), and the final -u marks the indicative mood — a plain ongoing or habitual statement.

22.meaning: A phrase 'in Allah / by Allah', combining the preposition 'with/in/by' and the divine name Allah, the proper name of the One God.
22.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') prefixed to the divine name Allah. A preposition always forces the following noun into the genitive case, which is why Allah here ends in -i. With verbs of believing, bi- conveys the object of faith — to believe IN.
22.root: — (Allah is the proper name of God and is not derived from a triliteral root in the usual sense)

23.meaning: "And the Day" — a stretch of time, a day; also used for the appointed Day of Judgement and Resurrection. The opening element is the conjunction 'and'.
23.grammar: A masculine singular noun with the definite article 'the' and the conjunction 'and'. The final -i is the genitive case ending: it typically signals that the word is linked to a preceding noun ('… of …') or governed by a preposition or oath particle.

24.meaning: An adjective meaning 'the last,' 'the latter,' or 'the final' — that which comes at the end of a sequence. It is the common counterpart to 'the first,' and is often used as a name for the world or life to come (the Hereafter, the Last Day), i.e. the ultimate end of all things.
24.grammar: An active-participle-type adjective on the pattern fāʿil. It carries the definite article 'al-' ('the'). The final -i is the genitive case, signaling that the word is governed by a preceding preposition or particle, or stands as the second term of a possessive link ('… of …'). It is masculine singular.
24.root: ء-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — to be last, to come after, to defer / postpone

25.meaning: A demonstrative meaning 'that' addressed to a group of people (plural 'you'). It points to something at a distance — whether physical, or to a previously mentioned matter — and is directed at multiple listeners.
25.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun for something distant. The base 'dhā' carries the sense 'that', the 'li' is an element of distance, and the ending '-kum' tells you the speaker is addressing a plural 'you' — it specifies the audience, not the thing pointed at. It does not change for case.

26.meaning: Purer, more wholesome, or more conducive to growth and blessing; the comparative/superlative of being cleansed and thriving. It joins the ideas of moral purity and fruitful increase.
26.grammar: A comparative/superlative adjective ('more/most …') on the pattern 'afʿal. The initial a- prefix forms the comparative degree; this pattern is invariable for case and does not take the usual case endings.

27.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
27.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

28.meaning: And purer / cleaner — freer from defilement and impurity, more cleansed in both the physical and moral sense.
28.grammar: The conjunction 'and' plus a comparative adjective ('purer'), on the pattern 'afʿal formed by the a- prefix. The -u ending is nominative, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate describing it.

29.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
29.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
29.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

30.meaning: 'He/it knows' — a present-tense verb of knowing: to have knowledge of, be aware of, recognize, or understand something.
30.grammar: Present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it'). The ya- prefix marks 'he,' and the final -u marks the ordinary (indicative) present, 'he knows / does know.'
30.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — knowledge; knowing, being aware, recognizing
