9.grammar: The preposition li- ('for, to') with an attached object pronoun -hunna ('them', feminine plural). It expresses that something belongs to, is owed to, or is on behalf of a group of females. (The vowel appears as 'la-' before the pronoun.)

10.meaning: A noun meaning 'an ordained obligation, a fixed and binding portion,' and specifically a stipulated bridal gift (dower) that is set and due as a duty.
10.grammar: A singular feminine noun. The -an ending is the accusative indefinite (tanwīn): it commonly marks the noun as a direct object of a verb, or expresses 'as a(n) …' / a specified amount, and lacks the definite article ('the').
10.root: ف-ر-ض (f-r-ḍ) — to appoint, ordain, make obligatory, fix a portion

11.meaning: A noun meaning 'a half / one half (of something),' prefixed with 'then / so' to introduce a consequence.
11.grammar: A prefixed fa- means 'then' or 'so,' often introducing a result. The noun carries the -u nominative ending, which typically marks it as a subject or as the starting point of a statement (e.g. 'then [due is] half …').

12.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
12.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

13.meaning: A verb meaning 'you (plural, masculine) appointed / fixed / made obligatory,' especially the act of having stipulated a set dower or duty.
13.grammar: A past-tense verb. The suffix -tum marks a second-person masculine plural subject ('you all did'). The past tense presents the action as completed, or, in a conditional clause, as something supposed to have taken place.
13.root: ف-ر-ض (f-r-ḍ) — to appoint, ordain, make obligatory, fix a portion

14.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
14.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

15.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
15.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

16.meaning: A verb meaning 'they (women) pardon / waive / forgo (a right),' i.e. willingly relinquish what is owed to them.
16.grammar: A present/imperfect verb. The ya- prefix with the -na ending marks a third-person feminine plural subject ('they', women). Note that in the feminine-plural form the verb's spelling is identical in indicative, subjunctive, and jussive, since the -na is fixed.
16.root: ع-ف-و (ʿ-f-w) — to pardon, excuse, remit, relinquish; effacement

17.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
17.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

18.meaning: A verb meaning 'the two of them pardon / waive / forgo (a right)' — referring to two parties who give up or excuse what they could otherwise claim.
18.grammar: A present/imperfect verb with a third-person masculine dual subject ('the two of them'). The final -ā (wāw + alif) is the dual marker: the full dual ending -āni is reduced to -ā in the subjunctive/jussive mood, the form a verb takes after certain particles (such as 'an, 'that').
18.root: ع-ف-و (ʿ-f-w) — to pardon, excuse, remit, relinquish; effacement

19.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
19.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

20.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in his hand,' i.e. in his possession, power, or control — the hand standing figuratively for authority over a matter.
20.grammar: The prefix bi- is a preposition ('in', 'with', 'by'). Because of it, the noun 'hand' takes the -i genitive ending. The attached -hi is a third-person masculine singular possessive pronoun ('his'); the vowel is 'hi' (rather than 'hu') because it follows the -i sound.
20.root: ي-د-ي (y-d-y) — hand; by extension power, possession, agency

21.meaning: A noun meaning 'a knot, a tie, a binding contract' — a firmly fastened bond, used figuratively for a solemn, binding agreement.
21.grammar: A singular feminine noun. The -u ending is nominative, which typically marks the word as the subject of a sentence or as a predicate. The noun stands in a possessive ('of …') construction with whatever noun follows it.
21.root: ع-ق-د (ʿ-q-d) — to tie, knot, bind, contract; a binding agreement

22.meaning: A noun meaning 'the marriage, the marriage contract,' and by extension the lawful union and intimacy it establishes.
22.grammar: A verbal noun with the definite article al- ('the'). Because 'n' is a sun letter, the article's 'l' assimilates to the following 'n' in pronunciation ('an-nikāḥ'). The -i ending is genitive, typically indicating that the word is linked to a preceding noun in an 'of …' relationship or follows a preposition.
22.root: ن-ك-ح (n-k-ḥ) — to marry, wed; the marriage bond

23.meaning: A two-part connector: 'and that.' The 'wa' joins what precedes, and 'an' is the subordinating particle 'that,' which introduces a following verb-clause (often steering it into the subjunctive) — used to report or quote a command, statement, or purpose.
23.grammar: The conjunction wa- ('and') plus the particle an, a subordinator meaning 'that' which heads a clause and commonly puts a following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood (often expressing purpose, intention, or reported speech). It is a particle and does not itself take a case ending.

24.meaning: A verb meaning 'you (plural, masculine) pardon / waive / forgo (a right)' — to graciously relinquish what is due to you.
24.grammar: A present/imperfect verb. The ta- prefix with the -ū ending marks a second-person masculine plural subject ('you all'). The ending lacks the indicative nūn, marking a subjunctive/jussive mood taken after certain particles (such as 'an, 'that').
24.root: ع-ف-و (ʿ-f-w) — to pardon, excuse, remit, relinquish; effacement

25.meaning: A comparative adjective meaning 'nearer, closer, more proximate' — describing something as having greater nearness, whether in space, time, or affinity.
25.grammar: A comparative/superlative adjective on the 'afʿal pattern ('more …' / 'most …'). The -u ending is nominative, typically marking the word as a subject or as a predicate (the thing being described). It is commonly followed by 'to / for' (li-) to name what something is nearer to.

26.meaning: A phrase meaning 'to / for godliness' — taqwā being the deep, protective God-consciousness that makes one wary of wrongdoing and careful to do right, as if shielding oneself from Allah's displeasure.
26.grammar: The prefix li- is a preposition ('to', 'for'). It is followed by the noun with its definite article al- ('the'), whose 'l' merges with the noun's initial 't' ('at-taqwā'); the doubling shows in 'li-ttaqwā'. The word ends in a fixed long -ā that does not change for case.
26.root: و-ق-ي (w-q-y) — to guard, shield, protect oneself; wariness, mindful piety

27.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
27.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

28.meaning: A verb meaning 'you (plural, masculine) forget / neglect / overlook' — letting something slip from mind or memory.
28.grammar: A present/imperfect verb. The ta- prefix with the -ū ending marks a second-person masculine plural subject ('you all'). The ending lacks the indicative nūn, indicating a subjunctive/jussive mood (used, for example, after a particle of negation or prohibition).
28.root: ن-س-ي (n-s-y) — to forget, neglect, let slip from memory

29.meaning: A noun meaning 'bounty, grace, favor, excess given freely' — generosity beyond what is strictly owed, and superiority in goodness.
29.grammar: A singular masculine noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -a ending is accusative, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon).
29.root: ف-ض-ل (f-ḍ-l) — excess, surplus, bounty, favor, superiority

30.meaning: Between you / among you; the space or relation linking the members of a group.
30.grammar: An adverb of place ('between/among') with an attached pronoun. The fixed -a ending is characteristic of such place-words; the ending -kum means 'you' for a group, so the whole means 'among you all'.
30.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation/interval; the space between two things

31.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
31.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

32.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
32.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

33.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
33.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

34.meaning: You (all) do / work / act — to carry out deeds or labor.
34.grammar: A present-tense verb (Form I). The 'ta-' prefix with the '-ūna' ending marks the second-person masculine plural ('you all'). The '-ūna' (with final 'n') is the indicative form, marking a plain ongoing or habitual statement.
34.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, work, act; deeds

35.meaning: 'All-Seeing / fully observant' — one who sees clearly and with complete insight; as a divine attribute, the One who perceives all things.
35.grammar: An intensive adjective on the faʿīl pattern, denoting one who possesses sight to a high degree — 'all-seeing'. The -un ending (tanwīn) is nominative plus indefiniteness, the form used for a subject or for a predicate ('[He] is all-seeing').

1.meaning: A command meaning 'guard, preserve, observe diligently / keep careful watch over' — to maintain something faithfully and without lapse.
1.grammar: An imperative (command) verb of the form III pattern, which adds a sense of sustained, diligent effort ('keep on guarding'). The -ū ending directs the command to a masculine plural audience ('you all, guard!').
1.root: ح-ف-ظ (ḥ-f-ẓ) — to guard, preserve, protect, keep, memorize

2.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
2.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
2.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

3.meaning: A noun meaning 'the prayers / the ritual prayers' — the formal acts of worship (ṣalāh), here in the plural denoting more than one such prayer.
3.grammar: A feminine plural noun (the -āt suffix marks the plural) with the definite article al- ('the'), whose 'l' assimilates to the initial 'ṣ' in pronunciation ('aṣ-ṣalawāt'). The -i ending on a sound feminine plural serves for both the genitive and the accusative case: it marks the noun either as an object of a verb or as linked to a preposition/preceding noun.
3.root: ص-ل-و (ṣ-l-w) — to pray, worship, supplicate; the ritual prayer

4.meaning: The ritual Prayer (ṣalāh) — the formal, prescribed act of worship; more broadly, prayer and supplication directed to Allah.
4.grammar: Begins with 'wa-' ('and') and 'al-' ('the'). The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 's' (a sun letter), which is why the 's' is doubled — a pronunciation effect, not a separate piece. The feminine '-t-' ending carries the final '-i,' which is the genitive case — the form taken after a preposition or in an 'of' linkage to a preceding word.

5.meaning: The middle one; the central or median member of a series, neither first nor last. As a feminine singular adjective it can also carry the sense of 'the best' or 'most balanced,' since the middle of a thing is often its most excellent and well-proportioned part.
5.grammar: A feminine singular adjective of the elative/superlative pattern (fuʿlā), the feminine counterpart of 'awsaṭ.' It carries the definite article 'al-' ('the'). The fixed -ā ending (alif maqṣūra) does not change for case, so the word stays the same whether it functions as subject, object, or after a preposition.

6.meaning: And stand up; rise to your feet, take an upright standing posture. By extension the verb can mean to establish, undertake, or carry out a thing dutifully.
6.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a group of males or a mixed group ('you all'), prefixed with 'wa' ('and'). The -ū ending marks the masculine plural addressee; the long 'ū' inside the stem comes from the hollow root's middle wāw. The written final alif after the wāw is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

7.meaning: A two-part word: the preposition 'li-' meaning 'to', 'for', or 'belonging to', attached to the name 'Allah'. It conveys 'to Allah' or 'for Allah'.
7.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('to/for') pulls the following noun into the genitive case, which is why 'Allah' ends in '-i' (llāhi). The '-i' ending is the regular result of a noun governed by a preposition.

8.meaning: Standing in humble, sustained devotion; people who are reverently obedient and submissive before Allah, often while standing in prayer. The word conveys quiet, wholehearted, persistent piety rather than a single act.
8.grammar: An active participle (one who is qānit) in the masculine sound plural. The -īna ending is the masculine plural form used when the word is an object or follows certain governing words (the accusative/genitive plural), as opposed to -ūna used for the subject.
8.root: ق-ن-ت (q-n-t) — devout obedience, humble submission, standing in prayer

1.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'fa-' ('then', 'so', 'but') drawing a consequence, joined to the conditional particle 'in' ('if'). Together: 'then if …', 'but if …'.
1.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that signals a result or transition ('then/so'). 'in' is the conditional particle 'if', introducing a supposed condition. Both are indeclinable particles with no case ending.

2.meaning: 'You (all) feared,' 'you became afraid/apprehensive.' It states that a group experienced fear or wary concern in the past.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb. The ending -tum marks the subject as second-person masculine plural, 'you all (did).' The hollow root's middle letter has dropped before the consonant ending, leaving the short stem khif- (compare khāfa, 'he feared').
2.root: خ-و-ف (kh-w-f) — to fear, be afraid, be in awe

3.meaning: Then on foot; people walking, as opposed to riding. 'Rijāl' here is the plural of 'rājil' (one who goes on foot, a pedestrian), distinct from the identical-looking plural meaning 'men.'
3.grammar: A plural noun prefixed with 'fa' ('then, so'). The -an ending (tanwīn fatḥ, written with an alif) marks the indefinite accusative — the case used for objects and, as here, for describing the state or manner in which something is done ('while on foot').
3.root: ر-ج-ل (r-j-l) — foot, going on foot; (also man)

4.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
4.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

5.meaning: Riding; people mounted on animals such as horses or camels. 'Rukbān' is the plural of 'rākib' (a rider, a mounted person).
5.grammar: An indefinite plural noun. The -an ending (tanwīn fatḥ, written with an alif) marks the indefinite accusative — the case used for objects and for describing the manner or state in which an action is performed ('while riding').

6.meaning: Then, when… — a connective opening that introduces a circumstance and its consequence: 'and so, at the time when (such-and-such happens)…'
6.grammar: A two-part connective. The prefix fa- means 'then/so', linking to what came before. The particle idhā means 'when' and points to a future or general circumstance, setting up a condition whose result then follows. It is an indeclinable particle, so it has no case ending.

7.meaning: You (all) became safe and secure; you felt safe, free from fear or danger. The verb denotes the arrival of a state of security and trust.
7.grammar: A past-tense verb with the suffix -tum, which marks the doer as 'you all' (masculine plural). The past tense presents the action as completed, though after a conditional word it often carries the sense 'when/if you become secure.'

8.meaning: A call to remember, mention, invoke, or call to mind — especially to remember Allah by mentioning Him and being mindful of Him. The opening 'then/so' links the command to something preceding.

parts.en: remember / mention! (command stem with plural wāw)

8.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a group: the -ū ending means 'you (plural masculine), do it!'. The prefixed fa- means 'then' or 'so', connecting the order to a preceding statement or condition. The initial alif is a helping vowel to make the command pronounceable.
8.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — to remember, mention, call to mind, invoke

9.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
9.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

10.meaning: A two-part comparative expression meaning 'just as' or 'in the same way that.' It combines the likeness-particle 'like/as' with a connector that introduces a following clause, so the whole means 'in the manner that…'
10.grammar: A fixed particle compound. 'ka' expresses likeness ('like, as'); 'mā' here is a connector turning the phrase into 'as / just as.' It is indeclinable and has no case ending.

11.meaning: He taught you; He imparted knowledge or skill to you. The doubled middle consonant gives the sense of teaching thoroughly or instructing carefully.
11.grammar: A past-tense verb of the intensive (faʿʿala) pattern, whose doubled middle letter conveys causing or carefully imparting. The bare verb with final -a indicates a single masculine 'he' did it in the past; the attached -kum is the object pronoun 'you all.'

12.meaning: A short, highly versatile particle 'mā.' It can mean 'what' or 'that which,' can negate ('not'), and can serve as an intensifier attached to another word. Its precise force depends on what it accompanies, but its core is to point to a thing or to add emphasis.
12.grammar: A multifunctional particle. It does not take case endings. Depending on usage it can be a relative ('that which'), an interrogative ('what?'), a negator ('not'), or — when joined to another particle — an emphasizer. It is uninflected and indeclinable.

13.meaning: A negating particle, 'not', used specifically to deny that an action happened in the past, even though it attaches to a present-tense verb form. It turns 'you do X' into 'you did not do X'.

parts.en: did not (negation of a completed act)

13.grammar: An indeclinable particle that governs the verb after it, putting that verb into the jussive (clipped) mood and giving it past-time meaning. In short: lam + a present-form verb = 'did not [verb]'.

14.meaning: You (plural) are / you happen to be. A form of the 'hollow' verb kāna ('to be'), which links a subject to a state or description, or expresses simply being or existing.
14.grammar: Present/imperfect verb, 2nd person masculine plural ('you all'). The ta- prefix marks 2nd person; the -ū ending marks masculine plural. The dropping of the usual final -na (so takūnū rather than takūnūna) shows the verb is in the subjunctive or jussive mood — the form expected after conditional or subordinating particles.
14.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

15.meaning: A verb addressed to a group: 'you (all) know', 'you have knowledge', 'you are aware'. From the root meaning 'to know'.
15.grammar: The 'ta-' prefix marks a present/future verb addressed to 'you'. The '-ūna' ending marks a masculine plural subject and is the full 'indicative' form, signalling an ongoing, factual statement ('you (all) do know'), as opposed to the shortened '-ū' used after certain particles.

1.meaning: 'And those who': a connective phrase introducing a specified group of people (masculine plural) about whom something will be said. It links them to what came before.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'), which is masculine plural. A relative pronoun stands for a group and is normally followed by a clause describing them. Its form does not change for case; it stays alladhīna whatever its grammatical role.

2.meaning: A verb meaning 'they are taken in full (in death)', i.e. 'they pass away' — their souls are taken back completely. The passive of a verb meaning to take a thing fully and entirely.

parts.en: taken in full, caused to die

2.grammar: A present-tense passive verb, third-person masculine plural ('they'). The yu- prefix plus the -na ending mark a 'they' subject, and the yu- with the verb's vowel pattern makes it passive — the action is done to them. The root sense 'to take fully' becomes, in this idiom, 'to have one's soul taken', i.e. to die.
2.root: و-ف-ي (w-f-y) — to be complete, to fulfil; to take in full

3.meaning: 'From you / among you (plural)' — indicating a part taken out of, or belonging to, a group of people being addressed.
3.grammar: The preposition min ('from, of, among') joined to the attached pronoun -kum ('you all,' masculine plural). Together they express partition or origin: a part drawn 'from / among' the addressed group.

4.meaning: A verb meaning 'they leave behind' or 'they leave remaining' — to let something stay or remain after departing. Conveys leaving a thing in place.
4.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine plural ('they'), joined by wa- ('and'). The ya- prefix together with the -na ending mark a 'they' subject and the indicative mood, used for an ongoing or general statement of fact. This verb is used only in the present/imperative; it means to let remain or leave behind.
4.root: و-ذ-ر (w-dh-r) — to leave, to leave behind (used only in present/command)

5.meaning: A noun meaning 'spouses', 'mates', or 'wives' — the plural of a word denoting one of a pair joined together, hence a husband or wife. Context determines whether husbands or wives are meant.
5.grammar: A plural noun with the -an ending, which is accusative and indefinite. The accusative typically marks the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon). The azC-ā-C shape is a broken-plural pattern. The singular denotes either partner of a married pair.
5.root: ز-و-ج (z-w-j) — to pair, to join as a couple; spouse, mate

6.meaning: A bequest or will; a directive a person makes about what should be done after their death, especially concerning property or the care of dependents. More broadly, an earnest injunction or solemn charge to do something.
6.grammar: A feminine singular noun prefixed with 'wa' ('and'); the doubling of the wāw reflects assimilation of that 'and' to the following sound. The -tan ending (tāʾ marbūṭa with tanwīn fatḥ) marks the indefinite accusative, the case for objects of verbs.
6.root: و-ص-ي (w-ṣ-y) — to enjoin, bequeath, charge, instruct

7.meaning: For their spouses; belonging to or for the benefit of their partners in marriage. 'Azwāj' is the plural of 'zawj,' which denotes a spouse or a member of a pair.
7.grammar: A plural noun built from the preposition 'li-' ('for, to') + the noun + the possessive pronoun -him ('their'). The -i vowel on the stem is the genitive case, required because the noun follows the preposition 'li-' and is possessed by an attached pronoun.

8.meaning: Provision, enjoyment, or maintenance; goods, comfort, or sustenance that one is given to benefit from for a time. The word suggests something useful and enjoyable that is, by nature, temporary.
8.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The -an ending (tanwīn fatḥ, written with alif) marks the indefinite accusative; this case commonly serves as the object of a verb or expresses purpose ('as provision').
8.root: م-ت-ع (m-t-ʿ) — to provide enjoyment/benefit; goods, comfort

9.meaning: 'To / toward / up to' — a preposition marking the endpoint, goal, or limit of an action or motion: the direction something moves toward or the boundary at which it stops.
9.grammar: An invariable preposition. It has no case ending of its own but puts the noun that follows it into the genitive ('of / to' state). It indicates direction toward, or the terminal limit of, something.

10.meaning: The year; a full annual cycle. 'Ḥawl' carries the underlying sense of something coming round full circle, hence a complete turn of the year.
10.grammar: A definite singular noun with the article 'al-' ('the'). The -i ending is the genitive case: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… of the year') or follows a preposition.
10.root: ح-و-ل (ḥ-w-l) — to turn, revolve, change; a year (full cycle)

11.meaning: 'Other than / different from / not'. A noun used to express difference or negation — 'something other than X', and so 'not-X'. It functions to exclude or contrast with what follows.
11.grammar: A noun of difference/exception. The -a ending marks the accusative case, the form it takes when it serves as a direct object or as a descriptive substitute standing in an object position; it governs a following noun in the genitive ('other than …'). That it takes case endings and tanwīn confirms it is a true noun, not a particle.
11.root: غ-ي-ر (gh-y-r) — to be other, different; otherness, change

12.meaning: An expelling or driving out; the act of forcing someone or something to leave a place. The form names the action itself (a 'turning-out').
12.grammar: A verbal noun (the name of the action) of the causative (ʾafʿala) pattern, meaning 'to make go out.' The -in ending (tanwīn kasr) marks the indefinite genitive — used after prepositions or when linked to a preceding noun.
12.root: خ-ر-ج (kh-r-j) — to go out, exit; (causative) to bring/drive out

13.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'fa-' ('then', 'so', 'but') drawing a consequence, joined to the conditional particle 'in' ('if'). Together: 'then if …', 'but if …'.
13.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that signals a result or transition ('then/so'). 'in' is the conditional particle 'if', introducing a supposed condition. Both are indeclinable particles with no case ending.

14.meaning: They (women) went out, departed, or left a place. The verb describes a group of females exiting.
14.grammar: A past-tense verb with the suffix -na, which marks the doers as 'they' (a group of females). The past tense presents the action as completed.
14.root: خ-ر-ج (kh-r-j) — to go out, exit, depart

15.meaning: A two-part word: the connective particle 'fa-' meaning 'so', 'then', or 'therefore' (drawing a consequence from what precedes), joined to 'lā', the particle of negation/prohibition. Together they convey 'so do not …' or 'so there is no …'.
15.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that links a clause to what came before and often signals a result or consequence. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a present-tense verb it commonly forms a prohibition ('do not …') or a simple negation ('not'). It carries no ending of its own.

16.meaning: Blame, sin, or fault — moral liability incurred by a wrong action; the sense of wrongdoing that counts against a person, or any leaning toward error.
16.grammar: A masculine noun. The final -a is the accusative case ending; this ending appears, among other uses, on the noun governed by a negating particle (as in the common construction 'there is no blame …').
16.root: ج-ن-ح (j-n-ḥ) — to incline, lean, tilt (toward wrong); hence fault/sin

17.meaning: A small unit: the preposition 'upon / on / over' — also carrying the sense of an obligation 'incumbent upon' — joined to the pronoun 'you (plural)'. So: 'upon you / it is your duty'.
17.grammar: 'ʿalā' is the preposition 'upon/on/over'; before an attached pronoun it appears as 'ʿalay-'. The suffix -kum is 'you' for a group of men (or a mixed group). The phrase often conveys duty or burden resting on someone ('it is upon you to …'). Pronouns attached to a preposition always take the genitive form.

18.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
18.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
18.root: — (particle)

19.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
19.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

20.meaning: 'They did / made / performed' — to do or carry out an act (said of a group of females).
20.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb. The suffix -na is the third-person feminine plural ending: 'they (females) did.' It marks a completed action performed by a group of females. The root f-ʿ-l is also the model verb Arabic grammarians use to illustrate all verb patterns.

21.meaning: The preposition 'in / within / during.' It places something inside a container, period, place, or matter.
21.grammar: A preposition. It governs the noun that follows, putting it in the genitive case and situating something inside it — in space, in time ('during'), or in a circumstance.

22.meaning: 'Themselves' — literally 'their own selves/souls' (of females). Anfus is the plural of nafs ('self, soul, person'); with the attached pronoun it expresses the reflexive 'their own selves.'
22.grammar: A plural noun ('selves') with an attached possessive pronoun -hinna ('their,' feminine plural). The -i ending is genitive: the noun is governed by a preceding preposition or is in a possessive ('of …') construction.

23.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
23.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

24.meaning: What is recognized as good and fitting; honorable, decent, and customary conduct. 'Maʿrūf' is literally 'that which is known/recognized,' i.e., behavior commonly acknowledged as right and proper.

parts.en: what is good and recognized (indefinite genitive)

24.grammar: A passive participle (literally 'that which is known/recognized'). The -in ending (tanwīn kasr) marks the indefinite genitive — the case used after prepositions or when the word is linked to a preceding noun. The doubled initial mīm reflects assimilation of a preceding 'and' (wa) into this word.
24.root: ع-ر-ف (ʿ-r-f) — to know, recognize; what is commonly known as good

25.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
25.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
25.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

26.meaning: Mighty, invincible, and supremely honoured; one who possesses overwhelming power and dignity such that none can overcome or resist Him. As a divine descriptor it conveys unassailable might joined with exalted worth.
26.grammar: A descriptive noun (adjective) on an intensive pattern, conveying a deep, enduring quality. The -un ending is indefinite and nominative: it typically marks the word as a subject or as a predicate describing something ("is mighty").

27.meaning: Wise; possessing perfect, far-reaching wisdom that places everything in its right order and purpose. It implies sound judgement and flawless governance, not merely cleverness.
27.grammar: A descriptive noun (adjective) on an intensive pattern, expressing a settled, profound quality. The -un ending is indefinite and nominative: it typically marks a subject or a predicate describing something ("is wise").
27.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — wisdom, sound judgement, to govern

1.meaning: And for the divorced women; women who have been released from the marriage bond. 'Muṭallaqāt' refers to those who have been divorced (set free) by their husbands.
1.grammar: A feminine plural passive participle ('the ones who have been divorced') of the intensive (faʿʿala) pattern, prefixed with 'wa' ('and'), 'li-' ('for'), and the article 'al-' (the 'a' elides after li-). The final -i is the genitive case, required after the preposition 'li-'; for the feminine sound plural this -i also serves where an object (accusative) case would otherwise call for it.
1.root: ط-ل-ق (ṭ-l-q) — to set free, release; divorce

2.meaning: Provision, enjoyment, or maintenance; a beneficial gift of goods, comfort, or sustenance that one is given to make use of, typically for a limited time.
2.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The -un ending (tanwīn ḍamm) marks the indefinite nominative — the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or for the thing being stated to exist ('there is a provision').
2.root: م-ت-ع (m-t-ʿ) — to provide enjoyment/benefit; goods, comfort

3.meaning: 'In a fitting / honourable / customary way' — bi- ('with/in') joined to al-ma'rūf, literally 'that which is known and recognised', i.e. what is right, decent, and approved by sound custom and morality.

parts.en: what is right / recognised as good

3.grammar: The bi- prefix is a preposition 'with / in'. The l- is 'the'. The stem is a passive participle meaning 'that which is known/recognised (as good)'. The final -i is the genitive case, the form taken after a preposition like bi-.
3.root: ع-ر-ف (ʿ-r-f) — to know, recognise; hence what is recognised as good

4.meaning: A right, a due, or an obligation — that which is true, real, and rightfully owed; an established duty. As an adverbial accusative it conveys "as a duty/obligation, in truth, bindingly."
4.grammar: A noun in the indefinite accusative. The '-an' (nunation on the fatḥa, with a following alif) often functions adverbially here — "as a binding duty" or "in truth" — describing the manner or affirming the statement.
4.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — to be true, right, established; truth, right

5.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
5.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
5.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

6.meaning: The God-conscious / the mindful — those who guard themselves against wrongdoing out of reverent awareness of Allah (taqwā), shielding their souls by dutiful caution. The "al-" makes it definite ("the mindful ones").

parts.en: one who is God-conscious / guards himself

6.grammar: A definite active participle in the masculine sound plural (singular "muttaqin"). The "-īna" ending is the plural form in the genitive/accusative (oblique) case — used for governed nouns, objects, or after prepositions.

1.meaning: 'Like that / thus / in this manner.' A comparison word meaning that something is done or is the case in the way just mentioned.
1.grammar: The comparison particle ka- ('like/as') prefixed to the demonstrative 'that'. Together they form a fixed adverbial expression, 'like that / thus', which does not change its ending with grammatical position.
1.root: — (a particle of comparison joined to a demonstrative; no root)

2.meaning: He makes clear / He explains; to set something forth plainly so that its meaning is evident.
2.grammar: A Form II present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he'). The yu- prefix marks 'he', and the final -u marks the indicative mood — a plain, ongoing statement of fact (he makes clear / he is making clear).

3.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
3.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

4.meaning: 'For you / to you (plural)' — the preposition li- ('for, to, belonging to') joined to the attached pronoun for a group being addressed.
4.grammar: li- is a preposition meaning 'for/to'; its vowel appears here as 'la' before the attached pronoun. The -kum ending is the attached pronoun for a masculine plural 'you', so the whole means 'for you (all)'.

5.meaning: 'His signs / His verses.' The plural of a word meaning a sign, token, or mark that points to a greater reality — also used for the verses of revelation — here joined to 'his'.
5.grammar: A sound feminine plural ('signs') with an attached possessive 'his'. The -i ending is the genitive case, the form this plural takes when it follows a preposition or is linked as the object of a possessor; the -hi ('his') marks ownership: 'his signs'.
5.root: أ-ي-ي (ʾ-y-y) — a sign, token, mark; a verse of revelation

6.meaning: 'so that you may…,' 'in the hope that you…' — a particle expressing purpose, expectation, or hopeful anticipation, fused with 'you (plural).' It introduces a hoped-for or intended outcome; when used of Allah it conveys the desired result rather than uncertainty.

parts.en: so that / perhaps / in hope that

6.grammar: An emphatic particle of hope/purpose belonging to the 'inna' family, which attaches a pronoun as its subject. The particle's fixed form ends in '-a,' and the suffix '-kum' is 'you (plural),' giving 'so that you (all) may…'

7.meaning: You (all) use reason; you understand, comprehend, and think things through. The verb 'ʿaqala' means to grasp with the mind and to restrain oneself by sound judgment, reflecting the link between intellect and self-control.
7.grammar: A present/future-tense verb. The 'ta-' prefix together with the -ūna ending marks the subject as 'you all' (masculine plural). The full -ūna ending also signals the ordinary (indicative) mood — a plain statement or question, not a command or a negated/subordinate form.
7.root: ع-ق-ل (ʿ-q-l) — to reason, understand; intellect, restraint

1.meaning: 'Did not…?' — a particle combining a question with negation, used to ask 'Have I/has he not…?', often expecting agreement or serving as a gentle reminder.
1.grammar: An interrogative prefix 'a-' ('?') joined to the negation 'lam'. 'lam' negates a verb and places it firmly in the past ('did not'), and grammatically puts the following present-tense verb into the jussive (clipped) form. Together they form a rhetorical or confirming question.

2.meaning: You see, perceive, or take notice; to observe with the eye, or by extension to come to know or consider. Often used to draw attention, as in 'have you considered…?'
2.grammar: A present-tense verb addressed to a single male 'you,' marked by the 'ta-' prefix. The root's weak final letter has dropped, leaving the short final -a; this shortened form is the jussive/apocopated form, which appears after certain particles (such as 'did not' or in questions like 'have you not seen?').
2.root: ر-أ-ي (r-ʾ-y) — to see, perceive, consider, form an opinion

3.meaning: 'To / toward / up to' — a preposition marking the endpoint, goal, or limit of an action or motion: the direction something moves toward or the boundary at which it stops.
3.grammar: An invariable preposition. It has no case ending of its own but puts the noun that follows it into the genitive ('of / to' state). It indicates direction toward, or the terminal limit of, something.

4.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
4.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

5.meaning: They went out, departed, or left; a group exiting from a place. The verb denotes the act of going forth.
5.grammar: A past-tense verb with the -ū ending, which marks the doers as 'they' (a group of males or a mixed group). The past tense presents the action as completed. The written final alif after the wāw is a silent spelling convention.
5.root: خ-ر-ج (kh-r-j) — to go out, exit, depart

6.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
6.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

7.meaning: Their homes or dwellings; the places where they live. 'Diyār' is the plural of 'dār,' a house, abode, or region one inhabits.
7.grammar: A plural noun followed by the possessive pronoun -him ('their'). The -i vowel on the stem is the genitive case, here triggered by the attached possessor and typical after prepositions or in possessive linkage ('the homes of…').

8.meaning: 'While they / and they' — the word 'wa' (here 'while' or 'and') joined to the standalone pronoun 'hum' ('they'), referring to a masculine plural group.
8.grammar: A connective 'wa' — often circumstantial 'while' — plus the independent subject pronoun 'hum' ('they'), used for a masculine plural group. As an independent pronoun it usually stands as the subject of a following statement.

9.meaning: Thousands; a large number in the order of thousands. 'Ulūf' is a plural of 'alf' (a thousand), conveying a great multitude.
9.grammar: An indefinite plural noun. The -un ending (tanwīn ḍamm) marks the indefinite nominative — the case typically used for the subject of a sentence ('thousands [did/were]…').
9.root: ا-ل-ف (ʾ-l-f) — a thousand; (also to be familiar/joined)

10.meaning: 'out of fear / caution', or 'guarding against'. It denotes wary dread of something and taking precaution to avoid it.
10.grammar: A singular noun in the accusative case (marked by the final -a). In this form it commonly functions adverbially, expressing the reason or motive for an action — 'because of / out of fear (of)'.
10.root: ح-ذ-ر (ḥ-dh-r) — to be wary, beware, take caution

11.meaning: Death; the ending of life, the departure of the soul from the body. The definite form names death as a known reality.
11.grammar: A definite singular noun with the article 'al-' ('the'). The -i ending is the genitive case: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… of death') or follows a preposition.

12.meaning: 'Then he said / so he said' — the past-tense verb 'he said,' introduced by a connector meaning 'then / so,' marking what follows as the next or resulting step.
12.grammar: The prefix fa- means 'then / so,' linking this to what came before and often implying sequence or consequence. The verb is past-tense, third-person masculine singular ('he'); the final -a is the base vowel of the 3rd-person masculine singular past form, marking that a single masculine subject performed the action.

13.meaning: To them / for them — the preposition li- ('to, for') joined to the pronoun 'them'. It expresses that something is directed toward, belongs to, or is for the benefit of a group.
13.grammar: The preposition li- ('to/for') combined with the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). When li- takes a pronoun its vowel becomes 'la-'. The final -u here is a connecting vowel added to ease pronunciation before a following word; it carries no case meaning of its own.

14.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
14.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

15.meaning: Die!; a command to undergo death. As an imperative it expresses a decree or summons for life to cease.
15.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a group ('you all'), with the -ū ending marking the masculine plural addressee. The middle wāw belongs to the hollow root, surfacing here as the long 'ū.' The written final alif after the wāw is a silent spelling convention.

16.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
16.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

17.meaning: He gave them life, brought them to life, or revived them; the act of bestowing or restoring life. The causative form means to make something live.
17.grammar: A past-tense verb of the causative (ʾafʿala) pattern ('to make alive'), with the attached object pronoun -hum ('them'). The verb itself is third-person masculine singular ('he'), and the long final -ā reflects the weak final letter of the root.
17.root: ح-ي-ي (ḥ-y-y) — to live, be alive; (causative) to give life

18.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
18.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

19.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
19.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

20.meaning: An emphatic statement that someone is truly the holder or owner of something. The opening lām is a particle of emphasis ('surely/indeed'), and dhū means 'owner of, possessor of, the one endowed with' — it is a word that always governs a following noun to say someone is rich in or characterized by that thing.
20.grammar: The la- prefix is the 'lām of emphasis' that strengthens a statement ('indeed, surely'). Dhū is one of the special 'five nouns'; its long -ū ending marks the nominative (subject) case, the form used when this word is the doer or the thing being described, and it must be followed by a noun in the genitive ('possessor OF …').

21.meaning: Bounty, grace, favor; an overflowing generosity or surplus given freely. It denotes goodness and abundance bestowed beyond what is owed or expected, and by extension excellence or superiority.
21.grammar: The -in ending is genitive plus 'tanwīn' (the -n indicating indefiniteness, 'a bounty'). The genitive case typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF bounty') or follows a preposition.
21.root: ف-ض-ل (f-ḍ-l) — bounty, grace, excess goodness, superiority

22.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
22.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
22.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

23.meaning: Humankind, people, mankind — the collective of human beings.
23.grammar: A collective noun ('people, mankind') carrying the definite article al- ('the'); the 'l' of the article assimilates into the following 'n', doubling it (al-nās → an-nās). The genitive ending -i marks the word as governed by a preposition or as the second term of a possessive.
23.root: ء-ن-س (ʾ-n-s) — humankind, sociability, familiarity; the word for 'people' is most commonly traced to this root (related to insān, 'human being')

24.meaning: But; however; rather. A particle of correction or contrast that cancels or qualifies a preceding statement and introduces what is actually the case.
24.grammar: A connective wa- ('and') joined to the emphatic particle lākinna. Lākinna belongs to the 'inna family: it governs the noun that follows it, putting it in the accusative case, and adds a sense of firm contrast — 'but in fact …'.
24.root: — (particle)

25.meaning: More numerous, greater in quantity, the greater part or 'most'. It is the comparative/superlative form built from 'kathīr' (many), expressing 'more' or 'the most' in number or amount.
25.grammar: The pattern af'al makes this an 'elative' (comparative/superlative: 'more/most'). The -a ending is accusative, the case used for the object of a verb or for many adverbial roles.

26.meaning: Humankind, people, mankind — the collective of human beings.
26.grammar: A collective noun ('people, mankind') carrying the definite article al- ('the'); the 'l' of the article assimilates into the following 'n', doubling it (al-nās → an-nās). The genitive ending -i marks the word as governed by a preposition or as the second term of a possessive.
26.root: ء-ن-س (ʾ-n-s) — humankind, sociability, familiarity; the word for 'people' is most commonly traced to this root (related to insān, 'human being')

27.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
27.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

28.meaning: They give thanks, they are grateful — to acknowledge a kindness and respond to it with gratitude and praise. The verb conveys recognizing a benefit and honoring its giver.
28.grammar: A present/future-tense verb. The ya-…-ūna frame marks third-person masculine plural ('they …'). The full -ūna ending shows the indicative mood, the plain factual form used for ongoing or habitual action ('they do thank').

1.meaning: And fight / do battle. A command to engage in combat. The verb is the mutual third-pattern form, implying fighting against an opposing party.
1.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a second-person masculine plural ('you all'). It is the third (mutual/reciprocal) verb pattern, which conveys fighting against an adversary. The -ū ending marks the masculine-plural addressee; wa means 'and.'
1.root: ق-ت-ل (q-t-l) — to kill; in this pattern, to fight, do battle

2.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
2.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

3.meaning: 'path, way, road' — a route or course; figuratively a cause or way of life one travels along. In construct ('the way OF ...').
3.grammar: A singular noun with the '-i' (genitive) ending, which typically links it to a following noun ('the way OF ...') or follows a preposition. It marks the word as connected to or possessed by what comes after.

4.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
4.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

5.meaning: A command meaning 'and know! / and be aware (you, plural).' Form I of the root, an order to possess knowledge or take note of something.
5.grammar: An imperative (command) to a plural 'you,' joined by wa- ('and'). The -ū ending directs the order to a masculine plural group ('all of you, know…').
5.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know, to be aware

6.meaning: An emphatic particle meaning 'that' (as in 'I know that...') or 'indeed/surely.' It introduces a statement and gives it certainty and emphasis, presenting what follows as an established fact.
6.grammar: An emphatic particle that introduces a noun-clause ('that...'). It puts the following noun into the accusative case and lends the whole statement a sense of certainty and assertion. It typically comes after verbs of knowing, saying, or informing.

7.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
7.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

8.meaning: All-Hearing / ever-hearing — one who hears completely and perfectly, missing nothing of what is uttered or whispered; an intensive form stressing the fullness of the quality. The '-un' nunation marks it as indefinite nominative.
8.grammar: An intensive adjective (faʿīl pattern) conveying a constant, perfect quality. The '-un' (nunation on the ḍamma) marks it as indefinite and in the nominative case, typically used for a subject or predicate ("is all-hearing").

9.meaning: An intensive adjective/name meaning 'All-Knowing / fully aware' — one whose knowledge is complete, deep, and all-encompassing; as a divine attribute it denotes Allah's perfect knowledge.
9.grammar: An intensive adjective (the pattern faʿīl conveys 'thoroughly, abundantly'). The ending -un is the indefinite nominative — the nominative case marks it as the subject or the quality being affirmed, and the -n (nunation) signals 'a / an', i.e. indefinite. So it reads '(is) all-knowing'.

1.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
1.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

2.meaning: A demonstrative meaning 'this one' or 'the one' — a pointing word ('that/this') used to single out a person or thing. It often combines with the question particle to form 'who is it that…?'
2.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun ('this/that one'). It does not take case endings; the final -ā is part of the fixed word. It functions to point out or identify someone or something.

3.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
3.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

4.meaning: He lends, he gives a loan — to advance something of value with the expectation it will be repaid or returned. The verb pictures giving out wealth as a loan.
4.grammar: A present/future verb in the derived 'af'ala' pattern (causing/giving: 'to lend'). The yu- prefix marks third-person masculine singular ('he'), and the final -u marks the indicative mood, the plain factual form ('he lends').
4.root: ق-ر-ض (q-r-ḍ) — lending, a loan, cutting off (a portion given out)

5.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
5.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

6.meaning: A loan; something handed over to another to be repaid or given back later. It is the noun naming the act or object of lending.
6.grammar: The -an ending is accusative with 'tanwīn' (-n for indefiniteness, 'a loan'). The accusative is the case for the object of a verb, so this names what is being given or lent.

7.meaning: Good, fine, beautiful, excellent — pleasing and praiseworthy in quality. It describes something done well or possessing goodness and beauty.
7.grammar: An adjective ('good'). The -an ending is accusative with 'tanwīn' (-n, indefinite). As an adjective it agrees with and describes a noun; the accusative case matches a noun in that same case.

8.meaning: So that He multiplies it, doubles it, increases it many times over. The opening fa- means 'so/then', and the verb means to compound or multiply a thing into multiples of itself; the attached pronoun refers to the thing multiplied ('it').
8.grammar: Fa- is a connector ('so/then'). The verb is in the 'fā'ala' pattern (intensive: 'to multiply/double'). The yu- prefix marks 'he'; the -a ending here is subjunctive, a mood often signaling purpose or result ('so that He may multiply'). The attached -hu is an object pronoun ('it/him').

9.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
9.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

10.meaning: Multiples, manifold amounts, double-and-redoubled portions. It is the plural of 'ḍiʿf' (a double/multiple) and conveys increase folded many times over.
10.grammar: A broken (internal) plural meaning 'multiples'. The -an ending is accusative with 'tanwīn' (-n, indefinite); the accusative often serves to specify amount or manner ('by multiples, manifold').

11.meaning: Many, numerous, much — large in number or quantity. The feminine form of 'kathīr', describing abundance.
11.grammar: An adjective ('many'). The -at- (tā' marbūṭa) marks it feminine, so it describes a feminine noun; the -an is the accusative case with 'tanwīn' (-n, indefinite), matching a feminine noun in the accusative.

12.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
12.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
12.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

13.meaning: He withholds, restrains, grasps, or contracts — to draw in, hold back, or tighten (as opposed to spreading out). It can describe restricting provision or seizing/taking in.
13.grammar: A present/future verb. The ya- prefix marks third-person masculine singular ('he'); the final -u marks the indicative mood, the plain factual form ('he withholds').

14.meaning: And He spreads out, extends, expands, or grants generously — to lay open and enlarge (provision, a hand, the earth). The wa- means 'and'; the verb is the opposite of withholding, conveying open-handed abundance.
14.grammar: Wa- means 'and'. The verb is present/future; the ya- prefix marks third-person masculine singular ('he'), and the final -u marks the indicative mood, the plain factual form ('he spreads out').

15.meaning: And to Him / toward Him. The wa- means 'and'; ilā is the preposition 'to/toward' indicating direction or destination; the attached pronoun -hi means 'him'.
15.grammar: Wa- means 'and'. Ilā ('to/toward') is a preposition of direction; it takes the special form 'ilay-' before a pronoun. The attached -hi is the genitive pronoun 'him', the form pronouns take after prepositions; the -i vowel reflects that genitive attachment.

16.meaning: 'You are returned / brought back' — a passive verb from the root meaning to return: the subjects are made to go back, sent back to a point of origin, the action being done to them rather than by them.
16.grammar: Present/future passive. The tu- prefix with the -ūna ending marks a second-person masculine plural subject ('you all'), and the internal vowelling (u–a) makes it passive — the action is done TO the subject. The -ūna ending is the full ('indicative') plural form, used when the verb is not cut short by certain particles.

1.meaning: 'Did not…?' — a particle combining a question with negation, used to ask 'Have I/has he not…?', often expecting agreement or serving as a gentle reminder.
1.grammar: An interrogative prefix 'a-' ('?') joined to the negation 'lam'. 'lam' negates a verb and places it firmly in the past ('did not'), and grammatically puts the following present-tense verb into the jussive (clipped) form. Together they form a rhetorical or confirming question.

2.meaning: You see, perceive, or take notice; to observe with the eye, or by extension to come to know or consider. Often used to draw attention, as in 'have you considered…?'
2.grammar: A present-tense verb addressed to a single male 'you,' marked by the 'ta-' prefix. The root's weak final letter has dropped, leaving the short final -a; this shortened form is the jussive/apocopated form, which appears after certain particles (such as 'did not' or in questions like 'have you not seen?').
2.root: ر-أ-ي (r-ʾ-y) — to see, perceive, consider, form an opinion

3.meaning: 'To / toward / up to' — a preposition marking the endpoint, goal, or limit of an action or motion: the direction something moves toward or the boundary at which it stops.
3.grammar: An invariable preposition. It has no case ending of its own but puts the noun that follows it into the genitive ('of / to' state). It indicates direction toward, or the terminal limit of, something.

4.meaning: The chiefs, the leading assembly, the prominent council of a people — the eminent figures whose standing and counsel carry weight. It refers to a group of notables or elite leaders.
4.grammar: Al- is the definite article ('the'). The -i ending is genitive, the case used after a preposition or to link to a preceding noun ('… OF the chiefs').
4.root: م-ل-أ (m-l-') — to fill; hence a filled assembly, an eminent group

5.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
5.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

6.meaning: Children / sons of — the plural 'sons' or 'children' in a construct ('children of …'), used for descendants or a people named after an ancestor.
6.grammar: Plural of 'ibn' (son), in the construct ('possessed') state, so it leans on a following name or noun: 'children/sons OF …'. As a plural of this type, its construct form drops the final 'n' and ends in '-ī', which marks it as genitive or accusative — typically the object of a verb or governed by a preposition.

7.meaning: Israel — the proper name, traditionally understood as another name of the Prophet Jacob, and by extension the lineage and people descended from him (the "Children of Israel").
7.grammar: A proper name of foreign origin. Because such names do not take the usual indefinite -un/-in/-an endings, the single -a ending here covers both the accusative and genitive roles (a "diptote" pattern). It functions as a fixed name rather than a regular declined noun.

8.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
8.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

9.meaning: A noun/adverb meaning 'after' — the time or position following something; 'afterward', 'following'.
9.grammar: An adverb of time functioning as a noun, here in the genitive case marked by the final -i. The genitive ending typically appears after a preposition or as the second term of a construct ('after THE …'), linking 'after' to a following noun to specify what it comes after.
9.root: ب-ع-د (b-ʿ-d) — to be after, to follow, distance in place or time

10.meaning: Mūsā (Moses) — the proper name of the prophet. As a name it has no Arabic root meaning; it is a non-inflecting (indeclinable) noun whose ending does not change for case.
10.grammar: A proper name ending in a fixed long -ā (written as alif maqṣūra). It is fully indeclinable (invariable): the final -ā never changes, so the word shows no case distinction at all — it looks and sounds identical whether subject, object, or possessor. (This is unlike a diptote, which still alternates between two case vowels; here there is no alternation.)

11.meaning: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the time that', used to point back to a past moment or event and introduce a recollection of something that occurred.
11.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). It signals a point in past time, typically introducing a clause that recalls 'the time when' something happened.

12.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
12.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.

13.meaning: To a prophet / for a prophet. The li- is the preposition 'to/for', and 'nabiyy' means a prophet — one chosen and inspired by Allah to convey His guidance to people.
13.grammar: Li- is a preposition ('to/for') and always puts the following noun in the genitive case. The -in ending is genitive with 'tanwīn' (-n, indefinite: 'a prophet').
13.root: Two derivations are recognized: ن-ب-أ (n-b-') — news, tidings (a prophet as one who conveys news/revelation from Allah); and ن-ب-و (n-b-w) — to be high/elevated (a prophet as one of exalted rank). The latter underlies the unhamzated spelling نَبِيّ.

14.meaning: To them / for them / belonging to them. It combines the preposition li- ('to/for/belonging to') with the pronoun 'them' (masculine plural).
14.grammar: The preposition li- ('to/for') takes the form 'la-' before a pronoun. The attached -hum(u) means 'them' (masculine plural); its base vowel is shifted to -humu (instead of -hum) to ease pronunciation before a following word. Together it expresses possession or benefit ('belonging to them').

15.meaning: Send forth! Raise up! Appoint! A command to dispatch, commission, or set someone in place. The root also carries the sense of stirring up or rousing into action.
15.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a single male ('you, do this!'). The sukūn (no vowel) on the final consonant is the natural endpoint of this command form; the initial helping vowel (i-) lets the cluster be pronounced.
15.root: ب-ع-ث (b-ʿ-th) — to send, dispatch, raise up, rouse

16.meaning: A combination of the preposition 'for / to' with the pronoun 'us', meaning 'for us' or 'to us / on our behalf'.
16.grammar: A preposition ('for / to') joined to the attached pronoun 'us'. The pronoun -nā always means 'us / our' regardless of position. Together they express benefit or direction toward the speakers ('for us').

17.meaning: A king; a sovereign ruler who holds command and authority over a people. It denotes one possessing kingship and dominion.
17.grammar: A noun ('king'). The -an ending is accusative with 'tanwīn' (-n, indefinite: 'a king'). The accusative is the case used for the object of a verb.
17.root: م-ل-ك (m-l-k) — to own, rule; kingship, dominion

18.meaning: We fight, we do battle — to engage in combat or warfare. The verb is the mutual/intensive form of 'to kill', meaning to wage war against an enemy.
18.grammar: A present/future verb in the 'fā'ala' pattern (mutual action: 'to fight one another'). The nu- prefix marks 'we'. The final consonant carries no vowel (jussive/conditional form), the shortened form used in conditional or purpose constructions ('… so that we may fight').
18.root: ق-ت-ل (q-t-l) — killing; the derived form means to fight/wage war

19.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
19.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

20.meaning: 'path, way, road' — a route or course; figuratively a cause or way of life one travels along. In construct ('the way OF ...').
20.grammar: A singular noun with the '-i' (genitive) ending, which typically links it to a following noun ('the way OF ...') or follows a preposition. It marks the word as connected to or possessed by what comes after.

21.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
21.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

22.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
22.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

23.meaning: An interrogative particle that turns a statement into a yes/no question, roughly "is it that…?" or "do…?". It can also carry a rhetorical or expectant tone rather than a literal request for information.
23.grammar: A question particle placed before a sentence to ask whether something is the case. It has no case ending and does not change form; it simply marks the words that follow as a yes/no question.

24.meaning: You might / you may perhaps — an expression of expectation or possibility built on the verb 'asā ('it may be that, perhaps'). With the 'you (plural)' ending it introduces something feared or expected of the addressees.
24.grammar: This is the 'verb of expectation' 'asā ('perhaps, it may be that'). It carries the past-tense subject ending -tum, marking 'you' (masculine plural). Functionally it sets up an anticipated or feared possibility about the people addressed.
24.root: ع-س-ي (ʿ-s-y) — expectation, hopefulness/apprehension ('perhaps')

25.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
25.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

26.meaning: It has been written, decreed, prescribed, or made obligatory. The passive verb conveys that something has been set down as binding — whether literally inscribed or ordained as a duty.
26.grammar: A past-tense passive verb: the internal vowels u-i show that the subject is unknown or unstated ('it WAS written' rather than 'he wrote'). The final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('it/he'). It conveys that a thing has been decreed or made obligatory.
26.root: ك-ت-ب (k-t-b) — writing; hence to prescribe, decree, ordain

27.meaning: 'Upon / over you (plural)' — the preposition 'on, over, upon' combined with an attached pronoun meaning 'you all', expressing something resting on or directed toward a group.
27.grammar: A preposition with an attached object pronoun. The pronoun -kum addresses a group ('you all'); its final vowel appears as -u (kumu) as a connecting helper-vowel that smooths pronunciation into a following word beginning with a definite article. The preposition itself conveys 'on top of' or 'over' something.
27.root: — (preposition; relates to ع-ل-و, height/elevation)

28.meaning: Fighting, combat, or warfare — armed struggle between opposing parties.
28.grammar: A masculine verbal noun denoting mutual fighting. The prefix al- means 'the'. The final -u is the nominative ending, generally marking the word as the subject of a sentence or as the thing being described.
28.root: ق-ت-ل (q-t-l) — to kill, to fight; combat

29.meaning: A compound particle meaning 'that … not,' 'lest,' 'so as not to.' It introduces a clause of something feared, intended-to-prevent, or negated after a verb.
29.grammar: A merging of the particle an ('that,' which introduces a verb in the subjunctive) with the negative lā ('not'); the 'n' of an assimilates into lā, giving allā. Together they mean 'that … not' and put the following verb into the subjunctive mood, often after verbs of fearing, wishing, or commanding.

30.meaning: You fight, you do battle (addressed to a group) — to engage in combat or warfare. The mutual/intensive form of 'to kill', meaning to wage war.
30.grammar: A present/future verb in the 'fā'ala' pattern (mutual action: 'to fight'). The tu-…-ū frame marks second-person masculine plural ('you all'). The ending here is the shortened -ū (without final -na), the form used after certain particles or in subjunctive/jussive constructions ('that you fight').
30.root: ق-ت-ل (q-t-l) — killing; the derived form means to fight/wage war

31.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
