31.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.
31.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — saying, speech, utterance

32.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
32.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

33.meaning: A phrase meaning 'to us' or 'for us / belonging to us' — combining the preposition 'to/for' with the attached pronoun 'us', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward the speakers.
33.grammar: A preposition fused with an attached pronoun. The base 'li' ('to/for') shifts to 'la' before an attached pronoun, so it appears here with a fatḥa as 'la'; the suffix 'nā' means 'us' (first-person plural). Together it conveys 'for us' — indicating benefit, possession, or direction.

34.meaning: A compound particle meaning 'that … not,' 'lest,' 'so as not to.' It introduces a clause of something feared, intended-to-prevent, or negated after a verb.
34.grammar: A merging of the particle an ('that,' which introduces a verb in the subjunctive) with the negative lā ('not'); the 'n' of an assimilates into lā, giving allā. Together they mean 'that … not' and put the following verb into the subjunctive mood, often after verbs of fearing, wishing, or commanding.

35.meaning: We fight, we do battle — to engage in combat or warfare. The mutual/intensive form of 'to kill', meaning to wage war against an enemy.
35.grammar: A present/future verb in the 'fā'ala' pattern (mutual action: 'to fight'). The nu- prefix marks 'we'. The final -a is the subjunctive ending, a mood often expressing purpose or what is hoped/intended ('so that we may fight').
35.root: ق-ت-ل (q-t-l) — killing; the derived form means to fight/wage war

36.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
36.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
36.root: — (particle)

37.meaning: 'path, way, road' — a route or course; figuratively a cause or way of life one travels along. In construct ('the way OF ...').
37.grammar: A singular noun with the '-i' (genitive) ending, which typically links it to a following noun ('the way OF ...') or follows a preposition. It marks the word as connected to or possessed by what comes after.

38.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
38.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

39.meaning: 'And indeed / while already' — the word 'wa' ('and, while') joined to 'qad', a particle that, before a past-tense verb, stresses that the action has certainly and already happened.
39.grammar: A connective 'wa' ('and', or circumstantial 'while') plus the particle 'qad'. With a past-tense verb, 'qad' emphasizes completion and certainty ('has indeed already…'); with a present-tense verb it can mean 'sometimes' or 'may'.

40.meaning: A passive verb meaning 'we were driven out / expelled', i.e. forced to leave a place against our will. The passive voice leaves the one who did the expelling unnamed, focusing on the fact of being cast out.

parts.en: was caused to go out / expelled (passive)

40.grammar: A past-tense verb in the passive voice ('was made to go out'). The internal vowel pattern u-i marks it as passive (something was done TO the subject, the doer unmentioned). The attached -nā is a subject ending meaning 'we', so together: 'we were driven out'.
40.root: خ-ر-ج (kh-r-j) — going out, coming forth, exiting

41.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
41.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

42.meaning: 'Our dwellings / homes / homelands' — the plural of dār (an abode, house, or settled region) with 'our' attached. It denotes the places where people live and to which they belong.
42.grammar: A plural noun with the possessive 'our' (-nā) attached. The -i ending is genitive. Here the noun is the head of a possessive pairing, and the genitive marks it as possessed by the pronoun that FOLLOWS it (-nā, 'our'): 'dwellings of ours / our dwellings'.
42.root: د-و-ر (d-w-r) — turning, circling; a dwelling as an enclosed/encircling abode

43.meaning: 'And our sons / children' — the plural of ibn ('son'), with 'and' prefixed and 'our' attached. Abnā' is the broken plural commonly used for sons or, more generally, offspring.
43.grammar: A plural noun joined by the prefix wa- ('and') and carrying the possessive 'our' (-nā). The -i ending is genitive. The noun is the head of a possessive pairing, and the genitive marks it as possessed by the pronoun that FOLLOWS it (-nā, 'our'): 'sons of ours / our sons'.

44.meaning: A connector meaning 'then, when' — it joins to what came before ('then/so') and sets up a 'when…' clause whose outcome follows. It frames a moment: 'and then, at the point when…'.
44.grammar: A compound of the connecting particle fa- ('then/so', linking to the preceding statement) and lammā, a particle meaning 'when' that introduces a past circumstance and leads the listener to expect a following result clause.

45.meaning: It has been written, decreed, prescribed, or made obligatory. The passive verb conveys that something has been set down as binding — whether literally inscribed or ordained as a duty.
45.grammar: A past-tense passive verb: the internal vowels u-i show that the subject is unknown or unstated ('it WAS written' rather than 'he wrote'). The final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('it/he'). It conveys that a thing has been decreed or made obligatory.
45.root: ك-ت-ب (k-t-b) — writing; hence to prescribe, decree, ordain

46.meaning: 'Upon them / against them' — the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, against') carrying an attached plural pronoun referring to a group of males.
46.grammar: ʿalā ('upon') takes the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The -him ending is the attached pronoun for a masculine plural 'them'; its final vowel appears as -u (himu) to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with the definite article.

47.meaning: Fighting, combat, or warfare — armed struggle between opposing parties.
47.grammar: A masculine verbal noun denoting mutual fighting. The prefix al- means 'the'. The final -u is the nominative ending, generally marking the word as the subject of a sentence or as the thing being described.
47.root: ق-ت-ل (q-t-l) — to kill, to fight; combat

48.meaning: 'They turned away / they turned their backs / they turned aside'. It conveys turning oneself away from something, often implying rejection or withdrawal.
48.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb, third person masculine plural: the ending '-aw' means 'they (did) …'. The Form V pattern (with the 'ta-' prefix and doubled middle letter) gives a reflexive sense — turning oneself away. It states a completed act.
48.root: و-ل-ي (w-l-y) — to be near/turn toward; in this form, to turn away

49.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
49.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

50.meaning: 'A little / a small amount' — an adjective/noun meaning small in quantity, few, scant, or trifling.
50.grammar: A noun/adjective 'little' in the accusative case with indefinite marking (the -an ending, tanwīn). The accusative commonly marks an object or specifies amount/manner; the doubled -n sound marks it as indefinite, 'a little.'
50.root: ق-ل-ل (q-l-l) — fewness; being little, scant, or small in amount

51.meaning: 'Among them / from them / some of them' — the preposition 'min' ('from, of, among') joined to the attached pronoun 'hum' ('them').
51.grammar: The preposition 'min' ('from / of / among') with the attached pronoun 'hum' ('them'), referring to a masculine plural group. Together they often express 'part of them' or 'some among them'.

52.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
52.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
52.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

53.meaning: An intensive adjective/name meaning 'All-Knowing / fully aware' — one whose knowledge is complete, deep, and all-encompassing; as a divine attribute it denotes Allah's perfect knowledge.
53.grammar: An intensive adjective (the pattern faʿīl conveys 'thoroughly, abundantly'). The ending -un is the indefinite nominative — the nominative case marks it as the subject or the quality being affirmed, and the -n (nunation) signals 'a / an', i.e. indefinite. So it reads '(is) all-knowing'.

54.meaning: A noun phrase meaning 'of / about the wrongdoers' — those who do wrong, act unjustly, or put things out of their rightful place, especially by transgressing against truth and against themselves.
54.grammar: The prefix bi- is a preposition ('of', 'about', 'with'); al- makes the noun definite ('the'). The ending -īna is the masculine sound plural in its non-subject (oblique/genitive-accusative) form, which is the form required after a preposition. So it reads 'of the wrongdoers'.

1.meaning: 'And he said' — the act of speaking or stating, attributed to one masculine speaker, joined to what precedes by 'and.'
1.grammar: The connector 'wa-' ('and') with a past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he said.' The ending -a marks a completed action by one male, with the doer 'he' contained in the verb.

2.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
2.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

3.meaning: 'Their prophet' — the noun nabī ('a prophet', one who receives and conveys revelation from Allah) with the possessive 'their' attached.
3.grammar: A noun with the possessive 'their' (-hum, masculine plural) attached. The -u ending is nominative, the case that typically marks the subject/doer of a sentence ('the one who…').
3.root: ن-ب-أ (n-b-ʾ) — news, tidings; a prophet as a bearer of news from Allah

4.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
4.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

5.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
5.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

6.meaning: A short particle placed before a verb to emphasize or affirm it. Before a past-tense verb it means 'indeed / certainly / has already (happened)'; before a present-tense verb it can mean 'sometimes / may'. It sharpens and confirms the verb that follows.
6.grammar: An indeclinable particle (its form never changes). It does not take case or tense endings; its job is to color the following verb — affirming and intensifying a past action ('has indeed done') or signaling occasional possibility with a present verb.

7.meaning: 'He raised up / sent forth / dispatched' — a past-tense verb. The root sense is to rouse or set something in motion; of a person it means to send or commission, and of the dead it means to resurrect.
7.grammar: A complete past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he raised/sent'. The final -a is the standard past-tense ending for 'he' (a single male doer in completed past action).
7.root: ب-ع-ث (b-ʿ-th) — rousing, sending forth, raising up (including resurrection)

8.meaning: 'For you / to you (plural)' — the preposition li- ('for, to, belonging to') joined to the attached pronoun for a group being addressed.
8.grammar: li- is a preposition meaning 'for/to'; its vowel appears here as 'la' before the attached pronoun. The -kum ending is the attached pronoun for a masculine plural 'you', so the whole means 'for you (all)'.

9.meaning: Ṭālūt — a proper name, the king of the Israelites known in the Bible as Saul. As a name it carries no grammatical root meaning.
9.grammar: A proper name (a person). The -a ending is accusative, the case that typically marks the direct object of a verb (the one being acted upon, e.g. the one who is appointed or sent).

10.meaning: 'A king / sovereign' — malik denotes one who holds royal authority and rule over a people.
10.grammar: A singular indefinite noun. The -an ending combines the accusative case with indefiniteness ('a king'); this form often marks a direct object or describes the state/capacity in which someone is placed ('as a king').

11.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'they said' or 'they spoke,' attributing an utterance to a group of three or more (grammatically masculine or mixed).
11.grammar: Past-tense verb in the third-person masculine plural. The stem qāl- carries a long ā (from a weak middle root letter), and the plural subject is marked by the wāw vowel -ū fused onto it ('they'). The alif written after the wāw is silent — a purely orthographic spelling convention with no pronunciation.

12.meaning: A particle/adverb meaning 'in whatever manner,' 'from wherever,' or 'whenever' — it asks or denotes the how, where, or when of an action in an open-ended way.
12.grammar: An invariable interrogative/conditional adverb; it has no case ending and never changes form. It introduces the manner, place, or time of an action in a general, open sense ('in what way / from where / when').

13.meaning: 'It is / it comes to be' — the present-tense verb of being and becoming (from kāna). It expresses that something is the case, exists, or comes about.
13.grammar: A present/future-tense verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he/it is, becomes'. The ya- prefix means 'he/it', and the final -u is the indicative ending, marking a plain factual statement (as opposed to a command or a negated/subjunctive form).
13.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

14.meaning: To him / for him / he has — the preposition 'to/for' fused with a pronoun meaning 'him.' It expresses belonging, benefit, or possession (something is 'his' or done 'for him').
14.grammar: A preposition 'li-/la-' ('to, for') with the attached 3rd-person masculine singular pronoun 'him.' The pairing means 'to him' or 'for him' and often conveys possession ('he has …') or that an action is directed toward his benefit or detriment.
14.root: — (particle with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

15.meaning: 'The kingship / sovereignty / dominion' — al-mulk is rule and royal authority itself, the power and right to govern.
15.grammar: A definite noun with the article al- ('the'). The -u ending is nominative, the case that typically marks the subject of a sentence (the thing that 'is' or does something).

16.meaning: 'Upon us' / 'over us' / 'against us' — the preposition ʿalā ('on, over, upon') with an attached 'us'. It conveys something resting on, incumbent upon, or bearing against the group.
16.grammar: A preposition (ʿalā, 'upon/over') with an attached pronoun, first person plural (-nā, 'us'). When a pronoun is attached, ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay-. Such prepositional phrases put their pronoun in the object/genitive role.

17.meaning: 'And we' — the standalone pronoun 'we' (a group including the speaker), prefixed with the connector 'and'; often used to set up a contrast ('while we…').
17.grammar: A detached subject pronoun meaning 'we,' here introduced by wa- ('and' / 'while'). As an independent pronoun it stands on its own (not attached to a verb) and is invariable — it is fixed in form and takes no case ending that changes.

18.meaning: An adjective meaning 'more entitled, having a better/greater right, more deserving' of something.
18.grammar: A comparative/superlative adjective on the afʿal pattern, meaning 'more/most entitled'. The final -u is the nominative case ending, the form used when the word serves as the subject or as a predicate describing the subject.
18.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, right, just claim, what is due

19.meaning: 'To / for / by the kingship' — the noun al-mulk ('sovereignty, dominion') governed by the preposition bi-, which conveys senses such as 'with', 'by means of', or 'to/for'.
19.grammar: A definite noun preceded by the preposition bi- ('with/by/to'). The -i ending is genitive, the case required after a preposition, linking the noun to that preposition.

20.meaning: 'From it / out of it / from him'. It combines the preposition 'from / out of' with the pronoun 'it/him'.
20.grammar: The preposition min ('from / out of', indicating origin or source) with the attached pronoun -hu ('it' / 'him'), referring to a singular masculine thing or person. As object of the preposition, the pronoun is in the oblique form.
20.root: — (no triliteral root; a preposition with a pronoun)

21.meaning: 'And not' — the conjunction wa- ('and') joined to lam, a particle that negates a verb and pushes its meaning into the completed past ('did not …').
21.grammar: A connector wa- ('and') plus the negative particle lam. Lam negates a following present-tense verb but turns its sense into the past: 'has not / did not …'. It also causes that verb to take the jussive (clipped) ending.

22.meaning: A passive verb meaning 'he is/was given, granted' — from the verb 'to give, bring, bestow'. The passive leaves the giver unnamed and focuses on the recipient.

parts.en: be given (passive stem; final weak letter dropped in the jussive)

22.grammar: A present-tense passive verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he is given'. The yu- prefix with the internal vowel pattern marks the passive ('is given to him'). This is a defective (weak-final) verb: its underlying form is yuʾtā, but after the negative lam it takes the jussive, which deletes the final weak letter (yuʾtā → yuʾta), yielding a past-negated sense ('was not given').
22.root: أ-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — coming; (in this form) bringing, giving, bestowing

23.meaning: 'Ampleness / abundance / capacity' — saʿah denotes spaciousness and plenty, whether of means, wealth, or room. The root idea is being wide and roomy.
23.grammar: A singular indefinite noun ending in tā marbūṭa. The -an ending marks the accusative with indefiniteness ('an abundance'); this commonly signals a direct object — the thing given, possessed, or had. Before this ending the tā marbūṭa is pronounced as a full -t- (saʿat + an → saʿatan).

24.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
24.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

25.meaning: 'The wealth / property / possessions' — al-māl is material wealth: money, goods, and assets that a person owns.
25.grammar: A definite noun with the article al- ('the'). The -i ending is genitive, the case used after a preposition or when this noun is the possessed head of a pairing whose possessor follows it ('… of …').

26.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
26.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

27.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
27.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

28.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
28.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

29.meaning: 'He chose / selected / picked him out' — a past-tense verb from a root meaning to take the choicest, purest part. It conveys deliberate selection of someone as preferred or elect.
29.grammar: A past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he chose'), with the object pronoun -hu ('him') attached. This pattern (with the prefixed i- and infixed -ṭa-) carries the sense of picking out the very best. The verb form here is the completed past for 'he'.
29.root: ص-ف-و (ṣ-f-w) — purity, clearness; choosing the choicest/purest

30.meaning: A small unit: the preposition 'upon / on / over' — also carrying the sense of an obligation 'incumbent upon' — joined to the pronoun 'you (plural)'. So: 'upon you / it is your duty'.
30.grammar: 'ʿalā' is the preposition 'upon/on/over'; before an attached pronoun it appears as 'ʿalay-'. The suffix -kum is 'you' for a group of men (or a mixed group). The phrase often conveys duty or burden resting on someone ('it is upon you to …'). Pronouns attached to a preposition always take the genitive form.
30.root: — (preposition; no triliteral root)

31.meaning: 'And He increased / added to him' — the conjunction 'and' with the past-tense verb 'to increase, augment, give more', plus 'him' as object: to grant someone an increase or surplus.
31.grammar: A past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he increased'), prefixed by wa- ('and') and carrying the object pronoun -hu ('him'). The bare verb stem with no extra ending is the standard completed-past form for 'he'.
31.root: ز-ي-د (z-y-d) — increase, addition, growth, surplus

32.meaning: 'An expanse / extension / ampleness' — basṭah denotes a spreading-out or generous measure, hence abundance or greatness in something (e.g. in knowledge or physical stature).
32.grammar: A singular indefinite noun ending in tā marbūṭa. The -an ending marks the accusative with indefiniteness ('an expanse'); it commonly signals a direct object — the thing given or granted. Before this ending the tā marbūṭa is pronounced as a full -t- (basṭat + an → basṭatan).

33.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
33.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

34.meaning: The knowledge; sure and certain knowing, established information and understanding (with the definite article).
34.grammar: A definite verbal noun: al- means 'the'. The final -i is the genitive ending, which typically follows a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun in an 'of' relationship. It denotes knowledge as a settled, certain thing.
34.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know; knowledge, certainty

35.meaning: 'And the body / physical frame' — al-jism is the physical body or bodily build of a living being.
35.grammar: A definite noun with 'and' (wa-) prefixed and the article al- ('the'). The -i ending is genitive; here it agrees with a preceding genitive noun to which it is joined by 'and' (coordination), taking the same case as its partner.
35.root: ج-س-م (j-s-m) — body, physical mass, corporeal form

36.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
36.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
36.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

37.meaning: 'He gives / grants / bestows' — the present-tense verb of giving and bestowing (from ātā). It expresses an ongoing or habitual act of granting something to someone.
37.grammar: A present/future-tense verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he gives'. The yu- prefix means 'he', and the final long -ī is the retained weak ending of this verb, marking the plain factual (indicative) present — a statement that something is given.
37.root: أ-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — coming; (in this form) bringing, giving, bestowing

38.meaning: 'His kingship / dominion / sovereignty' — the noun mulk (royal authority and rule) with the possessive 'his' attached.
38.grammar: A noun with the possessive 'his' (-hu) attached. The -a ending is accusative, the case that typically marks the direct object of a verb (the thing being given or granted).
38.root: م-ل-ك (m-l-k) — ownership, dominion, kingship

39.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
39.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

40.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning 'he wills, he wishes, he chooses' — to want or intend something by one's own decision.
40.grammar: A present/ongoing action by a single masculine subject ('he'); the ya- prefix marks third-person masculine singular, and the final -u marks the indicative mood — a plain statement of fact ('he wills'), as opposed to a command or a verb governed by 'that.'
40.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʾ) — willing, wishing; the root behind 'thing' (shayʾ)

41.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
41.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
41.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

42.meaning: An adjective meaning 'vast, ample, all-embracing, boundless' — wide in capacity, encompassing; of Allah it conveys limitless reach in knowledge, mercy, and bounty.
42.grammar: An active participle ('one who is vast/encompassing') used adjectivally. The ending '-un' is the indefinite nominative (tanwīn), marking it as 'a vast one' and as a subject or predicate.
42.root: و-س-ع (w-s-ʿ) — breadth, capacity, amplitude, to encompass

43.meaning: An intensive adjective/name meaning 'All-Knowing / fully aware' — one whose knowledge is complete, deep, and all-encompassing; as a divine attribute it denotes Allah's perfect knowledge.
43.grammar: An intensive adjective (the pattern faʿīl conveys 'thoroughly, abundantly'). The ending -un is the indefinite nominative — the nominative case marks it as the subject or the quality being affirmed, and the -n (nunation) signals 'a / an', i.e. indefinite. So it reads '(is) all-knowing'.

1.meaning: 'And he said' — the act of speaking or stating, attributed to one masculine speaker, joined to what precedes by 'and.'
1.grammar: The connector 'wa-' ('and') with a past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he said.' The ending -a marks a completed action by one male, with the doer 'he' contained in the verb.

2.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
2.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

3.meaning: 'Their prophet' — the noun nabī ('a prophet', one who receives and conveys revelation from Allah) with the possessive 'their' attached.
3.grammar: A noun with the possessive 'their' (-hum, masculine plural) attached. The -u ending is nominative, the case that typically marks the subject/doer of a sentence ('the one who…').
3.root: ن-ب-أ (n-b-ʾ) — news, tidings; a prophet as a bearer of news from Allah

4.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
4.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

5.meaning: 'A sign / token / mark' — āyah is a sign that points to something beyond itself; it also denotes a miraculous proof and a verse of revelation.
5.grammar: A singular noun. The -a ending is accusative, the case that typically marks the direct object of a verb (the thing pointed to or presented), or stands as the predicate of certain particles.

6.meaning: 'Of his kingship / dominion' — the noun mulk (royal authority, sovereignty) with the possessive 'his' attached.
6.grammar: A noun with the possessive 'his' (-hi) attached. The -i ending is genitive; here the noun is the possessed head of a pairing, and the genitive marks it as possessed by the pronoun that FOLLOWS it ('… of his'). The pronoun appears as -hi (rather than -hu) because it follows this -i vowel.

7.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
7.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

8.meaning: 'It comes to you / will come to you' — the present-tense verb 'to come, arrive' with 'you (plural)' as its object: something approaching or reaching a group of people.
8.grammar: A present/future-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it comes'), with the object pronoun 'you (plural)' attached. The ya- prefix means 'he/it'. The verb's -a ending here is subjunctive/jussive (the clipped, non-indicative form taken after certain particles), expressing 'that it come' or 'it will come'. The pronoun's final vowel is -u (kumu) to ease pronunciation before a following word.

9.meaning: 'The chest / ark / coffer' — al-tābūt is a box or chest, used notably for the sacred Ark in which relics were kept.
9.grammar: A definite noun with the article al- ('the'). The -u ending is nominative, the case that typically marks the subject of a sentence (the thing that does or undergoes the action, e.g. that which 'comes').

10.meaning: 'In it / in him' — the preposition 'in, inside, within' joined to a pronoun referring to a single masculine or neuter thing. It locates something inside or as part of that referent.
10.grammar: A preposition with an attached object pronoun. The pronoun -hi refers to one masculine (or grammatically masculine) thing and stands as the object of the preposition; its vowel is -i because attached pronouns take that shape after the long -i of fi. Together they answer 'in what?' or 'in whom?'.

11.meaning: Tranquility, calm, and inner peace; a settled stillness of heart and reassurance that descends to steady a person, often understood as a divine gift of serenity.
11.grammar: A feminine singular noun. The -un ending (the 'nunation') marks it as indefinite ('a tranquility') and as nominative, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or what something is being identified as.
11.root: س-ك-ن (s-k-n) — to be still, settle, dwell, grow calm

12.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
12.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

13.meaning: Your Lord — the term Rabb meaning the Master, Sustainer, Owner, and Nurturer who creates, provides for, and governs; here joined to 'your' (plural). It conveys far more than 'lord': the one who brings up and cares for His creation.
13.grammar: A noun 'Rabb' (Lord, Sustainer) with the attached pronoun 'your' (plural). The -i ending is genitive: it appears because the word follows a preposition or is linked to a preceding noun, and it sits right before the possessive ending 'your'.
13.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, lord over

14.meaning: And a remnant, a remainder, or that which is left over and endures; a surviving portion that lasts after the rest has passed away.
14.grammar: The prefix wa- means 'and', joining this to what precedes. The stem is a feminine singular noun. The -un ending marks it as indefinite ('a remnant') and nominative, the case used for a subject or for what is being named or pointed out.
14.root: ب-ق-ي (b-q-y) — to remain, endure, be left over, last

15.meaning: A fused word combining the preposition 'min' ('from', 'of', 'about') with the relative/indefinite 'mā' ('what', 'that which'). Together: 'from what', 'about that which', 'of what'.
15.grammar: The preposition 'min' and the word 'mā' merge in pronunciation (the 'n' assimilating into the 'm'). 'min' governs a genitive, and 'mā' here functions as a relative pronoun introducing a clause ('that which …'). These are indeclinable particles without case endings.

16.meaning: He left behind / he left, abandoned, or relinquished — a completed act of leaving something or someone, including leaving property behind (as an inheritance).
16.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb. The final '-a' marks third-person masculine singular: "he" did the action, viewed as completed.

17.meaning: The family, household, or close folk of someone; the people belonging to a person, especially kin and intimate followers.
17.grammar: A masculine noun in the 'construct' state, meaning it is linked to a following name ('family OF …'). The -u ending is nominative, the case used for a subject or for what is being named; in this construct form it carries no nunation because it leans on the word that follows.
17.root: أ-و-ل (ʾ-w-l) — to return to, belong to (an origin); kin/household

18.meaning: Mūsā (Moses) — the proper name of the prophet. As a name it has no Arabic root meaning; it is a non-inflecting (indeclinable) noun whose ending does not change for case.
18.grammar: A proper name ending in a fixed long -ā (written as alif maqṣūra). It is fully indeclinable (invariable): the final -ā never changes, so the word shows no case distinction at all — it looks and sounds identical whether subject, object, or possessor. (This is unlike a diptote, which still alternates between two case vowels; here there is no alternation.)
18.root: — (proper name; non-Arabic origin)

19.meaning: And the family, household, or close folk of someone; the people belonging to a person, joined to a preceding mention.
19.grammar: The prefix wa- means 'and'. The stem is a masculine noun in the construct state, linked to a following name ('family OF …'). The -u ending is nominative (subject or named-thing case); the construct form takes no nunation because it depends on the following word.
19.root: أ-و-ل (ʾ-w-l) — to return to, belong to (an origin); kin/household

20.meaning: Aaron, the proper name of the brother of Moses, a prophet of Allah.
20.grammar: A proper name. Being a foreign/non-Arabic name, it is a 'diptote': it refuses the usual -i for the genitive and instead shows -a, and it never takes nunation. The -a ending here stands in for the genitive, the case used after a preceding noun ('… OF Aaron') or after a preposition.

21.meaning: She/it carries it, bears it, or lifts and conveys it; the act of taking up a load and transporting it.
21.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb. The ta- prefix marks a feminine singular subject ('she/it'). The -u on the verb stem is the ordinary present-tense (indicative) ending, signalling a real, ongoing or habitual action. The attached -hu is the object pronoun 'it/him', the thing being carried.
21.root: ح-م-ل (ḥ-m-l) — to carry, bear, lift, convey (also to bear a burden)

22.meaning: The angels; spiritual beings created by Allah who serve and obey Him and carry out His commands.
22.grammar: A collective plural noun ('the angels') made definite by the prefix al- ('the'). The -u ending is nominative, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or for the doer of an action.
22.root: م-ل-ك (m-l-k) — possess, command; an angel (some link the word to ʾ-l-k, to send a message, hence a messenger/envoy)

23.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
23.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

24.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
24.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
24.root: — (particle)

25.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
25.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

26.meaning: Surely a sign, a token, or a clear indication; a marker that points to a deeper truth and serves as evidence or a lesson.
26.grammar: The prefix la- is an emphasizer, adding force like 'surely' or 'indeed'. The stem is a feminine singular noun. The -an ending (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a sign') and accusative, the case used for objects and, characteristically, for the thing affirmed after certain emphatic constructions.
26.root: أ-ي-ي (ʾ-y-y) — a sign, mark, token; a verse of revelation

27.meaning: A two-part phrase meaning 'for you' (plural) — indicating benefit, possession, or that something is granted to the group addressed.
27.grammar: The preposition 'li' ('for/to'), here vowelled 'la-' before a pronoun, with the attached pronoun 'you all.' A preposition-plus-pronoun unit; it commonly expresses benefit or belonging ('for you').

28.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
28.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

29.meaning: A past-tense verb of 'being' addressed to a group: 'you (all) were', 'you (all) used to be'. From kāna, the core verb 'to be'. With a following predicate it often means 'you were (in a state of) …' or 'you used to …'.
29.grammar: This is a past-tense verb. The '-tum' suffix is the attached subject marker for a masculine plural 'you all'. Since the doer is built into the suffix, the verb stands in its base past form ('you all were').
29.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

30.meaning: Believers; those who have faith, who trust and affirm the truth and find security in that belief.
30.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer' word) meaning 'one who believes', here masculine plural. The -īna ending marks the sound masculine plural in its accusative/genitive form, i.e. the form used when the word is an object of a verb, follows a preposition, or is linked to a preceding noun (as opposed to -ūna for the subject form).
30.root: أ-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — to be secure, trust; to have faith, believe; safety

1.meaning: A connector meaning 'then, when' — it joins to what came before ('then/so') and sets up a 'when…' clause whose outcome follows. It frames a moment: 'and then, at the point when…'.
1.grammar: A compound of the connecting particle fa- ('then/so', linking to the preceding statement) and lammā, a particle meaning 'when' that introduces a past circumstance and leads the listener to expect a following result clause.

2.meaning: He set out and departed, separating himself from a place or group; to part company and go forth. The same verb can also mean to decide or distinguish clearly between things.
2.grammar: The prefix fa- means 'so' or 'then', linking to what came before. The stem is a completed (past-tense) verb. The bare -a ending marks a third-person masculine singular subject acting in the past: 'he set out / parted'.
2.root: ف-ص-ل (f-ṣ-l) — to separate, divide, part; to decide, make distinct

3.meaning: Saul, the proper name of the king appointed over the Children of Israel.
3.grammar: A proper name. Being non-Arabic in form, it is a 'diptote' and takes no nunation. The -u ending is nominative, the case used for the subject of a sentence or the doer of an action.

4.meaning: With the troops, the armed forces, or the soldiery; a body of fighting men gathered as an army.
4.grammar: The prefix bi- means 'with' or 'by means of'; l- is 'the'. The stem is a plural noun ('troops/forces'). The -i ending is genitive, the case required after a preposition such as bi- ('with the …').
4.root: ج-ن-د (j-n-d) — a host, troop, army; soldiers gathered together

5.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
5.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

6.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
6.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

7.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
7.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

8.meaning: One who is testing you, putting you to trial, or examining you; the actor who subjects someone to a test to reveal their true state.
8.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer' word) from a verb meaning 'to test/try', describing the one who carries out the testing. The attached -kum is the plural object pronoun 'you (all)', the ones being tested. In the construct with this pronoun the participle's final long vowel appears as -ī.
8.root: ب-ل-و / ب-ل-ي (b-l-w) — to test, try, put to trial; to afflict or prove

9.meaning: With a river; a flowing watercourse or stream of running water.
9.grammar: The prefix bi- means 'with' or 'by'. The stem is a masculine singular noun ('river'). The -in ending (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a river') and genitive, the case required after the preposition bi-.
9.root: ن-ه-ر (n-h-r) — to flow abundantly; a river, flowing stream

10.meaning: A compound meaning 'then whoever' or 'so whoever'. It combines 'then/so' with the conditional/relative 'who', introducing whatever person meets a stated condition.
10.grammar: The connector fa- ('then/so', often answering or following a condition) joined to man ('whoever / the one who'), which refers to people and introduces a condition: 'whoever does X…'. man does not change its ending; the clause after it supplies the rest of the meaning.

11.meaning: He drank, took in a liquid by mouth; the completed act of drinking.
11.grammar: A completed (past-tense) verb. The bare -a ending marks a third-person masculine singular subject acting in the past: 'he drank'.
11.root: ش-ر-ب (sh-r-b) — to drink, imbibe, take in liquid

12.meaning: 'From it / out of it / from him'. It combines the preposition 'from / out of' with the pronoun 'it/him'.
12.grammar: The preposition min ('from / out of', indicating origin or source) with the attached pronoun -hu ('it' / 'him'), referring to a singular masculine thing or person. As object of the preposition, the pronoun is in the oblique form.
12.root: — (no triliteral root; a preposition with a pronoun)

13.meaning: Then he/it is not; a negation that denies a present state or quality — 'is not the case', 'is not so'. The base word laysa specifically negates being or existence in the present.
13.grammar: The prefix fa- means 'so' or 'then'. The stem laysa is a special negating verb meaning 'is not', used to deny a present state. The -a ending marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it is not').
13.root: ل-ي-س (l-y-s) — negation of being; 'is not' (defective verb)

14.meaning: From me; indicating origin, belonging, or association with the speaker — 'coming from me' or 'of my side'.
14.grammar: The preposition min ('from/of') with the attached pronoun -ī ('me'). An extra n is inserted (giving the doubled 'nn') to join the preposition smoothly to the pronoun. The -ī is the first-person singular pronoun 'me/my'.

15.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
15.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

16.meaning: The particle 'lam', a negating word used to push a verb into the past: it means 'did not' / 'has not'. Though it sits before a present-tense verb form, it negates the action as something that did not happen.
16.grammar: 'lam' is a negating particle that governs a following present-tense verb but gives it past meaning ('did not …'). It also puts that verb into the shortened (jussive) form. 'lam' itself carries no ending.

17.meaning: He should taste it, sample it, or partake of it by mouth; tasting, here also covering taking food or drink.
17.grammar: A present-tense verb with the ya- prefix marking a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'). The stem ends in a vowelless (sukūn) form — the 'jussive', which signals a command, prohibition, or conditional sense rather than a plain statement. The attached -hu is the object 'it/him', the thing tasted.
17.root: ط-ع-م (ṭ-ʿ-m) — to taste, eat, partake of food; flavour

18.meaning: A cluster of three elements: a connective 'so/then', the emphasis particle 'inna' that strongly affirms a statement ('indeed, truly'), and 'he/it'. Together: 'so indeed he / then truly it'.
18.grammar: 'fa-' is a connecting particle showing sequence or consequence ('so, then'). 'inna' is an emphatic particle that strongly affirms the sentence that follows and grammatically governs the following noun/pronoun in the accusative. The attached 'hu' is that pronoun, 'he/it', here serving as the subject being emphasized.

19.meaning: From me; indicating origin, belonging, or association with the speaker — 'coming from me' or 'of my side'.
19.grammar: The preposition min ('from/of') with the attached pronoun -ī ('me'). An extra n is inserted (the doubled 'nn') to bind the preposition to the pronoun, and the final -ī is lengthened. The -ī is the first-person singular pronoun 'me/my'.

20.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
20.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

21.meaning: Who / whoever / the one who. A relative and conditional pronoun used for people, introducing a clause that describes or sets a condition about a person.
21.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun referring to persons; it does not change for case. The final -i is not a case ending but a helping vowel added to ease pronunciation before a following word that begins with a connecting (elidable) alif.

22.meaning: He scooped up or ladled out (water) by hand; the completed act of taking up a handful or hollow-of-the-hand of liquid.
22.grammar: A completed (past-tense) verb in a reflexive/effort pattern (Form VIII), which often adds a sense of doing something for oneself. The bare -a ending marks a third-person masculine singular subject acting in the past: 'he scooped up'.
22.root: غ-ر-ف (gh-r-f) — to scoop, ladle, take up water by the handful

23.meaning: A scoop or handful of water — the amount held in the cupped hollow of the hand; a single draught taken by hand.
23.grammar: A feminine singular noun; the -a(t) ending here marks a single instance ('one scoopful'). The -an ending (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a scoop') and accusative, the case typically used for the direct object of a verb.
23.root: غ-ر-ف (gh-r-f) — to scoop, ladle; a handful/scoop of water

24.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in his hand,' i.e. in his possession, power, or control — the hand standing figuratively for authority over a matter.
24.grammar: The prefix bi- is a preposition ('in', 'with', 'by'). Because of it, the noun 'hand' takes the -i genitive ending. The attached -hi is a third-person masculine singular possessive pronoun ('his'); the vowel is 'hi' (rather than 'hu') because it follows the -i sound.
24.root: ي-د-ي (y-d-y) — hand; by extension power, possession, agency

25.meaning: Then they drank; the completed act of drinking carried out by a group.
25.grammar: The prefix fa- means 'so' or 'then'. The stem is a completed (past-tense) verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject acting in the past: 'they drank'. (The written alif after the wāw is silent.)
25.root: ش-ر-ب (sh-r-b) — to drink, imbibe, take in liquid

26.meaning: 'From it / out of it / from him'. It combines the preposition 'from / out of' with the pronoun 'it/him'.
26.grammar: The preposition min ('from / out of', indicating origin or source) with the attached pronoun -hu ('it' / 'him'), referring to a singular masculine thing or person. As object of the preposition, the pronoun is in the oblique form.
26.root: — (no triliteral root; a preposition with a pronoun)

27.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
27.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.
27.root: — (particle)

28.meaning: 'A little / a small amount' — an adjective/noun meaning small in quantity, few, scant, or trifling.
28.grammar: A noun/adjective 'little' in the accusative case with indefinite marking (the -an ending, tanwīn). The accusative commonly marks an object or specifies amount/manner; the doubled -n sound marks it as indefinite, 'a little.'
28.root: ق-ل-ل (q-l-l) — fewness; being little, scant, or small in amount

29.meaning: 'Among them / from them / some of them' — the preposition 'min' ('from, of, among') joined to the attached pronoun 'hum' ('them').
29.grammar: The preposition 'min' ('from / of / among') with the attached pronoun 'hum' ('them'), referring to a masculine plural group. Together they often express 'part of them' or 'some among them'.

30.meaning: A connector meaning 'then, when' — it joins to what came before ('then/so') and sets up a 'when…' clause whose outcome follows. It frames a moment: 'and then, at the point when…'.
30.grammar: A compound of the connecting particle fa- ('then/so', linking to the preceding statement) and lammā, a particle meaning 'when' that introduces a past circumstance and leads the listener to expect a following result clause.

31.meaning: He crossed it, passed over it, or went beyond it; moving across a boundary, water, or limit to the far side.
31.grammar: A completed (past-tense) verb in a pattern (Form III) often implying acting upon or in relation to something. The -a ending marks a third-person masculine singular subject in the past ('he crossed'). The attached -hu is the object 'it/him', the thing crossed.
31.root: ج-و-ز (j-w-z) — to pass, cross over, traverse, go beyond

32.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
32.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

33.meaning: 'And those who': a connective phrase introducing a specified group of people (masculine plural) about whom something will be said. It links them to what came before.
33.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'), which is masculine plural. A relative pronoun stands for a group and is normally followed by a clause describing them. Its form does not change for case; it stays alladhīna whatever its grammatical role.

34.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
34.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.
34.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — safety, security, trust, faith

35.meaning: Together with him; in his company or alongside him.
35.grammar: An adverb of accompaniment, 'with', joined to the attached pronoun -hu 'him'. Together they mean 'with him / in his company'.

36.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
36.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.
36.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — saying, speech, utterance

37.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
37.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

38.meaning: Strength, capacity, or the power to endure; the ability to bear or withstand something, the energy one can muster for a task.
38.grammar: A feminine singular noun in the 'construct' state (iḍāfa), where it leans on a following noun ('strength OF / for …'). The tell-tale sign is that the final -a carries NO nunation: a free-standing accusative would normally take -an (tanwīn), so the bare -a without it marks the word as bound to what follows. The vowel itself is accusative, the form taken here as the noun governed in the 'no … whatsoever' negating construction with lā ('no strength to …').
38.root: ط-و-ق (ṭ-w-q) — capacity, ability, the utmost one can bear

39.meaning: A combination of the preposition 'for / to' with the pronoun 'us', meaning 'for us' or 'to us / on our behalf'.
39.grammar: A preposition ('for / to') joined to the attached pronoun 'us'. The pronoun -nā always means 'us / our' regardless of position. Together they express benefit or direction toward the speakers ('for us').

40.meaning: An adverb of time meaning 'the day,' very often used to mean 'today' or 'this day.' With the definite article it points to the present day as a defined, known span of time, and by extension can denote 'now' or 'the present moment.'
40.grammar: A masculine noun carrying the definite article 'al-' ('the'). The final '-a' is the accusative ending; on a noun of time it commonly marks it as an adverb answering 'when?' — fixing the action to that period ('on the day', 'today').
40.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, a span of time

41.meaning: The proper name Jālūt (the biblical Goliath), the giant warrior-king. Prefixed with 'bi-' it conveys the sense of 'with/against' him — engagement or confrontation with the named person.
41.grammar: A foreign proper name preceded by the preposition 'bi-' ('with', 'against', 'by means of'). Because it is a non-Arabic name it is diptote: it takes a single '-a' ending after the preposition rather than the usual genitive '-i', and it never takes nunation (no final '-n' sound).

42.meaning: 'And his troops/soldiers' — the plural of jund (an army, host, or body of soldiers), joined by 'and' and made possessive by an attached 'his', so: a person's military forces or supporters.
42.grammar: Connective 'wa-' ('and') + a broken (irregular) plural noun + the possessive suffix '-hi' ('his'). The '-i' before the suffix is the genitive ending, signalling that the noun is possessed by what follows (here the pronoun 'his') or governed by a preceding preposition. The suffix vowel '-hi' (with kasra) harmonises after that genitive '-i'.
42.root: ج-ن-د (j-n-d) — to recruit/muster; army, host

43.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
43.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

44.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
44.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

45.meaning: 'They think / are sure / expect' — to hold something as one's settled conviction or to reckon it likely; the verb spans from firm certainty to strong supposition.
45.grammar: The prefix 'ya-' marks a 3rd-person present-tense verb, and the '-ūna' ending makes the subject a masculine-inclusive plural 'they.' The '-ūna' is the indicative marker, signalling a plain factual or ongoing statement.
45.root: ظ-ن-ن (ẓ-n-n) — to think, suppose, be convinced

46.meaning: 'That they…' — an emphatic connector 'anna' ('that, indeed') fused with the pronoun 'they,' used to introduce an affirmed clause as the content of a thought or statement.
46.grammar: Built on the particle 'anna' ('that…, indeed'), which introduces and affirms a following clause (often after verbs of knowing, thinking, or saying) and puts its noun into the accusative. The attached '-hum' is the pronoun 'they/them' for a male-inclusive group.

47.meaning: 'Ones who meet / will meet' — those who encounter or come face to face with someone. Built on a form meaning a mutual meeting or encounter.
47.grammar: An active participle, 'ones who meet/encounter' (the 'mu-' prefix forms a doer). It is a masculine sound plural; the '-ū' ending here is the plural-subject form with its final 'n' dropped because it stands in an 'of'-construction directly before the following noun.
47.root: ل-ق-ي (l-q-y) — to meet, encounter, come upon

48.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
48.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

49.meaning: An interrogative-exclamatory particle meaning 'how many / how much.' It introduces a question or, very often, an exclamation of abundance ('how many a…!'), and is followed by a singular indefinite noun naming what is being counted.
49.grammar: An indeclinable particle (its form never changes for case). In its exclamatory use it asserts a large, indefinite number; in its interrogative use it asks for a quantity. The noun it counts comes next in the singular and indefinite, typically in the genitive (for exclamation) or accusative (for the question).

50.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
50.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

51.meaning: A group, band, or company of people — a detachment or faction, especially a body of fighters. It denotes a portion of a larger whole that has banded together.
51.grammar: A feminine singular noun, here indefinite (no 'the'). The ending '-in' (the tā' marbūṭa pronounced with nunation, '-tin') is the indefinite genitive: it marks the noun as 'a group' linked to/governed by a preceding word, such as a counting particle or preposition.
51.root: ف-أ-ي (f-ʾ-y) — to split off; a faction/group

52.meaning: 'Small, few, little' — an adjective describing something limited in number or amount. Applied to a group, it means few in size or membership.
52.grammar: A feminine singular adjective on the pattern faʿīl, marked feminine by the tā' marbūṭa. It is indefinite, and the '-in' ('-tin') ending is the indefinite genitive — an adjective takes the same case as the noun it describes, so this matches a genitive, indefinite, feminine noun.
52.root: ق-ل-ل (q-l-l) — to be few/little, to diminish

53.meaning: 'It (feminine) overcame / defeated / prevailed' — the act of gaining the upper hand and conquering an opponent, completed in the past.
53.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb. The suffix '-at' marks a completed action done by a third-person feminine singular subject ('she/it overcame'). The bare past stem without prefixes indicates the deed is finished, not ongoing.

54.meaning: A group, band, or company of people — the same noun as fi'a (a faction or detachment), here in the accusative state.
54.grammar: A feminine singular noun, indefinite. The ending '-an' ('-tan' with the tā' marbūṭa) is the indefinite accusative: it commonly marks the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon) — i.e., the group that something is done to.
54.root: ف-أ-ي (f-ʾ-y) — to split off; a faction/group

55.meaning: Many, numerous, much — large in number or quantity. The feminine form of 'kathīr', describing abundance.
55.grammar: An adjective ('many'). The -at- (tā' marbūṭa) marks it feminine, so it describes a feminine noun; the -an is the accusative case with 'tanwīn' (-n, indefinite), matching a feminine noun in the accusative.

56.meaning: 'By the leave of / with the permission of' — formed from 'with/by' plus 'permission, leave, sanction'. It conveys that something happens by someone's authorization or enabling will.
56.grammar: The prefix bi- is a preposition 'with/by'. The noun 'idhn' means 'permission, leave, sanction'. After the preposition it takes the genitive -i ending, the form used following a preposition and typically linking on to a following noun ('the permission OF …').
56.root: أ-ذ-ن (ʾ-dh-n) — to permit, give leave; also listening/ear

57.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
57.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

58.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
58.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
58.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

59.meaning: With, together with, alongside — indicating company, accompaniment, or being in the same place or time as another.
59.grammar: A preposition of accompaniment ('with, alongside'); grammatically it is an adverbial of place/time (ẓarf) that governs the genitive. It is placed before a following noun to put one thing in the company of another, and that following noun stands in the genitive. The -a is its fixed ending.

60.meaning: 'The patient ones / the steadfast' — those who endure hardship with calm perseverance, restraining themselves and holding firm under trial.
60.grammar: A definite plural noun/participle ('the ones who...') referring to males or a mixed group. The '-īna' ending is the plural form used when the word is an object or follows a preposition (roughly 'the patient ones' as a target of the sentence). The 'al-' prefix means 'the'.
60.root: ص-ب-ر (ṣ-b-r) — to be patient, endure, hold firm

1.meaning: A compound meaning 'and when' — it sets up a circumstance in past time, marking the moment at which something occurred, with the result clause typically following. It carries the sense of 'when, at the time that.'
1.grammar: A particle phrase introducing a past-time clause. Lammā signals 'when' for completed events and expects a following clause stating what then happened; the wa- prefix means 'and.'

2.meaning: 'They went forth / came out (into the open),' especially to step out for battle or to confront an opponent. The verb conveys emerging into open view, advancing prominently.

parts.en: to go forth, emerge into the open

2.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb. The suffix '-ū' marks a completed action by a third-person masculine plural subject ('they went forth'). The trailing silent alif (وا) is a spelling convention after this plural ending and is not pronounced.
2.root: ب-ر-ز (b-r-z) — to come out, emerge, stand forth

3.meaning: The name Jālūt (Goliath) preceded by 'li-', giving the sense 'for / to(ward) / to face' him — directing oneself at or against the named person.
3.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('to', 'for', and by extension 'to face/against') joined to a foreign proper name. Being a diptote non-Arabic name, it takes the single '-a' ending after the preposition instead of the usual genitive '-i', and carries no nunation.

4.meaning: 'And his troops/soldiers' — the plural of jund (an army, host, or body of soldiers), joined by 'and' and made possessive by an attached 'his', so: a person's military forces or supporters.
4.grammar: Connective 'wa-' ('and') + a broken (irregular) plural noun + the possessive suffix '-hi' ('his'). The '-i' before the suffix is the genitive ending, signalling that the noun is possessed by what follows (here the pronoun 'his') or governed by a preceding preposition. The suffix vowel '-hi' (with kasra) harmonises after that genitive '-i'.

5.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
5.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.

6.meaning: An address to Allah meaning 'Our Lord' — invoking the Sustainer, Master, and Nurturer who creates, owns, provides for, and brings His servants to maturity. 'Rabb' is a rich term: not merely 'lord' but the One who cherishes and governs all that He has made. The attached 'our' makes it a direct calling upon Him.
6.grammar: A noun ('Lord / Sustainer') with an attached possessive pronoun. The -a ending reflects the accusative, used here in the vocative sense (calling out, 'O our Lord') — the implied 'O' (yā) is dropped before a noun joined to a pronoun. The suffix -nā means 'our'. So it reads 'O our Lord / our Lord!'.
6.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master; lordship and cherishing care

7.meaning: 'Pour out! / Pour down!' — a command to make a liquid flow abundantly, and figuratively to bestow or shower something (such as strength or patience) lavishly and completely.
7.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a single male ('you, pour!'), from the causative (form IV) verb 'afragha' ('to pour out, to make flow'). The initial alif here is hamzat al-qaṭʿ — the permanent causative prefix that is built into every form IV verb and is always pronounced (never dropped); it is not a prosthetic helping vowel. The final consonant is left vowel-less (jussive), as is normal for an order.
7.root: ف-ر-غ (f-r-gh) — to be empty; to pour out/empty

8.meaning: 'Upon us' / 'over us' / 'against us' — the preposition ʿalā ('on, over, upon') with an attached 'us'. It conveys something resting on, incumbent upon, or bearing against the group.
8.grammar: A preposition (ʿalā, 'upon/over') with an attached pronoun, first person plural (-nā, 'us'). When a pronoun is attached, ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay-. Such prepositional phrases put their pronoun in the object/genitive role.

9.meaning: Patience, steadfast endurance, self-restraint — the inner strength to bear hardship calmly, persevere, and hold oneself firm without complaint. A rich virtue: composure under trial and constancy in obedience.
9.grammar: A masculine verbal noun, indefinite. The '-an' ending (written with a following alif) is the indefinite accusative, which commonly marks the direct object of a verb — the thing being given, poured, or brought about.
9.root: ص-ب-ر (ṣ-b-r) — to be patient, endure, restrain oneself

10.meaning: 'And make firm! / and steady! / and plant firmly!' — a command to fix something securely in place and keep it from slipping, whether literally (footing) or figuratively (resolve, hearts).
10.grammar: Connective 'wa-' ('and') + an intensive (form II) command verb addressed to a single male ('you, make firm!'). The doubled middle root letter conveys causing/intensifying — 'to make firmly fixed.' The final consonant is left vowel-less (jussive), the normal shape of a command.
10.root: ث-ب-ت (th-b-t) — to be firm, fixed, steadfast

11.meaning: 'Our feet' — the plural of qadam (foot), made possessive by an attached 'our'. By extension 'making the feet firm' is an idiom for granting steadfastness and stability.
11.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural noun + the possessive suffix '-nā' ('our'). The '-a' before the suffix is the accusative ending, which here marks the noun as the direct object — the thing being acted upon — while '-nā' shows it belongs to 'us'.

12.meaning: 'And help us! / give us victory! / aid us!' — a command to come to someone's aid and grant them support and triumph, with 'us' as the one helped.
12.grammar: Connective 'wa-' ('and') + a command verb addressed to a single male ('you, help!') + the object pronoun '-nā' ('us'). The initial alif is a prosthetic helping vowel (hamzat al-waṣl), added to begin this form I command whose stem starts with a vowel-less consonant; it drops in pronunciation when joined to a preceding word. The stem vowel is left vowel-less (jussive) as is normal for an order, and '-nā' is the one receiving the help.
12.root: ن-ص-ر (n-ṣ-r) — to help, aid, grant victory

13.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
13.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
13.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

14.meaning: 'The people / the folk' — a collective noun for a community, nation, or group of people regarded as a body. Often it carries the nuance of one's own people or a particular group sharing a trait.
14.grammar: A collective noun with the definite article 'al-' ('the'). The final '-i' is the genitive ending, which typically appears after a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun in an 'of …' relationship.
14.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand/rise; a people, community

15.meaning: 'The disbelievers / the ungrateful concealers' — those who reject faith and cover over the truth. The active participle of kufr names people characterised by denying Allah and being ungrateful for His favours.
15.grammar: An active participle ('one who disbelieves') with the definite article 'al-', in the sound masculine plural. The ending '-īna' is the plural marker used in the genitive or accusative cases — that is, when the word follows a preposition, is linked to a preceding noun, or serves as an object/descriptor of one in those cases (as opposed to '-ūna', used for the subject case).
15.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover/conceal; to disbelieve, be ungrateful

1.meaning: 'So they routed/defeated them' — to put an opponent to flight and crush their resistance, with a connecting 'so/then' showing it as a consequence, and 'them' as the defeated party.

parts.en: to defeat, rout, put to flight

1.grammar: The connective 'fa-' ('so/then', marking sequence or result) + a past-tense verb with the masculine plural subject suffix '-ū' ('they') + the object pronoun '-hum' ('them'). The completed past stem shows a finished deed; '-ū' is the doers and '-hum' the ones defeated. (The silent alif after '-ū' is just spelling.)
1.root: ه-ز-م (h-z-m) — to defeat, rout, put to flight

2.meaning: 'By the leave of / with the permission of' — formed from 'with/by' plus 'permission, leave, sanction'. It conveys that something happens by someone's authorization or enabling will.
2.grammar: The prefix bi- is a preposition 'with/by'. The noun 'idhn' means 'permission, leave, sanction'. After the preposition it takes the genitive -i ending, the form used following a preposition and typically linking on to a following noun ('the permission OF …').
2.root: أ-ذ-ن (ʾ-dh-n) — to permit, give leave; also listening/ear

3.meaning: The proper name of the One True God in Arabic, Allāh — the unique, absolute Divine Being, alone worthy of worship. Used by Arabic-speaking Muslims, Christians, and Jews for the one Creator and Lord of all.
3.grammar: The proper divine name. The final '-i' is the genitive ending, which typically follows a preposition or links this name to a preceding noun in a possessive 'of Allah / belonging to Allah' relationship.

4.meaning: 'And he killed / slew' — the act of putting someone to death, completed in the past, joined by 'and'.
4.grammar: Connective 'wa-' ('and') + a past-tense (perfect) verb. The final '-a' marks a completed action by a third-person masculine singular subject ('he killed'). The bare past stem signals the deed is finished.

5.meaning: The proper name Dāwūd (the Prophet and King David), to whom the Psalms (Zabūr) were revealed.
