5.grammar: A proper name. The final '-u' is the nominative ending, the case that typically marks the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. As a diptote name it takes a bare '-u' without nunation (no final '-n' sound).

6.meaning: The proper name Jālūt (the biblical Goliath), the giant warrior-king.
6.grammar: A foreign proper name. Being a non-Arabic, diptote name it carries a single '-a' ending and never takes nunation. Here that '-a' serves as the accusative, the case that commonly marks the direct object — the one acted upon.

7.meaning: 'And he gave him' — the act of granting or bestowing something on someone, completed in the past, with 'and' connecting it and 'him' as the recipient. The verb ātā means to hand over, grant, or bring to.
7.grammar: Connective 'wa-' ('and') + a past-tense causative (form IV) verb ('to give/grant') + the object pronoun '-hu' ('him'). This verb's weak final root letter appears as a long 'ā', and the third-person masculine singular past ('he') is shown by that ending rather than a separate vowel. '-hu' is the one given to.
7.root: أ-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (form IV) to bring/give

8.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
8.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

9.meaning: 'The kingship / sovereignty / dominion' — royal authority and the power to rule and dispose of a realm; the office and possession of a king.
9.grammar: A masculine noun with the definite article 'al-' ('the'). The final '-a' is the accusative ending, which commonly marks the direct object of a verb — the thing given, granted, or acted upon.

10.meaning: And wisdom; and sound judgment. Ḥikma is deep wisdom — knowledge joined to right understanding and the putting of things in their proper place.
10.grammar: A definite feminine noun ('the wisdom') in the accusative case. The feminine ending is the tāʾ marbūṭa, and the accusative case vowel (-a) is borne by that same tāʾ — there is no separate ending after it. The accusative typically marks the noun as the direct object of a verb. The article al- makes it definite ('the wisdom'), and wa- ('and') joins it to what precedes.

11.meaning: "and He taught him/it" — built on the intensive verb meaning to instruct, to impart knowledge thoroughly, the form implying careful, repeated teaching. The attached object pronoun makes it 'taught him' or 'taught it'.
11.grammar: A past-tense verb in the 'he' form (third-person masculine singular). The doubled middle consonant (ʿallama, Form II) intensifies the basic root sense of 'knowing' into active 'teaching/instructing'. The ending -a is the normal past-tense vowel; the attached -hu is the object 'him/it'.

12.meaning: From what / from that which — a fusion of the preposition 'from' with the relative 'what/which', introducing the thing or situation being referred to.
12.grammar: A merger of 'min' ('from') and 'mā' ('what/that which'); the 'n' of 'min' assimilates into the 'm' of 'mā', doubling it. The combination means 'from what ...' and typically introduces a following clause describing the thing referred to. Being particles, neither part takes a case ending.

13.meaning: "He wills / wishes / desires" — denotes an act of will or volition, the choosing of something. As an ongoing/present-tense verb it expresses willing as a continuous, sovereign act.
13.grammar: A present/future-tense verb in the 'he' form. The ya- prefix marks third-person masculine singular ('he'). The final -u ending is the indicative mood, marking a plain, ongoing statement of fact ('he wills').

14.meaning: "and were it not for / and if not for" — a compound particle introducing a hypothetical: it points to something whose existence prevents a stated consequence, i.e. 'had it not been for X, then Y would have happened'.

parts.en: were it not for / if not

14.grammar: A particle phrase, not a verb, so it carries no case or tense ending. It sets up a conditional that is contrary to fact, typically answered by a clause beginning with la- ('then certainly…'). The leading wa- is the connector 'and'.

15.meaning: "repelling / pushing back / warding off" — a verbal noun naming the act of driving something away or holding it back, the abstract idea of repulsion or defence.
15.grammar: A verbal noun (the action named as a thing). The final -u ending is the nominative case, the form a noun takes as a subject or as the leading term in a possessive chain ('the repelling OF …').
15.root: د-ف-ع (d-f-ʿ) — to push, repel, ward off

16.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
16.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

17.meaning: Mankind, humanity, people in general — the collective of human beings.
17.grammar: A definite noun ('the people') with the attached 'al-' ('the'). The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'n' (a sun letter), which is why the 'n' is doubled — this is a pronunciation effect, not a separate piece. The final '-a' ending is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb (the one being acted upon) or the subject of certain particles.
17.root: ن-و-س (n-w-s) — to move/sway; by extension, people

18.meaning: "some of them / a part of them" — the word baʿḍ means 'a portion/some', and with the attached pronoun it means 'some of them', singling out part of a group.
18.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive/partitive pronoun. The -a ending is the accusative case, the form a noun takes as the object of an action or the second term of certain constructions. The suffix -hum means 'them' (third-person masculine plural).
18.root: ب-ع-ض (b-ʿ-ḍ) — part, portion, some

19.meaning: 'In part / in some' — referring to a portion or some of a whole, here left indefinite. The bi- prefix gives the sense of disbelieving 'in' something.
19.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with') plus the noun baʿḍ ('a part, some'). The final -in (tanwīn kasr) is the genitive case with indefiniteness, required after bi- and marking the noun as 'some (unspecified) part.'
19.root: ب-ع-ض (b-ʿ-ḍ) — a part, portion, or some of a whole

20.meaning: "then it would surely have become corrupt / fallen into ruin" — built on the verb meaning to spoil, decay, or descend into disorder; the form conveys that ruin or corruption set in.
20.grammar: A past-tense verb in the 'she/it' form, marked feminine by the -t ending (here voweled -ti to ease pronunciation before a following word). The leading la- is an emphatic 'surely', the answer-particle that completes a contrary-to-fact conditional ('… then surely it would have…').
20.root: ف-س-د (f-s-d) — to be corrupt, spoil, ruin

21.meaning: A noun meaning 'the earth', 'the ground', or 'the land' — the terrestrial world, the soil and land surface as opposed to the sky.
21.grammar: A noun with the definite article 'al-' ('the'). The -u ending is nominative, which typically marks the word as the subject of a sentence (the one doing the action). This noun is grammatically feminine.

22.meaning: "but / however" (emphatic) — a contrastive particle that corrects or sets against what was just said, here in its stronger form that also asserts what follows.
22.grammar: A contrastive particle in its 'heavy' (doubled-n) form, which behaves like inna: it governs a following noun, putting it into the accusative case, and lends emphasis. It carries no case ending of its own. The leading wa- is 'and'.

23.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
23.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

24.meaning: Owner of / possessor of / endowed with — a word that does not stand alone but means 'the one who has' whatever noun follows it, ascribing that quality or possession to someone.

parts.en: possessor of, owner of, endowed with

24.grammar: A possessive noun meaning 'owner/possessor of', always followed by another noun in the genitive. The final -ū form here is the nominative case, used when this word names the subject or is the thing being described; it inherently requires a following noun to complete its sense ('owner OF …').
24.root: — (no triliteral root; an irregular noun of possession)

25.meaning: Bounty, grace, favor; an overflowing generosity or surplus given freely. It denotes goodness and abundance bestowed beyond what is owed or expected, and by extension excellence or superiority.
25.grammar: The -in ending is genitive plus 'tanwīn' (the -n indicating indefiniteness, 'a bounty'). The genitive case typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF bounty') or follows a preposition.
25.root: ف-ض-ل (f-ḍ-l) — bounty, grace, excess goodness, superiority

26.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
26.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
26.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

27.meaning: The worlds, all created realms — the totality of beings and peoples; in 'Lord of the worlds,' the whole of creation across all its kinds.
27.grammar: A definite plural noun ('the worlds') with 'al-' ('the'). The '-īna' ending marks a masculine sound plural in the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) form — the form used after a preposition, in an 'of' linkage, or as a direct object.
27.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know; a 'world' as a sign by which the Creator is known

1.meaning: That; a demonstrative used to point to something distant or already mentioned. It singles out a single feminine (or grammatically feminine) thing, roughly 'that one over there.'
1.grammar: A feminine singular demonstrative pronoun pointing to something far off. The -ka element signals remoteness ('that yonder' rather than 'this near'). Being a demonstrative, it does not take case endings; its form is fixed.

2.meaning: "signs / verses / tokens" — the plural of āya, a 'sign' or evident token that points to something beyond itself; it also denotes a verse of revelation, each one a sign.
2.grammar: A feminine plural noun (the -āt ending marks sound feminine plural). The final -u is the nominative case, the form taken as the subject of a sentence or the leading term of a possessive chain ('the signs OF …').

3.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
3.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

4.meaning: "We recite it / We relate it" — built on the verb meaning to recite aloud, to read out, to convey a text in sequence; with the object pronoun it means 'we recite them/it'.
4.grammar: A present/future-tense verb in the 'we' form. The na- prefix marks first-person plural ('we'). The attached -hā is the object 'it/them' (referring to a feminine or non-human-plural noun).
4.root: ت-ل-و (t-l-w) — to recite, read out, follow

5.meaning: "upon you / to you / against you" — the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over') with the 'you' pronoun, carrying senses of resting upon, being directed to, or bearing upon someone.
5.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The base ʿalā shifts to ʿalay- when a pronoun is added. The suffix -ka means 'you' (second-person masculine singular). Prepositions themselves take no case ending.

6.meaning: 'With the truth / by means of what is true and right.' Combines the preposition 'with/by' and 'the truth' — that which is real, established, correct, and rightfully due, as opposed to falsehood.
6.grammar: A noun governed by the attached preposition bi- ('with/by'). The -i ending is the genitive case, which is required after a preposition; here it links 'the truth' to 'with', giving 'with the truth'.
6.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, right, reality, that which is established and due

7.meaning: "and indeed you / and truly you" — the emphatic particle inna ('truly, indeed') joined to the 'you' pronoun, strongly affirming a statement about the person addressed.
7.grammar: An emphatic opening particle (inna) with an attached pronoun. Inna asserts and strengthens the sentence ('it is certainly the case that…') and grammatically takes its noun/pronoun in the accusative; the attached -ka ('you') is that accusative pronoun. The leading wa- is 'and'.

8.meaning: An emphatic 'truly/surely' joined to the preposition min ('from, among, of') — conveying 'surely (one) of / among', stressing belonging to a group.
8.grammar: Two particles. 'la-' is the emphatic prefix adding certainty (often paired with inna). 'min' is a preposition meaning 'from/among/of' and puts the noun after it into the genitive case. Its final -a here is a connecting vowel used before the definite article 'al-'.

9.meaning: "the messengers / the ones sent" — the definite plural of mursal, a passive participle meaning 'one who is sent'; it denotes those commissioned and dispatched, i.e. the divine messengers.
9.grammar: A definite masculine sound plural passive participle ('the sent ones'). The -īna ending is the accusative/genitive (object or after-preposition) form of the masculine plural, as opposed to -ūna which would mark the subject form.

1.meaning: That; a demonstrative used to point to something distant or already mentioned. It singles out a single feminine (or grammatically feminine) thing, roughly 'that one over there.'
1.grammar: A feminine singular demonstrative pronoun pointing to something far off. The -ka element signals remoteness ('that yonder' rather than 'this near'). Being a demonstrative, it does not take case endings; its form is fixed.

2.meaning: "the messengers" — the definite plural of rasūl, an envoy or messenger: one sent with a message or mission. With the article it denotes 'the messengers' as a defined group.
2.grammar: A definite broken (internally formed) plural noun. The leading al- is 'the', and its 'l' assimilates into the following r- (heard as rr-). The final -u is the nominative case, the form a noun takes as the subject of a sentence.

3.meaning: "We favoured / We gave preference / We caused to excel" — built on the intensive verb meaning to give one thing precedence or superiority over another, to bestow extra favour; 'we preferred / we made excel'.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb in the 'we' form. The doubled middle consonant (Form II) makes the root sense of 'bounty/excess' transitive and intensive: 'to make excel, to favour'. The suffix -nā marks the subject as 'we' (first-person plural).

4.meaning: "some of them / a part of them" — the word baʿḍ means 'a portion/some', and with the attached pronoun it means 'some of them', singling out part of a group.
4.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive/partitive pronoun. The -a ending is the accusative case, the form a noun takes as the object of an action or the second term of certain constructions. The suffix -hum means 'them' (third-person masculine plural).

5.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
5.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

6.meaning: 'Some (others)' / 'a part' — the same noun for 'a portion or some,' here left indefinite, often functioning as the counterpart in the 'one another' construction.
6.grammar: A noun 'part/some' in the genitive case with indefinite marking (the -in ending, called tanwīn). The genitive typically follows a preposition or links it to a preceding noun ('… of …'); the doubled -n sound marks it as indefinite ('a part / some').
6.root: ب-ع-ض (b-ʿ-ḍ) — a part, portion, or some of a whole

7.meaning: From them / among them — the preposition min ('from, out of, part of') joined to the pronoun 'them' (a group of males or a mixed group).
7.grammar: The preposition min ('from / among / part of') with the attached third-person masculine plural pronoun -hum ('them'). Pronouns after a preposition are in the genitive; the combination expresses origin, partition ('some of them'), or belonging to that group.

8.meaning: A versatile word meaning 'who / whoever / the one who.' It can ask a question ('who?') or introduce a clause ('whoever does…'), referring to persons.
8.grammar: An indeclinable particle/pronoun with a fixed form (it does not change for case). Used for rational beings ('who'), functioning either as an interrogative ('who?') or as a conditional/relative ('whoever, the one who').

9.meaning: "he spoke (to) / he addressed in speech" — built on the intensive verb meaning to talk to or address someone directly with words; it denotes the act of speaking to another.
9.grammar: A past-tense verb in the 'he' form (third-person masculine singular). The doubled middle consonant (Form II) shapes the root 'speech/word' into directed speaking ('to speak TO someone'). The final -a is the standard past-tense ending.

10.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
10.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

11.meaning: "and he raised / he lifted up / he elevated" — built on the verb meaning to raise high, to lift, to elevate in rank or position.
11.grammar: A past-tense verb in the 'he' form (third-person masculine singular). The final -a is the normal past-tense vowel. The leading wa- is the connector 'and'.

12.meaning: "some of them / a part of them" — the word baʿḍ means 'a portion/some', and with the attached pronoun it means 'some of them', singling out part of a group.
12.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive/partitive pronoun. The -a ending is the accusative case, the form a noun takes as the object of an action or the second term of certain constructions. The suffix -hum means 'them' (third-person masculine plural).

13.meaning: "degrees / ranks / levels / steps" — the plural of daraja, a step or grade in an ascending scale; it denotes ranks, levels, or stages of elevation.
13.grammar: A feminine plural noun (the -āt ending marks sound feminine plural). The final -in (with nunation/tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('degrees, ranks') and in the accusative/genitive case — the form used as an object or after a preposition.
13.root: د-ر-ج (d-r-j) — step, grade, to ascend by degrees

14.meaning: "and We gave / brought" — to give, bring, or grant something to someone.
14.grammar: The wa- prefix is "and." This is a past-tense causative verb meaning "to give/bring (to someone)." The -nā ending marks a first-person plural subject ("we") who completed the action.
14.root: ا-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (causative) to give, bring

15.meaning: "Isa" — the personal name of the prophet Jesus, son of Mary.
15.grammar: A proper name (a foreign/non-Arabic name). It is fully indeclinable: its ending does not change for case, so it stays the same as subject, object, or after a preposition.

16.meaning: "son" — a male child or descendant.
16.grammar: A noun beginning with a helping (elidable) vowel. The -a ending is accusative, which marks the word as the object of a verb or as an appositive describing a preceding accusative noun. When placed between two names, it functions as "son of …"

17.meaning: "Maryam" — the personal name Mary, the mother of the prophet Jesus.
17.grammar: A proper name (feminine, foreign origin). It is diptote: it takes no -n (nunation), and in the genitive and accusative it ends in -a rather than -i, so the -a ending shown serves for both object and "of" positions.

18.meaning: "the clear proofs / evident signs" — plural of a feminine word meaning a clear, manifest evidence, proof, or sign that makes the truth plain.
18.grammar: The al- prefix means "the." The -āt is the sound feminine plural ending. Its -i (here -ti) ending serves for both the genitive and the accusative in this plural pattern — marking the word as an object, or as governed by a preposition or a following noun.
18.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — to be clear, to make plain

19.meaning: "and We strengthened / supported him" — the conjunction "and" with a past verb meaning to reinforce, back up, or strengthen someone, plus the object "him."
19.grammar: The wa- prefix is "and." This is a past-tense verb of the intensive (doubled) form meaning "to strengthen/support." The -nā ending marks a first-person plural subject ("we"); the attached -hu is the object pronoun "him."

20.meaning: "with the spirit of" — the preposition "with" joined to the noun for spirit, breath of life, or animating principle, in a possessive ("… of …") construction.
20.grammar: The bi- prefix is a preposition ("with, by"). The -i ending is genitive: required after the preposition, and it also links this noun to a following noun ("the spirit OF …").

21.meaning: "the holiness / sanctity" — purity and holiness; that which is utterly pure and set apart from defect. Paired with "spirit," it forms the title "the Holy Spirit."
21.grammar: The al- prefix means "the." The -i ending is genitive, marking the word as the second noun in a possessive pair ("… of holiness") or as governed by a preposition.

22.meaning: 'and if' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the particle 'if'. This particular 'if' (law) introduces a hypothetical or contrary-to-fact condition: 'if (such-and-such had been the case)…', often implying it was not.
22.grammar: A conjunction plus a conditional particle. wa- means 'and'. law is a non-changing particle (no case ending) that sets up a supposition, typically answered by a clause beginning with la- ('… then certainly …').

23.meaning: A past-tense verb 'he willed / he wished / he so desired'. It denotes an act of will or volition bringing something about.
23.grammar: Past-tense (perfect) verb, third person masculine singular ('he'). The bare stem with no suffix is the basic 'he did' form. Its subject and object are typically supplied by context.

24.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
24.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
24.root: — (proper divine name)

25.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
25.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

26.meaning: "they fought one another / they fell into mutual combat" (he/it form base) — built on the reflexive-reciprocal verb of fighting, meaning to do battle against each other.
26.grammar: A past-tense verb in Form VIII (marked by the prefixed i- and infixed -t-), which here gives a reciprocal sense: 'to fight one another'. The final -a is the standard past-tense ending; the form is the base third-person singular shape that can take a plural subject after it.

27.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
27.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

28.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
28.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

29.meaning: "after them / following them" — the noun baʿd ('after, afterward') with the attached pronoun 'them', denoting what comes later in time than a group.
29.grammar: A time-noun used like a preposition, with an attached pronoun. The -i ending is genitive, the form taken after a preposition or as the second term of a possessive link. The suffix -him means 'them' (its vowel is -hi- to harmonise with the preceding -i).
29.root: ب-ع-د (b-ʿ-d) — afterness, what follows

30.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
30.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

31.meaning: A noun/adverb meaning 'after' — the time or position following something; 'afterward', 'following'.
31.grammar: An adverb of time functioning as a noun, here in the genitive case marked by the final -i. The genitive ending typically appears after a preposition or as the second term of a construct ('after THE …'), linking 'after' to a following noun to specify what it comes after.
31.root: ب-ع-د (b-ʿ-d) — to be after, to follow, distance in place or time

32.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
32.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

33.meaning: 'It / she came to them'. A past-tense verb of coming or arriving, with a feminine singular subject ('it/she'), and an attached pronoun 'them' as the ones reached.
33.grammar: 'jāa' is a past-tense verb 'came'. The '-t' suffix marks a feminine singular subject ('she' or a feminine 'it'). The attached '-hum' means 'them' (masculine plural) as the object reached; its vowel appears as '-humu' to ease pronunciation before a following word.
33.root: ج-ي-ء (j-y-ʾ) — to come, to arrive, to bring

34.meaning: The clear proofs / evident signs — plainly manifest, self-evident pieces of evidence that make the truth unmistakable.

parts.en: clear proofs / evident signs (the final -u is the nominative case ending, marking the subject)

34.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun (with 'al-' = 'the') meaning 'clear proofs.' The plural ending 'āt' marks a feminine plural, and the final -u is the nominative case ending, which typically marks the noun as the subject/doer of a sentence ('… the clear proofs came to you'). The pattern 'bayyina' denotes something that makes things plainly evident.
34.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — clarity, distinctness; to make plain or evident

35.meaning: "but / however" — a contrastive particle that sets what follows against what came before, correcting or qualifying the previous statement.
35.grammar: A contrastive particle in its 'light' (single-n) form, which simply links clauses and does not govern a following noun's case. The final -i here is a helping vowel added to ease pronunciation before a following word (it is not a case ending). The leading wa- is 'and'.

36.meaning: A verb meaning 'they differed / disagreed / fell into dispute', also 'they varied, became diverse'. The Form VIII root expresses people taking divergent positions or one thing succeeding and differing from another.
36.grammar: Past-tense (perfect) verb (Form VIII), third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending marks a completed action done by 'they' (a masculine or mixed group); the silent alif written after it is a spelling convention, not pronounced.
36.root: خ-ل-ف (kh-l-f) — to come after, succeed, differ, be at variance

37.meaning: "so / and among them / of them (there are)" — the preposition min ('from, among, of') with the pronoun 'them', expressing 'among them' or 'some of them', introduced by 'so/and'.
37.grammar: A connective particle plus a preposition with an attached pronoun. Fa- means 'so/and then', linking to what precedes. Min ('from/among') takes no case ending; the suffix -hum is 'them' (third-person masculine plural). The phrase often introduces a partition ('among them are…').

38.meaning: A versatile word meaning 'who / whoever / the one who.' It can ask a question ('who?') or introduce a clause ('whoever does…'), referring to persons.
38.grammar: An indeclinable particle/pronoun with a fixed form (it does not change for case). Used for rational beings ('who'), functioning either as an interrogative ('who?') or as a conditional/relative ('whoever, the one who').

39.meaning: 'He believed' — he had faith, trusted, and affirmed. The basic past-tense form of the verb meaning to believe and to find security in faith.
39.grammar: A past-tense verb on the causative (Form IV) pattern, from the root for security and faith. The -a ending marks a third-person masculine singular subject, 'he (believed)', stating a completed act of coming to faith.

40.meaning: 'And among them / and some of them' — a connective 'and' plus a preposition meaning 'from / among / part of,' joined to the pronoun 'them'; often introduces a subgroup ('among them are …').
40.grammar: A connective wa- ('and') with the preposition min ('from / among'), which always governs a following word in the genitive. Here that word is the attached pronoun -hum ('them'), giving 'and among them / and from them.' Particles like these do not themselves carry case or tense.

41.meaning: A versatile word meaning 'who / whoever / the one who.' It can ask a question ('who?') or introduce a clause ('whoever does…'), referring to persons.
41.grammar: An indeclinable particle/pronoun with a fixed form (it does not change for case). Used for rational beings ('who'), functioning either as an interrogative ('who?') or as a conditional/relative ('whoever, the one who').

42.meaning: He disbelieved / rejected — to refuse faith, deny the truth, and turn away ungratefully from Allah. The root also carries the sense of covering over or being ungrateful for a blessing.
42.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third-person masculine singular ('he disbelieved'). The final -a ending marks completed past action done by a single male. The verb denotes rejecting faith and being ungrateful, covering over the truth.
42.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover over, reject faith, be ungrateful

43.meaning: 'and if' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the particle 'if'. This particular 'if' (law) introduces a hypothetical or contrary-to-fact condition: 'if (such-and-such had been the case)…', often implying it was not.
43.grammar: A conjunction plus a conditional particle. wa- means 'and'. law is a non-changing particle (no case ending) that sets up a supposition, typically answered by a clause beginning with la- ('… then certainly …').

44.meaning: A past-tense verb 'he willed / he wished / he so desired'. It denotes an act of will or volition bringing something about.
44.grammar: Past-tense (perfect) verb, third person masculine singular ('he'). The bare stem with no suffix is the basic 'he did' form. Its subject and object are typically supplied by context.

45.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
45.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

46.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
46.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

47.meaning: "they fought one another / they engaged in mutual combat" — the plural of the reciprocal verb of fighting: to do battle against each other.
47.grammar: A past-tense verb in Form VIII (prefixed i- with infixed -t-), giving the reciprocal sense 'to fight one another'. The -ū ending marks the subject as 'they' (third-person masculine plural); the silent alif written after it is a spelling convention.

48.meaning: But; however; rather. A particle of correction or contrast that cancels or qualifies a preceding statement and introduces what is actually the case.
48.grammar: A connective wa- ('and') joined to the emphatic particle lākinna. Lākinna belongs to the 'inna family: it governs the noun that follows it, putting it in the accusative case, and adds a sense of firm contrast — 'but in fact …'.

49.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
49.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

50.meaning: "he does / he acts / he carries out" — built on the basic verb meaning to do, make, or perform; the present tense conveys ongoing or habitual action.
50.grammar: A present/future-tense verb in the 'he' form. The ya- prefix marks third-person masculine singular ('he'). The final -u ending is the indicative mood, marking a plain statement of ongoing or habitual fact ('he does').

51.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
51.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

52.meaning: "he wills / he intends / he wants" — built on the Form IV verb meaning to want, intend, or purpose something; it expresses directed intention or desire toward an aim.
52.grammar: A present/future-tense verb in the 'he' form, of Form IV (note the yu- prefix with 'u'). It conveys 'to intend/want'. The final -u ending is the indicative mood, marking a plain statement of ongoing fact ('he intends').

1.meaning: 'O…!' — a compound vocative expression used to call out and summon an audience before addressing them. It fuses the call-particle 'yā' ('O') with a noun that means 'the one(s) addressed,' yielding an emphatic 'O you…!' that introduces direct address.
1.grammar: A vocative (calling) construction. 'Yā' is the particle for calling out; 'ayyu' carries a nominative '-u' as the one being summoned; 'hā' is an attention-drawing particle. Together they function as 'O you…!,' setting up the noun of address that follows.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
3.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

4.meaning: A command addressed to a group: 'spend!' — give out or expend wealth, resources, or provisions. The verb often carries the nuance of charitable or purposeful giving, releasing what one has for a cause or for others.
4.grammar: An imperative (command) verb. The -ū ending marks a masculine-plural addressee: 'you all, do this.' Built on Form IV (the af'ala pattern), which here gives the sense of expending or paying out from one's wealth.
4.root: ن-ف-ق (n-f-q) — to spend, expend, give out (of wealth)

5.meaning: From what / from that which — a fusion of the preposition 'from' with the relative 'what/which', introducing the thing or situation being referred to.
5.grammar: A merger of 'min' ('from') and 'mā' ('what/that which'); the 'n' of 'min' assimilates into the 'm' of 'mā', doubling it. The combination means 'from what ...' and typically introduces a following clause describing the thing referred to. Being particles, neither part takes a case ending.

6.meaning: 'We provided you' / 'we granted you sustenance' — to bestow provision, livelihood, or sustenance upon someone. Marked for a 'we' subject acting upon 'you (plural)'.
6.grammar: A past-tense verb carrying two attached pronouns. The first suffix -nā marks the doer, 'we'; the second suffix -kum marks the receiver, 'you (plural)'. So the form means 'we provided you'. The verb denotes granting provision or sustenance.

7.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
7.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

8.meaning: A noun/adverb meaning 'before' — denoting that which precedes in time or order.
8.grammar: An adverb/noun of time. The -i ending is genitive, which here arises because it follows a preposition (commonly 'min', 'from'); it characteristically links to a following noun ('before … OF …').
8.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to precede, come before; the front or prior side

9.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
9.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

10.meaning: '(that) it comes' or 'so that it may come' — to arrive, come, or approach. The verb denotes something drawing near or coming to pass.
10.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it'). The final -a (subjunctive) ending, rather than the usual -u, signals that the verb is governed by a preceding particle such as 'that' or 'before/until' — giving the sense 'that it come' or 'so that it may come.'

11.meaning: 'a day' — a period of daylight, a single day, or more broadly an appointed time or epoch. It can refer to an ordinary day or to a momentous, decisive day.
11.grammar: A masculine singular noun. The -un ending is nominative and indefinite ('a day'): the doubled-n (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite, and the -u vowel typically marks it as the subject of a sentence or the doer of an action.

12.meaning: 'Not' — a particle of negation. Depending on context it denies a present fact, forbids an action, or rules something out ('do not / there is no').
12.grammar: A negating particle, 'not / no'. It is used to deny or prohibit — negating present-tense statements, expressing 'there is no...', or, with a command form, forbidding an action ('do not...').

13.meaning: 'trade / bargaining / a sale' — the act of buying and selling, a commercial transaction, or by extension any exchange or ransom by which one thing is given for another.
13.grammar: A masculine singular verbal noun. The -un ending is nominative and indefinite ('a trade'): the tanwīn (doubled-n) marks indefiniteness, and the -u vowel typically marks it as the subject of a sentence.

14.meaning: 'In it / in him' — the preposition 'in, inside, within' joined to a pronoun referring to a single masculine or neuter thing. It locates something inside or as part of that referent.
14.grammar: A preposition with an attached object pronoun. The pronoun -hi refers to one masculine (or grammatically masculine) thing and stands as the object of the preposition; its vowel is -i because attached pronouns take that shape after the long -i of fi. Together they answer 'in what?' or 'in whom?'.

15.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
15.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

16.meaning: 'close friendship / intimate bond' — a relationship of deep affection and loyalty between true friends. It denotes the kind of devoted, intimate friendship that might be hoped to bring help or favour.
16.grammar: A feminine singular noun (the -a / tā' marbūṭa marks the feminine). The -un ending is nominative and indefinite ('a friendship'): the tanwīn marks indefiniteness, and the -u vowel typically marks it as the subject of a sentence.

17.meaning: 'And not' — a connector 'and' joined to the negative particle 'not,' negating a following statement.
17.grammar: Two particles: the joining 'and' (wa) plus the negator lā ('not'). Lā commonly negates a present-tense verb or a noun. Neither particle takes case endings.

18.meaning: Intercession — pleading or mediating on someone's behalf so that they may be pardoned or helped.
18.grammar: A singular feminine verbal noun, indefinite ('an intercession'). The -un ending (tanwīn ḍamma) is the indefinite nominative, which typically marks the subject or the thing being spoken about.
18.root: ش-ف-ع (sh-f-ʿ) — to intercede, pair, double

19.meaning: 'and the deniers / and the disbelievers' — those who reject faith and cover over the truth. The root sense is 'to cover/conceal,' so a kāfir is one who covers up or ungratefully denies what is true.
19.grammar: A masculine-plural active participle ('those who deny'), prefixed with 'and' and 'the.' The -ūna ending marks a sound masculine plural in the nominative case — typically the subject of a sentence (had it been the object, it would read -īna).
19.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal, deny, be ungrateful

20.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (masculine plural). Standing on its own, it typically adds emphasis or marks the group out as the focus ('they, specifically', 'it is they who').
20.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It takes no case endings; the base is hum, and the final vowel appears as -u (humu) as a connecting vowel to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a definite article. Standing alone, it commonly emphasises or isolates the subject.

21.meaning: The wrongdoers; those who do wrong, act unjustly, or place things where they do not belong. The underlying image is one who oppresses, transgresses limits, and deals unjustly with others or with themselves.
21.grammar: An active participle (the doer of the action) made definite by the prefix al- ('the'). The -ūna ending marks a masculine plural in the nominative (subject) case, the form used when the word functions as the doer of a verb or the subject of a sentence.

1.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
1.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

2.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
2.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

3.meaning: God / object of worship — a deity that is worshipped. The bare noun names the concept of a worshipped god.
3.grammar: A singular noun carrying an -a ending. This short -a typically marks the accusative (object) case; it is also the form a noun takes immediately after the absolute-negation particle 'lā' to mean 'no … (at all).'
3.root: أ-ل-ه (ʾ-l-h) — godhood, worship, being a deity

4.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
4.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

5.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
5.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

6.meaning: 'the Ever-Living / the Living One' — possessing life in the fullest, absolute, and eternal sense: life that never began and never ends, the source of all life. As a divine name it affirms perfect, undying life.
6.grammar: A definite adjective/noun ('the Living'). The -u ending is nominative, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or for a noun in apposition (a descriptive title) to such a subject.

7.meaning: 'the Self-Subsisting Sustainer' — the One who exists wholly by Himself, needing nothing, and by whom all else is maintained and kept in being. It combines absolute self-existence with the constant upholding of everything that exists.
7.grammar: A definite noun in an intensive pattern (denoting permanence and totality). The -u ending is nominative, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or for an appositive descriptive title attached to such a subject.
7.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise, maintain, uphold

8.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
8.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

9.meaning: 'it takes/seizes Him' or 'overtakes Him' — to take, grasp, or lay hold of, with the object being 'Him.' The verb conveys something coming over or gripping a person.
9.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person feminine singular ('she/it takes'), with attached object pronoun -hu ('him'). The -u before the suffix is the indicative ending, marking a plain, ongoing statement of fact ('it takes / does take').

10.meaning: 'drowsiness / light slumber' — the heaviness or doze that precedes sleep, that first creeping of sleepiness over a person, as distinct from full sleep.
10.grammar: A feminine singular noun (the -a / tā' marbūṭa marks the feminine). The -un ending is nominative and indefinite ('drowsiness'): the tanwīn marks indefiniteness, and the -u vowel typically marks it as the subject of a sentence.

11.meaning: 'And not' — a connector 'and' joined to the negative particle 'not,' negating a following statement.
11.grammar: Two particles: the joining 'and' (wa) plus the negator lā ('not'). Lā commonly negates a present-tense verb or a noun. Neither particle takes case endings.

12.meaning: 'sleep' — full, deep sleep; the state of being asleep, in contrast to mere drowsiness.
12.grammar: A masculine singular noun. The -un ending is nominative and indefinite ('sleep'): the tanwīn (doubled-n) marks indefiniteness, and the -u vowel typically marks it as the subject of a sentence.

13.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
13.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

14.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
14.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

15.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
15.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

16.meaning: The heavens / the skies — the plural of 'heaven', referring to the skies above and the celestial realms; the elevated expanse over the earth.
16.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun with the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the heavens') or follows a preposition. In the sound feminine plural, this -i form also covers what would be an object role.

17.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
17.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

18.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
18.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
18.root: — (particle)

19.meaning: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
19.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').

20.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
20.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

21.meaning: A demonstrative meaning 'this one' or 'the one' — a pointing word ('that/this') used to single out a person or thing. It often combines with the question particle to form 'who is it that…?'
21.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun ('this/that one'). It does not take case endings; the final -ā is part of the fixed word. It functions to point out or identify someone or something.

22.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
22.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

23.meaning: '(he/it) intercedes' — to plead or mediate on another's behalf, interposing oneself to seek pardon or benefit for someone before a higher authority.
23.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he intercedes'). The final -u is the indicative ending, marking a plain statement of fact about an ongoing or general action.

24.meaning: 'With him / in his keeping / that he has' — combining the locational word 'ind ('at, with, in the presence/possession of') with the pronoun 'him'. It conveys that something is held by, present with, or belongs to him.
24.grammar: 'ʿinda' is an adverb of place/possession that always governs a following word in the genitive; here it takes the attached pronoun -hu ('him/his'). The -a on 'ʿinda' is its fixed accusative-style ending as an adverbial. The pronoun -hu means the thing is located with, or owned by, a single male.

25.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
25.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

26.meaning: 'By His permission / with His leave'. It joins 'with/by' to the noun 'permission, leave, sanction' and an attached pronoun 'His', indicating something done by the authorization of the one referred to.
26.grammar: The prefix 'bi-' is a preposition meaning 'with' or 'by (means of)'. It places the following noun in the genitive case, shown by the '-i' ending. The attached '-hi' is a possessive pronoun, 'His' (or 'its'), so the whole reads 'by His permission'.
26.root: أ-ذ-ن (ʾ-dh-n) — to permit, give leave; to hear/heed

27.meaning: 'He/it knows' — a present-tense verb of knowing: to have knowledge of, be aware of, recognize, or understand something.
27.grammar: Present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it'). The ya- prefix marks 'he,' and the final -u marks the ordinary (indicative) present, 'he knows / does know.'
27.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — knowledge; knowing, being aware, recognizing

28.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
28.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

29.meaning: Between; in the midst of two things. An adverb of place marking the space separating or lying among parties or points.
29.grammar: An adverb of place ('between'). It always ends in -a and grammatically governs what follows it, putting the following noun(s) into the genitive 'of' relationship. It does not change to show 'the' or a case of its own; the fixed -a is simply how this word is formed.
29.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies between

30.meaning: Their hands. The plural noun 'hands' carrying the masculine plural possessive 'their'; often used idiomatically for what people do, produce, or are responsible for through their own deeds.
30.grammar: A plural noun with an attached possessive pronoun '-him' meaning 'their' (a group of males, or mixed). 'aydī' is the irregular ('broken') plural of 'yad' (hand). The pronoun ending makes the whole construction definite and possessed; the 'i'-coloured stem before the suffix reflects its genitive/possessed state, the form typically following a preposition or standing as object.
30.root: ي-د-ي (y-d-y) — hand

31.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
31.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.
31.root: — (relative pronoun / particle)

32.meaning: 'behind them' — the space or position to the rear of a group; also figuratively what lies after them, what awaits them, or what is hidden from them.
32.grammar: An adverb of place ('behind') with the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The -a ending is accusative, the case regularly used for adverbs of place and time, indicating the location 'behind.'
32.root: خ-ل-ف (kh-l-f) — to be behind, come after, succeed

33.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
33.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

34.meaning: 'they encompass / they comprehend fully' — to surround, enclose, or grasp something completely, so that nothing of it escapes one's reach or understanding.
34.grammar: A present-tense Form IV verb, third-person masculine plural ('they encompass'). The -ūna ending marks the masculine-plural doers in the indicative mood — a plain statement of fact ('they do encompass').
34.root: ح-و-ط (ḥ-w-ṭ) — to surround, enclose, encompass

35.meaning: 'with something / with a thing' — by means of some thing or matter; 'shay'' is the most general word for 'a thing'.
35.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the noun 'thing'. The '-in' ending marks the noun as indefinite ('a thing, something') and in the genitive case required after a preposition.
35.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʾ) — thing; to will, to want

36.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
36.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

37.meaning: 'His knowledge' — knowing, awareness, or learning, here possessed by Him. 'Ilm denotes sure, comprehensive knowledge as opposed to guesswork.
37.grammar: A masculine verbal noun with the attached possessive pronoun -hi ('his'). The -i ending is genitive: this case typically follows a preposition or links the word to another as a possessor ('… of …'), and the pronoun appears here as -hi (rather than -hu) because it follows that -i vowel.

38.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
38.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.
38.root: — (particle)

39.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
39.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

40.meaning: A past-tense verb 'he willed / he wished / he so desired'. It denotes an act of will or volition bringing something about.
40.grammar: Past-tense (perfect) verb, third person masculine singular ('he'). The bare stem with no suffix is the basic 'he did' form. Its subject and object are typically supplied by context.
40.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʾ) — to will, wish

41.meaning: '(it) extended / encompassed / was vast enough for' — to be wide, spacious, or ample; to take in or embrace something fully within one's capacity. It conveys all-embracing breadth.
41.grammar: A past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it encompassed'). The final -a marks the completed action of a single masculine subject ('he/it did encompass / extend over').
41.root: و-س-ع (w-s-ʿ) — to be wide, spacious, to encompass

42.meaning: 'His seat / His throne-footstool' — a kursī is a seat, chair, or footstool, signifying a place of authority, dominion, and majesty. With the pronoun it denotes that seat as belonging to Him.
42.grammar: A masculine singular noun with the attached possessive pronoun -hu ('his'). The -u ending is nominative, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence (the doer or the thing being described).
42.root: ك-ر-س (k-r-s) — seat, chair, foundation

43.meaning: The heavens / the skies — the plural of 'heaven', referring to the skies above and the celestial realms; the elevated expanse over the earth.
43.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun with the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the heavens') or follows a preposition. In the sound feminine plural, this -i form also covers what would be an object role.

44.meaning: 'and the earth' — the ground, land, or the planet earth; the world we stand upon, often paired with the heavens to mean all of creation.
44.grammar: A feminine noun, prefixed with 'and' and 'the.' The -a ending is accusative, the case typically marking the object of a verb (the thing acted upon) or a noun governed by certain particles.

45.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
45.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

46.meaning: 'it wearies/burdens Him' — to weigh down, tire, or overtax someone, the object being 'Him.' The verb conveys a load that strains or exhausts.
46.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it wearies'), with attached object pronoun -hu ('him'). The -u before the suffix is the indicative ending, marking a plain statement of fact ('it wearies / does burden').
46.root: ا-و-د (ʾ-w-d) — to weigh down, burden, weary

47.meaning: 'the safeguarding of them both / preserving the two of them' — the act of guarding, keeping, or maintaining, here directed at two things together. Ḥifẓ is careful preservation and protection.

parts.en: the two of them / both of them

47.grammar: A masculine verbal noun with the attached pronoun -humā ('the two of them' — a special dual form for exactly two). The -u ending is nominative, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence (here, the act of guarding, presented as the subject).

48.meaning: 'And He' — the connective 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'He' (a single masculine person or thing), often introducing a new clause about the same subject.
48.grammar: A connective particle plus an independent pronoun. The wa- prefix means 'and', joining clauses or words. 'Huwa' is the detached third-person masculine singular pronoun; it carries no case ending, its final -a being fixed.

49.meaning: 'the Most High / the Exalted' — lofty, elevated, supreme in rank and majesty above all else. As a divine name it affirms transcendence and highest dignity.
49.grammar: A definite adjective/noun in an intensive pattern ('the Most High'). The -u ending is nominative, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or for an appositive descriptive title attached to such a subject.
49.root: ع-ل-و (ʿ-l-w) — to be high, lofty, exalted

50.meaning: 'the Most Great / the Immense' — vast, mighty, and tremendous in greatness and grandeur. As a divine name it conveys overwhelming magnificence and majesty.
50.grammar: A definite adjective/noun in an intensive pattern ('the Magnificent'). The -u ending is nominative, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or for an appositive descriptive title attached to such a subject.
50.root: ع-ظ-م (ʿ-ẓ-m) — to be great, mighty, immense

1.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
1.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

2.meaning: 'compulsion / coercion' — forcing someone to act against their will; constraint or duress applied to make a person do something unwillingly.
2.grammar: A masculine verbal noun (Form IV, the 'making someone do' pattern). The -a ending is accusative; this bare accusative form is regularly used after the absolute-negation particle to mean 'there is no … whatsoever.'
2.root: ك-ر-ه (k-r-h) — to dislike, be averse; (Form IV) to compel

3.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
3.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

4.meaning: 'the religion / the way of life' — dīn denotes religion in the full sense: a system of belief, worship, obedience, and a complete way of living; it also carries the senses of judgement and requital, the order one is accountable to.
4.grammar: A definite masculine noun. The -i ending is genitive: this case typically follows a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun in a possessive-type relationship ('… of …').

5.meaning: A short particle placed before a verb to emphasize or affirm it. Before a past-tense verb it means 'indeed / certainly / has already (happened)'; before a present-tense verb it can mean 'sometimes / may'. It sharpens and confirms the verb that follows.
5.grammar: An indeclinable particle (its form never changes). It does not take case or tense endings; its job is to color the following verb — affirming and intensifying a past action ('has indeed done') or signaling occasional possibility with a present verb.

6.meaning: It has become clear, distinct, and plainly apparent; it has emerged into evidence so as to be unmistakably set apart from its opposite.
6.grammar: A Form V past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ("he/it became"). The ta- prefix with the doubled middle radical gives a reflexive/intensive sense: the thing makes itself manifest. The final -a is the past-tense ending for a single masculine subject.
6.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — distinctness, clarity, separation between things

7.meaning: Right guidance, sound sense, and maturity of judgment; the state of being on the correct, rightly-directed course as opposed to error.
7.grammar: A definite masculine noun. The -u ending is nominative, the case that typically marks the doer or subject of a sentence ("the rightly-guided way [is/does …]"). The al- prefix makes it definite ("the").
7.root: ر-ش-د (r-sh-d) — right guidance, integrity, sound direction

8.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
8.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

9.meaning: Error, going astray, deviation; the misguided wrong course, the loss of right direction that stands opposite to sound guidance.
9.grammar: A definite masculine noun. The -i ending is genitive, the case that typically follows a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun ("… OF …"). The al- prefix makes it definite ("the").
9.root: غ-و-ي (gh-w-y) — going astray, error, deviation from the right way

10.meaning: A compound meaning 'then whoever' or 'so whoever'. It combines 'then/so' with the conditional/relative 'who', introducing whatever person meets a stated condition.
10.grammar: The connector fa- ('then/so', often answering or following a condition) joined to man ('whoever / the one who'), which refers to people and introduces a condition: 'whoever does X…'. man does not change its ending; the clause after it supplies the rest of the meaning.

11.meaning: To disbelieve, to reject faith; to deny the truth and to be ungrateful, covering over and refusing what is true.
11.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it'). The final consonant carries no vowel (jussive form), an ending that typically appears after conditional or commanding particles and gives the sense 'whoever/if … disbelieves'.
11.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover over; to disbelieve, reject, be ungrateful

12.meaning: In/by the false object of worship — any idol, tyrant, or power set up and obeyed in defiance of Allah; that which is wrongfully exalted and served besides Him.
12.grammar: The prefix bi- ("in/by/with") governs the following noun, which therefore takes the genitive -i ending. The al- prefix makes the noun definite ("the"). The word itself is an intensive form denoting one who or that which greatly exceeds all bounds.
12.root: ط-غ-ي (ṭ-gh-y) — to exceed all bounds, to transgress, to tyrannize

13.meaning: And he believes — places trust and faith, holds something to be true and commits to it with inner assent and security of heart.
13.grammar: A Form IV present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ("he believes"). The yu- prefix marks a single masculine subject; Form IV here carries the sense of granting faith/security. The final consonant takes a sukūn (no vowel), marking the jussive mood — the clipped form used when the verb is conditioned or governed (rather than the plain indicative, which would end in -u). The wa- prefix means "and."

14.meaning: A phrase 'in Allah / by Allah', combining the preposition 'with/in/by' and the divine name Allah, the proper name of the One God.
14.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') prefixed to the divine name Allah. A preposition always forces the following noun into the genitive case, which is why Allah here ends in -i. With verbs of believing, bi- conveys the object of faith — to believe IN.
14.root: — (Allah is the proper name of God and is not derived from a triliteral root in the usual sense)

15.meaning: 'Then/so, indeed …' — the connector 'then/so' joined to the particle 'qad', which before a past-tense verb stresses that the action has certainly and already happened.
15.grammar: A connecting particle 'fa-' ('then/so', often signalling a result) plus 'qad'. With a following perfect verb, 'qad' emphasises that the act is real and completed ('have indeed …'). The final -i on 'qad' is a helping vowel added to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a cluster; it carries no grammatical meaning of its own.

16.meaning: He took firm hold; he gripped and clung tightly, holding fast and refusing to let go.
16.grammar: A Form X past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ("he held fast"). The ista- pattern often adds an intensive or sought-after sense — here, a deliberate, firm seizing. The final -a is the past-tense ending for a single masculine subject.
16.root: م-س-ك (m-s-k) — to hold, grasp, retain, grip

17.meaning: By/with the handhold — the firm grip, the secure handle or loop that one seizes to keep from falling.
17.grammar: The prefix bi- ("by/with") governs the following noun, which therefore takes the genitive -i ending. The al- prefix makes the noun definite ("the"). It is a feminine singular noun.
17.root: ع-ر-و (ʿ-r-w) — to cling to, a handhold, a loop or bond one grasps

18.meaning: The most firm, the most trustworthy and secure; that which is strongest in its reliability and least likely to give way.
18.grammar: A definite feminine superlative adjective ("the most firm"). The fixed -ā ending belongs to this feminine superlative pattern and does not change for case. The al- prefix makes it definite and agrees with a feminine noun.
18.root: و-ث-ق (w-th-q) — firmness, reliability, a binding trust or covenant

19.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
19.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

20.meaning: A snapping apart, a breaking off, a severance; the act of being torn asunder or cleaved in two.
20.grammar: A Form VII verbal noun (the noun of the action "to be snapped apart"). The Form VII pattern (with the in- element) carries a passive/intransitive sense — the thing breaks of itself. The -a ending is accusative, the case commonly used for the object of a verb or, as here, the noun governed by a negating particle.
20.root: ف-ص-م (f-ṣ-m) — to snap, crack, or break apart without fully separating

21.meaning: 'For it / to it, belonging to it' — the preposition 'for/to' joined to a pronoun referring to a feminine singular thing; it expresses possession or benefit ('it has / it gets').
21.grammar: Preposition 'li-' (here vowelled 'la-' before a pronoun) plus an attached object pronoun. The -hā suffix means 'it/her,' a feminine singular. Pronouns that follow a preposition are in the genitive (object-of-preposition) role; -hā is a fixed form and does not change shape.

22.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
22.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
