22.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

23.meaning: All-Hearing / ever-hearing — one who hears completely and perfectly, missing nothing of what is uttered or whispered; an intensive form stressing the fullness of the quality. The '-un' nunation marks it as indefinite nominative.
23.grammar: An intensive adjective (faʿīl pattern) conveying a constant, perfect quality. The '-un' (nunation on the ḍamma) marks it as indefinite and in the nominative case, typically used for a subject or predicate ("is all-hearing").

24.meaning: An intensive adjective/name meaning 'All-Knowing / fully aware' — one whose knowledge is complete, deep, and all-encompassing; as a divine attribute it denotes Allah's perfect knowledge.
24.grammar: An intensive adjective (the pattern faʿīl conveys 'thoroughly, abundantly'). The ending -un is the indefinite nominative — the nominative case marks it as the subject or the quality being affirmed, and the -n (nunation) signals 'a / an', i.e. indefinite. So it reads '(is) all-knowing'.
24.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — knowledge, knowing

1.meaning: Allah — the proper name of the One God, the sole and absolute Deity worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a name, not a common noun, and refers to the Creator and Sustainer of all that exists.
1.grammar: The proper divine name. The final -u ending is nominative, the case typically marking the subject (the doer) of a sentence or the noun being identified.

2.meaning: A protector, guardian, ally, and intimate helper; one who is close and takes charge of another's affairs, supporting and safeguarding them.
2.grammar: A masculine singular noun. The -u ending is nominative, the case that typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that is being described ("… is the protector"). The pattern denotes one who possesses the quality intensely.
2.root: و-ل-ي (w-l-y) — nearness, alliance, guardianship, taking charge of another

3.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
3.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

4.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
4.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

5.meaning: He brings them out, leads them forth, draws them from one state or place into another.
5.grammar: A Form IV present-tense verb ("he brings out") with an attached object pronoun. The yu- prefix marks a single masculine subject acting now or habitually; Form IV makes it causative ("to cause to go out"). The suffix -hum means "them" (a group of males), the object of the action.
5.root: خ-ر-ج (kh-r-j) — to go out, exit, emerge; causatively, to bring/take out

6.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
6.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

7.meaning: Darknesses, layers of gloom; the manifold states of being deprived of light, whether literal or as a figure for ignorance and error.
7.grammar: A definite sound feminine plural noun ("the darknesses"). The -i ending here is genitive — the case taken by this plural after a preposition (the -āt plural shows genitive with -i rather than the -a it would take in the accusative). The al- prefix makes it definite ("the").
7.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — darkness; also wrongdoing and injustice

8.meaning: 'To / toward / up to' — a preposition marking the endpoint, goal, or limit of an action or motion: the direction something moves toward or the boundary at which it stops.
8.grammar: An invariable preposition. It has no case ending of its own but puts the noun that follows it into the genitive ('of / to' state). It indicates direction toward, or the terminal limit of, something.

9.meaning: Light — radiance and illumination that dispels darkness; often a figure for guidance, truth, and clarity.
9.grammar: A definite masculine noun. The -i ending is genitive, the case that typically follows a preposition or links to a preceding noun ("… OF …"). The al- prefix makes it definite ("the").

10.meaning: 'And those who': a connective phrase introducing a specified group of people (masculine plural) about whom something will be said. It links them to what came before.
10.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'), which is masculine plural. A relative pronoun stands for a group and is normally followed by a clause describing them. Its form does not change for case; it stays alladhīna whatever its grammatical role.

11.meaning: 'They disbelieved / rejected faith' — from a root meaning to cover over or conceal. To disbelieve in this sense is to cover up and refuse the truth, and also to be ungrateful, hiding or denying favours received.
11.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
11.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

12.meaning: Their protectors, guardians, and allies — those close ones who take charge of and support them.
12.grammar: The broken (irregular) plural of "protector/ally" with an attached possessive pronoun. The stem ends in a hamza that itself carries the nominative -u vowel (awliyāʾu), the case typically marking the subject or the word being described ("their protectors [are] …"); the case vowel is not a separable suffix but is borne by the noun's final letter. The suffix -hum means "their," referring to a group of males; its vowel appears as -u (-humu) for ease of pronunciation before what follows.
12.root: و-ل-ي (w-l-y) — nearness, alliance, guardianship, taking charge of another

13.meaning: The false object of worship — any idol, tyrant, or power wrongfully exalted and obeyed besides Allah; that which transgresses all bounds.
13.grammar: A definite noun. The -u ending is nominative, the case that typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word being described ("… is the false deity"). The al- prefix makes it definite ("the"). The word is an intensive form denoting that which exceeds all bounds.
13.root: ط-غ-ي (ṭ-gh-y) — to exceed all bounds, to transgress, to tyrannize

14.meaning: They bring them out, lead them forth, draw them from one state or place into another.
14.grammar: A Form IV present-tense verb (causative "to bring out") for a plural masculine subject, with an attached object pronoun. The -ūna ending means "they" (a group of males) acting now or habitually. The suffix -hum means "them" (a group of males), the object of the action.
14.root: خ-ر-ج (kh-r-j) — to go out, exit, emerge; causatively, to bring/take out

15.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
15.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

16.meaning: Light — radiance and illumination that dispels darkness; often a figure for guidance, truth, and clarity.
16.grammar: A definite masculine noun. The -i ending is genitive, the case that typically follows a preposition or links to a preceding noun ("… OF …"). The al- prefix makes it definite ("the").

17.meaning: 'To / toward / up to' — a preposition marking the endpoint, goal, or limit of an action or motion: the direction something moves toward or the boundary at which it stops.
17.grammar: An invariable preposition. It has no case ending of its own but puts the noun that follows it into the genitive ('of / to' state). It indicates direction toward, or the terminal limit of, something.

18.meaning: Darknesses, layers of gloom; the manifold states of being deprived of light, whether literal or as a figure for ignorance and error.
18.grammar: A definite sound feminine plural noun ("the darknesses"). The -i ending here is genitive — the case taken by this plural after a preposition (the -āt plural shows genitive with -i rather than the -a it would take in the accusative). The al- prefix makes it definite ("the").
18.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — darkness; also wrongdoing and injustice

19.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'those' — pointing to people or things that are distant or already known. It singles out a group ('those ones', 'it is those who').
19.grammar: A plural demonstrative pronoun, 'those'. It is fixed in form (no case endings). The -ka element signals distance/remoteness, pointing to something far off or notable. It can refer to people of either gender.

20.meaning: 'Companions / people of, dwellers, owners' — those closely associated with something, its inseparable folk, fellows, or inmates; literally the people who 'keep company with' a thing.
20.grammar: A masculine plural noun (the plural of ṣāḥib, 'companion'). The '-u' ending is nominative, typically marking the subject of a sentence; it appears here without nunation because the word is in a possessive construction ('companions OF …') with a following noun.

21.meaning: 'The Fire' — fire, flame; in religious usage often the Fire of Hell, the blazing punishment of the Hereafter.
21.grammar: The definite article 'al-' ('the') plus the feminine noun 'nār' ('fire'). The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'n' (so it is pronounced 'an-nār'). The '-i' ending is genitive, the case used after a preposition or to link the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the Fire').

22.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (referring to a group of males, or a mixed group). Because it stands on its own rather than being attached to a verb or noun, it often adds emphasis, singling out or stressing the subject ('they themselves', 'it is they who').
22.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It does not take case endings; the fixed -m simply marks the plural 'they'. Standing alone, it commonly serves to emphasise or isolate the subject.

23.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
23.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.

24.meaning: 'Ones abiding forever / dwelling eternally' — those who remain permanently and without end in a place or state.
24.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer' noun) in the masculine plural, meaning 'those who abide forever.' The '-ūna' ending marks a masculine plural in the nominative case, the form typically used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate describing 'they.'
24.root: خ-ل-د (kh-l-d) — perpetuity, eternity, abiding

1.meaning: 'Did not…?' — a particle combining a question with negation, used to ask 'Have I/has he not…?', often expecting agreement or serving as a gentle reminder.
1.grammar: An interrogative prefix 'a-' ('?') joined to the negation 'lam'. 'lam' negates a verb and places it firmly in the past ('did not'), and grammatically puts the following present-tense verb into the jussive (clipped) form. Together they form a rhetorical or confirming question.

2.meaning: You see, perceive, or take notice; to observe with the eye, or by extension to come to know or consider. Often used to draw attention, as in 'have you considered…?'
2.grammar: A present-tense verb addressed to a single male 'you,' marked by the 'ta-' prefix. The root's weak final letter has dropped, leaving the short final -a; this shortened form is the jussive/apocopated form, which appears after certain particles (such as 'did not' or in questions like 'have you not seen?').
2.root: ر-أ-ي (r-ʾ-y) — to see, perceive, consider, form an opinion

3.meaning: 'To / toward / up to' — a preposition marking the endpoint, goal, or limit of an action or motion: the direction something moves toward or the boundary at which it stops.
3.grammar: An invariable preposition. It has no case ending of its own but puts the noun that follows it into the genitive ('of / to' state). It indicates direction toward, or the terminal limit of, something.

4.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
4.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

5.meaning: He disputed, argued, and contended; he pressed a case back and forth against another, each trying to overcome the other with arguments.
5.grammar: A Form III past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ("he argued"). The Form III pattern (with the lengthened first vowel) conveys a mutual, back-and-forth action done toward another — here, contending in argument. The final -a is the past-tense ending for a single masculine subject.
5.root: ح-ج-ج (ḥ-j-j) — to argue, present a proof, dispute with evidence

6.meaning: Ibrahim (Abraham), the proper name of the patriarch and prophet.
6.grammar: A proper name of non-Arabic origin. Because such foreign names are 'diptotes,' they take a single -a ending for both the object (accusative) and possessive/after-preposition (genitive) roles, and they do not take the usual -n (nunation). The -a here shows it is functioning as an object or after a preposition.

7.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
7.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

8.meaning: His Lord, Master, and Sustainer — the One who owns, nurtures, governs, and brings to completion; expressing both ownership and loving care over the one belonging to Him.
8.grammar: A masculine noun with an attached possessive pronoun ("his Lord"). The -i vowel on the noun is genitive, here drawn out because of the following possessive suffix -hi ("his"). The suffix -hi means "his," and its i-form follows naturally after an i-vowel.
8.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship, ownership, nurturing and sustaining to completion

9.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
9.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

10.meaning: He gave him, granted and bestowed upon him; he brought something to him and handed it over.
10.grammar: A Form IV past-tense verb (causative "to give/bring to"), third-person masculine singular, with an attached object pronoun. The verb ends in a long -ā belonging to this weak-final root. The suffix -hu means "him," the recipient of the action.
10.root: أ-ت-ي ('-t-y) — to come; causatively (Form IV), to bring or give

11.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
11.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

12.meaning: 'The kingship / sovereignty / dominion' — royal authority and the power to rule and dispose of a realm; the office and possession of a king.
12.grammar: A masculine noun with the definite article 'al-' ('the'). The final '-a' is the accusative ending, which commonly marks the direct object of a verb — the thing given, granted, or acted upon.

13.meaning: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the time that', used to point back to a past moment or event and introduce a recollection of something that occurred.
13.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). It signals a point in past time, typically introducing a clause that recalls 'the time when' something happened.

14.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
14.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

15.meaning: Ibrāhīm (Abraham), the proper name of the patriarch and prophet, revered as a model of pure devotion to Allah.
15.grammar: A proper name (of non-Arabic origin). The final -u ending is nominative, the case used for the subject or the one doing/being something in a sentence. Being a foreign name, it does not take nunation (no '-un').

16.meaning: My Lord, Master, and Sustainer — the One who owns, nurtures, and governs me; expressing ownership together with intimate care.
16.grammar: A masculine noun with the attached first-person possessive ("my"). The suffix -iya means "my" and, being a possessive ending, fixes the noun's relationship rather than leaving it to a case vowel. It denotes that the Lord is being claimed as one's own.
16.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship, ownership, nurturing and sustaining to completion

17.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
17.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

18.meaning: He gives life, makes alive, revives; He brings the dead or lifeless into a living state.
18.grammar: A Form IV present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ("he gives life"), causative in sense ("to cause to live"). The yu- prefix marks a single masculine subject acting now or habitually. The long -ī is the natural final vowel of this weak-ending root.
18.root: ح-ي-ي (ḥ-y-y) — life, living; causatively, to give life

19.meaning: And He causes death, brings to an end, takes the soul; He makes the living to die.
19.grammar: A Form IV present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ("he causes to die"), causative in sense. The yu- prefix marks a single masculine subject acting now or habitually. The -u ending marks the plain (indicative) present tense, the form used for a simple statement of fact. The wa- prefix means "and."
19.root: م-و-ت (m-w-t) — death; causatively, to cause to die

20.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
20.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

21.meaning: I — the standalone pronoun used to declare or emphasize the speaker himself as the one in view.
21.grammar: A detached first-person singular pronoun ("I"). Being an independent pronoun, it has a fixed form with no case ending; it is used to state or stress who the subject is.

22.meaning: I give life / I bring to life — a first-person verb expressing the act of animating, making something living, or reviving it. It conveys bestowing life upon what was lifeless.
22.grammar: A present/future tense verb. The u- prefix marks the first-person singular doer ('I'). The root has two identical final letters (a doubled/weak-ending root, not a hollow one), and in this form the verb is causative — 'cause to live, give life'. The form indicates an action happening now or about to happen.

23.meaning: and I cause to die / and I bring about death — a first-person verb for putting an end to life, the deliberate act of causing death.
23.grammar: The wa- prefix means 'and', joining this to what precedes. The u- prefix marks the first-person singular doer ('I'). The verb is causative — to make something die. The final -u ending marks the indicative mood, the plain statement form of a present/future verb.

24.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
24.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.
24.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — saying, speech, uttering

25.meaning: Ibrāhīm (Abraham), the proper name of the patriarch and prophet, revered as a model of pure devotion to Allah.
25.grammar: A proper name (of non-Arabic origin). The final -u ending is nominative, the case used for the subject or the one doing/being something in a sentence. Being a foreign name, it does not take nunation (no '-un').

26.meaning: A two-part connector meaning 'so/then, indeed…'. It joins fa- ('so', 'then', marking a result or consequence) to inna, an emphatic particle that strongly affirms the statement that follows ('truly', 'verily').
26.grammar: fa- is a connective prefix signaling that what follows is a consequence or next step. inna is an emphatic particle that introduces a nominal sentence, puts its following noun in the accusative, and strengthens the assertion; it does not itself take a case ending.

27.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
27.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.
27.root: — (proper name)

28.meaning: he brings / he comes with — a third-person verb meaning to bring something forward or cause it to come, often by fetching or producing it.
28.grammar: A present/future tense verb. The ya- prefix marks a third-person singular masculine doer ('he/it'). Built on a weak root ending in a long vowel, it carries the sense of bringing or coming forth. The form expresses an ongoing or habitual action.

29.meaning: with the sun / by the sun — the sun as the daytime celestial body, here governed by a preposition meaning 'with' or 'by means of'.
29.grammar: The bi- prefix is a preposition meaning 'with', 'by', or 'by means of'. The l- prefix is the definite article 'the'. The final -i ending is genitive, which is required after the preposition bi-, linking the sun as the object of 'with/by'.
29.root: ش-م-س (sh-m-s) — sun

30.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
30.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

31.meaning: The east — the place of sunrise, the direction from which the sun comes up.
31.grammar: A noun of place on the mafʿil pattern (a mīm-prefixed noun naming where an action happens — here where the sun rises). The final -i is the genitive case, taken after a preposition or as the second term of a possessive (iḍāfa) construction ('the direction OF the east').
31.root: ش-ر-ق (sh-r-q) — rising (of the sun), shining, the east

32.meaning: so bring! / then come with! — a command addressed to one person, telling them to bring something forward or produce it.
32.grammar: The fa- prefix means 'so' or 'then', signalling a consequence or sequence. The rest is a command (imperative) directed at a single masculine listener: 'you, bring!' The clipped ending (no long final vowel) is typical of a command from this weak-rooted verb.

33.meaning: with it / by it — a preposition meaning 'with' or 'by means of' joined to a pronoun referring to a single feminine (or grammatically feminine) thing.
33.grammar: The bi- prefix is a preposition meaning 'with', 'by', or 'by means of'. The attached -hā is an object pronoun meaning 'it' or 'her', referring to something feminine in gender. Together they mean 'with it' or 'by means of it'.

34.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
34.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

35.meaning: the west — the direction of sunset; the place or quarter where the sun goes down.
35.grammar: The l- prefix is the definite article 'the'. The noun follows a pattern denoting a place — literally the location of the sun's setting. The final -i ending is genitive; the noun takes this case because it is governed by a preceding preposition (a separate word meaning 'from'), which puts whatever follows it into the genitive.
35.root: غ-ر-ب (gh-r-b) — to set (of the sun), the west

36.meaning: so he was struck dumb / then he was dumbfounded — a passive verb describing someone left utterly speechless and confounded, unable to reply.
36.grammar: The fa- prefix means 'so' or 'then', marking a result. The verb is past tense and passive (something was done to the subject, not by him): he was bewildered and silenced. The vowel pattern (u–i) is the mark of the passive, and the final -a marks third-person singular masculine.
36.root: ب-ه-ت (b-h-t) — to be dumbfounded, struck speechless

37.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
37.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

38.meaning: He disbelieved / rejected — to refuse faith, deny the truth, and turn away ungratefully from Allah. The root also carries the sense of covering over or being ungrateful for a blessing.
38.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third-person masculine singular ('he disbelieved'). The final -a ending marks completed past action done by a single male. The verb denotes rejecting faith and being ungrateful, covering over the truth.
38.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover over, reject faith, be ungrateful

39.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
39.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
39.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

40.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
40.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

41.meaning: 'He guides / leads on the right way' — to show someone the correct path, direct them rightly, or lead them to a goal, whether literally or in matters of belief and conduct.
41.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular: the ya- prefix means 'he'. The verb ends in a long -ī (a weak final letter); in this indicative form the long vowel stands in place of the usual -u mood marker, still conveying a plain, ongoing statement ('he guides').
41.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — guidance, showing the way, leading rightly

42.meaning: the people / the folk — a body of people, a community or group regarded collectively (here in the accusative form).
42.grammar: The l- prefix is the definite article 'the'. The final -a ending is accusative. Since the verb it follows is passive (and so takes no direct object), this accusative is adverbial — marking the circumstance or setting of the action ('before / in front of the people') rather than a thing being acted upon.
42.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, to arise; a people standing together

43.meaning: The wrongdoers — those who do wrong or injustice; literally those who put things out of their rightful place, transgressing limits and harming themselves or others. The root sense is darkness.
43.grammar: 'al-' is 'the' (its 'l' assimilates into the 'ẓ', doubling it). The stem is an active participle ('one who wrongs') made plural for masculine people. The -īna ending is the object/genitive form of the sound masculine plural, marking the word as an object of a verb or governed by a preposition.

1.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
1.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

2.meaning: like the one who / as the one who — a comparison particle joined to a relative pronoun, introducing a single masculine person being likened to something: 'like him who…'.
2.grammar: The ka- prefix is a particle of comparison meaning 'like' or 'as'. Attached to it is the relative pronoun 'the one who / which', which is masculine singular and introduces a following descriptive clause.

3.meaning: he passed / he passed by — a third-person past verb meaning to go past, to pass through or by a place or thing.
3.grammar: A past tense verb with a third-person singular masculine doer ('he'). The doubled final consonant reflects the root's repeated letter. The final -a marks the third-person singular masculine subject. It states a completed action: 'he passed'.
3.root: م-ر-ر (m-r-r) — to pass, to pass by

4.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
4.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

5.meaning: a town / a settlement — an inhabited place such as a village or city; a gathering of dwellings.
5.grammar: A singular feminine noun. The final -in ending carries two signals at once: the genitive case (used after prepositions or to link to a preceding word, '… of …') and the indefinite 'a/an' (no definite article), conveying 'a town'.
5.root: ق-ر-ي (q-r-y) — to gather; a settled place

6.meaning: and it / and she — the conjunction 'and' joined to a standalone subject pronoun meaning 'it' or 'she', pointing to something feminine in gender.
6.grammar: The wa- prefix means 'and'. The word hiya is an independent subject pronoun for a single feminine (or grammatically feminine) entity, 'it/she'. As a standalone pronoun it typically begins a descriptive statement about that thing.

7.meaning: fallen down / collapsed / lying in ruins — a descriptive word for something caved in, empty and tumbled-down, fallen upon itself.

parts.en: fallen in ruins / empty and collapsed

7.grammar: An active descriptive noun (participle), feminine in form, describing a feminine thing as 'collapsed' or 'in ruins'. The final -un ending marks the nominative case (the subject or predicate role) together with the indefinite 'a/an', so it reads as a description: '(is) fallen in ruins'.
7.root: خ-و-ي (kh-w-y) — to be empty, to collapse, to lie in ruins

8.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
8.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

9.meaning: its roofs — the roofs or overhead structures of a thing, joined to a pronoun showing they belong to it (something feminine).
9.grammar: A plural noun ('roofs') with an attached possessive pronoun -hā ('its/her'), referring to a feminine owner. The -i vowel before the pronoun is genitive, the case used after prepositions or to show possession ('the roofs of it').
9.root: ع-ر-ش (ʿ-r-sh) — to roof over, build a structure; throne, canopy

10.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
10.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

11.meaning: A particle/adverb meaning 'in whatever manner,' 'from wherever,' or 'whenever' — it asks or denotes the how, where, or when of an action in an open-ended way.
11.grammar: An invariable interrogative/conditional adverb; it has no case ending and never changes form. It introduces the manner, place, or time of an action in a general, open sense ('in what way / from where / when').

12.meaning: He gives life, makes alive, revives; He brings the dead or lifeless into a living state.
12.grammar: A Form IV present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ("he gives life"), causative in sense ("to cause to live"). The yu- prefix marks a single masculine subject acting now or habitually. The long -ī is the natural final vowel of this weak-ending root.
12.root: ح-ي-ي (ḥ-y-y) — life, living; causatively, to give life

13.meaning: This (feminine) — a pointing word ('this one here') used for a single nearby thing that is grammatically feminine.
13.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun ('this') for a single feminine thing close at hand. It is fixed in form and does not change for case; it commonly precedes the noun it points to.

14.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
14.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

15.meaning: After; following in time or order — the point or moment subsequent to something.
15.grammar: An adverb of time functioning much like a preposition ('after'). It is fixed in the accusative form ending in -a, and is normally followed by a noun in the 'of' relationship, giving 'after (the) …'.
15.root: ب-ع-د (b-ʿ-d) — afterness, that which comes later; distance/remoteness

16.meaning: Its death, its lifelessness or dormancy; the state of being dead, joined to a possessor.
16.grammar: A noun ('death') with an attached third-person feminine singular possessive pronoun ('its / her'). The -i vowel on the noun is genitive, the case taken before a possessor pronoun and after prepositions ('death of it').

17.meaning: so he caused him to die / then He made him die — a past causative verb with the doer acting upon a single male object: bringing about his death.
17.grammar: The fa- prefix means 'so' or 'then'. The verb is past tense and causative — 'to make/cause to die'. Its -a ending marks a third-person singular masculine doer ('he'). The attached -hu is an object pronoun meaning 'him', the one made to die.

18.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
18.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
18.root: — (proper divine name)

19.meaning: a hundred — the number one hundred (in the accusative form).
19.grammar: A noun naming the number 'hundred'. The final -a ending is accusative, the case often used for the object of a verb or for a span of measure (such as a counted duration). A counted noun typically follows it in the singular genitive.

20.meaning: a year — a full year, a complete cycle of time; sometimes carrying the sense of a year of plenty or season.
20.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The final -in ending shows the genitive case together with the indefinite 'a/an'. The genitive here is typical of a noun being counted after a number ('a hundred of year') or linked to a preceding word.
20.root: ع-و-م (ʿ-w-m) — a year, an annual cycle

21.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
21.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

22.meaning: then He raised him up / then He resurrected him — a past verb of sending forth or raising, here with the doer raising a single male object back to life or rousing him.
22.grammar: A past tense verb meaning to raise up, rouse, or send forth. Its -a ending marks a third-person singular masculine doer ('he'). The attached -hu is an object pronoun meaning 'him', the one raised or sent.
22.root: ب-ع-ث (b-ʿ-th) — to raise up, send forth, resurrect

23.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
23.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

24.meaning: How many / how much — a particle expressing a large or questioned quantity. It can ask "how many?" or exclaim "how many a…!" to stress abundance.
24.grammar: A quantity word used either to ask about a number ("how many?") or to declare a great number ("how many a…!"). It has no case ending; the noun it counts normally follows it in the singular.

25.meaning: you stayed / you remained / you tarried — a past verb addressed to one person, meaning to remain, linger, or abide for a span of time.
25.grammar: A past tense verb meaning to stay or linger. The suffix -ta marks the doer as second-person singular masculine ('you'), so it states 'you remained' — a completed staying in the past.

26.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
26.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

27.meaning: I stayed / I remained / I tarried — a past verb meaning to remain or abide for a period, with the speaker as the one who stayed.
27.grammar: A past tense verb meaning to stay or linger. The suffix -tu marks the doer as first-person singular ('I'), stating 'I remained' — a completed staying in the past.
27.root: ل-ب-ث (l-b-th) — to stay, remain, tarry

28.meaning: A day; a defined stretch of time. Often used for a momentous appointed day such as a day of judgement or reckoning.
28.grammar: A singular masculine noun, indefinite ('a day'). The -an ending (tanwīn fatḥa) is the indefinite accusative case, which typically marks the object of a verb or a noun otherwise governed in the accusative.

29.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
29.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

30.meaning: a part of / some of / a portion of — a noun denoting a piece or fraction of a larger whole (in the accusative form).
30.grammar: A noun meaning 'part' or 'some'. The final -a ending is accusative, marking it as a direct object or, with a measure of time, an adverbial span. It is normally followed by a noun in the genitive ('part of …').
30.root: ب-ع-ض (b-ʿ-ḍ) — a part, a portion, some

31.meaning: a day — a day, the basic unit of daytime or a twenty-four-hour span; figuratively a time or occasion.
31.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The final -in ending marks the genitive case together with the indefinite 'a/an'. The genitive is the case used after prepositions or to link this noun to a preceding word ('… of a day').
31.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — a day, a span of time

32.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
32.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

33.meaning: A particle of retraction meaning 'rather,' 'no, but,' or 'nay' — it cancels or sets aside what was just said and shifts to a corrected or contrasting statement that follows.
33.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it never changes form). Its function is to redirect the discourse: it dismisses a prior idea and introduces what is actually the case.

34.meaning: you stayed / you remained / you tarried — a past verb addressed to one person, meaning to remain, linger, or abide for a span of time.
34.grammar: A past tense verb meaning to stay or linger. The suffix -ta marks the doer as second-person singular masculine ('you'), so it states 'you remained' — a completed staying in the past.
34.root: ل-ب-ث (l-b-th) — to stay, remain, tarry

35.meaning: a hundred — the number one hundred (in the accusative form).
35.grammar: A noun naming the number 'hundred'. The final -a ending is accusative, the case often used for the object of a verb or for a span of measure (such as a counted duration). A counted noun typically follows it in the singular genitive.

36.meaning: a year — a full year, a complete cycle of time; sometimes carrying the sense of a year of plenty or season.
36.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The final -in ending shows the genitive case together with the indefinite 'a/an'. The genitive here is typical of a noun being counted after a number ('a hundred of year') or linked to a preceding word.
36.root: ع-و-م (ʿ-w-m) — a year, an annual cycle

37.meaning: An imperative meaning 'look!', 'observe!', or 'consider!', addressed to a single male. The attached 'fa-' prefix adds the sense 'so', 'then', or 'and so', linking the command to what precedes it as a consequence or next step.
37.grammar: A command (imperative) directed at one male person ('you'). The verb carries no subject suffix because the 'you (masc. sing.)' is built into the imperative form itself. The 'fa-' is a connecting particle expressing sequence or consequence ('so', 'then').
37.root: ن-ظ-ر (n-ẓ-r) — to look, see, observe, consider

38.meaning: A preposition meaning 'to,' 'toward,' or 'up to' — pointing to the end-point, goal, or limit of a motion, direction, or extent.
38.grammar: A preposition (a small linking word). It governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the genitive case, and points to a destination or limit ('to,' 'toward,' 'as far as').

39.meaning: 'Food', meaning that which is eaten; nourishment or a meal, with the attached pronoun marking it as belonging to a single male ('your food').
39.grammar: A noun joined to the possessive pronoun '-ka' ('your', addressed to one male). The '-i' vowel before the pronoun is the genitive ending, which regularly appears when a noun is possessed by a following attached pronoun or governed by a preposition.

40.meaning: 'And your drink' — 'drink' meaning a beverage or that which is drunk, joined by 'and' and marked as belonging to a single male.
40.grammar: The connecting particle 'wa' ('and') plus a noun joined to the possessive '-ka' ('your', one male). The '-i' before the pronoun is the genitive ending, typical of a noun possessed by a following pronoun.
40.root: ش-ر-ب (sh-r-b) — to drink; a drink, beverage

41.meaning: A negating particle, 'not', used specifically to deny that an action happened in the past, even though it attaches to a present-tense verb form. It turns 'you do X' into 'you did not do X'.

parts.en: did not (negation of a completed act)

41.grammar: An indeclinable particle that governs the verb after it, putting that verb into the jussive (clipped) mood and giving it past-time meaning. In short: lam + a present-form verb = 'did not [verb]'.

42.meaning: A verb meaning 'to change for the worse with the passage of years', 'to go stale', or 'to spoil over time' — the alteration that long ageing brings to something.
42.grammar: A present-tense verb with the 'ya-' prefix marking a third-person masculine singular subject ('it' / 'he'). The verb form (with doubled middle and the pattern of reflexive/intensive verbs) conveys something happening to the subject itself — undergoing change. Its vowel-less ending (jussive/apocopate form) is the shape the verb takes after certain particles, such as a negative or conditional word.
42.root: س-ن-ه / س-ن-و (s-n-h / s-n-w) — year; the passage of years, ageing

43.meaning: An imperative meaning 'look!', 'observe!', or 'consider!', addressed to a single male, with the attached 'wa-' meaning 'and'.
43.grammar: A command (imperative) to one male person ('you'), with the 'you (masc. sing.)' built into the form so no subject suffix is needed. 'wa-' is the connecting particle 'and'.
43.root: ن-ظ-ر (n-ẓ-r) — to look, see, observe, consider

44.meaning: A preposition meaning 'to,' 'toward,' or 'up to' — pointing to the end-point, goal, or limit of a motion, direction, or extent.
44.grammar: A preposition (a small linking word). It governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the genitive case, and points to a destination or limit ('to,' 'toward,' 'as far as').

45.meaning: 'Donkey' — the animal, an ass, used as a beast of burden or for riding; here marked as belonging to a single male ('your donkey').
45.grammar: A noun joined to the possessive pronoun '-ka' ('your', addressed to one male). The '-i' vowel before the pronoun is the genitive ending, regular for a noun possessed by a following attached pronoun.

46.meaning: 'And so that We may make / appoint you' — the verb 'to make, render, or appoint (something into something)', with 'We' as subject and 'you' (one male) as object, framed by 'and' and a purpose particle expressing 'so that' or 'in order to'.
46.grammar: A present-tense verb with the 'na-' prefix marking the subject 'we', and the object pronoun '-ka' ('you', one male) attached at the end. The 'li-' is a purpose particle ('so that', 'in order to'), and following it the verb takes the '-a' (subjunctive) ending, which marks an intended or hoped-for action rather than a plain statement of fact. 'wa' is 'and'.
46.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, render, place, appoint

47.meaning: 'A sign' — a token, mark, or proof that points to something beyond itself; a miraculous indication, a lesson, or an evidence. (The same word also denotes a verse of the Qur'an.)
47.grammar: An indefinite noun. The '-an' ending (accusative with 'tanwīn', the doubled final 'n' of indefiniteness) typically marks the noun as the direct object of a verb, or as the thing one is being made or named, and signals 'a / an' rather than 'the'.

48.meaning: For the people, for mankind, for humankind. The preposition 'for/to' joined to 'the people' as a collective term for human beings.
48.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('for/to') prefixed to the noun 'al-nās' ('the people'). The article 'al-' loses its 'a' sound after 'li-' and its 'l' assimilates into the noun's initial n (hence the doubled 'nn'). The -i ending is genitive, the case required after a preposition.

49.meaning: An imperative meaning 'look!', 'observe!', or 'consider!', addressed to a single male, with the attached 'wa-' meaning 'and'.
49.grammar: A command (imperative) to one male person ('you'), with the 'you (masc. sing.)' built into the form so no subject suffix is needed. 'wa-' is the connecting particle 'and'.
49.root: ن-ظ-ر (n-ẓ-r) — to look, see, observe, consider

50.meaning: 'To / toward / up to' — a preposition marking the endpoint, goal, or limit of an action or motion: the direction something moves toward or the boundary at which it stops.
50.grammar: An invariable preposition. It has no case ending of its own but puts the noun that follows it into the genitive ('of / to' state). It indicates direction toward, or the terminal limit of, something.

51.meaning: 'The bones' — the hard skeletal framework of the body; the plural of 'bone'.
51.grammar: A definite plural noun with the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The '-i' ending is genitive, the case that regularly appears after a preposition or when the noun is linked to a preceding noun in a possessive ('… of …') relationship.

52.meaning: An interrogative meaning 'how?' — asking about the manner, condition, or state of something ('how?', 'in what way?'). It can also express astonishment.
52.grammar: An interrogative particle (kayfa) ending in an invariable -a; it does not change for case. It asks about the manner or state of an action ('how…?') and is sometimes used rhetorically to express wonder or rebuke rather than a genuine question.

53.meaning: A verb meaning 'We raise them up', 'We set them up', or 'We knit / assemble them together' — lifting and joining the pieces back into place, with 'We' as subject and 'them' (feminine plural) as object.
53.grammar: A present-tense verb with the 'nu-' prefix marking the subject 'we' (the 'u' vowel reflects a causative verb pattern — to cause something to rise). The object pronoun '-hā' ('them', feminine, as for a group of feminine or non-human plural things) is attached at the end. The '-u' on the verb stem is the indicative ending, marking a plain factual statement.
53.root: ن-ش-ز (n-sh-z) — to rise, be raised up, elevated

54.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
54.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

55.meaning: A verb meaning 'We clothe them' or 'We cover / overlay them' — dressing or wrapping something as with a garment, with 'We' as subject and 'them' (feminine plural) as object.
55.grammar: A present-tense verb with the 'na-' prefix marking the subject 'we', and the object pronoun '-hā' ('them', feminine plural) attached at the end. The verb is built on a weak (final-'w') root, so its ending appears as the long 'ū' before the pronoun. It expresses a plain factual action.

56.meaning: 'Flesh' or 'meat' — the soft muscular tissue of the body.
56.grammar: An indefinite noun. The '-an' ending (accusative with the doubled final 'n' of indefiniteness) typically marks it as a direct object or as the substance with which something is covered or supplied, and signals 'some / a' rather than 'the'.

57.meaning: A connector meaning 'then, when' — it joins to what came before ('then/so') and sets up a 'when…' clause whose outcome follows. It frames a moment: 'and then, at the point when…'.
57.grammar: A compound of the connecting particle fa- ('then/so', linking to the preceding statement) and lammā, a particle meaning 'when' that introduces a past circumstance and leads the listener to expect a following result clause.

58.meaning: It became clear, plain, or evident — to come out into the open and be distinctly seen or understood; for something to be made manifest and unmistakable.

parts.en: it became clear / it grew evident

58.grammar: A past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular: 'it became clear'. The pattern (with the ta- prefix and doubled middle root letter) often gives the sense of a state coming about of itself. The final -a marks a single thing/male as the doer of a completed action.
58.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — to be distinct, clear, evident

59.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
59.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

60.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
60.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

61.meaning: 'I know' — a present-tense verb of knowing: to have certain knowledge or awareness of something.
61.grammar: A present/future (Form I) verb, first-person singular ('I'), marked by the prefix a-. This a- is the first-person agreement marker built into the conjugation, not a free-standing pronoun. The final -u marks the indicative — a plain statement of ongoing or habitual knowing.

62.meaning: An emphatic particle meaning 'that' (as in 'I know that...') or 'indeed/surely.' It introduces a statement and gives it certainty and emphasis, presenting what follows as an established fact.
62.grammar: An emphatic particle that introduces a noun-clause ('that...'). It puts the following noun into the accusative case and lends the whole statement a sense of certainty and assertion. It typically comes after verbs of knowing, saying, or informing.

63.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
63.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

64.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
64.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

65.meaning: 'every,' 'each,' or 'all' — a word expressing totality or completeness. It indicates the entirety of something: when joined to a singular indefinite noun it means 'every (single) one,' and when joined to a definite noun it can mean 'all of' or 'the whole of.'
65.grammar: A noun of totality. The final '-i' ending is genitive (the 'of/possession' case): it marks the word as governed by a preceding preposition or as the first term of a possessive link to a following noun, so it typically reads 'of every…' or 'every…' leading into what follows.

66.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
66.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
66.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

67.meaning: All-powerful, fully able, ever-capable — possessing complete and effective power to do whatever is willed; one whose ability never falls short.
67.grammar: An intensive adjective on the faʿīl pattern, which stresses a deep, abiding quality ('thoroughly able'). The final -un is the indefinite nominative (nunation) — the doubled-n shows no 'the', and the -u base vowel marks the nominative case, used when the word is a subject or a predicate ('… is all-powerful').

1.meaning: 'And when / and at the time when' — the connective 'and' joined to a word that points to a past moment or circumstance ('when'), introducing the recollection of an event or situation.
1.grammar: A connective particle plus a time-word. The wa- prefix means 'and'. 'Idh' is an invariable adverb pointing to a definite time in the past ('when, at the moment that'); it has no case ending and typically introduces a clause recalling a past event.

2.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
2.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

3.meaning: Ibrāhīm (Abraham), the proper name of the patriarch and prophet, revered as a model of pure devotion to Allah.
3.grammar: A proper name (of non-Arabic origin). The final -u ending is nominative, the case used for the subject or the one doing/being something in a sentence. Being a foreign name, it does not take nunation (no '-un').

4.meaning: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'my': the One who owns, sustains, nurtures, and governs — combining mastery, ownership, and loving cultivation. With the attached 'my' it is an intimate address, 'my Lord.'
4.grammar: A noun, rabb, with the first-person possessive (the original 'my' yāʾ being reduced to a final -i, so 'my Lord'). The word denotes the Master who creates, owns, and lovingly sustains. Used as a heartfelt vocative, calling upon one's Lord.
4.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

5.meaning: 'Show me!' or 'let me see!' — a request that someone cause the speaker to see or perceive something; the verb 'to show / cause to see' with 'me' as the one shown.
5.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to one person, from a causative verb ('to make someone see' = 'to show'). The ending '-nī' is the object pronoun 'me' (the 'n' is a connecting sound that links certain pronouns to a verb). So the whole means '(you) cause me to see'.

6.meaning: An interrogative meaning 'how?' — asking about the manner, condition, or state of something ('how?', 'in what way?'). It can also express astonishment.
6.grammar: An interrogative particle (kayfa) ending in an invariable -a; it does not change for case. It asks about the manner or state of an action ('how…?') and is sometimes used rhetorically to express wonder or rebuke rather than a genuine question.

7.meaning: A verb meaning 'You give life' or 'You bring to life / revive' — the act of causing the dead or lifeless to live, addressed to a single subject ('You').
7.grammar: A present-tense verb with the 'tu-' prefix marking a second-person masculine singular subject ('you'); the 'u' vowel reflects a causative pattern — to cause to live. Built on a weak (final-'y') root, it ends in '-ī'. It expresses the giving of life as an action of the one addressed.
7.root: ح-ي-ي (ḥ-y-y) — life; to live, to give life

8.meaning: 'The dead' — those who have died or are without life; the lifeless, as a group.
8.grammar: A definite plural noun/adjective ('the dead'). It is of a plural pattern that ends in a fixed long -ā, so its ending does not change with grammatical position; it refers collectively to those who are dead.

9.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
9.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

10.meaning: A compound opening a question and a negation at once: roughly 'and have … not …?' or 'is it not the case that …?'. It combines a questioning particle, the connector 'and', and a negative that places the following verb in the past, often expecting the listener to agree.
10.grammar: Three particles fused together: the interrogative 'a-' (turning the statement into a question), the connector 'wa' ('and'), and the negator 'lam'. 'lam' negates a verb and shifts its meaning into the past ('has not / did not'), and it puts the following present-tense verb into the jussive (vowel-less) form. The combination often invites the listener to affirm ('have you not …?').

11.meaning: A verb meaning 'to believe', 'to have faith', or 'to place one's trust and security'. Its core sense unites inward faith with the granting of safety and trust.
11.grammar: A present-tense verb with the 'tu-' prefix marking a second-person masculine singular subject ('you'); the 'u' vowel belongs to this verb's pattern (the form used for 'to believe'). The vowel-less ending (jussive) is the shape the verb takes after a negating or questioning particle such as 'lam'.

12.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
12.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

13.meaning: Yes indeed / nay, rather — an affirmative reply used specifically to contradict a preceding negative and assert the positive: 'Yes (it is so), on the contrary.'
13.grammar: A response particle. Unlike a plain 'yes', it is used to overturn a negative statement or question and affirm what was denied. It does not inflect; the final long '-ā' is part of its fixed form.

14.meaning: 'But / however / yet' — a particle of correction and contrast that sets aside what came before and affirms something different instead.
14.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') attached to lākin ('but / however'). Lākin is a particle of rectification: it draws a contrast with, or corrects, the preceding idea and introduces an opposing or qualifying statement ('... but rather...').

15.meaning: 'So that (it / my heart) may be reassured / set at ease / find rest and certainty' — the verb 'to become tranquil, calm, and assured', preceded by a particle meaning 'so that' or 'in order that'.
15.grammar: A present-tense verb with the 'ya-' prefix marking a third-person masculine singular subject ('it' / 'he'). The 'li-' is a purpose particle ('so that'), after which the verb takes the subjunctive, marking an intended or desired outcome. The final doubled 'nn' belongs to this quadriliteral verb's own root and stem, conveying settled calm and assurance.
15.root: ط-م-ا-ن / ط-م-ء-ن (ṭ-m-’-n) — tranquillity, reassurance, calm certainty

16.meaning: 'Heart' — in its physical and, more often, its spiritual sense: the inner seat of feeling, understanding, intention, and faith; here marked as the speaker's own ('my heart').
16.grammar: A noun joined to the possessive pronoun '-ī' ('my'). When this 'my' is attached, it absorbs the noun's case ending, so the word is read with the '-ī' suffix marking first-person ownership ('my heart').
16.root: ق-ل-ب (q-l-b) — heart; to turn over, turn about

17.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
17.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

18.meaning: An imperative meaning 'take!', 'seize!', or 'take hold of!', addressed to a single male, with the attached 'fa-' meaning 'so' or 'then'.
18.grammar: A command (imperative) to one male person ('you'), with the 'you (masc. sing.)' built into the form. 'fa-' is a connecting particle expressing sequence or consequence ('so', 'then').
18.root: ا-خ-ذ / ء-خ-ذ (’-kh-dh) — to take, seize, take hold of

19.meaning: 'Four' — the cardinal number 4.
19.grammar: A number functioning as a noun. The '-an' ending (accusative with the doubled final 'n' of indefiniteness) typically marks it as the direct object of a verb, signalling 'four' as an indefinite quantity being acted upon. (By the rules of Arabic counting, the feminine '-a(t)' form of this number is used for counting masculine things.)
19.root: ر-ب-ع (r-b-ʿ) — four; fourth, a fourth part

20.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
20.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

21.meaning: 'Birds' or 'flying creatures' — a collective term for birds as a kind.
21.grammar: A definite collective noun with the prefix 'al-' ('the'); the 'l' of 'al-' assimilates in sound into the following 'ṭ' (a 'sun letter'), shown by the doubling. The '-i' ending is genitive, the case that regularly follows a preposition or links the noun to a preceding one in a possessive ('… of …') relationship.

22.meaning: A verb meaning 'incline them toward yourself', 'draw / gather them to you', or (by another reading) 'cut them up'; the core idea is making the objects bend or come toward you. The object 'them' refers to a feminine plural group.
22.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to one person, with the object pronoun '-hunna' ('them', for a group of three or more feminine things) attached at the end. 'fa-' is the connecting particle 'so' / 'then'.
22.root: ص-و-ر / ص-ي-ر (ṣ-w-r / ṣ-y-r) — to incline, bend, turn toward; to gather

23.meaning: 'To you' (addressing one person): indicating direction or motion toward a single individual — that toward which something moves or is directed.
23.grammar: The preposition ilā ('to, towards') with an attached pronoun; before a suffix ilā takes the form ilay-. The -ka ending is the pronoun 'you' for a single male addressee. Pronouns following a preposition stand in the genitive relationship, though their form does not visibly change for case.

24.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
24.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

25.meaning: Make! / Render! — a command to bring something into a state or to appoint/turn one thing into another. The verb jaʿala can mean to make, set, place, or designate.
25.grammar: A second-person masculine singular imperative ('you, make!'). The opening 'i-' is a helping vowel that lets the consonant cluster be pronounced, and the silent (jussive) ending with no final vowel is characteristic of the command form addressed to one male.
25.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, set, place, appoint, render

26.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
26.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

27.meaning: 'every,' 'each,' or 'all' — a word expressing totality or completeness. It indicates the entirety of something: when joined to a singular indefinite noun it means 'every (single) one,' and when joined to a definite noun it can mean 'all of' or 'the whole of.'
27.grammar: A noun of totality. The final '-i' ending is genitive (the 'of/possession' case): it marks the word as governed by a preceding preposition or as the first term of a possessive link to a following noun, so it typically reads 'of every…' or 'every…' leading into what follows.
27.root: ك-ل-ل (k-l-l) — totality, comprising the whole

28.meaning: 'Mountain' or 'hill' — a large natural elevation of the earth.
28.grammar: An indefinite noun. The '-in' ending (genitive with the doubled final 'n' of indefiniteness, 'tanwīn') signals 'a mountain' (not 'the') and is the case that regularly follows a preposition or links the noun to a preceding one in a possessive ('… of a …') relationship.

29.meaning: 'Of them' or 'from them', referring to a feminine plural group — combining the preposition 'from / of / part of' with the pronoun 'them'.
29.grammar: The preposition 'min' ('from', 'of', or 'a part of') joined to the attached pronoun '-hunna' ('them', for a group of three or more feminine things). Pronouns following a preposition stand in the genitive, which is why this form of 'them' is used.
29.root: — (preposition + pronoun)

30.meaning: A part, portion, share, or fraction of a larger whole; a piece set apart from the rest of something.
30.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The -an (tanwīn fatḥ) ending marks the accusative case and, being indefinite, signals 'a portion' (not 'the portion'). The accusative is the case typically taken by the object of a verb or by a word specifying amount or manner.
30.root: ج-ز-ء (j-z-') — to divide into parts, to portion out

31.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
31.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

32.meaning: A command addressed to one person: 'summon them / call upon them' — to call out to or invite a group of feminine beings or things to come.
32.grammar: A command (imperative) verb directed at a single addressee ('you'), built on a stem whose final weak letter has dropped, leaving the rounded 'u' sound. The attached -hunna is the object pronoun 'them', specifically for a group that is grammatically feminine plural.
32.root: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — to call, summon, invite, supplicate

33.meaning: 'They (feminine) will come to you' — an act of coming or arriving directed toward a single male addressee, performed by a feminine plural subject.
33.grammar: A present-tense verb with the feminine-plural ending -na ('they', referring to females or feminine things). The y- prefix marks third person. The attached -ka is the object 'you', addressed to one male. The feminine-plural -na form stays fixed and does not show further case change.
33.root: ا-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come, to arrive, to bring

34.meaning: Running, swift movement, striving, or earnest effort; can denote literal hastening as well as exertion toward a goal.
34.grammar: An indefinite verbal noun in the accusative case (-an, tanwīn fatḥ). In this case a noun like this commonly functions adverbially, describing the manner of an action — e.g. doing something 'running' or 'in haste'.
34.root: س-ع-ي (s-ʿ-y) — to run, hasten, strive, exert effort

35.meaning: 'And know!' — a command to one person to know, to be aware, or to recognize a fact, joined to what precedes by 'and'.
35.grammar: The prefix wa- means 'and'. The rest is a command (imperative) verb addressed to a single person, with the silent (sukūn) ending typical of a masculine-singular command — 'be aware!' / 'know!'
35.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know, to be aware, knowledge

36.meaning: An emphatic particle meaning 'that' (as in 'I know that...') or 'indeed/surely.' It introduces a statement and gives it certainty and emphasis, presenting what follows as an established fact.
36.grammar: An emphatic particle that introduces a noun-clause ('that...'). It puts the following noun into the accusative case and lends the whole statement a sense of certainty and assertion. It typically comes after verbs of knowing, saying, or informing.

37.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
37.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

38.meaning: Mighty, invincible, and supremely honoured; one who possesses overwhelming power and dignity such that none can overcome or resist Him. As a divine descriptor it conveys unassailable might joined with exalted worth.
38.grammar: A descriptive noun (adjective) on an intensive pattern, conveying a deep, enduring quality. The -un ending is indefinite and nominative: it typically marks the word as a subject or as a predicate describing something ("is mighty").
38.root: ع-ز-ز (ʿ-z-z) — might, honour, strength

39.meaning: 'All-Wise,' 'profoundly wise.' It describes one whose every judgement, decree, and act is perfectly sound, fitting, and placed exactly where it should be. As a divine attribute of Allah it points to flawless wisdom in all things.
39.grammar: An intensive adjective on the faʿīl pattern, conveying a deep, settled quality of wisdom. It is in the nominative case with indefinite marking, shown by -un, the form used for a predicate or descriptive noun that is not made definite.
39.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to judge, decide wisely; wisdom, governance

1.meaning: A likeness, comparison, parable, or illustrative example; a similitude used to make something abstract vivid and understandable.
1.grammar: A singular noun with the -u (nominative) ending, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or the thing being described. Being without tanwīn here, it commonly stands as the first term of a possessive phrase ('the likeness OF …').
1.root: م-ث-ل (m-th-l) — to resemble; likeness, similitude, example

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: 'They spend/give out': to expend wealth or provision, especially by giving it away in charity and in good causes. The word centers on disbursing what one has rather than hoarding it.
3.grammar: A present/future-tense verb in Form IV (anfaqa, 'to spend, expend'). The imperfect prefix is only yu-; the nūn that follows is the first root letter (of ن-ف-ق), not part of the prefix. The yu- prefix together with the -ūna ending marks the subject as 'they' (masculine plural) doing the action now or habitually.
