The -ūna ending also signals the indicative mood, the default 'plain' form used for ongoing or repeated action.
3.root: ن-ف-ق (n-f-q) — to spend, expend, give out

4.meaning: 'Their wealth / their possessions' — property, riches, and goods belonging to a group of males or a mixed group.
4.grammar: A plural noun (the plural of 'māl', wealth) carrying the -a accusative ending, which marks it as the object of a verb or otherwise governed into the accusative. The attached -hum means 'their', referring to a masculine or mixed group.

5.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
5.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

6.meaning: 'path, way, road' — a route or course; figuratively a cause or way of life one travels along. In construct ('the way OF ...').
6.grammar: A singular noun with the '-i' (genitive) ending, which typically links it to a following noun ('the way OF ...') or follows a preposition. It marks the word as connected to or possessed by what comes after.

7.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
7.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

8.meaning: An expression meaning 'like the likeness of' or 'as the example of.' It joins the comparison word 'ka' (like, as) to the noun for a likeness/parable, setting up a comparison: 'comparable to the case of…'
8.grammar: The comparison particle ka- ('like, as') prefixed to a noun. Because ka- functions like a preposition, the noun takes the -i genitive ending, the case used after prepositions and to link 'the likeness OF …' to a following noun.

9.meaning: A single grain or seed, such as a kernel of grain; one small seed-unit of a plant.
9.grammar: An indefinite singular noun with the -in (tanwīn kasr) ending, marking the genitive case. The noun ends in tā' marbūṭa, which is sounded as 't' once a case-ending follows it, so the form reads 'ḥabbatin'. The genitive is the case taken after a preposition or when a noun is possessed by another ('… of a grain'); the indefiniteness gives 'a grain'.
9.root: ح-ب-ب (ḥ-b-b) — grain, seed; also love, affection

10.meaning: 'It produced / brought forth (growth)' — the act of causing plants, seeds, or shoots to sprout and grow, done by a single feminine subject.

parts.en: it caused to grow / brought forth

10.grammar: A past-tense verb in the causative pattern, meaning to make something grow or bring it forth (not merely to grow oneself). The -at ending marks a third-person feminine singular subject ('she/it') in the past.
10.root: ن-ب-ت (n-b-t) — to grow, sprout; plants, vegetation

11.meaning: 'Seven' — the cardinal number seven.
11.grammar: A cardinal number. The final -a is the accusative case ending, the form a noun typically takes when it is the direct object of a verb (the thing being acted upon) or otherwise governed into that case. The counted noun following it normally appears in the genitive ('of') form.

12.meaning: Ears or spikes of grain — the seed-bearing heads of cereal plants such as wheat (plural).
12.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural. Because it follows a plural pattern that is 'diptote', it takes a plain -a for the accusative without tanwīn, and would use the same -a in the genitive. The accusative typically marks the object of a verb.

13.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
13.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

14.meaning: 'every,' 'each,' or 'all' — a word expressing totality or completeness. It indicates the entirety of something: when joined to a singular indefinite noun it means 'every (single) one,' and when joined to a definite noun it can mean 'all of' or 'the whole of.'
14.grammar: A noun of totality. The final '-i' ending is genitive (the 'of/possession' case): it marks the word as governed by a preceding preposition or as the first term of a possessive link to a following noun, so it typically reads 'of every…' or 'every…' leading into what follows.

15.meaning: A single ear or spike of grain — one seed-bearing head of a cereal plant.
15.grammar: An indefinite singular noun with the -in (tanwīn kasr) genitive ending. The noun ends in tā' marbūṭa, which is sounded as 't' when a case-ending follows, so the form reads 'sunbulatin'. The genitive is used after prepositions or in possessive constructions ('… of an ear of grain'); the indefiniteness yields 'an ear of grain'.

16.meaning: The number one hundred (100).
16.grammar: A cardinal number functioning as a noun, with the -u (nominative) ending — the case of a subject or of the thing being described. The word ends in tā' marbūṭa, sounded as 't' once a case-ending follows, so the form reads 'mi'atu'. Without tanwīn, it commonly leads a possessive phrase ('a hundred OF …'), and a counted noun after it stands in the singular genitive.

17.meaning: A single grain or seed, such as a kernel of grain; one small seed-unit of a plant.
17.grammar: An indefinite singular noun with the -in (tanwīn kasr) ending, marking the genitive case. The noun ends in tā' marbūṭa, which is sounded as 't' once a case-ending follows it, so the form reads 'ḥabbatin'. The genitive is the case taken after a preposition or when a noun is possessed by another ('… of a grain'); the indefiniteness gives 'a grain'.
17.root: ح-ب-ب (ḥ-b-b) — grain, seed; also love, affection

18.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
18.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
18.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

19.meaning: 'He multiplies / doubles / increases manifold' — to give back many times over, to compound or augment something repeatedly.
19.grammar: A present-tense verb in the Form III pattern, here carrying a multiplicative sense — to increase something many-fold. The yu- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it'), and the final -u marks the plain indicative mood (a simple statement of ongoing or habitual action).
19.root: ض-ع-ف (ḍ-ʿ-f) — to double, multiply; also weakness

20.meaning: 'for whoever / to the one who' — the preposition 'for/to' joined with the relative word 'who', introducing the person(s) about whom something is said.
20.grammar: A preposition ('for/to') combined with the relative/interrogative word 'man' ('who, whoever'). Together they single out a person or group as the focus ('for the one(s) who...').

21.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning 'he wills, he wishes, he chooses' — to want or intend something by one's own decision.
21.grammar: A present/ongoing action by a single masculine subject ('he'); the ya- prefix marks third-person masculine singular, and the final -u marks the indicative mood — a plain statement of fact ('he wills'), as opposed to a command or a verb governed by 'that.'
21.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʾ) — willing, wishing; the root behind 'thing' (shayʾ)

22.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
22.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
22.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

23.meaning: An adjective meaning 'vast, ample, all-embracing, boundless' — wide in capacity, encompassing; of Allah it conveys limitless reach in knowledge, mercy, and bounty.
23.grammar: An active participle ('one who is vast/encompassing') used adjectivally. The ending '-un' is the indefinite nominative (tanwīn), marking it as 'a vast one' and as a subject or predicate.
23.root: و-س-ع (w-s-ʿ) — breadth, capacity, amplitude, to encompass

24.meaning: An intensive adjective/name meaning 'All-Knowing / fully aware' — one whose knowledge is complete, deep, and all-encompassing; as a divine attribute it denotes Allah's perfect knowledge.
24.grammar: An intensive adjective (the pattern faʿīl conveys 'thoroughly, abundantly'). The ending -un is the indefinite nominative — the nominative case marks it as the subject or the quality being affirmed, and the -n (nunation) signals 'a / an', i.e. indefinite. So it reads '(is) all-knowing'.
24.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — knowledge, knowing

1.meaning: Those who / the ones who — a plural relative pronoun (masculine) introducing a description: 'those (people) who …'.
1.grammar: A relative pronoun, masculine plural, meaning 'those who / the ones who'. It refers back to a group already in view and introduces a clause describing them. Its form is fixed and does not change for case.

2.meaning: 'They spend/give out': to expend wealth or provision, especially by giving it away in charity and in good causes. The word centers on disbursing what one has rather than hoarding it.
2.grammar: A present/future-tense verb in Form IV (anfaqa, 'to spend, expend'). The imperfect prefix is only yu-; the nūn that follows is the first root letter (of ن-ف-ق), not part of the prefix. The yu- prefix together with the -ūna ending marks the subject as 'they' (masculine plural) doing the action now or habitually. The -ūna ending also signals the indicative mood, the default 'plain' form used for ongoing or repeated action.
2.root: ن-ف-ق (n-f-q) — to spend, expend, give out

3.meaning: 'Their wealth / their possessions' — property, riches, and goods belonging to a group of males or a mixed group.
3.grammar: A plural noun (the plural of 'māl', wealth) carrying the -a accusative ending, which marks it as the object of a verb or otherwise governed into the accusative. The attached -hum means 'their', referring to a masculine or mixed group.

4.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
4.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

5.meaning: 'path, way, road' — a route or course; figuratively a cause or way of life one travels along. In construct ('the way OF ...').
5.grammar: A singular noun with the '-i' (genitive) ending, which typically links it to a following noun ('the way OF ...') or follows a preposition. It marks the word as connected to or possessed by what comes after.

6.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
6.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

7.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
7.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

8.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
8.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

9.meaning: 'They follow up / make follow / cause to follow after' — to attach or append one thing after another, said of a male or mixed group.
9.grammar: A present-tense verb in the causative pattern ('to make X follow Y' / 'to follow something up with'). The yu- prefix is third person and the -ūna ending marks a masculine plural subject ('they') in the plain indicative mood, stating an ongoing or habitual action.

10.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
10.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

11.meaning: 'They spent / disbursed' — the act of laying out wealth, giving it away, or expending it, done by a group in the past.
11.grammar: A past-tense verb in a pattern meaning to spend or expend (especially wealth). The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'); the silent alif written after it is a spelling convention and is not pronounced.

12.meaning: Reproachful reminding of a favor done — to follow a gift by recounting it so as to belittle or shame the recipient; also more neutrally a bestowed favor or boon.
12.grammar: An indefinite verbal noun in the accusative case (-an, tanwīn fatḥ). The accusative commonly marks the object of a verb or the thing accompanying or specifying an action.
12.root: م-ن-ن (m-n-n) — to bestow a favor; also to remind of a favor reproachfully

13.meaning: 'And not' — a connector 'and' joined to the negative particle 'not,' negating a following statement.
13.grammar: Two particles: the joining 'and' (wa) plus the negator lā ('not'). Lā commonly negates a present-tense verb or a noun. Neither particle takes case endings.

14.meaning: Harm, hurt, or an affliction — something offensive or injurious, ranging from a minor irritation or ailment to anything that causes discomfort or distress.
14.grammar: An indefinite noun. The -an ending (written with tanwīn) is the indefinite accusative: it marks 'a harm / some harm' as the object of a verb or as part of a descriptive phrase, with the 'n' sound signalling indefiniteness ('a/an').
14.root: أ-ذ-ي (ʾ-dh-y) — to harm, hurt, injure, cause discomfort

15.meaning: 'For them / to them / theirs' — a preposition 'for / to / belonging to' joined to the pronoun 'them,' expressing that something pertains, belongs, or is owed to that group.
15.grammar: The preposition li- ('for / to / belonging to'), whose vowel becomes -a before an attached pronoun, joined to -hum ('them'). It commonly expresses possession or benefit — 'theirs / for them.' Particles like this carry no case or tense of their own.

16.meaning: "Their reward / wage / recompense" — payment or recompense earned for work or conduct, whether a worldly wage or an otherworldly reward, bound to a 'their'.
16.grammar: A masculine singular noun with an attached possessive pronoun 'hum' ('their', masculine plural). The -u before the pronoun is the nominative case ending, typically marking the word as the subject of a sentence or the thing being asserted to exist.

17.meaning: 'With / in the presence of / near' — an adverb of place and relation meaning at, by, in the sight or estimation of someone. It indicates nearness, possession, or what holds in someone's view (as in 'with Allah' = in His sight).
17.grammar: An adverb of place that is always followed by a noun it relates to. It carries a fixed -a ending; this accusative-type vowel is characteristic of such adverbs of place and shows the word is functioning to locate something ('at, near, in the presence of').

18.meaning: 'Their Lord' — the base 'rabb' means Lord, Master, Sustainer: the one who owns, nurtures, governs, and brings to maturity. As a divine title it conveys Allah as Creator and Sustainer of all.
18.grammar: The noun 'rabb' ('Lord, Sustainer') with the attached pronoun '-him' ('their'). The '-i' before the pronoun is the genitive case, the form used after a preposition or, as in a possessive linkage, to show belonging ('of/their').
18.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, master, sustain; lordship

19.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
19.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

20.meaning: 'Fear' — a state of being afraid, dread, or alarm; apprehension of something harmful or threatening.
20.grammar: A singular indefinite noun. The '-un' ending (nunation) marks it as nominative and indefinite — 'a fear' or simply 'fear' — and the nominative typically signals the doer or subject of a sentence, or the subject of an existential statement ('there is fear').

21.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon them' or 'against them': the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over, against') joined to the plural pronoun 'them'. It conveys something resting on, being incumbent upon, or weighing against a group.
21.grammar: ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The suffix -him is the attached pronominal suffix for a masculine plural group ('them'); after a preposition it carries genitive/prepositional force, and the -i- vowel reflects its position after this preposition. Together they signal a relationship of something being over, upon, or burdensome to that group.
21.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

22.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
22.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

23.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (referring to a group of males, or a mixed group). Because it stands on its own rather than being attached to a verb or noun, it often adds emphasis, singling out or stressing the subject ('they themselves', 'it is they who').
23.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It does not take case endings; the fixed -m simply marks the plural 'they'. Standing alone, it commonly serves to emphasise or isolate the subject.

24.meaning: 'They grieve / will grieve' — to feel sorrow, sadness, or distress; to be saddened over loss or hardship.
24.grammar: A present/future-tense verb, third-person masculine plural. The 'ya-' prefix marks third person, and the '-ūna' ending marks a masculine plural subject ('they') with the verb in its full (indicative) form, describing ongoing or future action. Read together the word is 'yaḥzanūna.'
24.root: ح-ز-ن (ḥ-z-n) — grief, sorrow

1.meaning: A saying, an utterance, a statement, or speech; words that are spoken.
1.grammar: An indefinite singular noun (verbal noun of 'to say') with the -un (tanwīn ḍamm) ending, marking the nominative case — the case of a subject or of the thing being described — and signaling 'a saying' rather than 'the saying'.
1.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, speak; speech, word

2.meaning: Recognized as good and fitting; kind, decent, honorable — that which is commonly known to be right and acceptable.

parts.en: known to be good / kind / proper

2.grammar: A passive participle ('that which is known/recognized') used to mean 'good, kind, fitting'. The -un (tanwīn ḍamm) ending marks the indefinite nominative — the case of a subject or of a describing word.
2.root: ع-ر-ف (ʿ-r-f) — to know, recognize; the recognized good

3.meaning: 'And forgiveness / pardon' — the covering over and remitting of faults, joined by 'and'.
3.grammar: The prefix wa- means 'and'. The noun is a verbal noun meaning 'forgiveness'; it ends in tā' marbūṭa, which is sounded as 't' once a case-ending follows, so the form reads 'maghfiratun'. Its -un (tanwīn ḍamm) ending marks the indefinite nominative — the case of a subject or a thing being described.
3.root: غ-ف-ر (gh-f-r) — to forgive, pardon, cover over

4.meaning: 'Better / best; good' — an adjective of comparison meaning more good, preferable, or superior. It also serves broadly for 'goodness' and that which is good and beneficial.
4.grammar: A noun/adjective bearing the ending -un (nunation): the doubled-u 'n' sound marks the word as both indefinite ('a/an', no 'the') and nominative — the case used for the subject of a sentence or the predicate that describes it.
4.root: خ-ي-ر (kh-y-r) — good, goodness, that which is choice and beneficial

5.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
5.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

6.meaning: Charity — a freely given gift to the poor or needy, an act of giving that expresses sincerity of faith.
6.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The -in ending is the indefinite genitive: it typically follows a preposition or links to a preceding noun ('… of …'), with the 'n' sound marking it as indefinite ('a charity').
6.root: ص-د-ق (ṣ-d-q) — truthfulness, sincerity; giving that confirms one's faith

7.meaning: 'It is followed by / there follows it' — an act of something coming after, with the thing followed being feminine singular.
7.grammar: A present-tense verb 'to follow'. The ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it'), and the -u (here preserved before the pronoun) marks the plain indicative mood. The attached -hā is the object 'it/her', referring to something feminine singular.

8.meaning: Harm, hurt, or an affliction — something offensive or injurious, ranging from a minor irritation or ailment to anything that causes discomfort or distress.
8.grammar: An indefinite noun. The -an ending (written with tanwīn) is the indefinite accusative: it marks 'a harm / some harm' as the object of a verb or as part of a descriptive phrase, with the 'n' sound signalling indefiniteness ('a/an').
8.root: أ-ذ-ي (ʾ-dh-y) — to harm, hurt, injure, cause discomfort

9.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
9.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
9.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

10.meaning: Rich, wealthy, self-sufficient; one who is free of need and dependent on no one — when said of Allah, the One utterly without need of anything.
10.grammar: An adjective in the intensive 'faʿīl' pattern, denoting a firmly established quality of being rich and free of need. The -un (tanwīn ḍamm) ending marks the indefinite nominative — the case of a subject or a describing word.
10.root: غ-ن-ي (gh-n-y) — to be free of need, rich, self-sufficient

11.meaning: An intensive adjective meaning 'most forbearing, clement, gentle' — one who is patient and does not rush to anger or punishment despite having the power to act, but bears with wrongdoing calmly.
11.grammar: An adjective on the intensive faʿīl pattern, conveying a deep and constant quality. The final -un (nominative with tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('a forbearing one') and is the ending typical of a subject or a predicate describing something.

1.meaning: 'O…!' — a compound vocative expression used to call out and summon an audience before addressing them. It fuses the call-particle 'yā' ('O') with a noun that means 'the one(s) addressed,' yielding an emphatic 'O you…!' that introduces direct address.
1.grammar: A vocative (calling) construction. 'Yā' is the particle for calling out; 'ayyu' carries a nominative '-u' as the one being summoned; 'hā' is an attention-drawing particle. Together they function as 'O you…!,' setting up the noun of address that follows.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
3.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

4.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
4.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

5.meaning: '(That) you (plural) nullify / render void / cancel out' — to make an action worthless or invalid, addressed to a group.
5.grammar: A present-tense verb in the causative pattern, meaning to make something void or worthless. The tu- prefix marks a second-person subject ('you'). The ending is the plural 'you', but its normal final -na has dropped (leaving -ū), which happens after certain particles that put the verb in the subjunctive or jussive — e.g. after 'do not' or 'so that'.
5.root: ب-ط-ل (b-ṭ-l) — to be void, false, in vain; to nullify

6.meaning: 'Your charitable gifts / acts of charity' — voluntary or due almsgiving belonging to a group of people.
6.grammar: A sound feminine plural noun ('charities'). For this plural type the ending -i serves for both the genitive and the accusative (as opposed to -u for the nominative); here it appears before the attached pronoun. The -kum means 'your', addressed to a group of males or a mixed group.
6.root: ص-د-ق (ṣ-d-q) — truthfulness; charity (giving that proves sincerity)

7.meaning: 'With the reproachful reminding (of a favor)' — by means of recounting a gift so as to belittle the one who received it.
7.grammar: The prefix bi- is a preposition meaning 'with / by means of', and al- is 'the'. The noun carries the -i (kasra) genitive ending, which is required after the preposition bi-; the preposition is what pulls the noun into the genitive case.
7.root: م-ن-ن (m-n-n) — to bestow a favor; also to remind of a favor reproachfully

8.meaning: And the harm, the injury, or the hurt — referring to causing offense or distress to others, especially the kind of wounding remark or reproach that spoils an act of giving.
8.grammar: Begins with 'wa' (and) joined to the definite article 'al-' (the). The base noun ends in a long 'ā' (written with a dagger-alif), a fixed ending that does not change for case; the word names an abstract thing — harm or injury inflicted on someone.
8.root: ا-ذ-ي (ʾ-dh-y) — to harm, hurt, cause injury

9.meaning: like the one who / as the one who — a comparison particle joined to a relative pronoun, introducing a single masculine person being likened to something: 'like him who…'.
9.grammar: The ka- prefix is a particle of comparison meaning 'like' or 'as'. Attached to it is the relative pronoun 'the one who / which', which is masculine singular and introduces a following descriptive clause.

10.meaning: He spends, lays out, or disburses (wealth) — to expend money or resources, whether for good or ill.
10.grammar: Present/future tense verb of Form IV. The 'yu-' prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'), and the '-u' ending marks the indicative mood — a plain statement that the action happens or is happening.

11.meaning: His wealth, property, or possessions — the goods and money a person owns, here marked as belonging to him.
11.grammar: A noun followed by the attached pronoun '-hu' (his). The '-a' on the noun before the pronoun is the accusative ending, which typically marks a word as the direct object of a verb (the thing being acted upon).

12.meaning: Showing off, ostentation, or doing something to be seen by people — performing an act for the sake of others' eyes and praise rather than sincerely.
12.grammar: A verbal noun of Form III, conveying mutual seeing — acting so as to be observed by others. The '-a' ending is accusative; in this pattern it often expresses purpose or motive ('out of / for the sake of showing off').
12.root: ر-ا-ي (r-ʾ-y) — to see, to be seen

13.meaning: Humankind, people, mankind — the collective of human beings.
13.grammar: A collective noun ('people, mankind') carrying the definite article al- ('the'); the 'l' of the article assimilates into the following 'n', doubling it (al-nās → an-nās). The genitive ending -i marks the word as governed by a preposition or as the second term of a possessive.
13.root: ء-ن-س (ʾ-n-s) — humankind, sociability, familiarity; the word for 'people' is most commonly traced to this root (related to insān, 'human being')

14.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
14.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

15.meaning: He believes; he has faith. The verb denotes giving heartfelt trust and assent, especially affirming faith in Allah and what He has revealed; the form also carries the sense of granting security.
15.grammar: A present/future verb, third-person masculine singular ('he'). The yu- prefix marks 'he' for this verb pattern (form IV), and the final -u marks the indicative mood — a plain ongoing or habitual statement.

16.meaning: A phrase 'in Allah / by Allah', combining the preposition 'with/in/by' and the divine name Allah, the proper name of the One God.
16.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') prefixed to the divine name Allah. A preposition always forces the following noun into the genitive case, which is why Allah here ends in -i. With verbs of believing, bi- conveys the object of faith — to believe IN.
16.root: — (Allah is the proper name of God and is not derived from a triliteral root in the usual sense)

17.meaning: "And the Day" — a stretch of time, a day; also used for the appointed Day of Judgement and Resurrection. The opening element is the conjunction 'and'.
17.grammar: A masculine singular noun with the definite article 'the' and the conjunction 'and'. The final -i is the genitive case ending: it typically signals that the word is linked to a preceding noun ('… of …') or governed by a preposition or oath particle.

18.meaning: An adjective meaning 'the last,' 'the latter,' or 'the final' — that which comes at the end of a sequence. It is the common counterpart to 'the first,' and is often used as a name for the world or life to come (the Hereafter, the Last Day), i.e. the ultimate end of all things.
18.grammar: An active-participle-type adjective on the pattern fāʿil. It carries the definite article 'al-' ('the'). The final -i is the genitive case, signaling that the word is governed by a preceding preposition or particle, or stands as the second term of a possessive link ('… of …'). It is masculine singular.
18.root: ء-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — to be last, to come after, to defer / postpone

19.meaning: Then his likeness, parable, or example — a comparison or illustration that stands for him, introduced as a consequence of what precedes.
19.grammar: Opens with 'fa' (then, so), which links to and draws a result from what came before. The noun 'mathal' (likeness, parable) carries the attached pronoun '-hu' (his); the '-u' before the pronoun is the nominative ending, typically marking the subject or topic of a sentence.

20.meaning: An expression meaning 'like the likeness of' or 'as the example of.' It joins the comparison word 'ka' (like, as) to the noun for a likeness/parable, setting up a comparison: 'comparable to the case of…'
20.grammar: The comparison particle ka- ('like, as') prefixed to a noun. Because ka- functions like a preposition, the noun takes the -i genitive ending, the case used after prepositions and to link 'the likeness OF …' to a following noun.

21.meaning: A smooth, hard rock or slab of stone — a bare, slick boulder with nothing growing on it.
21.grammar: A noun ending in '-in', which combines the genitive case with nunation (the 'n' sound that marks an indefinite noun, like 'a smooth rock'). The genitive typically follows a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …').
21.root: ص-ف-و (ṣ-f-w) — to be smooth, clear, pure

22.meaning: A preposition fused with a pronoun, meaning 'upon him', 'on him', or 'toward him'. It marks the one to whom an action is directed or upon whom something rests.
22.grammar: The preposition 'upon/on' with an attached object pronoun -hi ('him', third-person masculine singular); its -i vowel is the regular form the pronoun takes after the 'y' sound. Paired with a verb of turning, this 'upon/toward him' marks the person the action reaches.

23.meaning: Dust, fine earth, or soil — loose surface dirt.
23.grammar: A noun ending in '-un', which combines the nominative case with nunation (the 'n' marking an indefinite noun, 'dust / some dust'). The nominative typically marks the subject of a sentence or a thing being identified.

24.meaning: Then it struck it, befell it, or hit it — used of something (such as rain or a calamity) reaching and landing upon a target.
24.grammar: Begins with 'fa' (then, so), marking a consequence. The verb is past tense, Form IV, with a built-in third-person masculine singular subject ('it/he'); the attached '-hu' is the object pronoun ('it/him'), the thing struck.
24.root: ص-و-ب (ṣ-w-b) — to hit, strike, befall, reach a target

25.meaning: A heavy downpour or violent rainstorm — rain falling in large, forceful drops.
25.grammar: An active-participle noun ending in '-un' (nominative case plus the nunation that marks it as indefinite, 'a downpour'). The nominative typically marks the subject of a sentence or the doer of an action.

26.meaning: Then he/it left it, abandoned it, or left it in a certain state — to let something remain as it has become.
26.grammar: Opens with 'fa' (then, so), signaling a result. The verb is past tense with a built-in third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it'); the attached '-hu' is the object pronoun ('it/him'), the thing left behind.
26.root: ت-ر-ك (t-r-k) — to leave, abandon, let remain

27.meaning: Bare, smooth, and hard — a surface left clean and slick with nothing on it, stripped of any covering of soil.
27.grammar: An adjective ending in '-an', combining the accusative case with nunation ('bare'). This accusative form often describes the resulting state of something — how a thing ends up after an action.
27.root: ص-ل-د (ṣ-l-d) — to be hard, smooth, barren

28.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
28.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

29.meaning: They are able, they have power over, or they have control — to be capable of doing or disposing of something.
29.grammar: Present/future tense verb. The 'ya-...-ūna' frame marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'), and the final '-na' marks the indicative mood — a plain statement that the action holds true.
29.root: ق-د-ر (q-d-r) — power, ability, capacity, measure

30.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
30.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

31.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
31.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
31.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

32.meaning: A fused word combining the preposition 'min' ('from', 'of', 'about') with the relative/indefinite 'mā' ('what', 'that which'). Together: 'from what', 'about that which', 'of what'.
32.grammar: The preposition 'min' and the word 'mā' merge in pronunciation (the 'n' assimilating into the 'm'). 'min' governs a genitive, and 'mā' here functions as a relative pronoun introducing a clause ('that which …'). These are indeclinable particles without case endings.

33.meaning: 'They earned / they acquired / they gained' — past-tense action of a group obtaining something through their own effort, whether good or bad. The root carries the sense of working to acquire, and is often used of the deeds people accrue.
33.grammar: A past-tense verb. The ending -ū marks a masculine plural subject ('they') who completed the action in the past.

34.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
34.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
34.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

35.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
35.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

36.meaning: 'He guides / leads on the right way' — to show someone the correct path, direct them rightly, or lead them to a goal, whether literally or in matters of belief and conduct.
36.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular: the ya- prefix means 'he'. The verb ends in a long -ī (a weak final letter); in this indicative form the long vowel stands in place of the usual -u mood marker, still conveying a plain, ongoing statement ('he guides').
36.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — guidance, showing the way, leading rightly

37.meaning: the people / the folk — a body of people, a community or group regarded collectively (here in the accusative form).
37.grammar: The l- prefix is the definite article 'the'. The final -a ending is accusative. Since the verb it follows is passive (and so takes no direct object), this accusative is adverbial — marking the circumstance or setting of the action ('before / in front of the people') rather than a thing being acted upon.
37.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, to arise; a people standing together

38.meaning: The disbelievers / the ungrateful — those who reject faith and cover over the truth; the word also carries the sense of covering up or being ungrateful for what one has been given.
38.grammar: 'al-' is 'the'. The stem is an active participle ('one who disbelieves/is ungrateful') made plural for masculine people. The -īna ending is the accusative/genitive form of the sound masculine plural: it marks the word as an object of a verb or as governed by a preposition, as opposed to the subject form -ūna.
38.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; ingratitude, disbelief

1.meaning: 'And the likeness / parable / comparison.' A 'mathal' is a similitude or illustrative example — a model case held up to make an abstract truth vivid by comparison.
1.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') plus a noun. The final -u is the nominative ending, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or for a noun standing as the topic of a statement.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: 'They spend/give out': to expend wealth or provision, especially by giving it away in charity and in good causes. The word centers on disbursing what one has rather than hoarding it.
3.grammar: A present/future-tense verb in Form IV (anfaqa, 'to spend, expend'). The imperfect prefix is only yu-; the nūn that follows is the first root letter (of ن-ف-ق), not part of the prefix. The yu- prefix together with the -ūna ending marks the subject as 'they' (masculine plural) doing the action now or habitually. The -ūna ending also signals the indicative mood, the default 'plain' form used for ongoing or repeated action.
3.root: ن-ف-ق (n-f-q) — to spend, expend, give out

4.meaning: Their wealth, properties, or possessions — the goods and money belonging to a group (plural of 'māl').
4.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural noun with the attached pronoun '-hum' (their), here vowelled '-humu' for smooth pronunciation before a following word. The '-a' on the noun before the pronoun is the accusative ending, typically marking the direct object of a verb.

5.meaning: Seeking, earnestly pursuing, desiring to attain — the act of going after something diligently. As a verbal noun it means 'a seeking / out of desire for.'

parts.en: seeking / earnest pursuit (the final -a is the accusative case ending, here expressing purpose/motive)

5.grammar: A verbal noun (the 'act of seeking') in the accusative case, shown by the final -a. In this role the accusative commonly expresses purpose or motive — 'out of a desire for / in seeking.' It is built on a Form VIII pattern conveying earnest, deliberate pursuit.
5.root: ب-غ-ي (b-gh-y) — to seek, desire, strive after something

6.meaning: Good pleasure / approval / contentment of someone — the state of being well-pleased. Used especially of seeking the pleasure and approval of Allah.
6.grammar: A feminine verbal noun meaning 'good pleasure, approval.' The final -i is the genitive case ending, which typically links the word to a following noun ('the pleasure OF …') or follows a preposition. So it sets up a possessive link: 'the good pleasure of (someone).'
6.root: ر-ض-ي (r-ḍ-y) — to be pleased, satisfied, content; approval and good pleasure

7.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
7.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

8.meaning: And a making-firm, a strengthening, or a steadfast confirmation — the act of grounding and steadying something (such as one's soul or resolve).
8.grammar: Begins with 'wa' (and) before a Form II verbal noun (the abstract act of firmly establishing). The '-an' ending combines the accusative case with nunation; in this pattern it commonly expresses cause or purpose ('out of / for a strengthening').
8.root: ث-ب-ت (th-b-t) — to be firm, steady, established

9.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
9.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

10.meaning: Themselves / their own selves — the noun nafs ('self, soul, person, inner being') joined to a pronoun 'their'. Used reflexively it means 'their own selves' and conveys the inmost self, the seat of desires and the person as a whole.
10.grammar: The plural noun anfus ('selves') carries the genitive -i ending followed by the possessive pronoun -him ('their'). The genitive marks the noun as governed by a preposition or joined to a preceding word; -him makes it 'their selves'.
10.root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s) — self, soul, breath, inner being

11.meaning: An expression meaning 'like the likeness of' or 'as the example of.' It joins the comparison word 'ka' (like, as) to the noun for a likeness/parable, setting up a comparison: 'comparable to the case of…'
11.grammar: The comparison particle ka- ('like, as') prefixed to a noun. Because ka- functions like a preposition, the noun takes the -i genitive ending, the case used after prepositions and to link 'the likeness OF …' to a following noun.

12.meaning: A garden — a cultivated, lush plot of trees and greenery; the word also carries the sense of a hidden, sheltered place because of its dense covering.
12.grammar: A feminine noun ending in '-in', combining the genitive case with nunation ('a garden'). The genitive typically follows a preposition or links the noun to a preceding word ('… of …'). The small mark indicates the following sound is pronounced lightly (hidden nunation).

13.meaning: On a raised ground, an elevated place, or a hill — a piece of high, rising land.
13.grammar: Opens with the preposition 'bi' (on, at, with). The noun ends in '-in' (genitive case plus the nunation marking it indefinite, 'a height') — the genitive is required here because the word follows a preposition.
13.root: ر-ب-و (r-b-w) — to rise, grow, swell, be high

14.meaning: It struck it, befell it, or fell upon it — used of something (such as rain) reaching and landing on a target that is feminine in gender.
14.grammar: Past tense verb, Form IV, with a built-in third-person masculine singular subject ('it/he'). The attached '-hā' is the object pronoun for a feminine thing ('it'), the thing that is struck or reached.
14.root: ص-و-ب (ṣ-w-b) — to hit, strike, befall, reach a target

15.meaning: A heavy downpour or violent rainstorm — rain falling in large, forceful drops.
15.grammar: An active-participle noun ending in '-un' (nominative case plus the nunation that marks it as indefinite, 'a downpour'). The nominative typically marks the subject of a sentence or the doer of an action.

16.meaning: So it brought forth, it gave, or it yielded — used of land or a tree producing its fruit or crop.
16.grammar: Begins with 'fa' (so, then), marking a result. The verb is past tense, Form IV; the final '-t' (the feminine ending) marks a third-person singular feminine subject ('she/it'), referring to something grammatically feminine.
16.root: ا-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come, to bring, to give forth

17.meaning: Its produce, fruit, or harvest — that which is eaten from a plant or garden, here marked as belonging to it.
17.grammar: A noun followed by the attached pronoun '-hā' (its, for a feminine owner). The '-a' on the noun before the pronoun is the accusative ending, which typically marks the direct object of a verb (the thing being acted upon).
17.root: ا-ك-ل (ʾ-k-l) — to eat; produce, food, fruit

18.meaning: Twofold, double, or two times over — twice the usual amount.
18.grammar: A dual noun (referring to exactly two). The '-ayni' ending marks the dual in the accusative/genitive — the special form Arabic uses for a pair, here meaning 'a double, twice as much'.
18.root: ض-ع-ف (ḍ-ʿ-f) — to double, multiply; a multiple, fold

19.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'fa-' ('then', 'so', 'but') drawing a consequence, joined to the conditional particle 'in' ('if'). Together: 'then if …', 'but if …'.
19.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that signals a result or transition ('then/so'). 'in' is the conditional particle 'if', introducing a supposed condition. Both are indeclinable particles with no case ending.

20.meaning: The particle 'lam', a negating word used to push a verb into the past: it means 'did not' / 'has not'. Though it sits before a present-tense verb form, it negates the action as something that did not happen.
20.grammar: 'lam' is a negating particle that governs a following present-tense verb but gives it past meaning ('did not …'). It also puts that verb into the shortened (jussive) form. 'lam' itself carries no ending.

21.meaning: (That) it strike it, befall it, or fall upon it — used of something (such as rain) reaching a feminine target, in a form that depends on a preceding condition or particle.
21.grammar: Present-tense verb, Form IV, with the 'yu-' prefix marking a third-person masculine singular subject ('it/he'). The bare, vowelless stem ending ('-ṣib' rather than '-ṣību') is the jussive mood, the form used after conditional or negating particles (e.g. 'if … strikes it' or 'does not strike it'). The attached '-hā' is the feminine object ('it').
21.root: ص-و-ب (ṣ-w-b) — to hit, strike, befall, reach a target

22.meaning: A heavy downpour or violent rainstorm — rain falling in large, forceful drops.
22.grammar: An active-participle noun ending in '-un' (nominative case plus the nunation that marks it as indefinite, 'a downpour'). The nominative typically marks the subject of a sentence or the doer of an action.

23.meaning: Then a light rain, a drizzle, or a fine dew — a gentle, soft fall of moisture.
23.grammar: Opens with 'fa' (then, so), often introducing the answer to a condition ('then …'). The noun ends in '-un' (nominative case plus the nunation marking it indefinite, 'a drizzle'); the nominative typically identifies a subject or a thing being named.
23.root: ط-ل-ل (ṭ-l-l) — fine rain, dew, light moisture

24.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
24.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
24.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

25.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
25.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

26.meaning: You (all) do / work / act — to carry out deeds or labor.
26.grammar: A present-tense verb (Form I). The 'ta-' prefix with the '-ūna' ending marks the second-person masculine plural ('you all'). The '-ūna' (with final 'n') is the indicative form, marking a plain ongoing or habitual statement.
26.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, work, act; deeds

27.meaning: 'All-Seeing / fully observant' — one who sees clearly and with complete insight; as a divine attribute, the One who perceives all things.
27.grammar: An intensive adjective on the faʿīl pattern, denoting one who possesses sight to a high degree — 'all-seeing'. The -un ending (tanwīn) is nominative plus indefiniteness, the form used for a subject or for a predicate ('[He] is all-seeing').
27.root: ب-ص-ر (b-ṣ-r) — sight, seeing, insight

1.meaning: Does … wish, would … like, or would … love — opens a question about whether someone would desire something. Built on a verb of loving/wishing that pairs strong affection with active wanting.
1.grammar: Begins with the interrogative 'a-' (introducing a yes/no question). The verb is present tense; the 'ya-' prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'), and the '-u' ending marks the indicative mood — stating the wishing as a fact being asked about.
1.root: و-د-د (w-d-d) — to love, wish, desire affectionately

2.meaning: One of you, any one of you — a single individual taken from among a group of people being addressed.
2.grammar: The noun 'aḥad' (one, any one) joined to the attached pronoun '-kum' (you, plural). The '-u' on the noun before the pronoun is the nominative ending, which typically marks the subject of a sentence — the one doing or being asked about.
2.root: ا-ح-د (ʾ-ḥ-d) — one, oneness, a single one

3.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
3.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

4.meaning: A verb meaning 'it is / it comes to be / it exists.' From kāna, the core verb of being, here in its present form expressing being or coming into a state.
4.grammar: A present/imperfect verb of being. The ta- prefix marks a third-person feminine singular subject ('it/she'). The final -a is the subjunctive ending, which typically appears after particles meaning 'that,' 'so that,' or 'until,' giving a sense of 'that it be' or 'so that it may be.'
4.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

5.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
5.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

6.meaning: A garden or orchard — a lush, enclosed expanse of trees and greenery. The word evokes ground so densely planted that its foliage conceals the soil beneath; by extension it is the standard term for the Garden of Paradise.
6.grammar: A singular feminine noun. The final -un (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a garden') and as nominative, the case used for the subject of a sentence or the thing being described.
6.root: ج-ن-ن (j-n-n) — to cover, conceal, screen from sight

7.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
7.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

8.meaning: Date-palms — the tall palm trees that bear dates. The form is a collective noun naming the species as a whole rather than counting individual trees.
8.grammar: A collective noun. The final -in (nunation) marks it as indefinite and genitive — the case that typically follows a preposition or links a word to a preceding noun in an 'of' relationship.
8.root: ن-خ-ل (n-kh-l) — the date-palm; also the notion of sifting/filtering

9.meaning: And grapevines — grapes or the vines that produce them. The base noun is a plural denoting grapes collectively, prefixed with 'and'.
9.grammar: A plural noun preceded by the connector wa- ('and'). The final -in (nunation) marks it as indefinite and genitive — the case used after prepositions or in an 'of' linkage, here also matching a preceding noun in a list.

10.meaning: A verb 'it flows, runs, streams' — used of water and rivers moving along, and of things that run or course freely. It describes continuous, ongoing motion.
10.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, 3rd person feminine singular. The ta- prefix here marks a feminine 'it/she' subject. The verb describes an ongoing or habitual action: 'it flows / keeps flowing.'

11.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
11.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

12.meaning: 'Beneath it / underneath it' — the noun for the underside or lower region of something, with an attached pronoun 'its' (referring to a feminine thing). It points to the space below or underneath a thing.
12.grammar: A location noun ('underneath') with the attached pronoun '-hā' ('its/her'), referring to a feminine noun. The -i ending is the genitive case, normally triggered here because words of place like 'under' commonly follow a preposition such as 'from' (min taḥti = 'from beneath').

13.meaning: 'The rivers / the streams' — the definite plural of a word for a flowing river or watercourse. It denotes large, running channels of water.
13.grammar: A definite plural noun ('the rivers'). The -u ending is the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence — the doer of the verb or the thing being described.

14.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
14.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

15.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
15.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.

16.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
16.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

17.meaning: 'every,' 'each,' or 'all' — a word expressing totality or completeness. It indicates the entirety of something: when joined to a singular indefinite noun it means 'every (single) one,' and when joined to a definite noun it can mean 'all of' or 'the whole of.'
17.grammar: A noun of totality. The final '-i' ending is genitive (the 'of/possession' case): it marks the word as governed by a preceding preposition or as the first term of a possessive link to a following noun, so it typically reads 'of every…' or 'every…' leading into what follows.

18.meaning: 'the fruits,' 'the produce,' 'the crops' — the fruits and yields of plants and trees, taken collectively. By extension 'thamarāt' can mean the produce or beneficial outcomes that something brings forth.
18.grammar: A definite sound feminine plural ('the fruits'). The '-āt' marks the feminine plural, and the final '-i' is the case-vowel that sound feminine plurals take for BOTH the genitive (after a preposition or in a possessive link) and the accusative (object) roles — they do not use a separate '-a.' 'Al-' makes it definite; the 'th' doubles because it is a 'sun letter' absorbing the 'l' of 'al-.'
18.root: ث-م-ر (th-m-r) — to bear fruit; fruit, produce

19.meaning: And it struck him / befell him — the connector 'and' joined to a verb meaning that something reached, hit, or overtook a male person, with 'him' as its object. The verb conveys an event landing squarely upon someone.
19.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third-person masculine singular ('he/it … '), so the act is completed. The attached -hu is the object pronoun 'him'. Prefixed with wa- ('and').
19.root: ص-و-ب (ṣ-w-b) — to hit the mark, befall, be correct/on target

20.meaning: Old age — the advanced years of life, the state of having grown old. The definite article makes it 'the old age' as a known, general condition.
20.grammar: A definite singular noun (with al-, 'the'). The final -u marks the nominative case, used for the subject or the thing performing/undergoing an action.
20.root: ك-ب-ر (k-b-r) — to be great, large; to grow old, increase

21.meaning: And for him / and he has — the connector 'and', the preposition 'for/to', and the pronoun 'him'. Together it expresses possession or belonging ('and to him belongs …', 'and he has …').
21.grammar: A small phrase, not a verb: the connector wa- ('and') + the preposition la- ('for/to') + the pronoun -hu ('him'). The preposition with a pronoun commonly conveys having or belonging ('he has', 'belonging to him').

22.meaning: Offspring — one's descendants, children, and progeny; the line of those who issue from a person. A collective term covering posterity as a whole.
22.grammar: A singular collective noun, grammatically feminine. The final -un (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('offspring') and nominative — the case for a subject or for the thing being described.
22.root: ذ-ر-ر (dh-r-r) — to scatter, disperse (offspring being 'scattered' forth); also linked to ذرأ, to create/multiply

23.meaning: Weak ones — those who are feeble, frail, or lacking strength. This is the plural, describing a group of weak or vulnerable persons.
23.grammar: A plural adjective/noun (singular ḍaʿīf, 'weak'). The final -u marks the nominative case — used for a subject or a predicate describing the subject. This pattern of plural takes no nunation.
23.root: ض-ع-ف (ḍ-ʿ-f) — to be weak, feeble; also to double/multiply

24.meaning: So it struck it / then it befell it — the consequence-connector 'so/then' joined to a verb meaning something reached or fell upon a feminine entity, with 'it (her)' as the object. Conveys an event landing as a result of what preceded.
24.grammar: A past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular, so the act is completed; prefixed with fa- ('so/then'), which signals result or sequence. The attached -hā is the feminine object pronoun 'it/her'.
24.root: ص-و-ب (ṣ-w-b) — to hit the mark, befall, be on target

25.meaning: A whirlwind — a fierce, spiraling windstorm, often one carrying scorching heat or fire. It denotes a violent rotating gust that sweeps up and destroys.
25.grammar: A singular noun. The final -un (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a whirlwind') and nominative — the case for a subject or the thing being described.
25.root: ع-ص-ر (ʿ-ṣ-r) — to press/squeeze, to wring; related to violent wind and to 'ʿaṣr', an era

26.meaning: 'In it / in him' — the preposition 'in, inside, within' joined to a pronoun referring to a single masculine or neuter thing. It locates something inside or as part of that referent.
26.grammar: A preposition with an attached object pronoun. The pronoun -hi refers to one masculine (or grammatically masculine) thing and stands as the object of the preposition; its vowel is -i because attached pronouns take that shape after the long -i of fi. Together they answer 'in what?' or 'in whom?'.

27.meaning: Fire — flame, blaze, or burning. The basic word for fire, and by extension a name for the Fire of punishment.
27.grammar: A singular feminine noun. The final -un (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a fire') and nominative — the case for a subject or a predicate.
27.root: ن-و-ر (n-w-r) — light, illumination; fire as a source of light and heat

28.meaning: So it burned up / then it was consumed by fire — the result-connector 'so/then' joined to a verb meaning a feminine thing caught fire and was wholly burnt. The verb form conveys the burning happening to the thing itself.
28.grammar: A past-tense verb of the reflexive 'i-…-ta-' pattern, where the action falls back on the doer — so it means 'caught fire / burned up' rather than burning something else. The ending -at marks a third-person feminine singular subject ('it/she'). Prefixed with fa- ('so/then'), signalling result.
28.root: ح-ر-ق (ḥ-r-q) — to burn, scorch, consume by fire

29.meaning: 'Like that / thus / in this manner.' A comparison word meaning that something is done or is the case in the way just mentioned.
29.grammar: The comparison particle ka- ('like/as') prefixed to the demonstrative 'that'. Together they form a fixed adverbial expression, 'like that / thus', which does not change its ending with grammatical position.
29.root: — (a particle of comparison joined to a demonstrative; no root)

30.meaning: He makes clear / He explains; to set something forth plainly so that its meaning is evident.
30.grammar: A Form II present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he'). The yu- prefix marks 'he', and the final -u marks the indicative mood — a plain, ongoing statement of fact (he makes clear / he is making clear).
30.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — clarity, distinctness, making evident

31.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
31.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
31.root: — (proper divine name)

32.meaning: 'for you,' 'to you,' 'for your benefit' — the preposition 'for/to' joined to 'you (plural).' It marks the party for whose sake, benefit, or possession something is done or given.
32.grammar: A preposition ('for/to') with the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you, plural'). Such prepositions assign a benefit, purpose, or recipient. The pronoun's vowel appears as '-u' (kumu) to ease pronunciation when a word follows.

33.meaning: 'The signs / the verses' — the plural of 'sign,' referring to clear indicators, proofs, miracles, or the verses of revelation that point to truth.
33.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun ('the signs'), made definite by the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The sound feminine plural takes the -i ending when it is an object of a verb or linked after a preposition or possessor — that is, when it is grammatically governed rather than serving as the subject.

34.meaning: 'so that you may…,' 'in the hope that you…' — a particle expressing purpose, expectation, or hopeful anticipation, fused with 'you (plural).' It introduces a hoped-for or intended outcome; when used of Allah it conveys the desired result rather than uncertainty.

parts.en: so that / perhaps / in hope that

34.grammar: An emphatic particle of hope/purpose belonging to the 'inna' family, which attaches a pronoun as its subject. The particle's fixed form ends in '-a,' and the suffix '-kum' is 'you (plural),' giving 'so that you (all) may…'

35.meaning: You reflect / ponder deeply — to think something over thoroughly, turning it about in the mind. The verb form intensifies plain thinking into sustained, careful contemplation, addressed to a group.
35.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ta- prefix marks a second-person subject ('you'), and the -ūna ending makes it masculine plural and indicative (a plain, ongoing statement: 'you ponder'). The doubled middle pattern adds intensity, i.e. thinking carefully and repeatedly.

1.meaning: 'O…!' — a compound vocative expression used to call out and summon an audience before addressing them. It fuses the call-particle 'yā' ('O') with a noun that means 'the one(s) addressed,' yielding an emphatic 'O you…!' that introduces direct address.
1.grammar: A vocative (calling) construction. 'Yā' is the particle for calling out; 'ayyu' carries a nominative '-u' as the one being summoned; 'hā' is an attention-drawing particle. Together they function as 'O you…!,' setting up the noun of address that follows.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
3.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

4.meaning: A command addressed to a group: 'spend!' — give out or expend wealth, resources, or provisions. The verb often carries the nuance of charitable or purposeful giving, releasing what one has for a cause or for others.
4.grammar: An imperative (command) verb. The -ū ending marks a masculine-plural addressee: 'you all, do this.' Built on Form IV (the af'ala pattern), which here gives the sense of expending or paying out from one's wealth.
4.root: ن-ف-ق (n-f-q) — to spend, expend, give out (of wealth)

5.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
5.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

6.meaning: 'Good things' — wholesome, pure, pleasant things; that which is lawful, agreeable, and beneficial, especially good foods. A feminine plural of an adjective used as a noun.
6.grammar: A sound feminine plural noun. The ending -āt marks it as a feminine plural ('good things'). The final -i vowel is the genitive case, which typically links the word to a following noun ('the good things OF…') or follows a preposition. For this plural pattern the genitive and accusative share the same -i form.

7.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
7.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

8.meaning: 'You earned / acquired, gained' — the same verb of earning addressed to a group of people, referring to the deeds they have done.
8.grammar: Past-tense verb. The -tum suffix marks the subject as second-person masculine plural, 'you (all).' The past tense presents the action as completed.
8.root: ك-س-ب (k-s-b) — to earn, acquire, gain (esp. deeds)

9.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and from/out of that which' or 'and from what'. It joins a new item to what precedes and points to an unspecified thing or category ('whatever it is that...').
9.grammar: A combination of the connector wa ('and'), the preposition min ('from, out of, part of'), and the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). The nūn of min has assimilated into the mīm of mā, doubling it (mim-mā). The whole phrase is invariable and does not take case endings.

10.meaning: We brought forth / We caused to come out — a verb meaning to make something emerge or be produced, with 'We' as the doer. The causative form means 'to bring/take out' rather than simply going out.
10.grammar: A past-tense verb, so the act is completed. The attached -nā marks a first-person plural subject ('we'). The 'a-' causative pattern turns 'to go out' into 'to make come out, bring forth'.
10.root: خ-ر-ج (kh-r-j) — to go out, exit, emerge

11.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
11.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

12.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
12.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

13.meaning: The earth — the ground, land, or soil; also the Earth as a whole. With the definite article it is 'the earth' as a known, encompassing thing.
13.grammar: A definite singular feminine noun (with al-, 'the'). The final -i marks the genitive case — used after a preposition or to link the word to a preceding noun in an 'of' relationship.

14.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
14.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

15.meaning: Deliberately seek out / head for — to set one's aim toward something and go for it on purpose. The verb stresses intentional pursuit; addressed as a command to a group ('aim at it, single it out').
15.grammar: A command (imperative) verb directed at a group. The ending -ū marks the masculine plural addressee ('you all, do …'). The doubled middle pattern conveys purposeful, deliberate aiming.
15.root: ي-م-م (y-m-m) — to aim for, betake oneself toward, intend

16.meaning: The bad / impure thing — that which is foul, corrupt, or of poor quality, the opposite of wholesome and good. With the article it names 'the bad part' as a known category.
16.grammar: A definite singular adjective/noun (with al-, 'the'). The final -a marks the accusative case — typically the object of a verb (the thing being acted upon) or the focus of the action.
16.root: خ-ب-ث (kh-b-th) — to be foul, wicked, impure, of bad quality

17.meaning: 'From it / out of it / from him'. It combines the preposition 'from / out of' with the pronoun 'it/him'.
17.grammar: The preposition min ('from / out of', indicating origin or source) with the attached pronoun -hu ('it' / 'him'), referring to a singular masculine thing or person. As object of the preposition, the pronoun is in the oblique form.
17.root: — (no triliteral root; a preposition with a pronoun)

18.meaning: You spend / give out — a verb meaning to expend wealth or resources, especially by giving it away in charity or for a cause. Addressed to a group as an ongoing action.
18.grammar: A present-tense verb. The tu- prefix marks a second-person subject ('you') in a causative-style pattern ('to expend'), and the -ūna ending makes it masculine plural and indicative (a plain statement: 'you spend').
18.root: ن-ف-ق (n-f-q) — to spend, expend, disburse; to use up

19.meaning: While you are not — the connector 'and/while', joined to a 'to be' verb that negates a state, with 'you (plural)' as the subject. It sets up a circumstance: 'whereas you would not …'.
19.grammar: A special negating verb (laysa) meaning 'is/are not'. The ending -tum marks a second-person masculine plural subject ('you all'). Prefixed with wa-, which here introduces an accompanying circumstance ('while you are not …').
19.root: ل-ي-س (l-y-s) — negation of existence/being ('to not be')

20.meaning: Taking it / ready to take it — the preposition 'with/as', joined to the doer-noun 'takers/receivers' and the object 'it'. It describes ones who would accept or take something, here introduced by a particle that emphasizes the negation ('would not be takers of it').
