18.meaning: Buying and selling; trade, commerce, a sale transaction. The exchange of goods for a price by mutual agreement.
18.grammar: A definite masculine verbal noun (al- = 'the'). The final -u is the nominative case, the form a noun takes when it is the doer or subject, or simply named on its own.
18.root: ب-ي-ع (b-y-ʿ) — to sell, trade, transact

19.meaning: 'The like (of),' 'an equivalent,' 'something matching or comparable.' It denotes a counterpart of equal measure or kind to something else.
19.grammar: A noun in the nominative case, shown by the final -u, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the thing being identified ('X is …'). It is regularly followed by a noun in the genitive to mean 'the like OF …'.

20.meaning: Usury or interest: the prohibited practice of lending money or commodities for a guaranteed, unearned increase paid back over and above the principal. The underlying sense is of something that swells, grows, or is augmented beyond its origin.
20.grammar: A definite masculine noun (the prefix al- marks 'the'). It is written with a long final ā (the alif), and as an invariable noun of this pattern its ending does not visibly change for case. It names the concept itself.
20.root: ر-ب-و (r-b-w) — to grow, increase, swell, augment

21.meaning: And He made lawful — He permitted and declared something allowed and free to do. The root carries the idea of loosening or untying, hence making a thing licit and unrestricted.
21.grammar: The prefix wa- means 'and'. The stem is a past-tense verb on a causative pattern ('to make/declare lawful'), third-person masculine singular; the final -a is the standard ending for a completed action done by 'he'.
21.root: ح-ل-ل (ḥ-l-l) — to loosen, untie; to be/make lawful

22.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
22.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

23.meaning: Buying and selling; trade, commerce, a sale transaction. The exchange of goods for a price by mutual agreement.
23.grammar: A definite masculine verbal noun (al- = 'the'). The final -a is the accusative case, the form a noun takes when it is the object of a verb (the thing being acted upon).

24.meaning: And He forbade — He prohibited and declared something off-limits and sacred to violate. The root denotes setting a thing apart as inviolable, hence unlawful to approach.
24.grammar: The prefix wa- means 'and'. The stem is a past-tense verb on an intensive/causative pattern (Form II, 'to make unlawful, to forbid'), third-person masculine singular; the final -a marks a completed action done by 'he'.
24.root: ح-ر-م (ḥ-r-m) — to forbid, prohibit; to be sacred/inviolable

25.meaning: Usury or interest: the prohibited practice of lending money or commodities for a guaranteed, unearned increase paid back over and above the principal. The underlying sense is of something that swells, grows, or is augmented beyond its origin.
25.grammar: A definite masculine noun (the prefix al- marks 'the'). It is written with a long final ā (the alif), and as an invariable noun of this pattern its ending does not visibly change for case. It names the concept itself.
25.root: ر-ب-و (r-b-w) — to grow, increase, swell, augment

26.meaning: A compound meaning 'then whoever' or 'so whoever'. It combines 'then/so' with the conditional/relative 'who', introducing whatever person meets a stated condition.
26.grammar: The connector fa- ('then/so', often answering or following a condition) joined to man ('whoever / the one who'), which refers to people and introduces a condition: 'whoever does X…'. man does not change its ending; the clause after it supplies the rest of the meaning.

27.meaning: It came to him / he came to him — arrival reaching a particular person. The act of coming or arriving, directed toward someone.
27.grammar: A past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it came'), with the final -a marking a completed action; the attached -hu is the object 'him' (the one reached or come to).
27.root: ج-ي-ء (j-y-ʾ) — to come, arrive

28.meaning: An admonition or exhortation: earnest counsel that warns, reminds, and stirs the heart, often appealing to consequences so as to soften and reform the listener.
28.grammar: A feminine singular noun; the feminine ending (tāʾ marbūṭa) is part of the base word itself. The final tanwīn -un marks it as indefinite ('an admonition') and in the nominative case, the form used for a subject or for naming the thing on its own.

29.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
29.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

30.meaning: A phrase meaning 'his Lord'. 'Lord' (rabb) denotes the Master, Owner, Sustainer, and Nurturer who creates, provides for, and governs — far richer than a mere title; here joined to 'his'.
30.grammar: The noun 'Lord' with the genitive -i ending followed by the attached pronoun -hi ('his'). The genitive case appears because the noun is linked to a preceding word ('… OF his Lord') or follows a preposition. The lengthened -hī reflects how this pronoun is pronounced after an -i vowel.
30.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship, nurturing, ownership, sustaining and bringing to completion

31.meaning: So he desisted and stopped — he reached the end of an action and held back from it. Conveys ceasing, refraining, and coming to a limit.
31.grammar: The prefix fa- means 'so' or 'then'. The stem is a past-tense verb on a reflexive pattern (Form VIII, 'to bring oneself to a stop, to desist'), third-person masculine singular ('he'); its final long -ā is how this completed-action verb ends because its last root letter is a weak (vowel-like) letter.
31.root: ن-ه-ي (n-h-y) — to forbid, restrain; to reach an end, cease

32.meaning: So for him / then his is; a linking word 'so/then' joined to 'for him,' expressing that something belongs or accrues to a single male — 'so to him belongs…'
32.grammar: A cluster of particles: the connector fa- ('so, then, and as a result') + the preposition la- ('for, belonging to') + the pronoun -hu ('him'). Together they assign possession or entitlement to a single male: 'so for him (is)…'

33.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
33.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

34.meaning: It passed, went before, or is now bygone — belonging to the past and already gone by. The root denotes what precedes or is sent ahead in time.
34.grammar: A past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('it passed / went before'); the final -a marks a completed action. The same root also yields a noun meaning 'predecessors / those who went before.'
34.root: س-ل-ف (s-l-f) — to precede, go before, be past

35.meaning: And his affair / his case / his matter — a situation, command, or business belonging to him. The word amr spans both 'command, order' and 'affair, matter.'
35.grammar: The prefix wa- means 'and'. The noun amr is masculine; the -u before the pronoun is the nominative case (the form for a subject or for naming). The attached -hu means 'his.'

36.meaning: 'To / toward / up to' — a preposition marking the endpoint, goal, or limit of an action or motion: the direction something moves toward or the boundary at which it stops.
36.grammar: An invariable preposition. It has no case ending of its own but puts the noun that follows it into the genitive ('of / to' state). It indicates direction toward, or the terminal limit of, something.

37.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
37.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

38.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
38.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.
38.root: — (pronoun/particle; no triliteral root)

39.meaning: He returned, went back, or did it again — reverting to a former state or repeating a prior action. The core sense is of coming back round to where one was.
39.grammar: A past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he returned / repeated'); the final -a marks a completed action done by 'he.'
39.root: ع-و-د (ʿ-w-d) — to return, go back, repeat

40.meaning: So those / then those are the ones — a connector 'so/then' joined to a demonstrative pointing to a distant or already-mentioned group: 'those people, they (are the ones who)…'.
40.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector meaning 'so/then', often introducing a result or consequence. 'ulā'ika' is a plural demonstrative ('those') pointing to people, typically picking up a previously described group and setting them up as the subject. It is fixed in form and does not change for case.
40.root: — (demonstrative — no root)

41.meaning: 'Companions / people of, dwellers, owners' — those closely associated with something, its inseparable folk, fellows, or inmates; literally the people who 'keep company with' a thing.
41.grammar: A masculine plural noun (the plural of ṣāḥib, 'companion'). The '-u' ending is nominative, typically marking the subject of a sentence; it appears here without nunation because the word is in a possessive construction ('companions OF …') with a following noun.

42.meaning: 'The Fire' — fire, flame; in religious usage often the Fire of Hell, the blazing punishment of the Hereafter.
42.grammar: The definite article 'al-' ('the') plus the feminine noun 'nār' ('fire'). The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'n' (so it is pronounced 'an-nār'). The '-i' ending is genitive, the case used after a preposition or to link the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the Fire').
42.root: ن-و-ر (n-w-r) — fire, blaze, burning

43.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (referring to a group of males, or a mixed group). Because it stands on its own rather than being attached to a verb or noun, it often adds emphasis, singling out or stressing the subject ('they themselves', 'it is they who').
43.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It does not take case endings; the fixed -m simply marks the plural 'they'. Standing alone, it commonly serves to emphasise or isolate the subject.

44.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
44.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.

45.meaning: 'Ones who abide / remain forever; everlasting dwellers.' The plural of an active participle describing those who stay, persist, and endure in a state or place without end — abiding permanently.
45.grammar: An active participle in the masculine plural. The -ūna ending marks a sound masculine plural in the nominative case — the form used when such a group is the subject of a sentence or is being described as being in that state.
45.root: خ-ل-د (kh-l-d) — to remain forever, endure, be everlasting

1.meaning: He erases, wipes out, or strips away — gradually effacing something until it is depleted of blessing or worth. The root denotes a wearing-down to nothing, like the waning of the moon.
1.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, third-person masculine singular ('he'). The final -u marks the indicative mood, signalling an ongoing or habitual action ('he wipes out / he keeps effacing').
1.root: م-ح-ق (m-ḥ-q) — to efface, obliterate, strip away, diminish

2.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
2.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

3.meaning: Usury or interest: the prohibited practice of lending money or commodities for a guaranteed, unearned increase paid back over and above the principal. The underlying sense is of something that swells, grows, or is augmented beyond its origin.
3.grammar: A definite masculine noun (the prefix al- marks 'the'). It is written with a long final ā (the alif), and as an invariable noun of this pattern its ending does not visibly change for case. It names the concept itself.
3.root: ر-ب-و (r-b-w) — to grow, increase, swell, augment

4.meaning: And He causes to grow / makes increase — He makes a thing multiply and expand. The same root that yields 'usury' here means to nurture growth and add to something.
4.grammar: The prefix wa- means 'and'. The stem is a present/imperfect verb on a causative pattern (Form IV, 'to make grow'), third-person masculine singular ('he'); the final long -ī is how this verb ends in the indicative because its last root letter is weak (vowel-like).
4.root: ر-ب-و (r-b-w) — to grow, increase; (causative) to make grow

5.meaning: Acts of charity, alms, voluntary or obligatory gifts given for the sake of Allah — the giving that flows from sincere faith (the word is linked to the notion of truthfulness/ṣidq, as such giving confirms the genuineness of one's faith).
5.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun (with 'the'). The sound-feminine plural ending -āt takes the vowel -i, which serves for both the genitive and the accusative in this plural pattern — marking the word either as object of a preposition / linked to a preceding noun, or as a direct object.
5.root: ص-د-ق (ṣ-d-q) — to be truthful, sincere; charity

6.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
6.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
6.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

7.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
7.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

8.meaning: He loves / likes / holds dear. To have affection for and approval of something or someone.
8.grammar: A present-tense verb in the fourth pattern, third-person masculine singular ('he…'). The yu- prefix signals a single masculine subject, and the final -u ending marks the indicative mood, presenting the action as an established fact or ongoing reality.
8.root: ح-ب-ب (ḥ-b-b) — love, affection; to hold dear

9.meaning: All, every, the whole of — totality. When followed by a singular it means 'every (one)'; when followed by a definite plural or whole it means 'all of.'
9.grammar: A noun of totality, almost always joined to a following noun in the genitive ('every … / all of …'). The final -a is the accusative case, the form used when the word functions as an object of a verb.

10.meaning: One who is utterly ungrateful and persistently denying — an emphatic form of the denier/disbeliever, marked by deep, habitual ingratitude toward favours received.
10.grammar: A masculine noun/adjective on an intensive pattern (faʿʿāl) that signals 'one who does this much or constantly.' The final -in (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('an ungrateful one') and in the genitive case, the form used after a preceding noun or a preposition.
10.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to be ungrateful, to disbelieve

11.meaning: A sinner; one steeped in sin and wrongdoing. An emphatic form denoting someone given over to guilt and transgression.
11.grammar: A masculine adjective/noun on an intensive pattern (faʿīl) ('deeply, habitually sinful'). The final -in (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('a sinner') and in the genitive case, the form used after a preceding noun or a preposition.
11.root: أ-ث-م (ʾ-th-m) — to sin, do wrong; guilt

1.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
1.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
3.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

4.meaning: A two-part word: 'and' + 'they did / worked / performed.' The verb denotes doing deeds, working, putting effort into action — practical doing as opposed to mere speaking or believing.
4.grammar: A conjunction 'wa' + a past-tense verb, 3rd person masculine plural. The -ū ending marks the subject as 'they' (a group of males or a mixed group): 'and they did / worked.'

5.meaning: 'The righteous deeds / good works' — the definite plural of a word meaning that which is sound, wholesome, upright, and beneficial. As a noun it refers to good, virtuous actions that set things right.
5.grammar: A definite sound feminine plural noun ('the good deeds'). The -i ending is the oblique case used by feminine plurals to mark either the genitive ('… of …' / after a preposition) or the accusative (direct object); for this plural pattern the accusative and genitive share the same -i ending.
5.root: ص-ل-ح (ṣ-l-ḥ) — to be sound, good, upright, set right

6.meaning: And they established / set up and kept up — they put a thing firmly in place and maintained it duly. Often used of upholding prayer, i.e. performing it properly and consistently.
6.grammar: The prefix wa- means 'and'. The stem is a past-tense verb on a causative pattern (Form IV, 'to make stand, to set up and keep up'); the -ū ending is the subject 'they' (masculine plural), marking a completed action they performed.
6.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; (causative) to set up, uphold

7.meaning: The ritual prayer (ṣalāh): the prescribed formal worship of standing, bowing, and prostrating before Allah at appointed times. As a verbal noun it also carries the underlying sense of calling upon, supplicating, and blessing.
7.grammar: A definite feminine noun. The -a ending is accusative: it generally marks the word as the direct object of a verb (the thing being acted upon, e.g. that which is established or performed), or the object of certain particles.

8.meaning: And they gave / handed over — they brought and delivered something to its recipient. The verb means to come with a thing and present it, i.e. to give.
8.grammar: The prefix wa- means 'and'. The stem is a past-tense verb on a causative pattern (Form IV, 'to bring/give'); the plural 'they' ending appears here as -awū because the verb's last root letter is weak (vowel-like). It marks a completed action performed by 'they.'
8.root: أ-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (causative) to bring, give

9.meaning: The purifying alms (zakāt) — the obligatory portion given from one's wealth that purifies it and causes it to grow; an act of worship and social due.
9.grammar: A definite feminine noun (the tied tā' marks the feminine). The final -a is the accusative ending, typically marking the noun as the direct object of a verb ('the alms').
9.root: ز-ك-و (z-k-w) — to be pure; to grow, increase, be blessed

10.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
10.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

11.meaning: "Their reward / wage / recompense" — payment or recompense earned for work or conduct, whether a worldly wage or an otherworldly reward, bound to a 'their'.
11.grammar: A masculine singular noun with an attached possessive pronoun 'hum' ('their', masculine plural). The -u before the pronoun is the nominative case ending, typically marking the word as the subject of a sentence or the thing being asserted to exist.

12.meaning: 'With / in the presence of / near' — an adverb of place and relation meaning at, by, in the sight or estimation of someone. It indicates nearness, possession, or what holds in someone's view (as in 'with Allah' = in His sight).
12.grammar: An adverb of place that is always followed by a noun it relates to. It carries a fixed -a ending; this accusative-type vowel is characteristic of such adverbs of place and shows the word is functioning to locate something ('at, near, in the presence of').

13.meaning: 'Their Lord' — the base 'rabb' means Lord, Master, Sustainer: the one who owns, nurtures, governs, and brings to maturity. As a divine title it conveys Allah as Creator and Sustainer of all.
13.grammar: The noun 'rabb' ('Lord, Sustainer') with the attached pronoun '-him' ('their'). The '-i' before the pronoun is the genitive case, the form used after a preposition or, as in a possessive linkage, to show belonging ('of/their').
13.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, master, sustain; lordship

14.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
14.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

15.meaning: 'Fear' — a state of being afraid, dread, or alarm; apprehension of something harmful or threatening.
15.grammar: A singular indefinite noun. The '-un' ending (nunation) marks it as nominative and indefinite — 'a fear' or simply 'fear' — and the nominative typically signals the doer or subject of a sentence, or the subject of an existential statement ('there is fear').

16.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon them' or 'against them': the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over, against') joined to the plural pronoun 'them'. It conveys something resting on, being incumbent upon, or weighing against a group.
16.grammar: ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The suffix -him is the attached pronominal suffix for a masculine plural group ('them'); after a preposition it carries genitive/prepositional force, and the -i- vowel reflects its position after this preposition. Together they signal a relationship of something being over, upon, or burdensome to that group.
16.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

17.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
17.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

18.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (referring to a group of males, or a mixed group). Because it stands on its own rather than being attached to a verb or noun, it often adds emphasis, singling out or stressing the subject ('they themselves', 'it is they who').
18.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It does not take case endings; the fixed -m simply marks the plural 'they'. Standing alone, it commonly serves to emphasise or isolate the subject.

19.meaning: 'They grieve / will grieve' — to feel sorrow, sadness, or distress; to be saddened over loss or hardship.
19.grammar: A present/future-tense verb, third-person masculine plural. The 'ya-' prefix marks third person, and the '-ūna' ending marks a masculine plural subject ('they') with the verb in its full (indicative) form, describing ongoing or future action. Read together the word is 'yaḥzanūna.'

1.meaning: 'O…!' — a compound vocative expression used to call out and summon an audience before addressing them. It fuses the call-particle 'yā' ('O') with a noun that means 'the one(s) addressed,' yielding an emphatic 'O you…!' that introduces direct address.
1.grammar: A vocative (calling) construction. 'Yā' is the particle for calling out; 'ayyu' carries a nominative '-u' as the one being summoned; 'hā' is an attention-drawing particle. Together they function as 'O you…!,' setting up the noun of address that follows.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
3.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

4.meaning: Be mindful and wary of — guard yourselves by placing a protective barrier between yourselves and harm or wrongdoing. This is the verb of taqwā: God-conscious caution that shields one from what is forbidden.
4.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a group ('you all'). The -ū ending directs the order to a masculine plural 'you.' Built on a reflexive pattern (Form VIII), it conveys 'protect yourselves / be on guard.'

5.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
5.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

6.meaning: And leave it / give it up — let a thing be and abandon it. A command to relinquish or forsake something; this verb supplies the present and command forms for 'to leave / forsake.'
6.grammar: The prefix wa- means 'and'. The stem is a command (imperative) meaning 'leave / forsake'; the -ū ending directs the order to a masculine plural 'you all.'
6.root: ذ-ر-و (dh-r-w) — to leave, abandon, forsake (final weak letter)

7.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
7.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

8.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'it remained, stayed behind, was left over, persisted, endured.' It denotes what continues to exist after others have gone or what is left as a residue or remainder.
8.grammar: A complete past-tense (perfect) verb in the third-person masculine singular: 'he/it remained.' The bare form with the final -a vowel marks a single masculine subject and an action viewed as already accomplished.
8.root: ب-ق-ي (b-q-y) — remaining, staying, enduring, what is left over

9.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
9.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

10.meaning: A noun meaning 'usury' or 'interest' — literally an 'increase' or 'growth' added to a loan or owed amount. It is the term for an unlawful surplus charged on top of a principal, the gain taken without just exchange.
10.grammar: A definite noun: the prefix al- ('the') makes it specific, pointing to usury as a known, defined thing rather than just 'some increase.' The base noun is spelled with a final wāw (-ā written long), a fixed feature of this word's form.

11.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
11.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

12.meaning: A past-tense verb of 'being' addressed to a group: 'you (all) were', 'you (all) used to be'. From kāna, the core verb 'to be'. With a following predicate it often means 'you were (in a state of) …' or 'you used to …'.
12.grammar: This is a past-tense verb. The '-tum' suffix is the attached subject marker for a masculine plural 'you all'. Since the doer is built into the suffix, the verb stands in its base past form ('you all were').
12.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

13.meaning: 'Believers / faithful ones' — the plural of muʾmin, one who has faith and trust in Allah and grants assent to the truth.

parts.en: believers (form IV participle, oblique masculine sound plural)

13.grammar: An active participle ('one who believes') from the form IV pattern, here a masculine sound plural. The single suffix -īna is the oblique (accusative/genitive) form of the masculine plural — used for a direct object or after a preposition — as opposed to the -ūna form used for the subject. Its nūn is part of the one ending and is not a separable morpheme.
13.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — security, trust; hence faith and belief

1.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'fa-' ('then', 'so', 'but') drawing a consequence, joined to the conditional particle 'in' ('if'). Together: 'then if …', 'but if …'.
1.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that signals a result or transition ('then/so'). 'in' is the conditional particle 'if', introducing a supposed condition. Both are indeclinable particles with no case ending.

2.meaning: The particle 'lam', a negating word used to push a verb into the past: it means 'did not' / 'has not'. Though it sits before a present-tense verb form, it negates the action as something that did not happen.
2.grammar: 'lam' is a negating particle that governs a following present-tense verb but gives it past meaning ('did not …'). It also puts that verb into the shortened (jussive) form. 'lam' itself carries no ending.

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'you (plural) do/make/act' — referring to an action carried out by a group being addressed. Built on the very common root for doing or performing a deed, it is the standard word for engaging in or carrying out an act.
3.grammar: Present/imperfect verb, 2nd person masculine plural. The ta- prefix signals a 'you' subject; the -ū ending marks a plural ('you all'). The bare -ū without a final nūn (rather than -ūna) shows the verb is in the subjunctive/jussive mood, the form used after particles of negation, purpose, or condition.

4.meaning: A command meaning 'then take notice, be informed, be on alert' — a directive to receive and register an announcement or warning, to know with certainty what is being declared.
4.grammar: A plural command (imperative) prefixed with fa- ('then/so'), which links it as a consequence of something preceding. It is a Form I imperative built on the root ʾ-dh-n: the leading alif is a connecting (elidable) alif carrying the glottal onset, and the -ū ending addresses a group of males (or a mixed group), instructing them all to take heed.
4.root: ا-ذ-ن (ʾ-dh-n) — giving ear, listening, taking notice, permission

5.meaning: A phrase meaning 'with/of a war' — naming armed conflict, hostility, or warfare. The attached preposition gives the sense 'by means of' or 'with' a war.
5.grammar: A noun 'war' carried by the preposition bi- ('with/by'). The final -in ending is the genitive with nunation (indefinite), as required after a preposition; the nunation marks it as 'a war' (one not yet specified).

6.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
6.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

7.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
7.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

8.meaning: A phrase meaning 'and His Messenger' — referring to one who is sent, an envoy or apostle bearing a message, joined by 'and' and possessed by 'His.'
8.grammar: 'Messenger' joined by wa- ('and') and followed by the possessive pronoun -hi ('his'). The -i vowel before the pronoun is the genitive case, here because the word is linked in possession ('Messenger OF Him'); the pronoun takes the -hi form (with i-vowel) when it follows an i-sound.
8.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — sending, dispatching; a message or one who is sent

9.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
9.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

10.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'you (all) repented, turned back.' It conveys turning away from wrongdoing and returning to Allah in remorse and amendment.
10.grammar: A past-tense verb with the subject-ending -tum, meaning 'you all' (a group of males or a mixed group) did the action. The action is presented as completed.

11.meaning: A phrase meaning 'then for you (all)' — expressing that something belongs to, is due to, or is in favor of the addressees. The lām conveys possession or entitlement.
11.grammar: Built from fa- ('then/so'), the preposition la- ('for/to'), and the attached pronoun -kum ('you all,' masc. or mixed). Together they mean 'then it is for you / yours,' often expressing entitlement.

12.meaning: A noun meaning 'heads' — the plural of 'head.' By extension it denotes the chief or principal part of a thing, hence the 'principal sum' or capital of money (the original 'head' amount, apart from any increase).
12.grammar: A plural noun with the final -u ending, the nominative case. The -u typically marks the word as the subject or the thing being identified (the 'doer' or topic), as opposed to an object or a possessed noun.
12.root: ر-أ-س (r-ʾ-s) — head; chief, principal, the top or main part

13.meaning: A phrase meaning 'your (plural) wealth / properties / possessions.' The base noun is the plural of māl ('wealth, property, goods'), denoting accumulated assets of any kind.
13.grammar: A plural noun followed by the possessive pronoun -kum ('your,' for a group). The -i vowel before the pronoun is the genitive case, here signalling possession ('wealth OF you').

14.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
14.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

15.meaning: A present/future-tense verb meaning 'you (all) wrong, do injustice, oppress, deal unfairly.' Its core sense is placing something where it does not belong — withholding a due right or transgressing against another.
15.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ta- prefix with the -ūna ending marks a plural masculine subject ('you all'). The full -ūna ending shows the verb is in its base (indicative) form, describing an ongoing or habitual action that is actually happening.
15.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — wrongdoing, injustice, oppression; putting a thing out of its place

16.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
16.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

17.meaning: You are wronged / treated unjustly — to have injustice done to one, to be deprived of a right or given less than one's due; the passive of doing wrong or oppression.
17.grammar: Present-tense passive verb, 2nd person masculine plural ('you all are …'). The tu- prefix with this vowel pattern marks the passive and the 'you' subject; the -ūna ending marks a plural subject and the indicative mood — the plain factual form stating something that happens or will happen. Passive voice means the people receive the action ('are wronged') rather than do it.
17.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — to wrong, to do injustice, oppression

1.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
1.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

2.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

2.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

3.meaning: Owner of / possessor of / endowed with — a word that does not stand alone but means 'the one who has' whatever noun follows it, ascribing that quality or possession to someone.

parts.en: possessor of, owner of, endowed with

3.grammar: A possessive noun meaning 'owner/possessor of', always followed by another noun in the genitive. The final -ū form here is the nominative case, used when this word names the subject or is the thing being described; it inherently requires a following noun to complete its sense ('owner OF …').
3.root: — (no triliteral root; an irregular noun of possession)

4.meaning: A noun meaning 'hardship, difficulty, straitened circumstances' — especially financial distress, a state of being hard-pressed and lacking means.
4.grammar: A noun with the -in ending (with nunation, written here as -tin where the feminine ending joins the case vowel). This is the genitive indefinite ('a hardship'), the form used after prepositions or in a linked 'of' relationship.
4.root: ع-س-ر (ʿ-s-r) — difficulty, hardship, being hard or straitened

5.meaning: A phrase meaning 'then a postponement, a granting of more time, a deferral.' It names the act of giving a debtor extra time and waiting patiently for repayment.
5.grammar: A noun prefixed with fa- ('then/so'). The -un ending (with nunation, here -tun joining the feminine ending) is the nominative indefinite, marking the word as the subject or the thing being stated — 'then [there is/let there be] a respite.'
5.root: ن-ظ-ر (n-ẓ-r) — looking, waiting, granting time, observing

6.meaning: A preposition meaning 'to,' 'toward,' or 'up to' — pointing to the end-point, goal, or limit of a motion, direction, or extent.
6.grammar: A preposition (a small linking word). It governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the genitive case, and points to a destination or limit ('to,' 'toward,' 'as far as').

7.meaning: A noun meaning 'ease, a time of ease, prosperity, affluence' — a state of comfort and sufficient means, the relief that follows hardship.
7.grammar: A noun with the -in ending (with nunation, here -tin where the feminine ending joins the case vowel): the genitive indefinite ('an ease / a time of ease'), the form used after a preposition or in an 'of' linkage.
7.root: ي-س-ر (y-s-r) — ease, facility, being easy or well-off

8.meaning: A two-part connector: 'and that.' The 'wa' joins what precedes, and 'an' is the subordinating particle 'that,' which introduces a following verb-clause (often steering it into the subjunctive) — used to report or quote a command, statement, or purpose.
8.grammar: The conjunction wa- ('and') plus the particle an, a subordinator meaning 'that' which heads a clause and commonly puts a following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood (often expressing purpose, intention, or reported speech). It is a particle and does not itself take a case ending.

9.meaning: A verb meaning 'you (all) give as charity, donate freely, remit out of generosity.' Its sense is to give up something willingly for the sake of Allah, including waiving a debt as an act of charity.
9.grammar: A Form V verb (tafaʿʿala pattern, with a doubled middle root letter, giving the sense of doing the act for and upon oneself, willingly). The -ū ending marks a plural masculine subject, 'you all.' This particular form serves as a plural imperative ('give charity, you all'), a direct command rather than a statement.
9.root: ص-د-ق (ṣ-d-q) — truthfulness, sincerity; giving charity (ṣadaqa) as a proof of sincere faith

10.meaning: 'Better / best; good' — an adjective of comparison meaning more good, preferable, or superior. It also serves broadly for 'goodness' and that which is good and beneficial.
10.grammar: A noun/adjective bearing the ending -un (nunation): the doubled-u 'n' sound marks the word as both indefinite ('a/an', no 'the') and nominative — the case used for the subject of a sentence or the predicate that describes it.
10.root: خ-ي-ر (kh-y-r) — good, goodness, that which is choice and beneficial

11.meaning: 'for you,' 'to you,' 'for your benefit' — the preposition 'for/to' joined to 'you (plural).' It marks the party for whose sake, benefit, or possession something exists or is given.
11.grammar: A preposition ('for/to') with the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you, plural'). It assigns a benefit, purpose, or recipient — 'for you (all).' The suffix '-kum' is the plural 'you,' showing the recipients are a group.

12.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
12.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

13.meaning: A past-tense verb of 'being' addressed to a group: 'you (all) were', 'you (all) used to be'. From kāna, the core verb 'to be'. With a following predicate it often means 'you were (in a state of) …' or 'you used to …'.
13.grammar: This is a past-tense verb. The '-tum' suffix is the attached subject marker for a masculine plural 'you all'. Since the doer is built into the suffix, the verb stands in its base past form ('you all were').
13.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

14.meaning: A verb addressed to a group: 'you (all) know', 'you have knowledge', 'you are aware'. From the root meaning 'to know'.
14.grammar: The 'ta-' prefix marks a present/future verb addressed to 'you'. The '-ūna' ending marks a masculine plural subject and is the full 'indicative' form, signalling an ongoing, factual statement ('you (all) do know'), as opposed to the shortened '-ū' used after certain particles.

1.meaning: A command addressed to a group: 'guard yourselves / be mindful and on your guard.' The verb conveys taqwā — protecting oneself by being conscious of Allah and shielding oneself from wrongdoing and its consequences.
1.grammar: An imperative (command) verb addressed to a plural 'you (all).' The -ū ending marks the masculine plural addressees ('you all'). The pattern (form VIII, from waqā 'to protect') gives the sense of taking protective care for oneself.
1.root: و-ق-ي (w-q-y) — to guard, shield, protect oneself

2.meaning: A day; a defined stretch of time. Often used for a momentous appointed day such as a day of judgement or reckoning.
2.grammar: A singular masculine noun, indefinite ('a day'). The -an ending (tanwīn fatḥa) is the indefinite accusative case, which typically marks the object of a verb or a noun otherwise governed in the accusative.

3.meaning: 'You are returned / brought back' — a passive verb from the root meaning to return: the subjects are made to go back, sent back to a point of origin, the action being done to them rather than by them.
3.grammar: Present/future passive. The tu- prefix with the -ūna ending marks a second-person masculine plural subject ('you all'), and the internal vowelling (u–a) makes it passive — the action is done TO the subject. The -ūna ending is the full ('indicative') plural form, used when the verb is not cut short by certain particles.

4.meaning: 'In it / in him' — the preposition 'in, inside, within' joined to a pronoun referring to a single masculine or neuter thing. It locates something inside or as part of that referent.
4.grammar: A preposition with an attached object pronoun. The pronoun -hi refers to one masculine (or grammatically masculine) thing and stands as the object of the preposition; its vowel is -i because attached pronouns take that shape after the long -i of fi. Together they answer 'in what?' or 'in whom?'.

5.meaning: 'To / toward / up to' — a preposition marking the endpoint, goal, or limit of an action or motion: the direction something moves toward or the boundary at which it stops.
5.grammar: An invariable preposition. It has no case ending of its own but puts the noun that follows it into the genitive ('of / to' state). It indicates direction toward, or the terminal limit of, something.

6.meaning: The proper name of the One True God in Arabic, Allāh — the unique, absolute Divine Being, alone worthy of worship. Used by Arabic-speaking Muslims, Christians, and Jews for the one Creator and Lord of all.
6.grammar: The proper divine name. The final '-i' is the genitive ending, which typically follows a preposition or links this name to a preceding noun in a possessive 'of Allah / belonging to Allah' relationship.

7.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
7.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

8.meaning: A present/future-tense passive verb meaning 'it is paid in full, repaid completely, given its full due.' The pattern conveys discharging an obligation entirely, leaving nothing owed.
8.grammar: A present-tense passive verb (the tu- prefix with the inner vowel pattern marks 'is being done to'). It is third-person feminine singular: 'she/it is paid in full.' The verb is built on the Form II intensive pattern (doubled middle root), stressing completeness — full and thorough payment. The final long -ā reflects the weak final root letter.
8.root: و-ف-ي (w-f-y) — fulfilling, completing, paying in full, keeping faith with an obligation

9.meaning: A noun meaning 'all, every, each, the whole of.' It expresses totality — when joined to a following noun it means 'every (one)' or 'the entirety of' that thing.
9.grammar: A noun of totality with the final -u ending (nominative). The -u typically marks it as the subject or the thing being spoken about. It normally attaches to a following noun to mean 'every / all of' it.

10.meaning: A noun meaning 'soul, self, person, living being.' It denotes the inner self or the whole individual — the seat of life and identity, and by extension a 'person' as a single unit.
10.grammar: A noun with the -in ending (with nunation): the genitive indefinite ('a soul'). This form appears after prepositions or in an 'of' linkage with a preceding noun (such as 'every soul').
10.root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s) — soul, self, breath; the inner being

11.meaning: A short, highly versatile particle 'mā.' It can mean 'what' or 'that which,' can negate ('not'), and can serve as an intensifier attached to another word. Its precise force depends on what it accompanies, but its core is to point to a thing or to add emphasis.
11.grammar: A multifunctional particle. It does not take case endings. Depending on usage it can be a relative ('that which'), an interrogative ('what?'), a negator ('not'), or — when joined to another particle — an emphasizer. It is uninflected and indeclinable.

12.meaning: 'It earned / acquired, gained' — said of deeds and their consequences; the root means to gain or acquire something, especially the moral 'earnings' of one's actions.
12.grammar: Past-tense verb. The -t (sukūn-marked -at) suffix marks a third-person feminine singular subject, 'she/it.' The past tense presents the action as completed.
12.root: ك-س-ب (k-s-b) — to earn, acquire, gain (esp. deeds)

13.meaning: 'While they / and they' — the word 'wa' (here 'while' or 'and') joined to the standalone pronoun 'hum' ('they'), referring to a masculine plural group.
13.grammar: A connective 'wa' — often circumstantial 'while' — plus the independent subject pronoun 'hum' ('they'), used for a masculine plural group. As an independent pronoun it usually stands as the subject of a following statement.

14.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
14.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

15.meaning: A present/future-tense passive verb meaning 'they are wronged, treated unjustly, dealt with unfairly.' It is the receiving end of injustice — to have one's due withheld or to be oppressed.
15.grammar: A present-tense passive verb: the yu- prefix with the inner a-vowel pattern marks 'are being done to,' and the -ūna ending marks a plural masculine subject ('they'). The full -ūna shows the base (indicative) form — an action genuinely taking place: 'they are [being] wronged.'
15.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — wrongdoing, injustice, oppression; putting a thing out of its place

1.meaning: 'O…!' — a compound vocative expression used to call out and summon an audience before addressing them. It fuses the call-particle 'yā' ('O') with a noun that means 'the one(s) addressed,' yielding an emphatic 'O you…!' that introduces direct address.
1.grammar: A vocative (calling) construction. 'Yā' is the particle for calling out; 'ayyu' carries a nominative '-u' as the one being summoned; 'hā' is an attention-drawing particle. Together they function as 'O you…!,' setting up the noun of address that follows.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
3.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

4.meaning: 'When' — a particle introducing a time or circumstance, generally pointing to something expected or definite to come ('when/whenever it happens'). It sets up a condition or moment whose outcome then follows.
4.grammar: An indeclinable adverb/particle of time; it has no case ending and never changes form. It typically introduces a clause about a future or recurring event ('when …'), and is normally followed by a verb describing what takes place.

5.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'you (all) dealt with one another in lending/borrowing, contracted a mutual debt, transacted credit between yourselves.' The pattern signals a reciprocal action done between parties.
5.grammar: A past-tense verb in the Form VI reciprocal pattern (tafāʿala: the ta- prefix with a long vowel after the first root letter conveys 'doing something to one another'). The -tum ending marks the subject as 'you all' (masculine or mixed group), with the action presented as completed.
5.root: د-ي-ن (d-y-n) — debt, loan, owing; also obligation and recompense

6.meaning: A phrase meaning 'with/by a debt' — a debt being something owed, a loan or obligation to be repaid, especially over a stated term.
6.grammar: The noun 'debt' carried by the preposition bi- ('with/by'). The -in ending (with nunation) is the genitive indefinite ('a debt'), required after the preposition.

7.meaning: "to / towards" — a preposition marking the end-point, goal, or direction of a movement or extent ("up to," "as far as," "toward").
7.grammar: An indeclinable preposition; it has no case ending of its own and always governs a following noun in the genitive case.

8.meaning: A noun meaning 'a fixed term, an appointed time, a set deadline, a span allotted before something falls due.' It denotes the limit or end-point of a period.
8.grammar: A noun with the -in ending (with nunation): the genitive indefinite ('a term'). This form occurs after a preposition or in an 'of' linkage with a preceding noun.
8.root: ا-ج-ل (ʾ-j-l) — appointed term, fixed time, deadline

9.meaning: A passive participle meaning 'named, specified, designated, made definite.' It describes something that has been clearly stated and fixed by name — a term that is precisely set rather than vague.
9.grammar: A passive participle (the mu- prefix forms a 'one that is …' word from the Form II intensive pattern, with a doubled middle root letter) meaning 'named/specified.' It carries the indefinite ending -an, written with alif maqṣūra (a final ya-shaped letter sounded as -ā). Because it ends in this weak final letter, the form stays the same whether nominative, accusative, or genitive — context shows it is describing an indefinite noun.
9.root: س-م-ي (s-m-y) — name, naming; to give or assign a name

10.meaning: A command meaning 'then write it down, record it' — an instruction to put something into writing and document it.
10.grammar: A plural command prefixed with fa- ('then/so'), with the -ū ending addressing a group ('you all,' masc. or mixed) and the object pronoun -hu ('it') attached at the end: 'then write it down.' The pronoun takes the -hu form (with u-vowel) after the long -ū.

11.meaning: A phrase meaning 'and let him write' — issuing an indirect command in the third person, directing that a particular writer should do the writing.
11.grammar: Built from wa- ('and') plus the command-particle li- (here pronounced l-) attached to a present-tense verb, which together form a third-person command: 'let him write.' The verb is third-person masculine singular ('he'), and the particle puts it into its shortened (jussive) form, ending in a bare consonant, which is how 'let him do…' is expressed.

12.meaning: An adverb of place meaning 'between' or 'among', joined to a 'you (plural)' pronoun, so it conveys 'between you all' or 'amongst you' — pointing to a space or relationship shared by a group.
12.grammar: An adverb of place in the accusative (the fixed -a of 'bayna'), naturally read as 'between/among'. The attached -kum is a possessive/object pronoun for a group of males or a mixed group ('you all').
12.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinctness, what lies in the midst

13.meaning: An active participle meaning 'one who writes' — a writer, scribe, or recorder; the person performing the act of writing.
13.grammar: An active participle (the 'doer' pattern fāʿil) in the singular indefinite. The -un ending (nominative with tanwīn) marks it as 'a scribe' standing typically as a subject or as the thing being described.

14.meaning: The noun 'justice / fairness / equity' introduced by the preposition 'with/in', giving the sense 'with justice' or 'in fairness' — doing something in a balanced, even-handed manner.
14.grammar: A preposition 'bi-' plus the definite noun 'al-ʿadl'. The -i ending is genitive, which is required after the preposition; the whole phrase functions adverbially ('with/in justice').
14.root: ع-د-ل (ʿ-d-l) — justice, fairness, balance, setting straight

15.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
15.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

16.meaning: A verb meaning 'to refuse', 'be unwilling', or 'decline' — to hold back from doing something, often out of reluctance or disdain.

parts.en: refuse (verb stem; hamza is the first root letter)

16.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular ('he refuses'). The ya- prefix marks 'he' as the doer; the stem 'ʾaba' opens with the hamza (ء), the first radical of the root, followed by the -a vowel that reflects a subjunctive/jussive shaping (commonly after a particle), signalling 'should/would refuse' rather than a plain statement.

17.meaning: An active participle meaning 'one who writes' — a writer, scribe, or recorder; the person performing the act of writing.
17.grammar: An active participle (the 'doer' pattern fāʿil) in the singular indefinite. The -un ending (nominative with tanwīn) marks it as 'a scribe' standing typically as a subject or as the thing being described.

18.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
18.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'
18.root: — (particle; no root)

19.meaning: A verb meaning 'he writes' or 'he should write' — the act of putting something down in writing.
19.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular. The ya- prefix means 'he'; the final -a is the subjunctive vowel, which appears after certain particles (like 'that' or 'so that') and gives the sense 'that he write / for him to write'.

20.meaning: 'Just as / in the same way that' — a phrase of comparison joining 'like / as' to 'what', meaning 'like that which...' or 'in the manner that...'.
20.grammar: The comparison particle ka- ('like / as') joined to mā ('what / that which'). Together they introduce a likeness or manner — 'just as...', 'in the same way that...' — comparing one thing or action to another.

21.meaning: A verb meaning 'he taught him' or 'he instructed him' — to impart knowledge or skill to someone, with intensive force (thorough teaching).
21.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb of the doubled/intensive pattern (Form II faʿʿala), 3rd person masculine singular. The -a ending marks 'he' as the one who did it in the past; the attached -hu is the object 'him' (the one taught).

22.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
22.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

23.meaning: A command-form verb meaning 'so let him write' — an indirect imperative directing that someone should perform the act of writing.
23.grammar: A connector 'fa-' ('so/then') plus the imperative lām ('let…') attached to a present-tense 3rd person masculine verb. This combination forms a command directed at a third party ('let him write'); the verb takes the jussive (vowel-less ending -b), the mood used for such commands.

24.meaning: A command-form verb meaning 'and let (him) dictate' — directing that someone should dictate or state aloud the wording for another to write down.
24.grammar: Connector 'wa-' ('and') plus the imperative lām ('let…') on a present-tense 3rd person masculine causative verb (Form IV). It forms a third-party command ('and let him dictate'); the verb is jussive, and the final -i is a helping vowel added only to ease pronunciation before a following word.
24.root: م-ل-ل (m-l-l) — dictating, stating for someone to write down

25.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
25.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

26.meaning: A preposition fused with a pronoun, meaning 'upon him', 'on him', or 'toward him'. It marks the one to whom an action is directed or upon whom something rests.
26.grammar: The preposition 'upon/on' with an attached object pronoun -hi ('him', third-person masculine singular); its -i vowel is the regular form the pronoun takes after the 'y' sound. Paired with a verb of turning, this 'upon/toward him' marks the person the action reaches.

27.meaning: 'The truth / the reality; what is right, real, and rightfully due.' A weighty noun meaning that which is firmly true and real, as opposed to falsehood; it also carries the senses of a rightful claim, a duty owed, and justice. With the article it denotes 'the Truth' in a definite, absolute sense.
27.grammar: A definite noun: the prefix al- ('the') plus the stem. The final -u ending is the nominative case, typically used for the subject of a sentence or for a word identifying what something is (as in 'X is the truth').
27.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, reality, rightness; that which is established and rightfully due

28.meaning: A command-form verb meaning 'and let him be mindful of / fear / guard himself before' — directing someone to hold a reverent, God-conscious awareness that restrains wrongdoing (the concept of taqwā).

parts.en: he is mindful / fears (reflexively guards himself)
ending after a dropped weak letter

28.grammar: Connector 'wa-' ('and') plus the imperative lām ('let…') on a present-tense 3rd person masculine reflexive verb (Form VIII). It forms a third-party command ('and let him be mindful'); the verb is jussive, and the final -i appears because the original weak final letter (yāʾ) is dropped, leaving the short vowel.
28.root: و-ق-ي (w-q-y) — guarding, shielding, protecting oneself; the basis of taqwā (God-conscious mindfulness)

29.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
29.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.
29.root: — (proper name)

30.meaning: The noun 'Lord' joined to a 'his' pronoun — 'his Lord'. Rabb conveys the Master and Sustainer who owns, nurtures, and brings a thing to its full development; far richer than 'lord' alone.
30.grammar: A noun with the attached possessive pronoun -hu ('his'). The -a ending is accusative, the case used when the noun is an object of a verb or otherwise governed into that case; -hu means it belongs to 'him'.
30.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship, ownership, nurturing and sustaining to completion

31.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
31.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

32.meaning: A verb meaning 'to diminish', 'to short-change', or 'to give less than is due' — to deduct or withhold part of what rightfully belongs to another.
32.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular. The ya- prefix marks 'he' as the doer; the vowel-less ending (-s, jussive) typically appears after a negating or conditional particle, e.g. 'let him not diminish' or 'if he diminishes'.
32.root: ب-خ-س (b-kh-s) — diminishing, defrauding, giving short measure

33.meaning: 'From it / out of it / from him'. It combines the preposition 'from / out of' with the pronoun 'it/him'.
33.grammar: The preposition min ('from / out of', indicating origin or source) with the attached pronoun -hu ('it' / 'him'), referring to a singular masculine thing or person. As object of the preposition, the pronoun is in the oblique form.
33.root: — (no triliteral root; a preposition with a pronoun)

34.meaning: A thing; something or anything. With a negation it commonly amounts to 'nothing at all.'
34.grammar: A singular masculine noun, indefinite ('a thing'). The -an ending (tanwīn fatḥa) is the indefinite accusative, often used here as an object or an adverbial 'in any respect / at all.'
34.root: ش-ي-أ (sh-y-ʾ) — thing, to will

35.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'fa-' ('then', 'so', 'but') drawing a consequence, joined to the conditional particle 'in' ('if'). Together: 'then if …', 'but if …'.
35.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that signals a result or transition ('then/so'). 'in' is the conditional particle 'if', introducing a supposed condition. Both are indeclinable particles with no case ending.

36.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

36.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.
36.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existence; to be

37.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
37.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

38.meaning: A preposition fused with a pronoun, meaning 'upon him', 'on him', or 'toward him'. It marks the one to whom an action is directed or upon whom something rests.
38.grammar: The preposition 'upon/on' with an attached object pronoun -hi ('him', third-person masculine singular); its -i vowel is the regular form the pronoun takes after the 'y' sound. Paired with a verb of turning, this 'upon/toward him' marks the person the action reaches.

39.meaning: 'The truth / the reality; what is right, real, and rightfully due.' A weighty noun meaning that which is firmly true and real, as opposed to falsehood; it also carries the senses of a rightful claim, a duty owed, and justice. With the article it denotes 'the Truth' in a definite, absolute sense.
39.grammar: A definite noun: the prefix al- ('the') plus the stem. The final -u ending is the nominative case, typically used for the subject of a sentence or for a word identifying what something is (as in 'X is the truth').
39.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, reality, rightness; that which is established and rightfully due

40.meaning: A noun/adjective meaning 'foolish', 'of weak judgment', or 'mentally immature' — someone lacking sound discernment in handling affairs.
40.grammar: A descriptive noun on the intensive pattern faʿīl, singular indefinite. The -an ending (accusative with tanwīn) marks it as 'a foolish one' standing as an object, or as a predicate describing someone.
40.root: س-ف-ه (s-f-h) — foolishness, deficiency of judgment, lightness of mind

41.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
41.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

42.meaning: A noun/adjective meaning 'weak', 'frail', or 'feeble' — lacking strength, whether in body, capacity, or means.
42.grammar: A descriptive noun on the intensive pattern faʿīl, singular indefinite. The -an ending (accusative with tanwīn) marks it as 'a weak one' standing as an object, or as a predicate describing someone.
42.root: ض-ع-ف (ḍ-ʿ-f) — weakness, feebleness, lack of strength

43.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
43.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

44.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
44.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

45.meaning: A verb meaning 'he is able / capable', 'he has the power to' — possessing the ability or capacity to do something. (Form X of the root, conveying 'to be able'.)

parts.en: is able / has the capacity (verb stem)

45.grammar: A present/imperfect verb of the seeking/capacity pattern (Form X istafʿala), 3rd person masculine singular. The ya- prefix means 'he'; the final -u is the indicative ending, marking a plain factual statement ('he is able / he can').
45.root: ط-و-ع (ṭ-w-ʿ) — willing obedience, capacity, being able

46.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
46.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

47.meaning: A verb meaning 'he dictates' or 'he can dictate' — to state aloud the wording for another to write down. (A variant form of the same act as 'yumlil'.)
47.grammar: A present/imperfect causative verb (Form IV), 3rd person masculine singular, with the two identical root letters merged (shown by the doubling/shadda). The yu- prefix marks 'he' in this pattern; the final -a is the subjunctive vowel, appearing after particles like 'that / so that' ('that he dictate').
47.root: م-ل-ل (m-l-l) — dictating, stating for someone to write down

48.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
48.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

49.meaning: A command-form verb meaning 'then let (him) dictate' — directing that someone should dictate or state aloud the wording for another to record.
49.grammar: Connector 'fa-' ('then/so') plus the imperative lām ('let…') on a present-tense 3rd person masculine causative verb (Form IV). It forms a third-party command ('then let him dictate'); the verb takes the jussive (vowel-less ending -l), the mood used for such commands.
49.root: م-ل-ل (m-l-l) — dictating, stating for someone to write down

50.meaning: The noun 'guardian / protecting ally / one in charge' joined to a 'his' pronoun — 'his guardian'. A walī is one who is close to and responsible for another, holding authority to act on their behalf.
50.grammar: A noun on the intensive faʿīl pattern with the attached possessive pronoun -hu ('his'). The -u ending is nominative, the case typically used for the subject or doer; -hu marks that the guardian belongs to 'him'.
50.root: و-ل-ي (w-l-y) — nearness, guardianship, allegiance, taking charge of another

51.meaning: The noun 'justice / fairness / equity' introduced by the preposition 'with/in', giving the sense 'with justice' or 'in fairness' — acting in a balanced, even-handed manner.
51.grammar: A preposition 'bi-' plus the definite noun 'al-ʿadl'. The -i ending is genitive, which is required after the preposition; the whole phrase functions adverbially ('with/in justice').
51.root: ع-د-ل (ʿ-d-l) — justice, fairness, balance, setting straight

52.meaning: A command-form verb addressed to a group meaning 'and call (someone) to bear witness', 'and seek out witnesses' — to summon people to testify or provide evidence. (Form X: 'to seek a witness'.)

parts.en: seek witnesses / call to testify (verb stem)

52.grammar: Connector 'wa-' ('and') plus a plural imperative of the seeking pattern (Form X istafʿala). The -ū ending is the masculine plural command marker, addressing a group ('you all, seek witnesses'); the silent alif after it is a spelling convention.
52.root: ش-ه-د (sh-h-d) — witnessing, being present, giving testimony

53.meaning: The noun 'witness' in the dual, meaning 'two witnesses' — exactly two people who testify or attest to something.
53.grammar: A noun on the intensive faʿīl pattern in the dual (exactly two). The -ayni ending marks 'two witnesses' and is the dual form used in the accusative/genitive (as an object, or after a preposition or governing word).
53.root: ش-ه-د (sh-h-d) — witnessing, being present, giving testimony
