5.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
5.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

6.meaning: A noun meaning 'its capacity', 'its scope', or 'what is within its power' — the full extent of ability or means that something possesses. From a word for room, breadth, or ability, with a possessive 'its'.
6.grammar: A noun with the accusative -a ending, the case typically marking the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon). The attached -hā means 'its' or 'her', so the whole means 'its capacity'. The accusative here signals it as what a verb falls upon.
6.root: و-س-ع (w-s-ʿ) — to be wide, spacious, to have room or capacity

7.meaning: 'For it / to it, belonging to it' — the preposition 'for/to' joined to a pronoun referring to a feminine singular thing; it expresses possession or benefit ('it has / it gets').
7.grammar: Preposition 'li-' (here vowelled 'la-' before a pronoun) plus an attached object pronoun. The -hā suffix means 'it/her,' a feminine singular. Pronouns that follow a preposition are in the genitive (object-of-preposition) role; -hā is a fixed form and does not change shape.

8.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
8.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

9.meaning: 'It earned / acquired, gained' — said of deeds and their consequences; the root means to gain or acquire something, especially the moral 'earnings' of one's actions.
9.grammar: Past-tense verb. The -t (sukūn-marked -at) suffix marks a third-person feminine singular subject, 'she/it.' The past tense presents the action as completed.
9.root: ك-س-ب (k-s-b) — to earn, acquire, gain (esp. deeds)

10.meaning: "and upon it / and against it" — wa- joins it on; ʿalā is the preposition 'upon / on / against,' and -hā means 'it/her,' so 'upon it' — often in the sense of something counting against a person.
10.grammar: A preposition ('upon/against') with an attached pronoun. The base ʿalā shifts to ʿalay- before a pronoun, and -hā means 'it/her' (referring to a feminine or grammatically feminine thing). It conveys something resting on, or held against, that thing.

11.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
11.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

12.meaning: "it earned / it acquired" — to gain or acquire something through one's own effort and deliberate action; the derived (eighth) form stresses personal, purposeful acquisition, often of what one is answerable for.
12.grammar: A past-tense verb in a derived (reflexive-effort) form, with the suffix -at ('she/it,' feminine). Past tense shows a completed action ('it earned'); the -t marks a feminine singular doer.
12.root: ك-س-ب (k-s-b) — to gain, earn, acquire by effort

13.meaning: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'our': the Master who creates, owns, sustains, and lovingly nurtures, addressed collectively as 'our Lord' — a communal calling upon the Sustainer.

parts.en: accusative ending (vocative of a possessed noun)

Because the noun is possessed (a muḍāf) and called out in the vocative, it takes the accusative; that -a case vowel sits on the doubled consonant before the pronoun. The pronoun -nā shows the address is made by a group.
13.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

14.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
14.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

15.meaning: "(do not) hold us to account / call us to reckoning" — to take someone to task, to seize and call them to answer for what they have done. The derived (mutual/intensive) form conveys confronting someone over their deeds.

parts.en: take to task / call to account

15.grammar: Present-tense verb, second-person masculine singular ('you'), in a derived (mutual/confrontational) form, with the object suffix -nā ('us'). The tu- prefix marks 'you (do)'; the bare final consonant (no end-vowel, sukūn on the ذ) is the shortened/jussive form, the form used after words like 'do not' or in requests; the -nā ending marks 'us' as the ones acted upon.

16.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
16.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

17.meaning: "we forgot / we have forgotten" — to fail to recall, to let something slip from the mind; can also carry the sense of neglecting or overlooking a duty.
17.grammar: A past-tense verb with the subject suffix -nā meaning 'we.' Past tense presents the action as completed ('we forgot'); the -nā shows 'we' are the ones who did it.
17.root: ن-س-ي (n-s-y) — to forget, to neglect, to overlook

18.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
18.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

19.meaning: "we erred / we made a mistake" — to do wrong unintentionally, to miss the mark or slip into a fault without meaning to (as opposed to deliberate wrongdoing).
19.grammar: A past-tense verb with the subject suffix -nā meaning 'we.' Past tense shows a completed action ('we erred'); the -nā marks 'we' as the doers.
19.root: خ-ط-ء (kh-ṭ-ʾ) — to err, miss the mark, make a mistake

20.meaning: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'our': the Master who creates, owns, sustains, and lovingly nurtures, addressed collectively as 'our Lord' — a communal calling upon the Sustainer.

parts.en: accusative ending (vocative of a possessed noun)

20.grammar: The noun rabb with the attached first-person plural pronoun -nā ('our'). It is used as a vocative, calling out 'O our Lord'. Because the noun is possessed (a muḍāf) and called out in the vocative, it takes the accusative; that -a case vowel sits on the doubled consonant before the pronoun. The pronoun -nā shows the address is made by a group.
20.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

21.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
21.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

22.meaning: "(do not) lay / load / impose" — to carry or bear, and so to place a load or burden upon someone, to make them bear it.
22.grammar: Present-tense verb, second-person masculine singular ('you'). The ta- prefix marks 'you (do),' and the bare final consonant (no end-vowel, -mil) is the shortened/jussive form, the form used after words like 'do not' or in requests and commands.

23.meaning: 'Upon us' / 'over us' / 'against us' — the preposition ʿalā ('on, over, upon') with an attached 'us'. It conveys something resting on, incumbent upon, or bearing against the group.
23.grammar: A preposition (ʿalā, 'upon/over') with an attached pronoun, first person plural (-nā, 'us'). When a pronoun is attached, ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay-. Such prepositional phrases put their pronoun in the object/genitive role.

24.meaning: "a heavy burden / a binding load" — a weight or obligation that presses down, often a severe, constraining duty or covenant that holds one back; sometimes a binding pledge.
24.grammar: A singular noun, indefinite ('a burden'). The -an ending combines the object (accusative) case with indefiniteness ('a/some'); it marks the noun as the undefined thing being acted upon.
24.root: ء-ص-ر (ʾ-ṣ-r) — to bind, confine; a heavy, binding burden

25.meaning: 'Just as / in the same way that' — a phrase of comparison joining 'like / as' to 'what', meaning 'like that which...' or 'in the manner that...'.
25.grammar: The comparison particle ka- ('like / as') joined to mā ('what / that which'). Together they introduce a likeness or manner — 'just as...', 'in the same way that...' — comparing one thing or action to another.

26.meaning: "You laid it / You placed it (as a load)" — to carry or bear, and so to load it onto someone or make them carry it; the attached -hu ('it') is the burden placed.
26.grammar: A past-tense verb with the subject suffix -ta ('you,' one male) and the object suffix -hu ('it'). Past tense shows a completed action ('you laid'); -ta marks 'you' as the doer and -hu marks 'it' as the thing laid.

27.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
27.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
27.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

28.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
28.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

29.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
29.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
29.root: — (preposition)

30.meaning: "our before / (the time) before us" — qabl is 'before' in time, what came earlier; the attached -nā means 'us,' giving 'before us' (those who preceded us, or the time prior to ours).
30.grammar: A time word ('before') with an attached pronoun. The -i ending is the genitive (possessive/'of') case, here because it follows a preposition; -nā means 'us.' Such words point to an earlier point in time.
30.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to precede, come before; priorness, frontness

31.meaning: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'our': the Master who creates, owns, sustains, and lovingly nurtures, addressed collectively as 'our Lord' — a communal calling upon the Sustainer.

parts.en: accusative ending (vocative of a possessed noun)

31.grammar: The noun rabb with the attached first-person plural pronoun -nā ('our'). It is used as a vocative, calling out 'O our Lord'. Because the noun is possessed (a muḍāf) and called out in the vocative, it takes the accusative; that -a case vowel sits on the doubled consonant before the pronoun. The pronoun -nā shows the address is made by a group.
31.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

32.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
32.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

33.meaning: "(do not) make us bear / load upon us" — to make someone carry a load, to impose a burden and force them to bear it. The doubled middle consonant intensifies it to 'make/force to carry.'
33.grammar: Present-tense verb, second-person masculine singular ('you'), in a derived (causative/intensive) form ('make to carry'), with the object suffix -nā ('us'). The tu- prefix marks 'you,' the bare final consonant (-mil, no end-vowel) is the shortened/jussive form used after 'do not' or in requests, and -nā marks 'us' as those acted upon.

34.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
34.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

35.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
35.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

36.meaning: Strength, capacity, or the power to endure; the ability to bear or withstand something, the energy one can muster for a task.
36.grammar: A feminine singular noun in the 'construct' state (iḍāfa), where it leans on a following noun ('strength OF / for …'). The tell-tale sign is that the final -a carries NO nunation: a free-standing accusative would normally take -an (tanwīn), so the bare -a without it marks the word as bound to what follows. The vowel itself is accusative, the form taken here as the noun governed in the 'no … whatsoever' negating construction with lā ('no strength to …').
36.root: ط-و-ق (ṭ-w-q) — capacity, ability, the utmost one can bear

37.meaning: A combination of the preposition 'for / to' with the pronoun 'us', meaning 'for us' or 'to us / on our behalf'.
37.grammar: A preposition ('for / to') joined to the attached pronoun 'us'. The pronoun -nā always means 'us / our' regardless of position. Together they express benefit or direction toward the speakers ('for us').

38.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
38.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

39.meaning: "and pardon / and efface" — wa- joins it on; the verb means to pardon and wipe away an offence, to overlook it so completely that it leaves no trace (its root sense is 'to erase').
39.grammar: A command/request verb addressed to one person ('pardon!'). It comes from a root whose last letter is a weak vowel, which is dropped in the command, leaving the final -u sound; it asks the one addressed to perform the act.
39.root: ع-ف-و (ʿ-f-w) — to erase, efface; to pardon, excuse

40.meaning: "from us / on our behalf" — ʿan is the preposition 'from / away from / concerning,' and the attached -nā means 'us,' giving 'from us' (often in the sense of pardoning faults away from us).
40.grammar: A preposition ('from / away from') with the attached pronoun -nā ('us'). The n of ʿan blends into the n of -nā (written doubled). It conveys moving away from, or being concerning, the thing named.
40.root: — (preposition)

41.meaning: "and forgive / and cover over" — wa- joins it on; the verb means to forgive, to cover over and shield a sin so it is not exposed or held against the person.
41.grammar: A command/request verb addressed to one person ('forgive!'). The bare consonant ending (-fir, no end-vowel) is the command form, and the helping vowel at the start (i-) lets the cluster be pronounced; it asks the one addressed to perform the act.
41.root: غ-ف-ر (gh-f-r) — to cover, shield; to forgive, pardon

42.meaning: "for us / to us" — li is the preposition 'for / to,' marking benefit or recipient, and the attached -nā means 'us,' giving 'for us' (in our favour).
42.grammar: A preposition ('for/to') with the attached pronoun -nā ('us'). The preposition li- is normally written with i, but takes the vowel 'a' (la-) before an attached pronoun. It marks the one who benefits or receives.
42.root: — (preposition)

43.meaning: A plea joined to what precedes it: 'and show us mercy / be merciful to us.' It is an appeal for Allah's compassion to be extended toward the speakers as a group.
43.grammar: A command (imperative) verb: it requests or pleads for an action to be done. The bare, vowelless stem (rḥam) is the singular command form, addressed to one party. The attached -nā is the object pronoun 'us,' marking the speakers as those toward whom the action is directed. The opening wa- means 'and,' linking it to a preceding statement.

44.meaning: 'You' — the standalone, independent pronoun for addressing a single male person directly.
44.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, second-person masculine singular. Unlike attached pronoun suffixes, it stands alone and is typically used to identify or emphasize the subject ('you [yourself]').

45.meaning: 'Our master / patron / protector.' Mawlā denotes one bound to another by a tie of loyalty and care — a guardian, lord, helper, or ally who is responsible for those under his charge; with the ending 'our,' it names such a one belonging to the speakers.
45.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive pronoun: the final -nā means 'our,' marking the noun as belonging to the speakers as a group. The base mawlā is a noun built on the pattern of a place/agent of nearness and loyalty.

46.meaning: A plea introduced by 'so/then': 'so grant us help / give us victory.' It asks for support and aid to be given to the speakers, especially the kind that brings triumph over an opponent.
46.grammar: A command (imperative) verb: it requests an action. The bare, vowelless stem (nṣur) is the singular command, addressed to one party; the inner vowel u is characteristic of this verb's command form. The attached -nā is the object 'us,' marking the speakers as the recipients of the aid. The opening fa- means 'so' or 'then,' linking this request as a consequence of what came before.

47.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
47.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
47.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

48.meaning: 'The people / the folk' — a collective noun for a community, nation, or group of people regarded as a body. Often it carries the nuance of one's own people or a particular group sharing a trait.
48.grammar: A collective noun with the definite article 'al-' ('the'). The final '-i' is the genitive ending, which typically appears after a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun in an 'of …' relationship.
48.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand/rise; a people, community

49.meaning: 'The disbelievers / those who reject faith' — also 'those who cover up or are ungrateful.' It names people characterized by rejecting the truth and concealing or denying it, in contrast to those who believe.
49.grammar: A definite plural noun: the prefix al- means 'the,' and the -īna ending marks a masculine 'sound' plural in the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) state — the form used when the word is an object of a verb or follows a preposition, as opposed to the subject form -ūna. It denotes many male persons (or a mixed group) of this description.
49.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; hence to disbelieve, reject, be ungrateful
